Α α.definition: indecl., first letter of the Gr. alphabet: as Numeral, = and but = 1,000

ἀβακής.definition: speechless: hence, calm, gentle, Sapph.72. Adv. Poet. ap. EM2.57:—also Hsch., Lex.Rhet.ap.Eust.1494.64

ἀβάκχευτος.definition: uninitiated in Bacchic orgies, E.Ba.472: generally, joyless, Id.Or.319 :—in late Prose, Luc.Laps.3, Jul.Or.7.221d

ἀβαμβάκευτος.definition: not seasoned, of food, Pyrgion ap.Ath.4.143e

ἄβαπτος.definition: of iron, not tempered, Hsch., Suid

ἀβασάνιστος.definition: not tortured, J.BJ1.32.3; untried, unexamined, Antipho1.13; Plb.4.75.3; Plu.2.59c. Adv. without due examination, Th.1.20, Plu.2.28b

ἀβασίλευτος.definition: not ruled by a king, Th.2.80, X.HG5.2.17: generally, free from rule, Plu.2.1125d, Artem.1.8

ἀβάσκανος.definition: free from envy, Telesp.56.1 H.; Ph.1.252; unprejudiced, J.BJ1.9.4. Adv. M.Ant.1.16

ἀβάστακτος.definition: not to be borne or carried, Plu.Ant.16; not removable, IGRom.4.446 . Adv. Hsch

ἄβατος.definition: also Pi.N.3.21:—untrodden; of holy places, not to be trodden, S.OC167,675; . . Id.Fr.88.7, cf. Porph.Abst.4.11; Pl.La.183b; Arist.Pr.924a5: metaph., pure, chaste, Pl.Phdr.245a

Ἀβδηρίτης.definition: a man of Abdera in Thrace, the Gothamite of antiquity, prov. of simpletons, D.17.23:—Adj. like an Abderite, i. e. stupid, Cic.Att.7.7.4, Luc.Hist.Conscr.2

ἄβδης.definition: said by Hsch. to mean scourge in Hippon.98

ἀβέβαιος.definition: unreliable, of remedies, Hp.Aph.2.27; of persons, unstable, fickle, D.58.63, Arist.EN1172a9. Adv. Men.Georg.Fr.2

ἀβεβαιότης.definition: instability, Plb.30.10.1; of persons, D.S.14.9, cf. Ph.1.276

ἀβέβηλος.definition: sacred, inviolable, Plu.Brut.20, cf. Cam.30; of persons, pure, Inscr.Prien.113.67

ἀβελτέρειος.definition: lengthd. for as for Hdn.Gr.1.137; prob. in Anaxandr.12

ἀβελτερία.definition: silliness, fatuity, Pl.Tht.174c, Smp.198d, D.19.98, Arist.Pol.1315a3, etc.; Id.Rh.1390b30; pl., Phld.Lib.p.41O

ἀβέλτερος.definition: silly, stupid, Ar.Nu.1201, Antiph.324, Pl.R.409c, etc.; Polystr.p.29W.; Anaxandr.21; D.19.338: c. inf., Hierocl.in CA10p.434M.: irreg. Comp. Gal.18.337: Sup. Ar.Ra.989; of Margites, Hyp.Lyc.7. Adv. Polystr.l. c., Plu.…

ἀβλεννής.definition: without mucus, Apollon.Lex.51.32 ; as name of fish, = II, Diph.Siph. ap. Ath.8.355f

ἄβολος.definition: that has not shed his foal-teeth, of; an unlucky throw of the dice, Poll.7.204

ἅβρα.definition: favourite slave, Men.64.3, al., LXXGe.24.61, Ex.2.5, al., Plu.Caes.10, Aristaen.1.22, Luc.Tox.14

ἁβροσταγής.definition: dropping rich unguents, Anon. ap.Suid. s.v

ἀβρότονον.definition: or wormwood, Artemisia arborescens, Thphr.HP6.7.3, Nic.Th.92, etc.; southernwood, Artemisia fragrans, Gal.11.804; lavender cotton, Santolina Chamaecyparissus, Dsc.3.24; written Ps.-Dsc. l. c

ἄβροτος.definition: also = , holy, in; without men, deserted of men, v.l. for A.Pr.2, as quoted by Sch.Ven.Il.14.78

ἁβροχίτων.definition: in soft tunic, softly clad, AP9.538; epith. of Dionysus, Inscr.Cos5.11; beds with soft coverings, A.Pers.543

Ἄβρων.definition: Abron, an Argive, proverbial for luxurious living, Suid., Zen.1.4

Ἄβυδος.definition: Abydos, on the Asiatic side of the Hellespont:- Adv. from Abydos, Il.4.500; at Abydos, 17.584:-Adj. of or from Abydos, Ath.13.572e, etc.: prov., a dessert of Abydos, i.e. something unpleasant, variously expl., Zen.1.1…

ἄβυσσος.definition: bottomless, unfathomed, Hdt.2.28; the great deep, LXXGe.1.2, etc.: the abyss, underworld, Ev.Luc.8.31, Ep.Rom.10.7, Apoc.9.1, etc.; the infinite void, PMag.Par.1.1120, cf. PMag.Lond.121.261

ἄβωλος.definition: not mixed with clods of earth, etc., PTeb.370.13 , etc

ἀγαθότης.definition: goodness, LXXWi.1.1, Ph.1.50, Alex.Aphr.in Metaph.695.37, Plot.4.8.6, Sallust.3, etc.; as a form of address, Jul.Ep.12,86

ἀγαθωσύνη.definition: goodness, kindness, LXXJd.9.16, al., Ep.Rom.15.14, Ep.Eph.5.9

ἀγάλαξ.definition: = foreg. I, only in pl; = foreg. II, Hsch., Suid

Ἀγαμέμνων.definition: Agamemnon, Hom., etc.: of a fatal feast, Eust.1507.60:—also epith. of Zeus at Sparta, Staphylus Hist.10, Eust.168.10.—Adj. Hom., also and Pi., A.: Patron

ἀγάννιφος.definition: much snowed on, snow-capt, Il.1.420; Epich.130

ἀγάρροος.definition: contr. strong- flowing, Il.2.845, 12.30; h.Cer.34; AP7.747 , cf. Q.S.10.174

ἀγάστονος.definition: much groaning, of the sea, Od.12.97, h.Ap.94: loud-wailing, lamentable, A.Th.99, cf. AP14.123; Naum. ap. Stob.4.22.32

ἀγάστωρ.definition: from the same womb: pl., twins, Hsch.: generally, near kinsman, Lyc.264

ἀγάσυρτος.definition: 'swept and garnished' , epith. given to Pittacus by Alc.37 B., cf. D.L.1.81

ἀγγελία.definition: Ion. and Ep. message; personified as daughter of Hermes, Pi.O.8.82

ἀγγελιώτης.definition: messenger, h.Merc.296, Call.Jov.68, Hec.1.1.6, Nonn.D.13.36: fem. Call.Del.216

ἄγγελος.definition: messenger, envoy, Il.2.26, etc; generally, one that announces or tells, e.g. of birds of augury, Il.24.292,296; of a poet, Thgn.769; . . Simon.74; of a beacon, Thgn.549; of the nightingale, . . S.El.149: c. gen. rei, …

ἀγελαῖος.definition: belonging to a herd, in Hom; in herds or shoals, gregarious, Hdt.2.93; gregarious animals, Pl.Plt.264d; opp. Arist.HA487b34, Pol.1256a23; ib.1253a8

ἀγελαιών.definition: a place for herds , pasture, Suid

ἀγελάτης.definition: Dor. chief of an II; = Hsch. , cf. GDI5142

ἀγελείη.definition: Ep. epith. of Athena, =; mystical name of Seven, Theol.Ar.42.30

ἀγένειος.definition: beardless, boyish; boys within the age to enter for certain prizes at the games, Pi.O.8.54, 9.89, cf. Ar.Eq.1373, Lys.21.4, Pl.Lg.833c, IG2.965, al., Paus.6.6.3

ἀγέραστος.definition: without a gift of honour, unrecompensed, Il.1.119, Hes.Th.395; E.Hec.115, Ba.1378; Luc.Tyr.3: c. gen., A.R.3.65: -cf

ἄγημα.definition: name of a district in the Heracleopolite nome, PHib.101.3, PTeb.3.38.4

ἀγήρατος.definition: ageless, E.IA567 , IG14.1930.3: also in Prose, Lys.2.79, X.Mem.4.3.13, Pl.Ax.370d, Arist.Cael.270b2, Gal.12.201. Epigr.Gr.35a , IG14.1188, Orac. ap. Ps.-Callisth.1.33.]

Ἀγήτωρ.definition: Leader, epith. of Zeus at Sparta, X.Lac.13.2

ἁγιωσύνη.definition: holiness, sanctity, LXX2 Ma.3.12; as title, PMeyer24.2

ἄγκιστρον.definition: fish-hook, Od.4.369, Hdt.2.70, etc.; hook of a spindle, Pl.R.616c; surgical instrument, Philum.Ven.2.6, Cael. Aur.TP5.1; generally, hook, D.C.60.35

ἄγκοινα.definition: halyard, IG2.794b20, al., prob. in Alc.18.9

ἄγκος.definition: properly, bend, hollow: hence, mountain glen, Il.20.490, Od.4.337, Hes.Op.389, Hdt.6.74, Theoc.8.33, etc.; Trag. only E.Ba.1051

ἀγκτήρ.definition: instrument for closing wounds; part of the throat, Poll.2.134, Hsch

ἀγκυλένδετος.definition: bound with thongs, i.e. javelin, Tim.Pers.23

ἀγκυλόδους.definition: crook-toothed, of a scimitar; barbed, AP6.176

ἀγκυρουχία.definition: a holding by the anchor, A.Supp.766

ἄγλαυρος.definition: daughter of Cecrops, worshipped on the Acropolis at Athens, Paus.1.18.2

ἀγλευκής.definition: not sweet, sour, X.Hier.1.21 , cf. Rhinth.28; opp. Arist.Pr.877b25; Luc.Lex.6; heterocl. acc. Nic.Al.171: metaph., of persons, sour, crabbed, Epich.140; of the style of Thuc., harsh, Hermog.Id.2.12, cf. [Longin.]Rh.p.…

ἀγλωσσία.definition: Att. want of eloquence, E.Fr.56, Antipho Soph.97

ἄγναμπτος.definition: unbending, inflexible, inexorable, B.8.73, Orph.L.27; Plu.Cat.Mi.11, cf. APl.4.278 ; cf

ἄγνοια.definition: want of perception, ignorance, A.Ag.1596; Supp.499; whom seeing you pretend not to know, S.Tr.419; X.Cyr.3.1.38, cf. Th.8.92, Ar.Av.577, D.9.64, etc.; opp. Pl.Tht.199d, Arist.APr.66b26; Pl.R.585b; opp. Arist.EN1110b25…

ἄγνος.definition: Att. = chaste-tree, the branches of; name of a fish, = Diph.Siph. ap.Ath.8.356a

ἀγνύς.definition: loom- weight, in pl., Plu.2.156b, cf. Poll.7.36

ἀγνώριστος.definition: unascertained, unknown, Thphr.HP1.2.3, cf. Poll.5.150, Hierocl.Facet.150; not recognized, Steph.in Hp.1.61 D

ἀγορά.definition: Ion. :—assembly; market-place, perh. not earlier than Hom.Epigr. 14.5 freq. in later authors, Pi.P.5.93; . . A.Th.272; S.Tr.424; Th.6.44; . . E.Or.919; market people, X.An.1.2.18; Ar.Eq.181, etc.; to go into the forum…

ἀγοραῖος.definition: of things, details of market-business, Pl.R.425c; frequenting the market, X.HG6.2.23; Arist.Pol.1291b19, etc.; . . , those who frequented the Hdt.1.93, 2.141; opp. X.Vect.3.13, but = traders , Ael.Tact.2.2:—hence, the…

ἀγός.definition: leader, chief, c. gen., Il.4.265, al., cf. Pi.N.1.51, A.Supp.248,904 , E.Rh.29 , AP9.219

ἄγος.definition: any matter of religious awe; pollution, guilt, Hdt.6.56; 6.91; . . A.Th.1022; Id.Eu.168, cf. AP7.268 ; A.Supp.375; S.Ant.256; Arist.Pol.1303a30; Plu.Cam.18: in concrete sense, the person or thing accursed, S.OT1426; =…

ἀγραῖος.definition: of the chase, epith. of Apollo, Paus.1.41.6; of Artemis, Paus.Gr.Fr.13; Opp.H.3.27

ἄγραπτος.definition: unwritten, S.Ant.454; action cancelled in consequence of a special plea, Poll.8.57

ἀγρεμών.definition: hunter, EM13.56; also glossed by Hsch.: = A.Fr.141

ἀγρέτης.definition: Dor. = Hsch.; prob; perh. from god of the fields, title of Apollo at Chios, GDI5666

ἀγρηνόν.definition: net, Hsch.:—also, net-like woollen robe worn by Bacchanals and soothsayers, Id., Poll.4.116

ἀγρίδιον.definition: Dim. of Sammelb.5230.29 , Arr.Epict.1.10.9, al., M.Ant.4.3

ἀγριμέλισσα.definition: wasp, metaph. of Hegesias, Hsch.; cf

ἄγριος.definition: Od.9.119; also . Il.19.88, Phoc.3.6, Pl.Lg.824a, Theoc.22.36: Comp. Th.6.60: Sup. Pl.R.564a : living in the fields, wild, savage. I. of animals, opp. wild, Il.5.52; 3.24, 9.539; even of flies, 19.30; etc., Hdt.7.86, e…

ἄγριππος.definition: Lacon. name for the wild olive, Suid., etc.; prov., Zen.1.60; in Hsch

Ἀγριώνιος.definition: epith. of Dionysus, transferred to Antony, Plu.Ant.24

ἄγροικος.definition: dwelling in the fields, opp. Arist.HA488b2; esp. of men, countryman, rustic, Ar.Nu.47; in Attica, = , Arist.Ath.13.2, D.H.2.8: mostly with the collat. sense of boorish, rude, Ar.Nu.628,646, etc., cf. Thphr.Char.4; Ar.…

ἀγροικόσοφος.definition: with rude mother-wit, Ph.1.448; in bad sense, ib.577

ἀγροφύλαξ.definition: guardian of the country, APl.4.243 , PRein.48 , PLond.403.11

ἄγρωσσα.definition: huntress, epith. of a hound, Simon.130

ἀγύναιξ.definition: wifeless, S.Fr.4:—also Phryn.Com.19; LXXJb.24.21, PGnom.79 , D.C.56.1, Porph.Abst.4.17, Man.1.173; Poll.3.48; Ar.Fr.735

ἀγχότερος.definition: Comp. of nearer, c. gen., Hdt.7.175. Adv. App.BC1.57

ἄγχουρος.definition: neighbouring, AP9.235 ; bordering on, Orph.A.124; Lyc.418; gold, from the name of the son of Midas, AP15.25.7 codd. , cf. Plu.2.306f

ἀγχώμαλος.definition: nearly equal, Th.3.49; a doubtful battle, Id.4.134; J.BJ6.2.6; Plu.Caes.42, cf. D.H.5.14:—neut. pl. as Adv., Lat. aequo Marte pugnare, Th.7.71; Luc.Herm.12. Adv. Id.VH2.37, App.Praef.11

ἀγωγή.definition: carrying away, Hdt.6.85, etc.; freight, carriage, . . Pl.R.370e, cf.X.Lac.7.5, PLond. 3.948.2 . b. intr., pursued his voyage, Th.4.29 ; movement, Pl.R.604b; tendency towards . . , Hp.Epid.1.1. 2. bringing to or in, yo…

ἀγώγιμος.definition: of things, capable of being carried; of persons, liable to seizure, X.HG7.3.11, cf. D.23.11, Plu.Sol.13, BGU1116.27 :—also of things, D.H.5.69

ἀγώγιον.definition: load of a wagon, X.Cyr.6.1.54; carriage of such a load, PPetr. l.c

ἀδαμάντινος.definition: adamantine, of steel, Pi.P.4.224; metaph., hard as adamant, . . . . Pl.R.360b; Id.Grg.509a; Metrod.Herc.831.12; of a girl, Theoc.3.39. Adv. Pl.R.618e

ἀδάπανος.definition: without expense, costing nothing; of persons, not spending, Arist.VV1251b7; Michel 1007.33 , cf. Inscr.Prien. 111.133

ἀδειγμάτιστος.definition: without a sample, or perh. without an official stamp, PHib.98.17 , PSI4.358.5

ἀδέκαστος.definition: unbribed, impartial, Arist.EN1109b8, Plu.Cim.10, Ael.NA17.16; D.H.Th.34, etc. Adv. Philostr.VA8.7.3, cf. Gal.11.417, Max.Tyr.6.6: Comp. Luc.Hist.Conscr.47

ἀδελφότης.definition: brotherhood, LXX1 Ma.12.10; the brotherhood, 1 Ep.Pet.2.17, 5.9

ἀδενοειδής.definition: glandular, Herophil. ap. Gal.UP14.11:— Plu.2.664f, cf. Gal.UP14.13, Sor.1.12

ἀδέσποτος.definition: without master or owner; of rumours or writings, anonymous, Cic. Fam.15.17.3, D.H.11.50, Plu.Cic.15, etc. Adv. J.Ap.1.16, Sch.Ar.Ra.1400

ἀδημιούργητος.definition: not fashioned, not made for getting up again, of a fallen elephant, D.S.3.27

ἀδημονία.definition: trouble, distress, Epicur.Fr.483, AP12.226 , Plu.Num.4: pl., Ph.2.541

ἀδήν.definition: gland, Hp.Art.11; later, Gal.UP3.9, al., Alex.Aphr.Pr.2.12, Hdn.Gr. l.c

ἀδηνής.definition: ignorant, inexperienced, Semon.7.53, cj. for but expl. as 'without malice prepense' by Hsch, EM17.11: so in Adv. without malice, GDI 5653 :—hence ignorance, Hsch

ἀδιαίρετος.definition: undivided, Arist.Pol.1265b4; indivisible, like Arist.Ph.231b3, al.; Comp., less divisible, Metaph.1052a21. Adv. Phryn.146

ἀδιακόντιστος.definition: which no dart can pierce, prob. in Ael.VH13.15

ἀδιάλλακτος.definition: irreconcilable, my relation to you admits no reconciliation, D.Ep.2.21, cf.24.8, D.Chr.38.17, etc. Adv. D.H.6.56, cf. Plu.Brut.45

ἀδίαντος.definition: as Subst., maidenhair, Adiantum Capillus-Veneris, Orph.A.915: Theoc.13.41; Thphr.HP7.10.5: pl., Plu.2.614b

ἀδικαιοδότητος.definition: where no justice can be got, D.S.39.20

ἀδίκαστος.definition: without judgement given, Pl.Ti.51c; IG12.530 ; undecided, Luc.Bis Acc.23. Adv. without judgement, Aesop.223

ἀδίστακτος.definition: undoubted, undisputed, PTeb.124.26 (ii; Act., undoubting: hence, instinctive, v.l. for I , Pall.in Hp.2.127 D. Adv. unhesitatingly, Phld.Rh.1.133 S., Syr.in Metaph.73.18, Procl.in Prm.p.756S

Ἁιδοβάτης.definition: one who has gone to the nether world, prob.l. for A.Pers.924

ἀδόκητος.definition: unexpected, Hes; either inglorious and glorious, or unexpecting and expectant, Pi.N.7.31, cf. Trag.Adesp.482 :—unexpecting, Memn.28.2, cf. Nonn.D.31.209

ἄδολος.definition: guileless, honest, Pi.O.7.53; in; unadulterated, genuine, A.Ag.95; Dsc.1.66; Eupolem. ap. Alex.Polyh.18; Poll.3.86; PHib.1.85, PGrenf.1.18; ib.2.29.14: metaph., pure, E.Supp.1029 ; 1 Ep.Pet.2.2

ἀδόξαστος.definition: not matter of opinion, i.e. certain, Pl.Phd.84a; Stoic, free from not opining, Aristo Stoic.1.78, Pers.ib.102; refusing to form opinions, Timo ap. Aristocl. ap. Eus.PE14.18. Adv. opp. S.E.P.1.15, etc

ἅδος.definition: or satiety, loathing, Il.11.88; decree, SIG45 , IG12.263.8 ; cf. Hsch. s.v

ἄδραστος.definition: Ion. not running away, not inclined to do so, of slaves, Hdt.4.142, PLond.2.251.14 : metaph., D.Chr.37.10.—In Il. only as pr. n

ἁδρεπήβολος.definition: the power of forming great conceptions, Longin.8.1:—in bad sense, ambitious, Vett. Val.43.2

Ἀδρίας.definition: Ion. the Adriatic, Hdt.5.9, etc.:— Adj. A.Fr.71, also E.Hipp.736 : later, of Italian wine, called Adriatic because imported through Corcyra, AP6.257 : Arist.GA749b29: Chrysipp. Tyan. ap. Ath.7.285d:—also fem. D.P.92

ἀδροσία.definition: want of dew, J.AJ2.5.5, Vett. Val.145.13: poet. POxy.1796.18

ἀδυνασία.definition: = Hdt.3.79, 7.172, Th.8.8: c. gen., Id.7.8:—also v.l. for in D.H.Dem.26, cf. Gloss. , and Dinol.9

ἀδυσώπητος.definition: not to be put out of countenance, inexorable, JHS32.274 , cf. Ph.2.543, Plu.2.64f. Adv. ib.534b

ἄδυτος.definition: not to be entered; never setting, of stars, Sch.Arat.632

ἀεκαζόμενος.definition: particip. form, = Od.13.277, cf. h.Cer.30, Od.18.135

Ἀελλώ.definition: contr. Storm-swift, name of a Harpy, Hes.Th.267

Ἀερία.definition: Ion. old name of Egypt, prob; name of plant, PMag.Par.1.2360

ἀέριος.definition: in the air, high in air, Id.Tr.546; of the air, aerial, opp. Id.Fr.27; Hp.Vict.1.10; title of work by Democr.; opp. PMag.Lond.121.893; Arist.Mu.392b14; ib.398b33; Pl.Epin.984e; Luc.Prom.Es6. Adv. Iamb.Myst.1.9

ἀέροψ.definition: Boeot. name for the bird , Sch.Ar.Av.1354

ἀέτωμα.definition: = IV, gable, Hp.Art.43; IG22.1271.6., cf. Timae.50, J.AJ3.6.4: IG3.162

Ἀζανία.definition: land of or i.e. Arcadia, St.Byz

ἄζευκτος.definition: unyoked, D.H.2.31; Sch.Ar.Lys.217: abs. in same sense, Sch.A.R.4.897

ἀζήμιος.definition: free from further payment, Hdt.6.92; without loss, scot-free, Id.1.212; Pl.Lg.865c; unpunished, E.Med.1050, Ar.Ra.408, Antipho3.3.10, etc.; Pl.R.366a; not liable to penalty, IG1.40; not deserving punishment, S.El.1102…

Ἀζησία.definition: a name of Demeter, S.Fr.981, cf

ἀζήτητος.definition: unexamined, untried, Aeschin.3.22, Aristox.Fr.Hist.15; outside the scope of inquiry, Thphr.Metaph.10. Adv. Ph.1.96; Hierocl.inCA10p.437M

Ἀζόσιος.definition: month at Epidaurus, IG4.1485.20, al. , ib.1539.4; ib.1062.12

ἄζυμος.definition: without process of fermentation, Pl.Ti.74d:—of bread, unleavened, Hp.Vict.3.79, TryphoFr.117; LXXEx.29.2, Le.2.4: abs., Ex.12.15; the feast of unleavened cakes, Ev.Marc.14.1; LXX2 Ch.8.13,al., Ev.Luc.22.1

ἄζωστος.definition: ungirt, from haste, Hes.Op.345, Call.Fr.225; not girded, Pl.Lg.954a; unarmed, SIG527.140 , Hsch

ἀήτης.definition: blast, gale, Il.15.626, Od.4.567, Hes.Op.621: abs., wind, Tim.Pers.117, Theoc.2.38.—Poet. word, Pl.Cra.410b

ἄητος.definition: = the constellation Aquila, Arat.315; only in phrase Il.21.395 ; also and , Hsch

ἀθανασία.definition: immortality, Pl.Phdr.246a; elixir or antidote, Gal.14.148, cf. 13.203

ἀθάρη.definition: gruel or porridge, Ar.Pl.673, Pherecr.108.3, Crates9, Nicoph.15, Anaxandr.41.42. ll.cc.: cf

ἀθαρσής.definition: discouraged, downhearted, Plu.Cic.35, Max.Tyr.25.4, Doroth.in Cat.Cod.Astr.2.195: want of courage, Plu.Nic.4. Adv. Id.Pomp.60, 2.150c

ἀθεάμων.definition: gen. not beholding, Men.Rh.p.383 S. Adv. i.q. Poll.4.10:— also Subst. ib.9

ἀθέατος.definition: unseen, invisible, Luc.Nav.44; that may not be seen, secret, Ps.-Phoc.100, Plu.Num.9, Luc.DMar.14.2; J.AJ14.16.3, etc

ἀθεΐα.definition: = Ael.Fr.39, Sm.Ho.4.15, Sallust.18 , Hierocl.in CA1p.418M.; v.l. for LXX1 Ma.16.17

ἀθεμείλιος.definition: without foundation, Ep. word implied by Hsch. and

ἀθεμελίωτος.definition: = foreg., Hsch.; of a ship, Secund.Sent.17

ἀθεότης.definition: godlessness, Pl.Plt.308e: in pl; atheism, Ph.1.360,368, etc., Plu.2.165c

ἀθεσία.definition: faithlessness, fickleness, Plb.2.32.8, LXXJe.20.8, al., IPE12.352.16 , D.S.18.32: pl., Plb.4.29.4

ἄθεσμος.definition: = LXX3 Ma.5.12, Ph.2.165, J.BJ7.8.1, Plu.Caes.10. Adv. LXX3 Ma.6.26 , Hsch

ἄθεστος.definition: not to be entreated, inexorable, of the Erinyes, Hsch

ἀθέσφατος.definition: beyond even a god's power to express, unutterable: or not according to a god's utterance, unblest, portentous, awful, Il.3.4, Od.7.273, 11.373; vast, Od.11.61, 13.244; 20.211; of great beauty, Hes.Op.662; Emp.134.4.—O…

Ἀθήνη.definition: Athene, Il.1.194, etc.; ib.400; casting vote, from that of A. given for Orestes, Philostr.VS2.3

ἀθήρα.definition: or = Hellanic.192, Sophr.77, PTeb.131 , Dsc.2.92, Eust.1675.60.—Egyptian, acc. to Plin.HN22.121

ἀθηρηλοιγός.definition: consumer of chaff, i.e. winnowing-fan, Od.11.128, 23.275

ἀθηρόβρωτος.definition: devouring chaff, i.e. a winnowing -fan, S.Fr.454

ἀθησαύριστος.definition: not hoarded, not fit for hoarding; Act., not hoarding, prodigal, Poll.3.117

ἄθικτος.definition: untouched: mostly c. gen., untouched by a; chaste, virgin, Ion Trag.11; E.Hel.795, cf. Arar.14; Epigr.Gr.248.8 ; Herod.1.55: of substances, virgin sulphur, Ps.-Democr.Alch.p.45B

ἄθλαστος.definition: which cannot be crushed or dinted; unbruised, of olives, Gp.9.29; of a food-stuff , PFay.333

ἄθλιος.definition: also E.Alc.1038, etc., Att; metaph., struggling, unhappy, wretched, miserable , freq. of persons, A.Th.922, etc.: Comp. S.OT815,1204: Sup. E.Ph.1679:—also of states of life, A.Th.779; E.Heracl.878, Hec.425:—of that wh…

ἆθλον.definition: Att. contr. from Ep., Ion., Lyr. ):-prize of contest, Il.23.413,620, etc., Pi.O.9.108, al., A.Supp.1033, E.Hel.43; inscr. on Attic prize amphorae, CIG776, etc.; IG2.814; in Prose, Th.2.46; Lys.1.47. Phrases: or prizes…

ἀθράνευτος.definition: expl. by prob. uncushioned, E.Fr.569, AB352

ἄθραυστος.definition: unbroken, E.Hec.17, IG2.1054d14, Melinno; unbreakable, Arist.Mete.385a14; indestructible, Placit.1.3.18

ἄθροισις.definition: Att. gathering, collecting, E.Hec.314; Th.6.26; Arist.Mete.340a31; Porph.Abst.1.29; collectively, Hermog.Id.1.4

ἄθροισμα.definition: that which is gathered, a gathering; process of aggregation, Pl.Tht.157b; aggregate, Chrysipp.Stoic.2.23; ib.2.228, cf. Gal.1.67; compound, Max.Tyr.40.5

ἀθροισμός.definition: = Thphr.CP1.10.7, cf. Epicur.Ep.2p.38U., Nat.14.4, S.E.P.3.188; Max.Tyr.6.7; condensation, Thphr.CP5.2.1

ἀθρόος.definition: together, in a body, he paid for all at once, Od.1.43; the citizens as a whole, opp. Th.2.60, cf. 1.141; Id.2.39; was assembled, X.Cyr.3.3.22; their assembled force, ib.4.2.20, cf. An.5.2.1; with one voice, E.Ba.725; …

ἄθρυπτος.definition: unbroken, imperishable; not enervated, Carm. Aur.35; of language, not affected, Plu.Lyc.21:—of a person, never breaking into laughter, Id.Per.5; Id.2.38b. Adv. Id.Fab.3

ἄθυτος.definition: not offered, i.e. omitted, Lys.26.6; not successfully offered, Aeschin.3.131, 152: metaph., of illegitimate children, Pl.Lg.841d, cf. Suid. s.v

ἀθωράκιστος.definition: without breastplate or body- armour, X.Cyr.4.2.31, Plu.Aem.19

Ἄθως.definition: acc. Aeschin.3.132, Theoc.7.77, etc., but in earlier writers Hdt.6.44, 7.22, Th.5.3: Ep. gen. Il.14.229; later gen. Str.Fr.33:—mount Athos, S.Fr.776

αἶα.definition: Ep. form used for metri gr; orig. name of Colchis, S.Fr.914: also part of Thessaly, ib.915

αἰανής.definition: Ion. poet. word, Archil.38; Pi.P.1.83, 4.236, I.1.49: also in Trag. , A.Eu.416; S.Aj.672; A.Eu.479,942 ; Id.Pers.636 ; ib.941 ; . . S.El.506; of Time, A.Eu.572, IG9.886.2 ; eternal, Lyc.928. Adv. for ever, A.Eu.672:— …

Αἰάντειος.definition: of Ajax: his tomb, Philostr.V A4.13; festivals in his honour, Hsch.: prov., of insane laughter, Zen.1.43. [Penult. short Pi.O.9.112.]

Αἰαντίδης.definition: son of Ajax, patron.: hence, one of the tribe in Attica, [D.]60.31

Αἴας.definition: Ajax, masc. pr. n., borne by two heroes, the Greater, son of Telamon, the Less, son of Oiïleus, Hom.:—nom. Alcm.68; voc. Pi.Fr.184, Aeol. Alc.48 A: pl. of tragedies named after Ajax, Arist.Po.1455b34

Αἰγαίων.definition: Aegaeon, the name given by men to the; the Aegaean sea, E.Alc.595

αἴγειος.definition: of a goat, Il.11.639, Hp.Nat.Mul.38; in a goat's skin, Il.3.247; a helmet of goatskin, Od.24.231; Arist.HA522a23; Hp.Acut.49

αἴγειρος.definition: black poplar, Populus nigra, Od.7.106, 10.510, cf. Il.4.482, S.Fr.23, etc.; Od.17.208, cf. 9.141, 5.64,239, E.Hipp.210 ; named among in Arist.Mu.401a4; Mir.835b2: prov., of a seat in the theatre which had no view of t…

αἴγεος.definition: Subst., , a goat's skin, Hdt.4.189; J.AJ1.18.6, cf. LXXNu.21.20; contr. Hdn.Gr.1.310

αἰγιαλός.definition: sea-shore, beach, Il.4.422, Od.22.385, Hdt.7.50, al., Th.1.7 , X.An.6.4.4, Thphr.HP7.13.8 , etc.; distinguished from Arist.HA547a10; also in E., IT425, IA210; a whole beach of voting-pebbles, Ar.V.110: prov., of deaf …

αἰγίθαλλος.definition: or titmouse , parus, Ar.Av.888, Alc.Com.3, cf. Arist.HA592b17, 616b3: prov., Apostol.1.76

αἰγίλιψ.definition: destitute even of goats, hence, steep, sheer, Il.9.15, al. , A.Supp.794 , Lyc.1325; also in form Hsch

αἰγίοχος.definition: aegis-bearing, epith. of Zeus, Il.2.375, al., Alc.85, Emp.142, etc

αἰγίπυρος.definition: rest-harrow, Ononis antiquorum, Thphr.HP2.8.3, Theoc.4.25; IG14.2508

αἰγλήτης.definition: Dor. the radiant one, epith. of Apollo, A.R.4.1716, IG12.259 , 412

αἰγυπιός.definition: vulture, Il.16.428, cf. 17.460, Od.16.217, Hes.Sc.405, Hdt.3.76, S.Aj.169, Arist.HA610a1, Nic.Th.406, cf. Ael.NA2.46

Αἰγύπτιος.definition: Egyptian, Hom., etc.: Adv; name of an ointment, Gal.13.643, etc. [In Hom. etc., are trisyll., Od.4.83, etc.]

Αἴγυπτος.definition: the river Nile, Od.4.477,al; King Aegyptus, A.Supp.9, etc

αἰγών.definition: name of a month at Alexandria, Ptol.Alm.10.9

ἀΐδηλος.definition: Dor. making unseen, annihilating, destructive: in Hom., as epith. of Arcs and Athena, Il.5.897,880; 2.455, al., Emp.109; Parm.10.3; Epigr.Gr.240.5 ; Opp.H.2.487; ib.1.150. Adv. = Il.21.220. II. Pass., unseen , unknown…

Ἅιδης.definition: or Att.; Ep. and Dor; place of departed spirits, first in Il.23.244 . . Luc.Cat.14; AP11.23; Ev.Luc.16.23

ἀΐδιος.definition: also Orph.H.10.21, al., :—everlasting, eternal, h.Hom.29.3, Hes.Sc.310; freq. in Prose, Antipho1.21; Th.4.20; of a tomb, X.Ages.11.16; eternity, Pl.Ti.37e; perpetual . . , Arist.Pol.1285a7, 1317b41, 1301b27; ib.1284b3…

ἀϊδιότης.definition: eternity, Arist.Cael.284a1, Ph.252b3, Ph.1.3,al., Plot.3.7.5, Procl.Inst.55, etc

ἀΐδρυτος.definition: with no fixed abode, Ar.Lys.809 ; D.25.52; Cratin.209

Ἀϊδωνεύς.definition: ), lengthd. poet. form of twice in Hom., Il.5.190, 20.61, cf. Hes.Th.913, A.Pers.650 ; prob. scanned S.OC1560 : gen. and dat. in later poets, Q.S.6.490, Nonn.D.30.172; Mosch.4.86:—hence epith. of Hecate, PMag.Par.1.2855

αἰζήϊος.definition: lengthd. form of Il.17.520, Od.12.83, Hes.Sc.408

αἰζηός.definition: lengthd. , in full bodily strength, vigorous; in Hom. as Adj., . . Il.16.716, cf. 23.432; of a stout, lusty slave, Hes.Op.441, cf. Th.863:— freq. as Subst., Il.2.660, Od.12.440, Call.Jov.70, A.R.4.268, Nic.Al.176, etc…

αἰθαλοκομπία.definition: empty boasting, that is nothing but smoke, Sch.Ar.Eq.696

αἰθέριος.definition: high in air, on high, A.Pr.158 , Th.81, S.OC1082, etc.; flew up into the air, E.Med.440, cf. Andr.830; of the moon, Pythag. ap. Simp.in Cael.511.26: epith. of Zeus, Arist.Mu.401a17

Αἰθίοψ.definition: a fish, Agatharch.109; Adj., Ethiopian, Hdt.3.19; A.Fr.300, E.Fr.228.4: Subst. title of Epic poem in the Homeric cycle; also name of a plant, silver sage, Salvia argentea, Dsc.4.104:— also E.Fr.349: Hdt., etc.; = Hp.M…

αἴθριος.definition: clear, bright, of weather; epith. of Heraclit.120, Theoc.4.43, cf. Arist.Mu.401a17, Thphr.CP5.12.2; of winds which cause a clear sky, h. Ap.433, Arist.Mete.364b29; esp. of the North wind, ib.358b1

αἶθρος.definition: the clear chill air of morn, Od.14.318, cf; = PLond.3.1023.20

αἴθυγμα.definition: gleam, glamour, Onos.28 ; D.Chr.80.5, cf. Plu.2.966b: metaph., spark, Plb.4.35.7 , 20.5.4; Phld.Sign.29; ib.18

αἶκλον.definition: or the evening meal at Sparta, Epich.37, Alcm.71, Polem.Hist.86, cf. Ath.4.139b:—also Hsch., Suid

αἴλινος.definition: cry of anguish, dirge; Adj., mournful, plaintive, E.Hel.171; unhappy, IG14.1502: neut. pl. as Adv., Call.Ap.20, Mosch.3.1: hence sing a dirge, cj. in Dosiad.Ara15

αἴλουρος.definition: Arist.HA540a10, Phgn.811b9, or; = Ps.-Dsc.2.178; also ibid

αἱμασιά.definition: wall of dry stones, to lay walls, Od.18.359; 24.224, cf. Hdt.2.69, Theoc.7.22; Hdt.2.138: of the walls of a city or fortress, Id.1.180, 191, Th.4.43; D.55.11; Theoc.1.47, cf. IG12.248

αἱματίτης.definition: blood-like, haematite, a red iron-ore, Dsc.5.126, cf. Athenod. Tars.4; a disease, Hp.Int.46:— fem., a vein as conductor of blood, Id.Morb.Sacr.15; a black-pudding, Sophil.5; , Thphr.Lap.37

αἱμύλιος.definition: = Od.1.56, h.Merc.317, Hes.Th.890, Thgn.704; in good sense, Eranos 13.87

αἱμύλος.definition: also AP7.643 :—wheedling, wily, mostly of words, Hes.Op.374; Pi.N.8.33, cf. Ar.Eq.687; also A.Pr.208; E.Rh.709; of persons, S.Aj.389 , cf. Pl.Phdr.237b, Lyc.1124; of foxes, Ar.Lys.1268

Αἰνείας.definition: Aeneas, Ep. gen. but in Il.5.534 also Il.13.541 , cf. S.Fr.373.1, etc

αἰνιγμός.definition: riddle, mostly like in pl., Ar.Ra.61, cf. Pl.Ti.72b, Aeschin.3.121; E.Rh.754; Anaxil.22.23: sg., Callisth. ap. Ath.10.452a

Αἰολεύς.definition: Aeolian; pl. Hdt.1.28, Att. or Th.7.57:—hence Adj. of or like the Aeolians, Theoc.1.56 ; of the Aeolic dialect, A.D.Adv.193.15,al.: Comp. 194.8; of Aeolic metre, Heph.7.5. Adv. in the Aeolian mode, Plu.2.1132d:—fem. H…

αἰολίας.definition: a speckled fish, Epich.44, Pl.Com.173.13; as Adj., Numen. ap. Ath.7.308e

αἰόλος.definition: as epith. of armour, glittering, Il.5.295; 7.222, 16.107; S.Aj.1025:—generally, changeful of hue, sheeny, Id.Tr.11; star-spangled night, ib.94 ; smoke flushed by fire-light, A.Th.494; speckled, Call.Dian.91, etc.; dis…

αἱρεσιώτης.definition: member of a sect, Porph.Abst.4.11 : —fem. Suid

αἱρησιτείχης.definition: taker of cities, name of play by Diphilus

αἴρινος.definition: of darnel, Dsc.2.112, Archig. ap. Orib.8.46.3; Aret.CA2.6

Αἶσα.definition: like the divinity who dispenses to; one's lot, destiny, . . . . Od.5.113: c. inf., 14.359, cf. 13.306, al.; . . by ill luck, Il.5.209; B.12.66; S.Aj.256 , cf. AP7.624

αἰσάλων.definition: a kind of hawk, prob. merlin, Falco aesalon, Arist.HA609b8, Hsch

αἴσυλος.definition: unseemly, evil, godless, Il.5.403 20.202; h.Merc.164, cf. AP7.624

αἰσχρότης.definition: ugliness, deformity, Pl.Grg.525a; filthy conduct, Ep.Eph.5.4; euphem. for fellatio, Sch.Ar.Ra.1308 :— Tz.H.11.229

Αἰσώπειος.definition: of Aesop, D.L.5.80, TheonProg.1, etc.; Him.Or.20.1; Plu.2.157b; prov. of an indelible stain, Zen.1.47

ἀΐτας.definition: Dor. word for a beloved youth, answering to or , Ar.Fr.738 , Theoc.12.14 , cj. in 23.63; generally, lover, Dosiad.Ara5, cf. Lyc.461:—fem. Hdn.Gr.1.105, 2.296, cf. Alcm.125

Αἰτναῖος.definition: of or belonging to Etna; sea-fish, Opp.H.1.512

Αἰτωλία.definition: Aetolia, Th.3.96, etc.:—hence Aetolians, Il.2.638, etc.: fem. Hdt.6.127: Adj. Th.4.30, etc

αἰφνίδιος.definition: unforeseen, sudden, A.Pr.680, Th.2.61, Arist.EN1117a18; Th.8.14. Adv. Id.2.53; also Plu.Num.15

αἰφνιδιοτυχής.definition: profiting by strokes of good fortune, Vett. Val.18.16

αἰψηροκέλευθος.definition: swift-speeding, epith. of Boreas, Hes.Th.379, Poet. ap. Apollod.3.4.4

ἀκαθαίρετος.definition: not to be put down, Ph.1.39,al.; not weakened, Sor.1.21

ἀκάθεκτος.definition: ungovernable, Ps.-Phoc.193, Plu.Nic.8. Adv. Ph.2.48; Sch.Opp.H.1.38

ἄκαινα.definition: spike, prick, goad; ten-foot rod used as a measure, Call.Fr.214, cf. Sch.A.R.l.c

ἀκαινοτόμητος.definition: = inlibatus, Gloss.; free from innovations, Just.Nov.61.1.4

ἀκάκης.definition: Dor. poet. form of A.Pers.855 ; epith. of Hades, IG7.117.3

ἀκακήσιος.definition: epith. of Hermes in Arcadia, = sq., Call.Dian.143, Paus.8.36.10

ἀκαλανθίς.definition: = Ar.Pax1079, Ant.Lib.9.3; epith. of Artemis, Ar.Av.872 , Hsch.; AB370; EM44.26)

ἀκαλήφη.definition: sea-anemone, so called from its stinging properties, Eup.60, Pherecr.24, Ar.Lys.549 , Arist.HA531a31, 588b20, Plu.2.670d

ἀκάλυπτος.definition: uncovered, unveiled, S.OT1427, Arist.HA489b5, 1 Enoch9.5; . of one who has no house over his head, Men.404. Adv. LXX3 Ma.4.6

ἀκαλυφής.definition: = foreg., S.Ph.1327, Arist.de Hippobot. ap. D.L.8.72

ἀκάμας.definition: untiring, etc., Il.18.239, 16.176, al. ; Pi.O.1.87; S.Tr.112 ; Critias18; unceasing, Arist.Fr.675; Them.Or.6.79c

ἀκάματος.definition: also Hes.Th.747, B.5.25; untiring, unresting, in Hom. always epith. of fire, Il.5.4, Od.20.123,al.; Emp.111.3; A.Pers.901; B.l.c.; earth that never rests from tillage, or inexhaustible, S.l.c.:—neut. as Adv., Id.El.164

ἀκανθοπλήξ.definition: wounded by the prickle of a fish , name of play of Sophocles

ἀκαριαῖος.definition: momentary, brief, D.56.30, cf. Arist.HA590a3, Phld.Ir.p.80 W., etc.; S.E.P.3.79; of a locus, Aristox.Harm.p.55 M. Adv. Alciphr.1.39

ἀκαρτέρητος.definition: Act., lacking in endurance, Vett. Val.222.12

ἀκατάγνωστος.definition: not to be condemned, LXX2 Ma.4.47, Ep.Tit.2.8, CIG1971 , IG14.2139; Keil-Premerstein Zweiter Bericht 225 . Adv. unexceptionably, IG5.152 , cf. POxy.140.15

ἀκαταγώνιστος.definition: unconquerable, D.S.17.26, Olymp.Hist.p.451 D., Procl.in Cra.p.112P.; epith. of the Stoic sage, Stoic.1.53

ἀκαταιτίατος.definition: not to be accused, J.BJ4.3.10, al.; not to be accused, blameless, ib.2.14.8

ἀκατάλλακτος.definition: irreconcilable, Zaleuc. ap. Stob.4.2.19, D.S.12.20. Adv. D.11.4; Plb.11.29.13; Ph.1.507; ib.479

ἀκάτειος.definition: prop. belonging to an q. v.; esp; Subst. small sail, opp. X.HG6.2.27, Epicr.10 , cf. Luc.Lex.15, J. Tr.46, Hist. Conscr.45; i.e. take to flight, prob. l. for in Epicur.Fr.163, cf. Ar.Lys.64

ἀκάτιον.definition: Dim. of light boat, used; sort of woman's shoe, Ar.Fr.739b, Hsch

ἀκατούλωτος.definition: not scarred over, Herod.Med. ap. Orib.10.11.3, Philum.Ven.10, Ruf.Fr.118

ἀκειρεκόμης.definition: Dor. = of Apollo, Pi.P.3.14, I.1.7, Philostr.Ep.16; of Asclepius, IG3.171; of Avars, APl.4.72

ἀκέλευστος.definition: unbidden, A.Ag.731 , S.Aj.1284, E.El.71, Pl.Lg.953d. Adv. Suid. s.v

ἀκέρατος.definition: without horns, Pl.Plt.265c sq., Arist.HA501a14, al

ἀκέφαλος.definition: headless: fabulous creatures in; without beginning, Pl.Phdr.264c, Lg.752a; without peroration, Luc.Scyth.9; of verses which lack the first mora, Heph.6.2,al., cf. Ath.14.632d. Adv. Hermog.Inv.2.7

ἀκή.definition: point, Hsch., Suid; silence, Mosch.2.18; Hsch

ἀκήλητος.definition: proof against enchantment, Od.10.329 , Pl.Phdr.259b; S.Tr.999 ; of the Dioscuri, Theoc.22.169; Porph. ap. Eus.PE5.10

ἀκηλίδωτος.definition: spotless, LXXWi.7.26, Ph.1.156, Porph.Abst.2.46: metaph., LXXWi.4.9, Ph.2.235; Steph.in Hp.2.238D

ἀκήπευτος.definition: not in a garden, wild, Posidon.29, cf. Gal.12.509

ἀκινάκης.definition: Persian word, short straight sword, Hdt. , cf. X.An.1.2.27 ; a Persian sword kept in the Parthenon, IG1.170.17, cf. 2.646.11; a Scythian oath, Luc.Tox.38, cf.JTr.42. [ăcīnăces in Hor.Od.1.27.5.]

ἄκλαστος.definition: unbroken, Thphr.CP1.15.17, AP9.322 , Phld.D.1.17: metaph., of motion, continuous in space, Arist.Cael.288a25; unbent, of a vein, Gal.5.659

ἄκλειστος.definition: Ion. Call.Hec.2, Att. contr. E.Andr.593, Th.2.93: :—not closed or fastened, ll. cc., X.Cyr.7.5.25, Nic.Dam.p.72 D., etc

ἄκλυστος.definition: = foreg., Zeno.Stoic.1.56, Lyc.736, Plu.Mar.15, Nonn.D.39.8, al.; D.S.3.44; free from inundation, Max.Tyr.414: fem., E.IA121

ἀκμή.definition: point, edge: prov; highest or culminating point of anything, flower, prime, zenith, esp. of man's age, S.OT741; Cratin.195; Pl.R.461a; 460e; ibid.; X.Cyr.7.2.20, etc.; Isoc.7.37; of corn, to be ripe, Th.4.2; Pl.Phdr.2…

ἀκμής.definition: also as neut., Paus.6.15.5: :—untiring, unwearied, Il.11.802, 15.697, S.Ant.353; AP9.526 :—also in late Prose, D.H.9.14, Paus. l.c., Plu.Cim.13, Onos.22.1

ἄκμων.definition: orig. prob. meteoric stone, thunderbolt; anvil, Il.18.476, Od.8.274, Hdt.1.68: metaph., Pi.P.1.86; very anvils to bear blows , A.Pers.51; Aristopho4; i. e. Hercules, Call.Dian.146

ἀκοίμητος.definition: sleepless, unresting, of sea, A.Pr.139; Theoc.13.44; Plu.Cam.20, Ael.NA11.3; LXXWi.7.10; Arr.Epict.1.14.12, etc.; IG9.317.4 . Adv. Ph.Fr.101 H

ἀκοίμιστος.definition: dub. in D.S.38/39.17; gloss on Phot

ἀκοινονόητος.definition: lacking in 'savoir-faire' , Cic.Att.6.3.7, cf. Gell.12.12, Juv.7.218. Adv. Cic.Att.6.1.7 codd

ἀκοίτης.definition: bedfellow, husband, Il.15.91, Od.5.120, Pi.N.5.28, S.Tr.525, E.El.166 :— fem. wife, Il.3.138, B.5.169, A.Pers.684, etc.—Poet. words

ἄκολος.definition: bit, morsel, Od.17.222, AP9.563 , cf. 6.176 , J.BJ5.10.3; Boeot.for Stratt.47.7

ἀκόλυμβος.definition: unable to swim, Batr.158, Str.6.2.9, Plu.2.599b

ἄκομος.definition: without hair, bald, Luc.VH1.23; of trees, leafless, Poll.1.236

ἄκομψος.definition: unadorned, Archil.158, cf. Jul.Caes.317c; 'rude I am in speech', E.Hipp.986, cf. M.Ant.6.30, Chor. in Jahrb.9.176; Phlp.in Ph.528.19. Adv. Plu.2.4f

ἀκονίατος.definition: unplastered, not whitewashed, Thphr.HP8.11.1, cf. Gal.13.356

ἄκοτος.definition: free from anger, cheerful, Pi.Pae.1.3, cf. Hsch

ἀκραγής.definition: not barking, of gryphons, A.Pr.803. Hsch. expl. by cf. · AB369

ἀκραῖος.definition: = Opp.H.2.395, Tab.Defix.18; dwelling on heights, epith. of Hera, E.Med.1379, Apollod.1.9.28; Aphrodite, Paus.1.1.3, 2.32.6; gods whose temples were Poll.9.40

ἀκραιφνής.definition: derived by Sch.Th.1.52, etc., from; untouched, inviolate, E.Alc.1052; in Att. Prose only Th.1.19,52; freq. later, as D.H.6.14, Procop.Aed.1.10, al.; innocent, Ph.1.515:—of troops, fresh, J.AJ18.10.7

ἀκραξόνιον.definition: end of the axle, Poll.1.145, Sch.A.R.1.752

ἀκράτωρ.definition: = II, Pl.R.579c, Criti.121a; Theopomp. Hist.39, cf. Ph.2.357, Ael.Fr.90

ἀκρητόχολος.definition: accompanied by bilious vomiting, of fever, Hp.Fract.43, Art.19

ἀκρία.definition: goddess of the citadel, epith. of Athena, Hsch

ἀκρίς.definition: grasshopper, locust, cricket, Il.21.12, Ar.Ach.1116, Arist.HA555b18, Thphr.Fr.174.3, Theoc.7.41, LXXEx.10.4, etc.:— sg., in collective sense, Men.Prot.p.108D.; Heph.Astr.1.21

ἀκρίσχιον.definition: end of the hip, Heliod. ap. Orib.48.55.1, SIG1025.53

ἄκρον.definition: like highest or farthest point: 1. mountain top, peak, Il.14.292; Od.11.597; heights, Hdt.6.100, Pl.Criti.110e, etc. b. ships’ tops, Alc.Supp.12.9. 2. headland, cape, Od.3.278. 3. end, extremity, Pl.Phd.109d, 109e; ha…

ἄκρος.definition: at the farthest; highest, topmost, Il.1.499, al.; = Il.6.88, cf. 257; 13.523; 14.352; . . at its surface, 16.162; surface of skin, Od.22.278; o mountain tops, S.OT1106: Sup. Sapph.93.2; Orac. ap. Hdt.7.140

ἀκρότης.definition: highest pitch, Hp.VM22; extreme, opp. Arist.EN1107a8; Diog Oen.Fr.38: metaph., excellence, perfection, Phld.D.3.5, cf. D.H.Dem.2, etc.; summit, Procl.Inst.147

ἀκρότητος.definition: not beaten down, Hld.9.8; not struck together or in unison, Trag.Adesp.93 = Com.Adesp.1254, cf. Phot. s.v

ἀκρουροβόρη.definition: swallowing the tip of her tail, metaph. of the Moon, Tab.Defix.Aud.41A7

ἄκρυπτος.definition: unhidden, E.Andr.834, Aen.Tact.39.6. Adv. Phryn.PSp.11 B

ἀκρωνία.definition: prob. = A.Eu.188; but expl. as by Hdn.Gr.1.294 ap.Sch. , cf. AB372

ἀκρωτήριον.definition: topmost or prominent part; end or extremity of anything, ornament of ship's stern- or stem-post, Hdt.8.121, cf. X.HG2.3.8, Polyaen.5.41, Michel 1116 ; h.Hom.33.10

ἀκταῖος.definition: on the shore or coast, epith; dwelling on the coast, belonging thereto, Hp.Aff.52; Orph.A.342; Babr.25.6

ἀκτέανος.definition: without property, poor, BCH15.430 , Man.4.114, AP7.353

ἀκτηρίς.definition: staff, Achae.21; bar of wood supporting chariot-pole, Poll.10.157

ἀκτινείδωλον.definition: ray-image, visual impression, Hestiaeus ap. Placit.4.13.5

ἀκυβέρνητος.definition: without steersman, Ph.1.219, Plu.Caes.28, Luc.JTr.46: metaph., Ph.Fr.110 H., cf. 1.696; Onos.33.2

ἀκύρβιστος.definition: prob. without patches or insertions, BCH35.43

ἄκυρος.definition: without authority, opp. hence; of laws, sentences, etc., invalid, unratified, obsolete, And.1.8; Pl.Lg.954e; Lys.18.15; set aside, Pl.Prt.356d, Is.1.21, etc.; not enforcing the laws, Th.3.37. Adv. Simp.in Ph.168.10

ἄκωλος.definition: without limbs, mutilated, Paus.1.24.3; ill-jointed, and so, moving slowly, gloss on Sch.Od.12.89

ἀκώλυτος.definition: unhindered, Luc.Tim.18; of death, Epigr.Gr. 149.8 , etc. Adv. Pl.Cra.415d, Chrysipp.Stoic.2.269, Str.17.1.25, Act.Ap.28.31, etc.; Procop.Ep.46; also [Democr.] in Fabr.Bibl.4.338

ἄκων.definition: javelin, dart, smaller and lighter than Il.15.709, Od.14.531, al., Pi.P.9.20, E.Ph.1402, etc.; in later Prose, Eratosth.Cat.33, Aristid.Or.26.84, Artem.1.57, Ant.Lib.41.5

ἀκώπητος.definition: not having oars : unequipt, AB373, Hsch

ἀλαβαστοθήκη.definition: case for alabaster ornaments, D.19.237 : generally, small box or casket, Ar.Fr.548 , PLond.2.12

ἀλάβης.definition: or a Nile fish, Str.17.2.4, Ath.7.312b, Gp.20.7.1, POxy.1857.2 ; in Plin.HN5.51 alabetes

ἀλάθητος.definition: gloss on Suid.: coupled; not escaping detection, Astramps.Orac.13.1

ἀλαλή.definition: Dor. loud cry, Pi.Fr.208; E.Ph.337 :— esp. war-cry, Pi.N.3.60; battle, Id.I.7.10: comically, Phoen.3.3 personified, Pi.Fr.78, cf. Plu.2.349c

ἄλαλος.definition: speechless, dumb, prob. in A.Fr.60, LXXPs.37.13, Ev.Marc.9.17, etc.; IG14.1627: Comp. Sch.Pi.N.8.41

ἅλας.definition: = salt, Arist.Mir.844b16, Lycon ap. Hdn.Gr.2.716, LXXLe.2.13, al., Ep.Col.44.6, Gal.14.327; POxy.1222.2

ἀλάστωρ.definition: avenging spirit or deity, with or; Pass., he who does deeds which merit vengeance, wretch, A.Eu.236, S.Aj.374; D.18.296; . . Id.19.305; Bato2.5, cf. Men.7D., Pk.408; Clearch.10

ἁλατοπωλία.definition: right of vending salt, Arist.Oec.1346b21, PFlor.16.33

ἄλγος.definition: pain of mind, grief, freq. in pl., Il.1.2, 2.39, al.: sg., Il.3.97, cf. Od.2.41, etc.; 19.471; 14.32; E.Supp.807; from pain, A.Eu.183; from grief for my shame, E.Hel.201; LXXSi.26.6

ἀλεής.definition: like in the warmth, S.Ph.859 (codd., Sch.; cj. Reiske

ἀλείτης.definition: sinner, of Paris and suitors of Penclope, Il.3.28, sinner against one, A.R.1.1338:—fem. Hdn.Gr.2.67; cf

ἄλειφα.definition: collat. form of sq., v.l. in Hes.Th.553, cf. SIG57.34 , A.Ag.322, Call.Fr.12, Q.S.14.265

ἀλειφόβιος.definition: one that lives by anointing; generally, poor, Ph.2.537, Hsch

ἄλεκτος.definition: not to be told, indescribable, Hp.Ep.13, Pherecr.157, Plb.30.22.12, App.Hann.40

ἄλεκτρος.definition: unwedded, S.Ant.917, Heraclit.All.44; marriage that is no marriage, i.e. unhallowed marriage, S.El.492; E.Tr.254 ; as Adv., S.El.962

ἀλεξίπονος.definition: warding off pain, S.Eleg.7, Carm.Pop.47.10; Maced.Pae.10

ἀλεπίδωτος.definition: without scales, Arist.PA697a7: to be read for Ael.NA12.27, and prob. for Ph.2.352

ἀλέπιστος.definition: not scaled, unscaled, Archestr.Fr.45.8B; unpeeled, Gp.10.11.1; of flax, not scutched, Sch.Ar.Lys.737

ἀλευρίτης ἄρτος.definition: bread of wheaten flour , Diph.Siph. ap. Ath.3.115c, Philistion ib.d; Ath.Med. ap. Orib.1.2.2

ἁλή.definition: only pl. salt-works, Str.12.3.39; . . Id.12.3.12; shd. be read for D.H.3.41, cf. 2.55, PRyl.92.22

ἀληθάργητος.definition: free from lethargy, energetic, CIG2804 ; JRS2.92 , cf. Hsch. s.v

Ἀλήιον πεδίον.definition: lit. land of wandering, in Lycia or Cilicia, . . Il.6.201, cf. Hdt.6.95

ἄληκτος.definition: unceasing, IG14.2126.6; Ph.1.381, al.; interminable, Demetr.Lac.Herc.1061.7. Adv. Ph.2.420; Eun.VSp.458.26B

ἁλής.definition: Ion., = Att. thronged, crowded, in a mass, Hp.Mul.1.5, cf. Hdt.1.133; Hdt.9.15, cf. 7.104, al.: sg. with collective nouns, 7.157; ib.236; Hp.Vict.2.45, Morb.2.4. Adv. prob. in Hp.Mul.1.36: neut. pl.as Adv., Aret.SD2.2…

ἄλητον.definition: meal, Hp.Art.36, Philotim. ap. Orib.4.10.1; Aret.CA1.1: pl., Sophr.39; Rhinth.3

ἀλίαστος.definition: not to be turned aside; = A.R.1.1326, acc. to Sch., cf.EM63.33

ἀλίγκιος.definition: resembling, like, Il.6.401; Od.8.174; of paintings, Emp.23.5; B.5.168; A.Pr.449; IG14.1356, cf. Arat.462, A.R.4.966, etc.:—but compd. is more freq

ἄλιθος.definition: without stones, not stony, of lands; without a stone set in it, of a ring, Poll.7.179

Ἁλικαρνασσός.definition: Ion. Halicarnassus, Hdt.1.144, etc.:—Adj. Ion. Halicarnassian, Hdt.l.c., SIG45.2 , etc.:— fem. Aristodem.1.5. Adv. from Halicarnassus, Luc.Dom.20

ἁλικός.definition: v. :—hence salt-tax, PSI 4.388.1 , PTeb.482 : charges for salt, PPetr.3p.106

ἀλίμενος.definition: metaph., shelterless, inhospitable, E.Hel.1132, Hec.1025; Ar.Av.1400; E.Cyc.349

ἁλιονείκης.definition: = victor in the at Rhodes, PLond.3.1178.67 , Rev.Arch.1915ii200

ἀλιπαρής.definition: not fit for a suppliant, dub. l. in S.El.451; expl. by Sch. as from priv

ἀλιτάνευτος.definition: inexorable, PMag.Par.1.1176, Gloss.; cf. Adv. AB374, EM57.30

ἀλιτρία.definition: sinfulness, mischief, S.Fr.48, Ar.Ach.907; but Et.Gud.z

ἄλκαρ.definition: only nom. and acc.:—safeguard, defence, Il.5.644; 11.823; E.Tr.590 : c. gen. obj., defence against old age, h.Ap.193; Call.Fr.124, A.R.2.1074: abs., remedy, Aret.CA1.1.—Ep. and Lyr. word, cf. Pi.P.10.52, Ps.-Phoc.128. cf

ἀλκή.definition: strength as displayed in action; strength to avert danger, defence, help, Il.15.490, cf.8.140; Od.12.120, 22.305; A.Pr.546; S.Ph.1151; E.Ph.1098: also defence or aid against thing, Hes.Op.201, Pi.N.7.96, S.OT218; give…

ἀλκίβιος.definition: = Cretan bugloss, Echium parviflorum, used as an antidote to snake-bite, Sch.Nic.Th.541

ἀλκυονίς.definition: Adj. with or without winter days during which the halcyon builds, and the sea is calm, hence prov. of undisturbed tranquillity, Ar.Av.1594, cf. Arist.HA542b15, Philoch.180, Luc.Halc.2, Suid.; placed in spring by Ps.-D…

ἀλκυών.definition: mythical bird, identified with the kingfisher, Alcedo ispida, Il.9.563, Alcm.26, Simon.12, Ar.Av.251, Arist.HA542b4, Theoc.7.57

ἀλλάντιον.definition: in later Gk., Dim. of Moer.12

ἀλλεπάλληλος.definition: one upon another, successive, EM702.20; Sch.Arat.982; cumulative, EM291.37; accumulation, Paus.9.39.4; alternating, varying, Vett. Val.331.22; constantly changing, 243.29. Adv. in varied style, 272.23:—also, in layers…

ἄλληκτος.definition: poet. for , unceasing, ceaseless, Od.12.325 ; S.Tr.985 ; implacable, Il.9.636 : neut. as Adv., Man.3.252,206.—So is restored for in Luc.Trag.6

ἀλλοτρίωσις.definition: estrangement, Phld.D.3 Fr.1; aversion, Gal.5.459; from one, App.BC5.78; 3.13; opp. Porph.Abst.3.19; Th.1.35:—Medic., loss of substance, mortification, Aët.13.3

ἄλογχος.definition: without lances or weapons; of a spear, without a head, Hsch.,EM70.36

ἀλοίτης.definition: = avenger, Emp.10:—fem. of Athena, Lyc.936: but = Ps.-Dsc.3.3; = Id.4.75

ἄλοπος.definition: not scutched, Ar.Lys.736: neut. pl., PTeb.120.16

Ἁλοσύδνη.definition: epith. of Thetis, Il.20.207; of seals, Od.4.404 ; of Nereids, A.R.4.1599; cf

ἀλουσία.definition: being unwashed, Hp.de Arte5; E.Or.226, cf. Alex.197: pl., . . Hdt.3.52, cf. Hp.Morb.2.71

ἁλοφόρος.definition: one who conveys salt, Jahresh. 7 Beibl.44, cf. ib.18 Beibl. 287

ἄλπνιστος.definition: Sup. of , sweetest, loveliest, Pi.I.5.12; cf. · Hsch. , Lat. volup.)

ἄλσος.definition: esp. sacred grove, Od.6.291, Hes.Sc.99, Hdt.5.119, Pl.Lg.761c, etc.:—hence, any hallowed precinct, even without trees, Il.2.506, Sch.Pi.O.3.31, cf. B.3.19, S.Ant.844; of the field of battle, viewed as a holy place, A.…

Ἄλτις.definition: sacred precinct of Zeus at Olympia, Pi.O.10.50, X.HG7.4.29, etc.: Elean for Paus.5.10.1

ἀλύμαντος.definition: unhurt, unimpaired, Plu.2.5e, Porph. ap. Eus.PE11.28

ἄλυρος.definition: without the lyre, unaccompanied by it, i.e. wild dirges , E.Alc.447; Hel.185; Poet. ap. Arist.Rh.1408a7; of death, S.OC1223 ; sad talk, Alexis162.6 ; Pl.Lg.810b

ἁλυσίδιον.definition: or Dim. of HeroSpir.1.38, Ph.2.152, POxy.496.3 , AB380

ἁλύσιον.definition: Dim. of sq., Men.258, Philippid.33, PHib.1.121.3 , PMeyer 22.6

ἀλύτης.definition: police-officer at Olympic games , Inscr.Olymp.483, EM72.14

ἀλυχή.definition: = Gal.19.76, cf. Hsch., who also has · cf

ἄλφα.definition: T-square, Eustr.in EN74.2; Phoenician for Hsch

ἀλφεσίβοιος.definition: bringing in oxen, maidens who yield their parents many oxen as presents from their suitors, i.e. much-courted, Il.18.593, h.Ven.119; of the Nile, water that yields fat oxen , A.Supp.855 ; Alex.Aet.3.8: pr. n. used at …

Ἀλφιτώ.definition: bugbear with which nurses frightened children, Chrysipp.Stoic.3.77

Ἀλφιῷος.definition: sc. name of month at Elis, GDI1168

ἁλωαῖος.definition: belonging to the threshing- floor: epith. of Demeter, Orph.H.41.5

ἀλώβητος.definition: unblemished, Ph.1.451; intact, Them.Or.3.43c, cf. Zos.2.5; sound in limb, Gal.13.1026

ἅλων.definition: = , rare in nom., Thphr.Sign.31 , LXXHo.9.2, BGU651.5 ; more freq. in oblique cases, BCH39.55 ), PLille13.3, Arist.Vent.973a14, LXXGe.50.10, etc

ἀλωπόχροος.definition: contr. fox-coloured, f.l. for AB381, Eust.1968.39

Ἀμαζών.definition: mostly pl., the Amazons, Il.3.189; epith. of Artemis, Paus.4.31.8:—Adj. Plu.Pomp.35, title of Epic by Onasus, Sch.A.R.1.1236, Sch.Theoc.13.46:—also Nonn.D.37.17; epith. of Apollo in Laconia, Paus.3.25.3

ἀμαιμάκετος.definition: also Hes.Sc.207:—irresistible, old Ep. word, also in Lyr. and Trag. ; of Chimaera, Il.6.179, 16.329; of fire vomited by her, Hes.Th.319; of fire generally, S.OT177; Hes.Sc.207, Pi.P.1.14; of ship's mast, proof against…

ἀμάλθακτος.definition: unmitigated, Aret.CA2.11; inexorable, AP5.233 ; Olymp.in Alc.p.66C

Ἀμάλιος.definition: sc. month at Delphi, GDI1694, al

Ἀμαλώιος.definition: sc. month at Cyme in Aeolis, BCH12.362

ἁμάμαξυς.definition: gen. or vine trained on two poles, Epich.24, Sapph.150, MatroConv.114

ἁμαμηλίς.definition: = medlar, Mespilus germanica, Hp.Mul.1.44, Aristomen.11, cf.Ath.14.650c

ἄμαξα.definition: Att. prop. frame-work; c. gen., wagon-load, X.An.4.7.10, Cyr.2.4.18; Pl.Euthd.299b; E.Cyc.385, cf. 473

ἁμαξοφόρητος.definition: carried in wagons, of the Scythians, Pi.Fr.104

ἀμαράντινος.definition: of amaranth, i. e. unfading; unfading, imperishable, 1 Ep.Pet.5.4

ἀμάραντος.definition: Subst. , never-fading flower, IG14.607e , Poll.1.229; = Dsc.4.57; = Ps.-Dsc.3.7; = Id.4.55

ἁμαρτάς.definition: Ion. and later Gk. for Hdt.1.91, 119, al., Hp.Acut.39, A.Fr.451C, S.Fr.999, Phld.Sto.339.15, Eus.Mynd.Fr.31, Olymp.in Mete.146.7; copyist's error, Str.13.1.54; sin, in religious sense, J.AJ3.9.3, al

ἀμαρυγή.definition: [Att. sparkling, twinkling, glancing, of objects in motion, as of the eye, h.Merc.45; of stars, A.R.2.42; of the sun, Procop.Vand.2.14; of any quick motion, Ar.Av.925:— also Hdn.Gr.2.743: Sch.A.R.3.1018

ἀμάρυγμα.definition: Aeol. sparkle, twinkle, flashing, radiant glance, Sapph.Supp.5.18, cf. A.R.3.288; of changing colour, and light, AP5.258 ; of gems, Tryph.71, etc.; of any quick, light motion, with the flashing steps of Graces, Hes.Fr…

ἀμάσητος.definition: unchewed, LXXJb.20.18, Archig. ap. Orib.8.46.11, Philum.Ven.3.3

Ἀμβολογήρα.definition: she that puts off old age, youth- prolonging, Spartan title of Aphrodite, Paus.3.18.1

ἄμβροτος.definition: also Pi.Fr.75.17, Tim.Fr.7: (v; epith. of all belonging to the gods, Il.5.339; 16.381; 17.194, Od.5.347; 10.222; 11.330:—also Pythag., = five, Theol.Ar.32

ἀμέθεκτος.definition: imparticipable, Alex.Aphr.in Metaph.637.12, Simp.in de An.218.5, Procl.Inst.23, al.; Chrysipp. Stoic.2.308. Adv. Ascl.in Metaph.115.36

ἀμέθελκτος.definition: free from distraction, dub. in Ph.2.427. Adv. Id.1.559

ἀμέθοδος.definition: not in logical form; without plan or system, Longin.2.2, S.E.P.2.21; esp. Medic., non-'methodic', Gal.10.51. Adv. Phld.Rh.1.127S., cf. S.E.M.8.300, Alex.Aphr.in Metaph.50.7

ἀμέθυσον.definition: = II.1, Dsc.1.123; = II.2, Thphr.Lap.30, Hld.5.13; v.l. in J.AJ3.7.5; cf. Hsch

ἀμέθυστος.definition: not drunken, without; not intoxicating, perh. so used in Nonn.D.19.133: as Subst., remedy against drunkenness, Archig. ap. Gal.12.572, Dsc.Eup.1.24; also Plu.2.15b, Ath.1.34c:—hence, such things as were supposed to ac…

ἀμείνων.definition: gen. irreg. Comp. of better; of persons, stouter, stronger, braver, freq. Hom., etc.: Il.22.158; Hes.Op.19: c. acc. vel inf., Il.15.641, cf. Hes.Op.445, A.Pr.337, etc.; the better sort, Pl.Lg.627a

ἀμειξία.definition: interruption of communications, PLond.2.301.20, PTeb.72.45 ; cf

ἄμεμπτος.definition: blameless, without reproach, E.IA1158; Act., not blaming, well content, or X.Cyr.4.5.52, 8.4.28. Adv. ib.4.2.37

ἀμεσολάβητος.definition: not seized by the middle, i.e. not thrown, of a victorious wrestler, BCH16.445 , LW3.363 : metaph., of the sun, Jul.Or.4.153c

ἄμετρος.definition: without or beyond measure, immense; immoderate, in moral sense, Pl.Lg.690e, etc. Adv. X.Cyr.1.6.34

ἄμη.definition: shovel, Ar.Av.1145, Pax426, X.Cyr.6.2.34; hod; water-bucket, pail, prov. of great abundance, Plu.2.963c

ἀμήνιτος.definition: not angry, Hdt.9.94; A.Supp.975; Id.Ag.649. Adv. ib.1036

ἀμήρυτος.definition: not to be wound up, i.e. tedious, A.R.2.221; Com.Adesp.837; Phld.Herc.873.8; Anon. ap. Stob.3.28.21

ἀμητίσκος.definition: Dim. of Telecl.1.12, cf. Pherecr.130.7 codd. Ath

ἀμητρίς.definition: fem. of dub. l. in Poll.1.122

ἀμήχανος.definition: Dor. without means or; incapable, awkward, h.Ap.192, cf. Theoc.1.85; A.Th.227; E.Hipp.643; awkward at thing, Id.Med.408. Adv., = A.Ch.407, E., etc

ἀμία.definition: kind of tunny, which ascends rivers, perh. bonito, Sotad.Com.1.26, Archipp.20,Arist.HA506b13, Fr.308:—also MatroConv.61:—gender indeterminate, Epich.59, cf.124, Arist.HA488a7, al

ἀμιγής.definition: virgin, Sch.E.Or.108; rolls containing a single author, opp. Tz.Proll.Ar

ἅμιλλα.definition: contest for superiority, conflict; c.gen.rei, trial of strength, Pi.N.9.12 ; A.Pr.129; E.IA212, Med.546, Andr.214; Pl.Lg.731b: c. gen. obj., contest for marriage, E.Hipp.1141; Gorg.Hel.5: abs., eager desire, Herod.6.6…

ἅμιππος.definition: keeping up with horses, i.e. fleet as; infantry mixed with cavalry, Th.5.57, X.HG7.5.23 , Arist.Ath.49.1, cf. Aristarch.ad Hdt.1.215 in PAmh.2.12

ἀμμά.definition: mother, EM84.24; foster-mother, nurse, SIG2868 :—also EM84.26, BGU449 ; epith. of Rhea and Demeter, Hsch

Ἄμμων.definition: the Libyan Zeus, Pi.P.4.16: said to be Egyptian, Hdt.2.42; , = Ps.-Dsc.2.130, etc.:—fem. Adj. Libyan, seat of Ammon, i. e. Libya, E.Alc.114, El.734: Subst. name of state- trireme, Din.Fr.14.2:—also Phot. s.v. AP7.687 …

ἄμναμος.definition: descendant, Lyc.144,872, etc.:—also Poll.3.19, cf. EM84.43

ἀμνημόνευτος.definition: unmentioned, Plb.2.35.4, Plu.Cam.29; Act., = unmindful, D.L.1.86, Numen. ap. Eus.PE14.7

ἀμνησία.definition: = forgetfulness, LXXWi.14.26; decree of amnesty, POxy.1668.18

ἀμνήστευτος.definition: unwooed; not sought in lawful wedlock , E.Fr.815: neut. pl. as Adv., without honourable wooing, Ps.-Phoc.198

Ἀμνιάς.definition: epith. of Eileithyia, Ruf.Onom.229; cf. sq

ἀμνός.definition: lamb, S.Fr.751, Ar.Av.1559; lambs in temper, Id.Pax935: metaph., Ev.Jo.1.36: fem. , Theoc.5.144,149, AP5.205.—Oblique cases usu formed from q. v

ἀμολγός.definition: Hom. always in the phrase usu. of dead of night, Il.11.173, 15.324, cf. h.Merc.7; also of evening twilight, Il.22.317 , and morning twilight, ib.28 ; A.Fr.69; alone, Orph.H.34.12, f.l. in E.Fr.781.6:—as Adj., ib.104

ἀμόλυντος.definition: undefiled, LXXWi.7.22; Act., not leaving any stain, Crito ap.Gal.12.487, cf. Antyll. ap. Orib.9.24.4, Olymp.in Mete.307.1

ἀμονάδιστος.definition: not reduced to a unit, Dam.Pr.117

ἀμόργη.definition: watery part which runs out when; kind of dye , Sch.Ar.Lys.150

ἀμοργίδιον.definition: Dim. of dub. l. in Paus.Gr.Fr.47

ἀμόργινος.definition: made of Ar.Lys.150, Pl.Ep.363a; Antiph.153, IG2.754.10; Clearch.25; Eup.241, Aeschin.1.97:—also expl. as pr. n., made in Amorgos, Poll.7.74; or purple, St.Byz. s.v. EM129.15, cf. 86.16, Sch.Ar.Lys.150

Ἀμοργός.definition: the island of Amorgos, Heraclid.Pol.47, etc.:—Adj. IG1.244, 2.17, etc.:—also Suid. s.v

ἀμπεχόνη.definition: fine shawl worn by women and; clothing, X.Mem.1.2.5, etc.; in pl., modes of dress, Pl.R.425b.:—Dim. AB388, Hsch

ἀμπρόν.definition: rope for drawing loads, , IG2.678B , cf. Sch.Ar.Lys.289

ἀμύθητος.definition: unspeakable, esp. unspeakably great, untold, D.4.34; 21.17; Arist.HA580b16; Id.Pol.1263a40, cf. Phld.Mort.29; Id.Herc.1005.7

ἀμύλιον.definition: Dim. of II, cake, Plu.2.466d, Aq.Ex.16.31 ; of III, starch, Hp.Mul.2.197, Arist.Pr.879a10, Dieuch. ap.Orib.4.7.24

ἄμυλος.definition: not ground at the mill: hence, of the; as Subst., cake of fine meal, Ar.Ach.1092, Pax1195, cf. Stratt.2 D., Theoc.9.21, Telecl.32:— also Ath.14.647f

ἀμφαρίστερος.definition: with two left hands, i.e. utterly awkward or clumsy , Ar.Fr.512: hence, luckless, Hsch., Eust.1228.44

ἄμφασμα.definition: cake soaked in wine and honey , Hsch

ἀμφηρεφής.definition: covered on both sides, close- covered, epith. of Apollo's quiver, Il.1.45: in late Prose, Agath.1.10, cf. 3.5; Zos.2.50

ἀμφήριστος.definition: contested on both sides, disputed, doubtful, i. e. made it a dead-heat, Il.23.382; Call.Jov.5; A.R.3.627; Plb.5.85.6; App.Pun.51; evenly matched, Str.8.4.8, cf. Q.S.5.310, Luc.Eun.4, etc.; of stars, of doubtful positi…

Ἀμφίβαιος.definition: epith. of Poseidon at Cyrene, = Tz.ad Lyc.749

ἀμφίβιος.definition: living a double life, esp. amphibious; metaph., of the soul, denizen of two worlds, Plot.4.8.4; of man, Hierocl.in CA23p.468M.; Dam.Pr.81, cf. 85; ib.399, cf. 400; of the moon, Max.Tyr.40.4; of Tiresias , Luc.Astr.11

ἀμφίβουλος.definition: double-minded: c. inf., half-minded to do, A.Eu.733

ἀμφίβροτος.definition: also covering the whole man, Hom. always Il.2.389; of body as surrounding soul, Emp.148; Nic.Al.216

ἀμφίγειος.definition: with land on both sides, Phot., Suid. s.v

Ἀμφιγυήεις.definition: epith. of Hephaestus, with both feet crooked, lame, Il.1.607, etc

ἀμφίγυος.definition: in Hom. always epith. of either with a limb at each end, double-pointed, or bending both ways, elastic, Il.13.147, Od.24.527; A.R.3.135; prob. stout rivals, S.Tr.504

ἀμφιδέα.definition: anything that binds or is bound around; iron rings, by which folding-doors were secured in hinges, Lys.Fr.37, IG2.834bii99: sg. IG 11.147.7

ἀμφιδεής.definition: afraid on all sides, Hsch., Phot., Suid

ἀμφιδεΐδιον.definition: Dim. of door-ring, prob. in BCH10.463

ἀμφιδεκάτη.definition: Arc. for the 21st of the month, Hsch. :— also IG5.363 ; cf

ἀμφιδιόρθωσις.definition: guarding oneself both before and after saying something which may seem too bold, Alex.Fig.1.5

ἀμφίδουλος.definition: slave both by father and mother, Eub.2 D., Eust.1445.5

ἀμφίδοχμος.definition: as large as can be grasped, X.Eq.4.4, cf. Poll.1.200, Hsch

ἀμφίδυμος.definition: two-fold, double, Od.4.847; A.R.1.940; Opp.H.2.179; Str.6.1.5; of double nature, Opp.C.3.483; with two barbs, 1.92

ἀμφιέλισσα.definition: Ep. Adj., only fem., in Hom. always of ships, Il.2.165,al., either curved at both ends , or wheeling either way, handy; in late Ep., twisting, doubling, Nonn.D.48.328; Jo.Gaz.1.319; wavering, doubtful, Tryph.667

ἀμφιθάλασσος.definition: Att. with sea on both sides, sea-girt, of Rhodes, Pi.O.7.33; of Attica, X.Vect.1.7, cf. Str.9.1.3

ἀμφιθέατρος.definition: having seats for spectators all round, of the Roman circus, D.H.4.44:- also Id.3.68; IGRom.4.861 : esp. neut. as Subst., amphitheatre, IGRom.1.1024.27 , Str.14.1.43, J.AJ15.8.1, Arr.Epict.1.25.27, Procop.Goth.3.23, etc

ἀμφίθετος.definition: in Il.23.270,616 acc. to Aristarch., a cup that will stand on both ends; acc. to others, with handles on both sides, that may be taken up by both sides, cf. Ath.11.501a sq., Eust.1299.55, Hsch

ἀμφικάρηνος.definition: two-headed, Nic.Th.373; in Al.417 v.l. for q.v

ἀμφικέφαλος.definition: two-headed, Eub.107.10 (in poet. form; of a couch, having two places for the head, i.e. two ends, IG1.277d

ἀμφικνέφαλλος.definition: with cushions at both ends, v. II

ἀμφίκοιλος.definition: hollowed on both sides, Suid; doubly concave, of a curvilinear angle, Procl.in Euc.Def.8 p.127F., al

ἀμφίκορος.definition: middle of three brothers, Hsch., Suid

ἀμφίκουρος.definition: lopped of its branches; shorn on both sides, Hsch., Phot.p.102 R

ἀμφίκρανος.definition: surrounding the head, in Ion. form AP6.90 , prob. l. in Nic.Al.417

ἀμφικρεμής.definition: overhanging, AP9.90; hanging round shoulder, APl.4.212 ; App.Anth.3.166

ἀμφικύπελλος.definition: in Hom. always double cup, such as forms a both at top and bottom, Il.1.584,al.: are compared with the cell of a honeycomb, as possessing Arist.HA624a9; but acc. to Aristarch., two-handled, cf. Ath.11.783b

ἀμφιλειπής.definition: incomplete at both ends, of the metrum Choerileum, [⏑]–⏑––|–⏑⏑–⏑⏑–||⏑–⏑–[–] Sch.Metr.Pi.N.11, Mar.Vict. 2559

ἀμφιλύκη νύξ.definition: = half light, morning twilight, Il.7.433; without A.R.2.671, Opp.C.1.135, AP5.280 , Lyd.Ost.65

ἀμφίμαλλος.definition: woolly on both sides, Pherecr.1 D., Ael.VH3.40, Poll.7.57

ἀμφιμάσχαλος.definition: with two arm-holes, Ar.Eq.882, cf. Pl.Com.229, Luc.Lex.10

ἀμφιορκία.definition: oath taken by each party in a lawsuit, Hsch.; also by heliasts, Poll.8.122, AB184

ἀμφιπέλεκκον.definition: double axe, wrongly read in Il.13.612, cf. Hsch

ἀμφίπολος.definition: busied about, busy, epith; later, handmaid of gods, priestess, E.IT1114; IG14.2111

ἀμφιπορφύρεος.definition: edged with purple, prob. in E.Or.1457

ἀμφιπρόστυλος.definition: having a portico on either front, Vitr.3.2.1

ἀμφιπρόσωπος.definition: double-faced, Emp.61; epith. of; on two fronts, Onos.10.2

ἀμφιρρεπής.definition: inclining both ways, Eustr.in EN119.29, Sch.E.Or.633; ambiguity, Eust.1394.57, cf. Sch.E.Or.866. Adv. Eust.200.11

ἀμφίρροπος.definition: doubtful, Polyaen.2.1.23; Agath.4.2. II. precipitous on both sides, Malch.p.415 D

ἀμφίρυτος.definition: also S.Aj.134, flowed around, sea-girt, Od. always fem. of islands, as 1.50; Pi.I.1.8; S. l. Hes.Th.983, Orac. ap. Hdt.4.163, 164

ἀμφισκέπαρνος.definition: dressed on both sides, Milet.7p.56; Rev.Phil.43.200

ἀμφιτάπης.definition: rug or carpet with pile on both sides, Alex.93, Diph.51; but also CIG3071 :—also Ael.Dion.Fr.304, Lycon ap.D.L.5.72; and PEdgar29.4 , LXXPr.7.16, Callix.2

ἀμφίτερμος.definition: bounded on all sides, hedged about, Hsch. Adv. S.Fr.123

ἀμφίτομος.definition: cutting on both sides, two-edged, A.Ag.1496; E.Hipp.1375, El.164; Q.S.11.190

Ἀμφιτρίτη.definition: Amphitrite, Poseidon's wife, Hom; poet., sea, Hymn Is.145, D.P.53, Opp.H.1.423: pl., D.P.99

ἀμφίτριψ.definition: rubbed all round: metaph., like practised knave, Archil.124, cf. Hsch

ἀμφιφῶν.definition: properly part. of cake offered to Munychian Artemis by double light, i.e. either surrounded by lighted tapers, or offered when sun and moon were both visible, Pherecr.156, Philem.67, cf. Poll.6.75, EM94.55

ἄμφοδον.definition: street, Ar.Fr.327, OGI483.80; block of houses surrounded by streets, Hyp.Fr.137, PMag.Par.1.349: prov., Plb.39.3.2: hence, ward, quarter of a town, LXXJe.17.27, SIG961.1 , Ph.Bel.92.42, BGU496 , etc.:—also Gal.UP16.1,…

ἀμφότερος.definition: Hom. has sg. only neut. as Adv., foll. by . . both together, prince as well as warrior, ib.3.179; . . Il.4.60; foll. by . . . . , Pi.P.4.79: also neut. pl., A.Eu.480; Pl.Phd.68c; Ion541b; by . . . . , Pi.O.1.104

ἄμφωμος.definition: round or on the shoulders, Hsch

ἀμώμητος.definition: blameless, Il.12.109, Archil.6.2, Pi.P.2.73, etc.; faultless, D.S.33.5,7; of victims, unblemished, Aristeas93, cf. Ph.Fr.69H.; 2 Ep.Pet.3.14, cf. Eus.Mynd.Fr.21; in epitaphs, CIG4642 , IG14.1937 . Adv. Hdt.3.82

ἄμωμος.definition: blameless, Semon.4; Hdt.2.177; unblemished, of victims, etc., LXXEx.29.1, al., 1 Ep.Pet.1.19, Ph.1.171, al

ἀναβασμός.definition: = Ar.Fr.46 D. , Michel1512 , cf. Paus.10.5.2: metaph., progress, in learning, Plot.6.7.36 , cf. Them.Or.13.177c

ἀνάβλεμμα.definition: looking up, of dogs, X.Cyn.4.4, Poll.2.56

ἀνάβλεψις.definition: looking up, seeing, Arist.Ph.247b8; recovery of sight, LXXIs.61.1, cf. Ev.Luc.4.18

ἀνάγυρος.definition: Anagyris foetida, stinking bean-trefoil, Ar.Lys.68:— also Dsc.3.150: prov., 'let sleeping dogs lie', Lib.Ep.78; 'the fat is in the fire', Ar.l.c.., cf. Sch.ad loc.—From it the Att. deme took its name, Adv. from Anagyr…

ἀνάδελφος.definition: without brother or sister, E.Or.310, Ph.2.291, Vett. Val.15.6, etc

ἀνάδυσις.definition: drawing back, retreat; emergence from underground, J.BJ7.2.2; of land from water, LXXWi.19.7; of bird from lake, Sch.Od.5.337

ἀνάθεσις.definition: setting up in public, dedicating of; putting off, adjournment, Poll.9.137; Ant.Lib.34.1

ἀνάθημα.definition: that which is set up; used by Hom. only in first sense of delight, ornament, Od.1.152, cf. 21.430, IG14.1390; of children, E.Fr.518, cf. Pl.Hp.Mi.364b; to help deserving poverty is D.H.19.14

ἀναίμακτος.definition: bloodless, unstained with blood, A.Supp.196; E.Ph.264; Pyth. ap. D.L.8.22; Nic.Th.90; Them.Or.5.66d, 2.37c, cf. Antyll. ap. Orib.44.23 32

ἀναιμορράγητος.definition: without haemorrhage, Antyll. ap. Orib.45.24.15, Leonid. ap. Aët.15.5

ἀναιμόσαρκος.definition: with bloodless flesh, of the cicada, Anacreont.43.17

ἀναίμων.definition: = bloodless, epith. of the gods, Il.5.342; of cuttlefish, Ion Trag.36; of wine, Plu.2.692e

ἀναίσχυντος.definition: shameless, impudent, Alc.Supp.21.5; of things, shameful, abominable, E.Cyc.416; Th.2.52

ἀναιτιολόγητος.definition: for which no cause can be assigned, Dsc.Ther.Praef.,Alex.Aphr.Pr.1.52, Ptol.Tetr.111

ἀναίτιος.definition: c. gen. rei, guiltless of a thing, Hdt.1.129, 7.233, etc.; A.Ag.1505, Ch.873; Pl.Ti.42d; X.Cyr.1.5.10: c. inf., it is blamable to do, ib.5.5.22

ἀνακάμψερως.definition: a herb the touch of which was said to bring back love, Sedum Anacampseros, Plu.2.939d, cf. Plin.HN24.167

ἀνάκαυσις.definition: setting on fire, kindling, J.Ap.2.39, cf. Plu.2.248d , Anon.Incred.8

Ἀνάκειον.definition: temple of the or Dioscuri, And.1.45, Th.8.93, D.45.80 , IG4.1028.4 ; ib.9.129 ; cf

ἀνακέλαδος.definition: loud shout or din, dub.l. in E.Or.185, where Sch. uses the Verb

ἀνάκουστος.definition: not hearing, deaf, cj. in Ph.2.417

Ἀνακρεόντειος.definition: of Anacreon, Heph.15.22, cf. Sch. Heph.p.118 C

ἀνάκρισις.definition: previous examination of parties concerned in a suit, preparation of the matter for trial, X.Smp.5.2, etc., cf. PSI4.392 , OGI374 , Act.Ap.25.26; of the magistrate, Pl.Chrm.176c, Lg.855e; of the parties, Is.6.13, etc.;…

ἀνακτορία.definition: lordship, rule, A.R.1.839; management of horses, h.Ap.234

ἀνακτόριος.definition: belonging to a lord or king, royal; = Hsch., Suid., v.l. in Hdt.9.65

ἀνάκτορον.definition: king's dwelling, palace, in pl., AP9.657 : mostly of the dwelling of gods, temple, shrine, ib.147 ; E.Andr.43: pl., ib.117, al., S.Fr.757; Hdt.9.65, cf. Hegesand.8, Posidon.41, Chor.p.86.24B

ἀνάκτωρ.definition: = of gods, A.Ch.357, E.IT1414: pl., Cerc.4.36, cf. Ptol.Tetr.122

ἀναλγησία.definition: want of feeling, insensibility, Democr.193, D.18.35, Arist.EN1100b32, Ph.2.318

ἀναλλοίωτος.definition: unchangeable, Arist.Metaph.1073a11, Cael.270a14; D.L.4.17; Ph.1.649; of undigested food, Gal.6.575; Stoic.2.114; not permitting change, Thphr.CP6.10.1

ἀναλογεῖον.definition: gloss on Hsch.; manuale lectorium, Gloss., cf. Poll.10.60, Hdn.Gr.2.457

ἀναλφάβητος.definition: not knowing one's a b c, Nicoch.2D

ἀναμασχαλιστήρ.definition: shoulder-strap, an article of female dress, Philippid.1

ἀνάμβατος.definition: of a horse, that one cannot mount, unbroken, X.Cyr.4.5.46

ἀνάμεσος.definition: in the midst, in the heart of a country, Hdt.2.108; simply, in the midst, between, PLond.2.267.189; Eudox.Ars16; Ph.Byz.Mir.1.2

ἀναμονή.definition: patient abiding, endurance, Sm.Ps.38.8; waiting, delay, Iamb.VP31.197, Ps.-Callisth.1.5, Sch.E.Or.1101

ἀναμπέχονος.definition: without upper garment, of a woman, Euph.53, Pythaen.6

ἀναμπλάκητος.definition: unerring, unfailing; of a man, without crime or error, A.Ag.345, S.Tr.120

ἀναμφίβολος.definition: unambiguous, Ascl.Tact.12.11; v.l. in D.H.3.57; Gal.17.370. Adv. M. Ant.1.8, Luc.Anach.24

ἀναμφίλεκτος.definition: = sq., D.H.9.44; Longin.7.4. Adv. PPar.15.3.56 , S.E.M.7.5, Luc.Rh.Pr.15

ἀναμφίλογος.definition: undisputed, undoubted, X.Mem.4.2.34, Smp.3.4 ; D.H.3.57. Adv. without dispute, willingly, X.Cyr.8.1.44; unquestionably, indisputably, Id.Ages.2.12, D.H.3.41, Luc.Herm.36

ἀνανθής.definition: flowerless, Pl.Smp.196a, Thphr.HP1.14.3, CP3.19.1, Plu.2.684c; Thphr.HP6.8.4

ἀνάνιος.definition: without pain: Act., not giving pain, Hsch., EM97.43. Adv. ib.44. cf

ἀνανταγώνιστος.definition: without a struggle, Th.4.92; irresistible, Ph.1.454, al., Plu.Phoc.14; Polem.Call.50

ἄναξ.definition: of the gods, esp. Apollo, Il.1.390, al.; A.Ag.509; ib.513, Eu.85, etc.; S.OT80; without Hdt.1.159, 4.150, al.; of Zeus, Hom. only in voc., Il.3.351, 16.233; A.Pers.762; . . Id.Supp.524; D.35.40; Poseidon, A.Th.130; of…

Ἀναξαγόρειος.definition: of Anaxagoras, Satyr.Vit.Eur.Fr.37; the saying of A., Plu.2.679a; Pl.Cra.409b

ἀναπάλη.definition: name of a dance, Ath.14.631b; a form of exercise, Ruf.Ren.Ves.2.33

ἀναπεπταμένος.definition: pf. part. Pass. of q. v. Adv. explicitly, Plot.5.1.8

ἀναπνοείτης.definition: one who restores breath to an athlete after a contest, BMus.Inscr.1109

ἀναπόνιπτος.definition: unwashen, Ar.Eq.357, Phryn.Com.3 D; = not to be washed out, Suid

ἀνάπραξις.definition: exaction of a debt or penalty, D.H.6.1; IG9.694.10

ἀνάπτυσις.definition: expectoration, Gal.15.480, Herod.Med. in Rh.Mus.58.93; Alex.Trall.5.5; of fistulae, opening out, Antyll. ap.Orib.44.23.6

ἀναρμόδιος.definition: unfit, Zos.1.29, Men.Prot.p.110 D., Davidin Porph.132.23. Adv. AB363

ἀνάρρινον.definition: = Dsc.4.130 , Gal.11.834; sternutative, Hp. ap. Gal.19.79

ἀνάρριψις.definition: throwing up, of a volcano, Plu.2.398e, v.l. ib.951c

ἀνάρρωσις.definition: recovery, Simp.in Ph.5.1, cf. Philum. ap. Aët.5.123, Hsch. s.v

ἀνάρσιος.definition: of persons, hostile, implacable, Il.24.365, Od.14.85; ib.10.459, 11.401, etc.; , of Apollo, A.Ag.511; enemies, S.Tr.853 ; opp. ib.641 , cf. Theoc.17.101

ἀνάρτυτος.definition: unseasoned, of food, Phld. Mus.p.53 K., Diogenian.2.12, Sm.Jb.6.6; cj. Coraës in Ath.12.511d

ἀνάσιλλος.definition: or with hair brushed up on the forehead as the Parthians wore it, Plu.Crass.24; restored by Sylburg in Arist.Phgn.809b24, 812b35, cf. PGrenf.1.10.11

ἀνάσσυτος.definition: rushing upwards, of air, Hp.Mul.2.124, cf. Hsch

ἀναστοφάγος.definition: not eating the , Orac. ap. Paus.8.42.6

ἀνάτασις.definition: abs., height, J.BJ6.9.1; Phlp.in Mete.37.10; stretching out, Hp.Art.11; Onos.17: metaph., threats of violence, Plb.4.4.7, Fr.108 ; Epict.Fr.25, cf. D.S.38.8

ἄναυος.definition: etym. of Att. A.D.Adv.145.4, cf. Eust.387.44

Ἄναυρος.definition: river in Thessaly, Hes.Sc.477, etc; as Appellat., mountain-torrent, Mosch.2.31, Nic.Al.235, Lyc.1424, IG 14.1089, etc

ἀναυτούργητος.definition: not to be cultivated by the lessor in person, PTeb.378.29

ἀναφαίρετος.definition: not to be taken away, Men.Mon.2, D.H.8.74, D.Chr.31.22; POxy.273.15 ; Just.Nov.68Pr.; inseparable, opp. accidental, Stoic.2.214 ; not diminished by subtraction, Theol.Ar.30. Adv. PFlor.47a4 , Just.Nov.2.3Intr

ἀνάφορον.definition: = I, Ar.Ra.8, Ec.833, Fr.559, cf. Phryn.PSp.15 B

ἀνδηρευτής.definition: workman employed on dikes, PRyl.157.15 , PFlor.369.9

ἀνδράποδον.definition: one taken in war and sold as a; low fellow, 'creature', Pl.Grg.483b, Thg.130b, X.Mem.4.2.39, D.Chr.31.109; of a female slave, Pherecr.16 D

ἀνδράχλη.definition: said to be Att. form for; warming-pan or brazier, Eust.1571.25, Poet. ap. Suid

ἀνδράχνη.definition: purslane, Portulaca oleracea, Id.CP1.10.4; = Dsc.4.168; but = Sedum stellatum, stone-crop, ib.90; also = Ps.-Dsc.2.186, Gal.19.146

ἀνδρεῖος.definition: Ion. (codd. of Hdt; manly, masculine, courageous, Hdt.7.153, etc.; even of women, Arist.Pol.1277b22, Po.1454a23; and in bad sense, stubborn, Luc.Ind.3: neut., = Th.2.39; E.Supp.510; Id.Andr.683. Adv. Ar.Pax498, al.: S…

ἀνδρεράστρια.definition: woman that is fond of men, Ar.Th.392

ἀνδριάς.definition: gen. : :— image of a man, statue, Pi.P.5.40, Hdt.1.183, 2.91, Ar.Pax1183, Th.1.134, etc.; Pl.R.515a; paint statues, ib.420c; esp. of portrait-statues, Plu.Lys.1; IG12.240 ; SIG730.26 ; of female figures, Ath.10.425f, …

ἀνδρίον.definition: Dim. of manikin, Ar.Pax51; pitiful fellow, E. ap.Phot.p.127 R., Theoc.5.40, cf. Eup.316

Ἀνδρομέδα.definition: Andromeda, Pherecyd.12 J., etc; the constellation Andromeda, Eudox. ap. Hipparch.1.2.13, Arat.189, etc

ἀνδρόμορφος.definition: of man's form or figure, Apollod.1.6.3, cf. Eust.1571.45

ἀνδρόσαιμον.definition: a kind of St. John's wort

ἀνεγγάρευτος.definition: = free from obligation to serve as Sammelb.4226

ἀνέγγραφος.definition: of which no written evidence exists, IG 5.357.162 , cf. Sch.Pl.Ap.19b, Suid

ἀνέγγυος.definition: not vouched for, not accredited, of uncertain weather, Anacr.113; of an illegitimate child, Pl.R.461b; unhallowed, E.ap.Phot.p.128R.; of a woman, unbetrothed, unwedded, Plu.Caes.14, Comp.Thes.Rom.6, D.C.59.12, etc.; D…

ἀνεγκαρτέρητος.definition: not to be endured, Phld.Herc.1251.4: v

ἀνέγκλιτος.definition: unchanging, Plu.2.393a, cf.Per.15; Gramm., not enclitic, A.D.Synt.136.7,al

ἀνέδραστος.definition: without firm foundation, of a rhetorical period, D.H.Comp.22; IG7.2543 ; of a bandage, liable to slip, Gal.18.379; unsteady, ib.819, cf. Plu.2.654a, Procl.in Prm.p.794 S., in Ti.3.122 D. Adv. gloss on Sch.Philum. ap. …

ἀνείδεος.definition: formless, Placit.1.2.3, cf. Ph.1.417, al., Plot.1.8.3, al., Ael.NA2.56; without specific difference, Dam.Pr.425; of persons, Aen.Gaz.Thphr.p.62B

ἀνεικόνιστος.definition: not registered with personal description, BGU 258.9

ἀνειλείθυια.definition: without the aid of Eileithyia, never having invoked her aid in childbirth, E.Ion453, cf. Eust.1861.44

ἀνείσοδος.definition: without entrance or access, Plu.Dio7, Pyrrh.29

ἀνείσπρακτος.definition: free from pecuniary liability, BGU1133.13 , POxy.270,286

ἀνεκτέος.definition: to be borne, S.OC883; Ar.Lys.477: Clearch.4

ἀνελεήμων.definition: gen. merciless, without mercy, Arist.Rh. Al.1442a13, Ep.Rom.1.31, Cat.Cod.Astr.2.173:—also Nicoch.20; and in AB400 Adv. Antipho1.25, LXXJb.6.21

ἀνέλκωτος.definition: without ulcers, Dsc.2.32, Aret.SD1.12; Leonid. ap. Aët.16.42, cf. 15.14, Aret.SD2.11

ἀνελλιπής.definition: unfailing, unceasing; not lacking, OGI194: abs., lacking nothing, Plot.5.8.7. Adv. = mean exactly, Alex.Aphr.in Top.43.3.—Also spelt Eutoc.in Archim.3.114.16 H., Ammon.in APr.32.22

ἀνεμέσητος.definition: not incurring the wrath of God, Pl.Cra.401a: Id.Smp.195a; also, not liable to blame, . . c. inf., Id.Tht.175e, Aeschin.3.66,Epicur.Fr.161,etc. Adv. Pl.Lg.684e

ἄνεμος.definition: cardinal point, quarter, LXXZa.2.6, Annales du Service19.40 , Ev.Matt.24.31, al., Vett.Val.140.6, PFlor.50.104: sg., ib.20.19 ; aspect, POxy.100.10

ἀνεμώτας.definition: ass sacrificed to the winds at Tarentum, Hsch

Ἀνεμῶτις.definition: she that stills the wind, Paus.4.35.8

ἀνενεχύραστος.definition: not liable to distraint, CPR1.15 , etc

ἀνεξίκμαστος.definition: not dried up, Arist.Pr.928a29, cf. Gal.8.367

ἀνεξικώμη.definition: expl. by Hsch. as Cratin.383, but rather

ἀνέπαφος.definition: untouched, unharmed, D.35.24, cf. Syngr.ib.11; not liable to seizure, Men.Per.8; GDI1532, cf. Thphr.Fr.97.2, IG2.584c, BGU193.19 ; PHamb.28.8 ; unencumbered, PThcad.1.12 : c. gen., unharmed by, M.Ant.3.4. Adv. Suid

ἀνερίθευτος.definition: unbribed, uncorrupted, GDI13585 , Michel473 ; not honeycombed by intrigues, Ph.2.555, cf. 538

ἀνερίναστος.definition: not ripened by caprification, of figs, Thphr.HP2.8.3, CP2.9.12, Suid.; cf

ἀνερμάτιστος.definition: without ballast; metaph., an empty table, Plu.2.704b; unstable, Dam.Pr.413; also of persons, without ballast, Ph.2.451, Plu.2.501d, Plot.1.8.8; Longin.2.2

ἀνερμήνευτος.definition: with none to interpret, E.Hyps.Fr.1; inexplicable, indescribable, S.E.M.7.65; Aristaenet.2.5

ἀνέσιμος.definition: given up to idleness, a holiday, Sch. Th.7.73; loose, Sch.Lyc.18

ἀνέστιος.definition: without hearth and home, homeless, Il.9.63; S.Fr.4, cf. Ar.Eq.1266; Luc.Sacr.11, cf. Eus.Mynd.59: metaph., Max.Tyr.14.8; savage, Opp.H.2.417

ἀνετεροίωτος.definition: unchangeable, Arist.Mu.392a32; unaltered, Phld.Po.994.3, S.E.M.8.455; undifferentiated, Dam.Pr.68, Procl.in Prm.p.926S

ἄνετος.definition: set free from labour, esp. of men and animals dedicated to a god, Hyp.Fr.72; Philostr.Im.1.28, cf. App.BC1.110; of land, consecrated and lying untilled, Ael.NA11.2, Poll.1.10

ἀνεύθυνος.definition: not accountable, irresponsible, opp; guiltless, innocent, Luc.Abd.22: c. gen., Id.Nigr.9; irreproachable, of athletes, Philostr.Gym.48. Adv. Poll.3.139, Just.Nov.8.12Intr.—In Att., was more common

ἀνεύρετος.definition: undiscovered, Pl.Lg.874a, D.S.5.20, Plu.2.700d, POxy.472.14 , etc

ἀνέφαπτος.definition: not to be claimed as a slave , GDI 1684 sqq

ἀνέφεδρος.definition: without drawing a bye, SIG1070.6 , IG5.680,al

ἀνέφελος.definition: unclouded, cloudless, Od.6.45; Arist.Mu.394a23; Plu.Arat.21, etc.: metaph., not to be veiled or hidden, S.El.1246

ἀνέφικτος.definition: out of reach, unattainable, Ph.1.228,al., Phld.Rh. 1.27S., Plu.2.54d, Luc.Herm.67, Jul.Or.2.82d

ἀνηγεμόνευτος.definition: without leader, unguided, Ph.1.337, cf. 696, Luc.Icar.9; M.Ant.12.14

ἀνήδυντος.definition: not sweetened or seasoned, Hp.Int.21; metaph., Id.Pol.1340b16; Plu.Phoc.5; Them.Or.18.218b; so, unpleasant, Hegesand.26; Plu.2.142b, 405d; ib.799d

ἄνηθον.definition: or Aeol. Alc.36, Sapph.78, 128, also Anacr. ap. Poll.6.107. Thphr.HP9.7.3:—dill, Anethum graveolens, Ar.Nu.982,Th.486, Thphr.HP1.11.2, Alex.127.5, Theoc.15.119, Ev.Matt.23.23, Dsc.3.58, SIG1170.26 , Bilabel

ἀνήκεστος.definition: incurable, desperate, fatal; of persons, X.Oec.14.8; Plu.Per.39; J.AJ18.6.10: Comp. f.l. in Antipho5.91: Sup., Ph.2.316

ἀνηλεγής.definition: unconcerned, reckless, Q.S.2.75: neut. in Hsch. Adv. Q.S.2.414

ἀνήλειπτος.definition: unanointed, should be read for in Antyll. ap. Orib.10.13.19:—also or D.C.56.30, Philagr. ap. Orib.5.19.10, Hp.Ep.17

ἀνήλικος.definition: not yet arrived at man's estate, Ps.-Callisth.1.38, Suid. s.v

ἀνήλιος.definition: Dor. without sun, unsunned, sunless, of the nether world, A.Th.859 ; Id.Pr.453, Ch.51; S.OC676 ; E.Andr.534

ἀνηλιποκαιβλεπέλαιος.definition: barefoot and unanointed , Epigr. ap. Hegesand.1

ἀνήνυτος.definition: endless, never-ending, Id.El.167, cf. Plb.9.24.4; Pl.Grg.507e; Phld.Herc.1251.17; etc., Ph.1.85, etc.: neut. pl. as Adv., Epicur.Fr.470

ἀνήνωρ.definition: unmanly, Od.10.301; a man; childless, Hsch

ἀνήροτος.definition: unploughed, A.Pr.708; without tillage, Od.9.109: neut. pl. as Adv., Opp.C.1.462: metaph., Luc.Lex.19

ἀνησιδώρα.definition: sending up gifts, epith. of Earth, Ath.Mitt.37.288 , cf. Sch.Ar.Av.971; of Demeter, S.Fr.826, Alciphr.1.3, Paus.1.31.4, Plu.2.745a; of Rome, ib.317a

Ἄνθεια.definition: epith. of Hera at Argos, Paus.2.22.1, EM108.47; at Miletus, in dat., Milet.3 No.31.5; of the Hsch.; also of Aphrodite at Cnossus, Id

ἄνθεμα.definition: name of dance, in Ath.14.629e, unless this be neut. pl. of

ἄνθεμον.definition: = Sapph.85, Semon.7.66, Pi.N.7.79; name of a plant, Matricaria Chamomilla var. eradiata, and Anthemis chia, Thphr.HP7.8.3

ἀνθερεών.definition: later, neck, throat, Euph.92.1 : sg., AP9.129 , Q.S.1.110: sg. in both senses, Ruf.Onom.47,48

ἀνθηδών.definition: the flowery one, i.e. the bee; eastern thorn, Crataegus orientalis, Thphr.HP3.12.5:—hence as epith. of Crataegus monogyna, hawthorn, ibid

ἀνθήλη.definition: the silky flower-tufts of the reed, Thphr.HP4.10.4, Dsc.1.85, cj. for in Hsch

ἄνθος.definition: gen. pl. freq. used for; generally, anything thrown out upon the surface, eruption, Hp.Coac.416; cf. froth or scum, Gal.11.628, Gp.6.3.9,7.15.6; = Nic.Th.257; v. = Poll.7.99

ἄνθρυσκον.definition: chervil, Scandix australis, Sapph.Supp.25.13, Cratin.98.6, Pherecr.109 , Thphr.HP7.7.1 :—in Hsch. in Poll.6.106

ἀνθρωπότης.definition: abstract humanity, Ph.1.206, S.E.M.7.273, Vett.Val.346.29, Plot.6.1.10, Dam.Pr.58

Ἀνθρωφηρακλῆς.definition: title of play by Pherecrates, Phot.p.145R

ἀνθύλλιον.definition: Dim. of M.Ant.4.20, Dsc.2.183; = sq. I, Plin.HN26.84, cf. 21.175

ἀνίατρος.definition: Ion. no-physician, Hp.Praec.7, Arist.Ph.191b6, Plot.6.7.37, Alex.Aphr.in Top.33.2: Adj., unworthy of a physician, Antyll. ap. Orib.10.23.24

ἀνιππία.definition: tax paid in lieu of service in cavalry, PSI4.388.36 , PPetr.2p.129 , PTeb.99.56

ἀνιπτόπους.definition: gen. with unwashen feet, epith. of the Dodonaean priests of Zeus, Il.16.235, cf. BCH7.276 ; applied to parasites by Eub.139; to the Great Bear, as metuens aequore tingi, by Nonn.D.40.285

ἄνιπτος.definition: unwashen, . . Il.6.266, cf. Hes.Op.725, Ev.Matt.15.20: prov., i.e. unprepared, Luc.Pseudol.4. 2. not to be washed out, A.Ag.1459

ἀνισότης.definition: inequality, Pl.Phd.74c, al., Arist.Pol.1302a26, etc.: pl., Procl.Hyp.5.3

ἀνίωτος.definition: not liable to rust, Arist.Mir.833b31, PLeid.X.36B

ἀνόδευτος.definition: impassable, Aq.Je.18.15; trackless, Hedyl. ap. Str.14.6.3; Lyd.Mag.1.50

ἀνοδία.definition: a road that is no road, Ph.2.156, al.; Porph.Chr.1; mostly in dat. through places with no roads, Plb.5.13.6, 4.57.8, D.S.19.5, Plu.2.508d, cf. Mar.37. II. ascent, Vett.Val.343.18

ἄνοθος.definition: = pure, genuine, unadulterated, Ph.1.454; 2.156. Adv. ib.216, al., Hsch
