ἀνοίκτιστος.definition: unmourned, [Arist.]Pepl.28; Act., pitiless, IG2.376 . Adv. Antipho1.25

ἄνοικτος.definition: pitiless, ruthless, E.Tr.787, Ar.Th.1022. Adv. without pity, without being pitied, S.OT180, E.Tr.756: also Ant.Lib.39

ἄνοιξις.definition: opening, Th.4.67,68; Thphr.Od.13; Plu.2.738c, cf. PMag.Lond.46.274 : pl., Porph.Antr.27; Hebraism for LXXEz.29.21, 2 Ep.Cor.6.11, Ep.Eph.6.19, etc

Ἀνολυμπιάς.definition: an Olympiad omitted in the list, Paus.6.22.3

ἀνομίλητος.definition: having no communion with others; c. gen., uneducated, Pl.Ep.332c: abs., Luc.Merc.Cond.14: c. dat., Gal.15.159, 18.287

ἀνομοθέτητος.definition: unregulated by law, Pl.Lg.781a, 785a, Arist.Pol.1269b19; D.H.7.41

ἀνομοιότης.definition: unlikeness, dissimilarity, Pl.Prm.159e, Plt.273d, Thphr.CP1.2.2, Hierocl.in CA26p.481M.: in pl., Pl.Plt.294, Arist.Po.1448a10

ἀνονόμαστος.definition: faulty form for Gal.7.425, Hdn.Epim.203, Suid

ἄνοος.definition: contr. without understanding, silly, Il.21.441; Pl.Ti.44a, etc.; of persons, S.Ant.99; ib.281; wealth without wit, AP9.43 : Comp. A.Pr.987: Sup. Pherecr.19D. Adv., Comp. S.Fr.589.1

ἄνοπλος.definition: without the or large shield, of the Persians, who bore only Hdt.9.62: generally, unarmed, PlEuthd.299b, Onos.42.17; opp. of citizens not entrusted with arms, Arist.Pol.1289b32:—of ships, unarmed, Plb.2.12.3

ἄνορμος.definition: without harbour, Anon. ap. Suid. s.v. metaph., S.OT423

ἀνοσία.definition: freedom from sickness; may he be accursed, Inscr. Cypr. 135.29 H. ; cf. sq

ἀνόσιος.definition: more rarely E.Tr.1316; of things, etc., Hdt.2.114, 3.65, S.OC981, etc.; Id.OT1289; Antipho2.4.7; X.Cyr.8.7.22; Id.Lac.8.5; a corpse with all the rites unpaid, S.Ant.1071; the holy rites have been profaned, Antipho5.84

ἀνοσιότης.definition: unholiness, wickedness, v.l. in Pl.Euthphr.5d; Isoc.12.121

ἄνοσμος.definition: = without smell, v.l. in Hp.Acut.63, cf. Arist.HA634b19, etc.; footsteps that leave no scent, Poll.5.12:—but was preferred

ἀνόστεος.definition: boneless, of the polypus, Hes.Op.524 cf. Hp.Epid.2.2.19; Arist.PA666b17; ib.655a2; Opp.H.1.639

ἀνότιστος.definition: free from moisture, dry, Dsc.1 Praef.9; Archig. ap. Orib.8.2.6

ἄνοτος.definition: without the south wind, Hsch. s.v

ἀνουθέτητος.definition: unwarned, unadmonished, Isoc.2.4; that will not be warned, Men.Mon.49, Plu.2.283f

ἀνουσίαστος.definition: without the use of an , PMag.Par.1.2441

ἀνοχή.definition: holding back, stopping, esp. of hostilities; time, opportunity, LXX1 Ma.12.25; delay of some days, POxy.1068.15

ἀνταῖος.definition: set over against, right; besought with prayers, epith. of Hecate, etc., A.R.1.1141, cf. Orph.H.41.1; . . A. ap.Hsch.; Sch.Il.22.113

ἀντακαῖος.definition: a sort of sturgeon, Hdt.4.53, Lync.1.9; Adj., Antiph.186

ἀντάμειψις.definition: exchanging, requital, v.l. in LXXPs.118 .112, Hsch

Ἀντάρης.definition: the star a Scorpii, Heph.Astr.1.3, Ptol.Calend.p.214W., Id.Alm.8.1

ἀντάρχων.definition: vice-president, IG22.1077, cf. ib.12 .35e ; pro- magistrate, SIG785.17 , POxy.907.21 ; AJA18.329

ἀντεραστής.definition: rival in love, Ar.Eq.733; generally, rival, Pl.R.521b, Arist.Rh.1388a14:—fem. Gloss

ἄντη.definition: prayer—a word preserved by Hsch. · and restored by Herm. for in S.El.139

ἀντήλιος.definition: opposite the sun, i.e; of the moon, reflecting the sun's rays, AB403 , cf. Suid.: hence metaph., imitation, reflection, Theopomp.Hist.367

ἀντηρίς.definition: prop, stay, support, E.Fr.1111: pl; = window, Suid.:—and in E.Rh.785 it must mean nostrils, if it be the right reading. E. ll.cc.: hence in Apollod.Poliorc.178.4, HeroBel.101.9, is wrong; so ib.89.4 is f.l. for as Ins…

ἀντιαττικιστής.definition: Anti-Atticist, title of grammatical work, AB77

ἀντίβασις.definition: resistance, Ph.Bel.73.14; ground of opposition, Phld.Sign.27

ἀντίβλημα.definition: stone inserted in vacant space in masonry, POxy.498.16

Ἀντίγονος.definition: name of several Macedonian kings:—hence of Antigonus, Polyaen.4.9.1; name of a festival in his honour, Plb.28.19.3, IG11.154A42 : also Plu.Arat.54:—fem. a kind of cup named from him, Polem.Hist.57, Plu.Aem.33:— to be …

ἀντιδάκτυλος.definition: thumb, Aq.Ex.29.20; in Metric, dactyl reversed, anapaest, Diom.1.478K., Choerob.in Heph.p.215C

ἀντιδίσκωσις.definition: doubling of the sun's disk, Lyd.Ost.9c

ἀντίδουπος.definition: re-echoing, A.Pers.121 ; ib.1040, parodied by Pl.Com.27D

ἀντίθυρος.definition: opposite the door, opposite the door of the house, Od.16.159, as the Sch.; or it may be a neut. Subst. the part facing the door, vestibule, as it is in S.El.1433, ubi v. Herm.: in Luc.Symp.8, the side of a room facing…

ἀντικάρδιον.definition: in Poll.2.165, pit of the stomach: but Ruf.Onom.68 makes it the depression in the throat above the clavicle, = cf. Hsch

ἀντικάτων.definition: Anticato, name of a book written by Caesar in reply to the Cato of Cicero, Plu.Caes.54, App.BC2.99

ἀντίκεντρον.definition: that which acts as a goad, A.Eu.136,466

ἀντικέφαλον.definition: back of the head, Lyd.Mens.4.54; as Adj. back to back, PMag.Par.1.2954

ἀντικνήμιον.definition: part of the leg in front of the , shin, Hippon.49, Hp.Fract.18, Ar.Ach.219, Eq.907

ἀντιμέτωπος.definition: front to front, face to face, X.HG4.3.19, Ages.2.12, Hld.9.16

ἀντιμίσιον.definition: table in a court of justice, Suid

ἀντίνωτος.definition: in pl., back to back, D.S.2.54, Ael.Tact.37.1, Arr.Tact.29.1

ἀντίπαλος.definition: properly, wrestling against; of things, nearly matched, nearly balanced, Th.1.91; equally large, Id.4.120; Id.1.11, Pl.Mx.240a; Th.3.49; fear caused by the balance of the power of the parties, mutual fear, ib.11; adeq…

ἀντιπατρίς.definition: name of a kind of silver vessel, IG11.110, al

ἀντίπλευρος.definition: with its side opposite, parallel, S.Fr.24.4; Hld.10.29

ἀντίποινος.definition: for recompense, Lyc.271; in substitution, Id.1201

ἀντιπολέμιος.definition: warring against, enemies, Th.3.90 codd. ; in Hdt.4.134,140, codd. vary between and but in 7.236, occurs without v.l., and is the only form cited by Hsch., cf. Onos.10.9,al

ἀντίπολις.definition: rival city, Str.3.5.3, v.l. in D.S.11.81

ἀντίπορθμος.definition: over the straits, plains on opposite sides of the straits, E.Ion1585; in the parts opposite Peloponnesus, Id.Fr.515, cf. Arist.Mu.392b23, Lyc.1071: c. dat., Str.8.6.21

ἀντιπορνόβοσκος.definition: title of a comedy by Dioxippus, Ath.3.100e

ἀντίπορος.definition: = on the opposite coast, i.e. Europe, as separated by a strait from Asia, A.Pers.66, cf. Supp.544, E.Med.210; i.e. her templeat Aulis over against Chalcis in Euboea, Id.IA1494 : —in X.An.4.2.18 simply, over against, o…

ἀντίπους.definition: gen. with the feet opposite, of one at the Antipodes, Pl.Ti.63a; so Arist.Cael.308b20, cf. Eratosth.16.19; the Antipodes, Str.1.1.13, Cleom.1.2, Cic.Acad.Pr.2.39.123, Plu.2.869c

ἀντίπρασις.definition: contract of sale executed by the purchaser, PLond. ined.2227

ἀντίπρῳρος.definition: with the prow towards; face to face, . . S.Tr.223 ; in front of them, E.Rh.136 ; Plu.de IraFr.27B

ἀντίρρινον.definition: calf's snout, Antirrhinum Orontium, Thphr.HP9.19.2 , Dsc.4.130

ἀντίσκηνος.definition: opposite the stage-buildings, prob. sc. Ephes. 2.41

ἀντίσκιος.definition: throwing a shadow the opposite way, Ach.Tat.Intr. Arat.31, Vett.Val.142.28, Jul.Or.4.147c; . . Nonn.D.7.311

ἀντισπόδιον.definition: substitute for [mineral] ashes, vegetable ashes, Orib.15.1.27, Gal.12.234:—also Dsc.1.109, 5.75

ἀντισταδιαῖος.definition: a furlong long, i. e. enormous, Sch.Od.12.90

ἀντίστεπνον.definition: the part of the spine opposite the breast, Sor.2.63 , Ruf.Anat.25

ἀντίστομος.definition: drawn up face to face, Ascl.Tact.11.3, cf. Ael.Tact.37.3, Arr.Tact.29.2, Hsch

ἀντιστράτηγος.definition: enemy's general, Th.7.86; at Rome, acting commander or governor, either pro consule, Plb.28.3.1, or pro praetore, D.C.41.43

ἀντιστρατιώτης.definition: soldier of the enemy, Gal.19.180, Chor.inLib.4.522 Reiske

ἀντισύγκλητος.definition: counter-senate, name given by Marius to his body-guard, Plu.Mar.35, Sull.8

ἀντιταμίας.definition: = Lat. pro quaestore, SIG745 , J.AJ14.12.13, D.C.41.43, etc., prob. in IG14.356 ; cf

ἀντίτραγος.definition: the eminence of the external ear, Aret.CD1.2, Poll.2.85, Ruf. ap. Orib.25.1.7

ἀντιφάρμακον.definition: antidote, Arist.Mir.837a18, Ceb.26, Ath.3.84f, Ruf.Fr.58.1, Apollon. ap. Philum.Ven.33.6, Dsc.1.125:—Adj. D.S.17.90

ἀντίχειρον.definition: thumb-breadth, HeroGeom.4.11; also thumb, Antyll. ap. Orib.7.9.8

ἀντίχθων.definition: opposite or counter-earth; southern hemisphere, Cic.Tusc.1.28.68; Jul.Or.5.173c: in pl., people of the southern hemisphere, Ach.Tat.Intr.Arat.30, Plin.HN6.81

ἀντίχορδος.definition: concordant, Hsch.: but; metaph., in reply or opposition to, Plu.2.663f

ἄντλος.definition: in Poll.1.92 also Hom., hold; bilge-water, . . let in no water, metaph. for 'let no enemy come in', A.Th.796; pump out water from a ship, E.Tr.691; metaph. for getting into a difficulty, Id.Heracl.168

ἄντομος.definition: dialectic form of stake or pale, cf. , Hsch.: hence collectively, paling, boundary-fence, Tab.Heracl.1.15, al.; also, road adjoining such a fence, ib.2.13, al

ἀντόπτρα.definition: name of a surgical instrument, Hermes 38.281

ἀντριάς.definition: = fem. of grot- Nymphs, AP6.224 , cf. Phryn.PSp.27 B

ἀντωμοσία.definition: oath or affidavit made by the prosecutor, Pl.Ap.19b, Lys.23.13; also, by the defendant, Is.3.6, cf. Harp. s. v., Poll.8.55

ἀνύβριστος.definition: not insulted, PRyl.117.26; Act., not insulting, decorous, Plu.Sert.26; Id.2.46c; 92d: Sup., D.Chr.3.98. Democr.73

ἄξος.definition: Cret., = St.Byz. s.v. B. Maced. word for Hsch

ἀξυγκρότητος.definition: for not welded together by the hammer: metaph. of rowers, not trained to pull together, Th.8.95; of style, not compact, rambling, D.H.Dem.19

ἄορνος.definition: without birds, S.Fr.748; heights no birds can reach, Plu.2.327c; lake Avernus, Arist.Mir.839a13; called by Str.5.4.5; a hill-fort on the Indus, D.S.17.85, Plu.2.181c

ἀπαιδαγώγητος.definition: without teacher or guide, Arist.EN1121b11; uneducated, untaught, in a thing, Id.Pol.1338b33 lack of education, Sor.1.33

ἀπαίσιος.definition: ill-omened, App.BC1.78; Plu.2.266d; Opp.H.1.372; Luc.Pseudol.12; Procl.in Cra.p.39P. Adv. Gal.1.292

ἀπάλαιστρος.definition: not trained in the palaestra; generally, awkward, clumsy, Cic.Orat.68.229, Quint.Inst.9.4.56, Phld.Rh.1.8 S

ἀπαλαίωτος.definition: not growing old or decaying, Hsch.s.v

ἀπάλαμνος.definition: in Lyr. and Eleg., reckless, lawless, Pi.O.2.57; of acts, Sol.28.12; Thgn.481; Id.281; E.Cyc.598

ἁπαλίας.definition: a sucking pig, D.L.8.20 ; cf. Hsch

ἀπανάγνωσμα.definition: fault in reading, faulty reading, A.D.Synt.146.24, al

ἀπανάστασις.definition: migration, Str.4.1.13, J.BJ1.15.3; departure, D.H.9.6, Philostr.Ep.11

ἀπαράγγελτος.definition: without formal declaration, . Adv. without signal of battle, Plb.16.3.1, Fr.11

ἀπαρακόντιστος.definition: not defeated in javelin-throwing, Ephes.2. No. 72

ἀπαρθένευτος.definition: unmaidenly, unfitting a maiden; deflowered, Sch.Theoc.2.41

ἄπαρσις.definition: setting out, departure, D.H.3.58, LXXNu.33.2, J.AJ17.9.3

ἄπαυστος.definition: unceasing, never-ending, Parm.8.27; not to be stopped or assuaged, insatiable, Th.2.49; Antiph.237.4; Eus.Mynd.1

ἀπείριτος.definition: = Od.10.195, Hes.Th.109; boundless, immense, D.P.4; Orph.Fr.91, al.: neut. pl. as Adv., Timo12

ἀπέλεθρος.definition: immeasurable, Il.5.245, cf. Od.9.538; sprang back immeasurably, Il.11.354; countless, Nonn.D.19.330

ἀπελέκητος.definition: unhewn, unwrought, LXX3 Ki.6.1, al.: metaph., Crantor ap.D.L.4.27

Ἀπέλλων.definition: Dor. form of IG5.145 , GDI 5075 , etc.; cf. Inscr.Cypr.140H

ἀπέπαντος.definition: not ripened, unripe, Thphr.CP2.8.4, AP9.561 , Dsc.5.34; cf. Hsch

ἀπερείσιος.definition: = ; countless ransom, Il.1.13, al.; 16.178; A.R.1.419; AP7.363

ἀπίαστος.definition: not to be caught, Hsch. s.v

ἀπίδιον.definition: Dim. of pear, Sch.Od.7.115 codd., Alex.Trall.Febr.3

ἀπίμελος.definition: without fat, not fat, Diocl.Fr.136, Arist.HA519b8, PA675b11, al.: Comp. ib.672a23: Sup. HA520a19

Ἆπις.definition: and Ion. Apis, a bull; a mythical king of Argos, v. II

ἀπλεονέκτητος.definition: free from anarice, Chaerem. ap; without excess, Theol.Ar.34

ἀπλήρωτος.definition: insatiable, Phld.Mus.p.78K., Ph.2.266; unfilled, Poll.1.121; absence of satiety, Plot.5.8.4

ἁπλοδίσημος.definition: dub.sens., apptly. of embroidery or weaving, PLond.ined.2132

ἀπνεής.definition: corrupt in AP9.420 as epith. of

ἀπόδρασις.definition: c. gen., escape from, avoidance of, D.21.166; evasion, Plu.2.641c

ἀπόδυσις.definition: stripping, undressing; gloss on Lat. obitus, POxy. 1099v42

ἀπόθερμος.definition: as Subst., = Sch.Ar.Pl.1122; = Sch.Theoc.9.21; a kind of drink, Hp.Mul.1.44, 2.207

ἀπόθεστος.definition: despised, Od.17.296, cf. Lyc.540, Call.Fr.302, Plu.2.159f

ἀποθέωσις.definition: deification, Str.6.3.9, CIG2832 , Cic.Att.1.16.13, Senec.Apoc.tit., PGen.36.18 , Hierocl.in CA27p.483M

ἀποθηρευτής.definition: drinking-cup used after hunting, IG11.113.17 , al

ἀπόθητος.definition: not desired, Hsch., dub. in Call.Fr.302

ἀποθυμίασις.definition: rising of smoke or vapour, Plu.2.647f

ἀποίητος.definition: not done, undone, Pi.O.2.18; Men.113. 2. not to be done, impossible, Plu.Cor.38. II. not artificial, unpolished, D.H.Lys.8; esp. unpoetical, opp. Id.Comp.1; opp. Phld.Po.1081; not used as material for poetry, ibid.; s…

ἀποίκιλος.definition: unadorned, simple, Ph.1.369, al.; homogeneous, Plot.6.7.13, cf. Iamb.VP23.103. Adv. Vett. Val.343.36

ἀποίκιλτος.definition: not elaborated, without convolutions; = foreg. in Adv. Sch.A.Pr.317

ἀπόκενος.definition: not quite full, Dsc.5.36, cf. Gal.17.163; empty, HeroSpir.2.24

ἀπόκινος.definition: comic dance, of an indecent nature, Cratin.120, Ar.Fr.275, Poll.4.101, Ath.14.629c: metaph., find some way of dancing off or off or escaping, Ar.Eq.20

ἀποκολοκύντωσις.definition: transformation into a pumpkin, a travesty of the of the Emperor Claudius, attributed to Seneca, D.C.60.35

ἀπόκομμα.definition: splinter, chip, Theoc.10.7; PHolm.1.40; shred, Luc.VH1.18; block of wood, of an idol, Aq.Ez.20.7; of stone, IG11.158A32

ἀπόκρυφος.definition: hidden, concealed, E.HF1070; c. gen., unknown to him, X.Smp.8.11

ἀπόκτησις.definition: deed of gift, PGrenf.2.70.26 (iii A; loss, Secund.Sent.19, cf. Paul.Al.N.4

ἀπόκτισις.definition: planting of a colony, Call.Ap.74, D.H.1.49

ἀπόκυνον.definition: dog's-bane, Marsdenia erecta; name of a poisoned cake for dogs, Hsch

ἀπολάντιον.definition: perh. name of a grass, PMag.Lond.1.121.209

Ἀπολλόδωρος.definition: pr. n., Apollodorus, Th.7.20, etc.:—hence Adj. Str.13.4.3

Ἀπόλλων.definition: Pythag. name of a number, Porph.Abst.2.36

ἀπολοιπασία.definition: remainder, in subtraction; list of arrears, POxy.1147.1 , cf. ib.1855.4

Ἀπόμυιος.definition: Averter of flies, epith. of Zeus and Heracles, Paus.5.14.1, EM131.23

ἀπομυξία.definition: dirt from the nose, AB432, Hsch

ἀπόξυσμα.definition: that which is shaved or scraped off: shavings, filings, Dsc.Eup.1.175, Sch.Ar.Pax48

ἀποπάλησις.definition: gloss on read by Erot. in Hp.Fract.42, cf. Gal.19.84

ἀπόπεμπτος.definition: dismissed, dub. in PPetr.2p.52 ; cf. Hsch

ἄποπτος.definition: seen or to be seen from a; out of sight of, far away from, S.OT762; Id.El.1489: abs., Far away, Id.Ph.467; Pl.Ax.369a; Plu.Eum.15; Phld.Rh.1.149S., Piet.27, cf. Gal.4.628

ἀπόπτυγμα.definition: portion of the folded back, IG 2.652A20

ἀπόρθητος.definition: not sacked, unravaged, . . Il.12.11; B.8.52, cf. 99; Hdt.6.28; Hell.Oxy.16.3; of Attica, E.Med.826, cf. A.Pers.348; of Laconia, Din.1.73, cf. Lys.33.7; Antiph.117

ἀπορραντήριον.definition: a vessel for sprinkling with holy water, E.Ion435, IG1.143, al

ἀπόρραξις.definition: a game of ball, Poll.9.103,105, Eust.1601.33

ἀπόρρυτος.definition: = running, Hes.Op.595; subject to efflux, opp. Pl.Ti.43a; of the sea, Arist.Mete.353b32; having an outflow, Porph.Sent.44

ἀπόρφυρος.definition: without purple attire, Plu.2.528b; esp. of a garment, without purple border, Id.Ant.71, POxy.1741.21

ἀποσκεπαρνισμός.definition: chipping off with an adze: name for a particular kind of wound in the head, Gal. ap. Orib.46.21.3, Sor.Fract.1,7

ἀποσκευή.definition: removal, riddance, i.e. assassination; baggage, in sg. and pl., Plb.2.3.7, 1.66.7, Plu.2.174a, etc.; household stuff, LXXGe.34.29, UPZ110iii90 , etc.; Ezek.Exag.209

ἀπόσκημμα.definition: support, prop, A.Fr.18; = Ruf. ap. Orib.45.30, Gal.18.133, Simp.in Epict.p.37 D

ἀπόσκηψις.definition: determination of humours to one part of the body, Hp.Aph.6.56, Prorrh.2.7; Aret.SD1.9; wrongly expl. as = by Gal.19.84

ἀποσπάδιος.definition: torn off or away from, Orph.H.18.13; = AP6.102

ἀπόσσυτος.definition: rushing away, Opp.H.2.560, Nonn.D.2.686, al.; thrown out of a chariot, ib.28.165; starting from a mark, of racers, Opp.H.4.102; departing from, Tryph.668

ἀπόσταγμα.definition: that which trickles down, Tz.ad Lyc.607, EM538.16

ἀποστράτηγος.definition: retired general, to remove him from the command, supersede him, D.23.149; also, general who has completed his term of office, Plu.Marc.22

ἀπόσυρμα.definition: that which is peeled off, abrasion; mark left by a rope dragged along, POxy.69.8

ἀπόταφος.definition: not buried in one's ancestral tomb; buried separately, IG12.656 , Hsch.,EM131.43

ἄποτμος.definition: unhappy, ill-starred, Il.24.388, Od.20.140; A.Pers.280 ; E.Hipp.1144 : Comp. Mosch.4.11: Sup. Od.1.219

ἀποτράγημα.definition: remains of a dessert, v.l. for Eup.284

ἀπουρία.definition: issue of free and slave, Suid., Zonar

ἀπουσία.definition: waste, as in smelting ore, Arist.Mete.383b3, Agatharch.28; POxy.1273.32

ἀποφύλιος.definition: having no tribe, i.e.foreign, A.Fr.287, Poll.3.56

ἀπόφυσις.definition: side-shoot, Thphr.HP6.4.4; in Anatomy, process of a bone, i. e. the prominence to which a tendon is attached, Hp.Art.45; processus dentatus, Gal.UP12.7, etc.; Ruf.Onom.142; of the ib.159

ἀποφώλιος.definition: acc. to the Ancients, = empty, vain, idle, Hom. only in Od., 8.177; 5.182; 14.212; are not barren, 11.249; Opp.C.3.447; Man.6.565; Orac. ap. Jul.Ep.89; of the Minotaur, a monstrous, hybrid birth, E.Fr.996; in Nic.Al.5…

ἀπόχιμος.definition: of or for a receipt, PCair.Preis.14.13

ἀποχλωρίας.definition: one whose complexion has become pale, Hsch

ἀπόχυμα.definition: that which is poured out; name of a kind of plaster, Aët.15.24

Ἀπραγόπολις.definition: Castle of Indolence, Sans-souci, as Augustus called his retreat on an island near Capri, Suet.Aug.98

ἄπρακτος.definition: Ion. Pi.I.8.7 codd; Act., unavailing, unprofitable, Il.2.121; ib.376; Simon.5.16, cf. Pi. l.c.; D.9.40; days when no business is done, holidays, Plu.2.270a, cf. BGU 255.8 ; restful, B.9.8; Proll.Hermog. in Rh.4.15 W. …

ἄπρατος.definition: unsold, unsaleable, dub. in Lys.7.6, cf. D.34.9, BGU 18.4 , al.; unprostituted, Aeschin.2.23. Adv. Sch.Il.1.99

ἀπριγδόπληκτος.definition: struck unceasingly, prob. l. for in A.Ch.425

ἄπριστος.definition: not to be sawed, Aen.Tact.20.2; unsawed, Q.S.12.137, prob. in CPHerm.28.11

ἄπροικος.definition: without portion or dowry, Is.3.29, cf. D.40.20; Lys.19.15, Diod.Com.3.4, cf. Men.Mon.371

ἀπροσωπόληπτος.definition: not respecting persons, Suid. s.v. Adv. without respect of persons, 1 Ep.Pet.1.17

ἀπτόητος.definition: poet. undaunted, LXXJe.26.28, Nonn.D.22.355, Sch.Il.1.56, etc. Adv. Phalar.Ep.103.2

ἅπτρα.definition: Dim. wick of a lamp, Sch.D.T.p.195 H

ἀπύθμενος.definition: without bottom or base, Thphr.Fr.94; Parth. ap. Ath.11.501a, cf. Dsc.Eup.1.235; Secund.Sent.14:—also Eust.870.28: Theognost.Can.86

ἀπύλωτος.definition: not secured by gates, X.HG5.4.20; Ar.Ra.838

ἀπύρετος.definition: free from fever, Hp.Aph.4.20, Luc.Philops.25, POxy.1582.9 ; not inducing fever, Hp.Art.69; Antiph.226.6; relieving fever, Archig. ap. Gal.13.173:— perh. to be read for f.l. in Thphr.Char.3.6

ἀπυρηνομήλη.definition: probe without a knob , Hp. ap. Gal.19.85

ἀπύρωτος.definition: not exposed to fire, brand-new, Il.23.270; uncooked, Thphr.Od.10; of the moon in eclipse, not fiery, Placit.2.29.2; incombustible, Thphr.Lap.19,22

ἀπφίδιον.definition: Sch.Luc.Cat.12, and Eust.565.23, Dim. of also Poll.3.74, cf. Hsch

ἀπώλεια.definition: destruction, Arist.EN1120a2, etc.: pl; loss, Id.Pr.952b26; opp. Plb.6.59.5 Schweigh., cf. BGU1058.35, al. ; Diog.Oen.1

ἀπώλευτος.definition: of horses, unbroken, Anon. ap. Suid

ἀπῶρυξ.definition: canal from a place; layer of a vine, LXXEz.17.6, Gp.5.18.1, POxy.1631.10

ἀπώτερος.definition: Comp., farther off, = Suid.: neut. as Adv., Euc.3.15,al.; opp. Id.Phaen.p.4 M

ἀραβοτοξότης.definition: Arab archer, employed for police duty in Egypt, PAmh.2.77.4 , etc

ἀραδιούργητος.definition: not dishonestly done, AB357, Suid. s.v. Adv. = sine fraude, Just.Edict.7.7

ἄραδος.definition: disturbance, Hp.Morb.4.56; Id.Acut.47; also of foods, Id.VM15; Id.Acut.10; palpitation of the heart, Nic.Th.775: generally, prob. in Plu.2.654b

ἀράκη.definition: = Hsch. s.v. , and s.v. : so in Ath.11.502b

Ἀράτειον.definition: shrine dedicated to Aratus, Paus.2.9.4, Plu.Arat.53

ἀραχνοειδής.definition: like a cobweb, of the scum of urine, Hp.Prog.12; also used of a feeble pulse, Gal.19.411; of capillary veins, Id.2.808; of nerves, ib.400; ib.366; in Medic., older name for the , i.e. the retina, Herophil. ap. Cels.7.…

Ἄραψ.definition: pl. Arab, Str.1.2.34, J.BJ1.19.4:—as Adj., of incense, Pae.Delph.11; Nonn.D.36.326: dat. pl. ib.26.23

ἀρβύλη.definition: strong shoe coming up to the ankle, half-boot, used by country people, hunters, travellers, A.Ag.944, Fr.259, E.Or.1470 ; Hp.Art.62; with shoes and all, E.Hipp.1189 , cf. Ba.1134; cf

ἀργαλέος.definition: painful, troublous, Il.13.795; of persons, troublesome, vexatious, Thgn.1208 codd. ; Emp.115.8, cf. Ar.Nu.450, Men.403.5: Sup., Ar.Eq.978: rare in Prose, Aeschin.1.61

Ἀργεῖος.definition: of or from Argos, Argive: in Hom., like for the Greeks in Argolis, Th.2.27, al.; women's shoes, Hsch.; , name of a throw at dice, Id

ἄργεμον.definition: albugo, a white speck on the eye; = Lappa canaria, Geum urbanum Avens, Plin.HN24.176:—also = Poll.2.65

ἀργεστής.definition: clearing, brightening, epith. of the; the north-west wind, Hes.Th.379, 870, cf. Acus.15J.; pr.n., Arist.Mete.363b24, Thphr.Sign.35, D.S.1.39, Plu.Sert.8, AP9.42

ἀργέτι.definition: v. = Nonn.D.16.124; voc. AP5.253 :—also nom. Max.587; Orac. ap. Phleg.Mir.3

ἀργής.definition: Ep. dat. and acc. (v; shining, white, of fat, Il.11.818; 21.127; of a robe, 3.419; A.Eu.45, cf. S.Tr.675; because of its chalky soil, Id.OC670 : neut., Nic.Th.105; Opp.C.2.140.—Poet. word, cf. Arist. l.c

ἀργόλας.definition: a kind of serpent, Suid.; cf

Ἀργοναύτης.definition: a sailor in the ship Argo, an Argonaut, Arist.Pol.1284a23, etc.; Str.14.2.13

Ἄργος.definition: name of several Greek cities, Il.9.141; 2.681, etc.; = acc. to Str.8.6.9, cf. Dionys. Epic. ap. St.Byz. s.v. Call.Fr.45:—hence Adjs. qq.v.: E.Rh.41 , Ar.Fr.298

ἀργύρεος.definition: silver-plated, Hdt.9.82; as Subst., silver coin, LXXZa.11.12, al., SIG731.20 , HeroMens.60.1,al

ἀργύριον.definition: small coin, piece of money; collectively, money, Ar.Pl.156,158, al.; a fixed sum, Th.2.70; calculated in our money, X.Cyr.3.1.33; 'hard cash', Theoc.15.36: in Com. with Art., the money, the cash, Ar.Nu.756; ib.1247; A…

Ἀργώ.definition: contr. Argo, the ship; the constellation Argo, Eudox. ap. Hipparch.1.2.20, Arat.342, etc

Ἀρέθουσα.definition: name of several fountains, e.g. in Ithaca, Od.13.408; at Syracuse, Str.6.2.4: pl., Choeril.2:— Adj. AP9.362.18

Ἀρειθύσανος.definition: tassel of Ares, word for a brave warrior, A.Fr.203

Ἄρειος.definition: also E.HF413 ; Ion; name of month in Thessaly, GDI1449, etc

Ἄρειος πάγος.definition: the hill of Ares, at Athens, Hdt.8.52, cf. A.Eu.685,690, etc.; IG1.38a , 2.476.59, al., D.18.133, cf. Lys.26.12, Arist.Ath.4.4; D.20.157, Aeschin.1.81, Arist.Pol.1273b39; IG3.824; become a member of the court, Isoc.7.…

Ἄρεος.definition: collat. form of the spring of Ares, Pi.N.9.41

ἄρεσκος.definition: pleasing, mostly in bad sense; the staff borne by on the stage, Poll.4.120

ἀρετή.definition: goodness, excellence, of any kind, in; later, of the gods, chiefly in pl., glorious deeds, wonders, miracles, SIG1172, Str.17.1.17; IG14.966, cf. 1 Ep.Pet.2.9: also in sg., IG2.1426b, cf. Isyll.62, BSA21.169,180

ἀρή.definition: bane, ruin, Il.12.334; 18.100; 24.489, cf. Od.2.59; so in A.Supp.84 , where the gloss of the Sch., confirms the reading for , perh. also perh. an old ē stem.)

Ἀρήϊος.definition: also Ion. for Hom., etc.; Jul.Or.4.154c:—pecul. fem. Q.S.1.187

Ἄρης.definition: the planet Mars, Arist.Cael.292a5, Cleom.1.11.59, etc.; D.C.37.19

ἄρθρον.definition: joint, Emp.17.22, etc; generally, of limbs, etc., esp. in pl., the ankles, Id.OT718, cf. 1032; of the legs, E.Hec.67 ; eyes, S.OT1270; the mouth, E.Cyc.625; lines, Arist.HA493b33; alone, genitals, Hdt.3.87, 4.2, Arist…

ἀριήκοος.definition: much heard of, Call.Del.308; Act., far-hearing, hearing readily, A.R.4.1707, Dam.Isid.279; Procl.H.2.14

ἀρικύμων.definition: gen. prolific, Hp.Superf.23, prob. in Aër.5

Ἀρισταῖος.definition: pr. n., Hes.Th.977: also epith. of Apollo, Pi.P.9.65; of Zeus, Call.Aet.3.1.33

Ἀριστάρχειος.definition: of Aristarchus , Str.2.3.8; Sch.Il.Oxy.221 iv 22, xi 15

ἀριστεία.definition: Ion. excellence, prowess, S.Aj.443, AP7.312 ; Alciphr.3.36: in pl., Gorg.Fr.11a, Pl.Lg.942d: Il.5,11,17 are called respectively cf. Cic.Att.16.9

ἀριστεροστάτης.definition: standing on the left, esp. in the Trag. chorus, Cratin.215, Aristid.2.161 J

ἄριστον.definition: morning meal, breakfast, twice in Hom., Od.16.2, cf. Il.24.124; A.Fr.182, cf. Ag.331: later, breakfast was called and was the midday meal, our luncheon, cf. Th.4.90, 7.81; Hdt.3.26, 6.78; Arist.HA619a15. contr. from c…

Ἀριστοφάνειος.definition: of Aristophanes, the anapaestic tetrameter, D.H.Rh.11.10, Heph.8, TheonProg.3

Ἀρκάς.definition: Arcadian, pl. Il.2.611: also as Adj., prob. in S.Fr.262

ἀρκεύθινος.definition: of juniper, Dsc.5.36; In LXX, of oleaster, 3 Ki.6.31; of fir, 2 Ch.2.8

Ἀρκτοῦρος.definition: the star Arcturus, Bearward; the time of his heliacal rising, i.e. the middle of September, Hp.Aër.10, S.OT1137; Pl.Lg.844e Th.2.78, etc

ἄρκυλλος.definition: young of the bear, Sch.Opp.H.2.248; cf

ἁρμαλιά.definition: sustenance allotted, food, Hes.Op.560,767; Theoc.16.35; stores in a ship, A.R.1.393:—also PTeb. 112 , 121.78

ἁρμάμαξα.definition: covered carriage, esp. used by Persians; Hdt.7.41, cf. 83; of ambassadors to Susa, Ar.Ach.70; used by women, X.Cyr.3.1.40, 6.4.11

ἁρματωλία.definition: acc. to the Sch. for with a play on Ar.Pax415

Ἀρμένιον.definition: copper carbonate, azurite, Dsc.5.90; Dim. of small tools, HeroAut.24.2, Sch.Opp.H.1.222

ἀρμενοθήκη.definition: store for ship's tackle, Hsch. s.v

ἁρμόδιος.definition: fitting together; fitting, Id.724; Pi.N.1.21; c. inf., Democr.187, cf. Aeschin.Socr.52; Plu.2.793a; Aen.Gaz.Thphr.p.60 B.: Comp. Hld.1.21: Sup. Arr.Tact.16.4; also, agreeable, Parth.16.2. Adv. Plu.Arist.24, PGiss.57.6

ἁρμοδιοτυπής.definition: of accordant mould or cast, Hsch

ἀρνακίς.definition: sheepskin coat, Ar.Nu.730, Pl.Smp.220b, Aristonym.6, Theoc.5.50

ἄρνειος.definition: of a lamb or Orac; name of month at Argos; Schwyzer90.3 , Conon19

ἀρνίς.definition: festival at Argos, in which dogs were slain, Conon19; cf

ἀρνῳδός.definition: one who sings for the prize of a lamb, Eust.6.26, cf. Hsch.,EM146.55

ἀρουραβάτης.definition: traversing the tilled land, epith. of the Nile, Epic. in BKT5.119

ἀρράβδωτος.definition: not ribbed, Arist.HA528a26, Fr.304; of columns, not fluted, IG1.322.55 , 65

ἀρραβών.definition: earnest-money, caution-money; generally, pledge, earnest, Antiph.123.6; . . Men.697, cf. LXXGe.38.17,18, Ep.Eph.1.14

ἀρραγής.definition: unbroken, Hp.VC12; that cannot be rent or broken, Thphr.HP5.5.6; D.P.1006: metaph., Ph.1.471 ; Max. Tyr.41.2; Anatolian Studies p.39 , cf. PLond. 1731.34

ἄρρατος.definition: = Pl.Cra.407d; Id.R.535c; prob. l. in Id.Ax.365a; Euph.24

ἀρρεπής.definition: of a balance, inclining to neither side: hence, without weight or influence, Plu.2.1070a, cf. 1015a; insignificant, Stoic.3.35; firm, unwavering, of ib.159, Dam.Pr.283. Adv. Ph.1.409, Hierocl.p.31 A.:—also Hdn.Epim.256

ἀρρευμάτιστος.definition: arresting discharge; not accompanied by discharge, free from discharge, Ruf. ap. Orib.8.24.54, Aët.7.38, 12.68

ἄρρευστος.definition: without flux or change, Dam. ap. Simp.in; not flowing, Sch.A.Ch.185 ; not fusible, Ps.-Democr.Alch.p.45 B

ἄρρηκτος.definition: unbroken, not to be broken, . . Il.15.20, cf. 13.37; Od.10.4, cf. Il.14.56; 21.447; 20.150; . . 13.360; 2.490; A.Pr.6; Id.Supp.190, S.Aj.576; i.e. invulnerable, Pi.I.6.47; of the crocodile, Hdt.2.68, cf. Arist.HA503a1…

ἀρρηνής.definition: fierce, savage, of dogs, Theoc.25.83, Hsch

ἄρριχος.definition: wicker basket, Ar.Av.1309, Thphr.CP1.7.2: masc. in AP7.410 :—also D.S.20.41, Marm.Par.55, IG12 .162.22,42

ἀρρύπαντος.definition: unsoiled, Eust.598.43. Adv. gloss on Tz.ad Hes.Op.337

ἀρρυσίαστος.definition: not carried off as a hostage, A.Supp.610; not liable to distraint, D.H.6.41

ἀρσενικόν.definition: yellow orpiment, Arist.Pr.966b28, Thphr.Lap.40 , Dsc.5.104, Str.15.2.14, Lyc. ap. Orib.8.25.15:—also Gal.12.212

ἄρσην.definition: gen. Ep., Ion., and; masculine, Id.Supp.951; E.Or.1204: metaph., mighty, S.Ph.1455 ; Id.Fr.480.3; Ar.Th.125 ; Aristid.Quint.2.12; of plants, robust, coarse, opp. , Thphr.HP3.9.3, cf. 2.2.6, Dsc.3.1, al., S.Tr.1196

ἀρτάβη.definition: Persian measure, artaba, = 1 medimnus + 3; Egyptian measure of capacity, varying from 24 to 42 OGI90.30 , PLond.2.265 , POxy.9v8 , etc

ἄρταμος.definition: butcher, cook, X.Cyr.2.2.4, Epicr.6; metaph., murderer, S.Fr.1025, Lyc.236, 797

Ἄρτεμις.definition: gen. also dat. SIG671 A6 , GDI1679 , etc.: acc. also h.Ven.16: Dor. , SIG765 , IG2.545.12 , etc.; dat. ib.4.577 : pl., = ib.7.3101 :—Artemis, Od.11.172, etc

Ἀρτεμίσιον.definition: temple of Artemis, place sacred to her; festival of Artemis, Michel 995 D 8

Ἀρτεπίβουλος.definition: Bread-thief, name of a mouse in Batr.261

Ἀρτίμπασα.definition: Scythian name for Aphrodite Urania, Hdt.4.59

ἀρτίσκιον.definition: Dim. of sq. 2, Damocr. ap. Gal.14.96

ἀρτίσκος.definition: Dim. of little loaf, Hp.Steril.216; pastille, Dsc.2.172, Gal.12.317

ἀρτύνας.definition: a magitrate at Argos and Epidaurus, Th.5.47:— also Plu.2.291d, Hsch., cf. Hdn.Gr.1.56

ἀρύσιμος.definition: that may be drawn, gloss on Sch.Nic.Al.584

ἄρυσος.definition: wicker-basket, Hdn.Gr.1.213; = not wrinkled, smooth, Aët.3.126

ἀρυστήρ.definition: = Alc.Supp.4.9, Semon.25, Hp.Genit.9, Inscr.Cos42b, IG11.154A66, 161 C63 : dat. pl. Call.Aet.1.1.17: name of a liquid measure, Hdt.2.168

ἀρύταινα.definition: fem. of Ar.Eq.1092, Antiph.25.3, Thphr.Char.9.8, PMagd.33.3

ἀρυταινοειδής.definition: shaped like an arytenoid cartilage of the larynx, Gal.UP7.11, cf. 18.951

ἀρυτήρ.definition: ladle or cup, Dsc.2.74; perh. irrigation, . . PLond.ined.2210

ἀρχάγγελος.definition: archangel, LXXDa.10.13, al., Ep.Jud.9, PMag.Lond.121.257 , Nicom. ap. Theol.Ar.43, Dam.Pr.96, Procop.Pers.2.11, al.:—Adj. Dam.Pr.130, cf. Procl.in Cra.p.37 P

ἀρχαιότης.definition: antiquity, old-fashionedness, Pl.Lg.657b, D.H.Pomp.2; simplicity, Alciphr.3.64; pristine state, SIG814.42 ; ancient history, J.Ap.1.1, al.; antiquity, ancient times, D.Chr.31.94

ἀρχαϊσμός.definition: old-world charm of style, D.H.Comp.22; use of obsolete expressions, Men.11 D., cf. Sch.E.Hipp.23

ἀρχέγονος.definition: original, primal, Corn.ND17; first author or origin, Damox.2.8, cf. D.S.1.88; Procl.Inst.152; Corn.ND8

ἀρχεῖον.definition: Ion. neut. of an Adj; public records, archives, prob. in SIG684.7 , cf. D.H.2.26, PTeb.397.19

ἀρχειοφύλαξ.definition: keeper of archives, = Lat. censualis, Lyd.Mag.2.30

ἀρχέμπορος.definition: president of a guild of merchants, OGI646.8

ἀρχενταφιαστής.definition: president of guild of embalmers, UPZ108.10,22

ἀρχή.definition: beginning, origin; with Preps. in adverbial usages, from the beginning, from the first, from of old, Od.1.188, Xenoph.10, etc.; S.OT385; D.54.3; X.Cyn.12.6; but anew, afresh, Ar.Pl.221; Pl.R.450a; the original argumen…

ἀρχίδιον.definition: Dim. of II.3, petty office; Dim. of I, dub. in Philol.21

ἀρχιερωσύνη.definition: high-priesthood, OGI244.21 , cf. BGU362v11 , etc.; = pontificatus maximus, Plu.Pomp.67; of the Jewish high-priesthood, LXX1 Ma.7.21, J.AJ15.3.1, al

Ἀρχιλόχειος.definition: of or used by Archilochus, Heph.15.2

ἄρωμα.definition: aromatic herb or spice, Hp.Aph.5.28, X.An.1.5.1, prob. in Supp.Epigr.1.414 , Arist.Pr.907a13, IG5.514.17 , Plu.Phoc.20

ἀσαλαμίνιος.definition: not having been at Salamis, Ar.Ra.204

ἀσάλευτος.definition: unmoved, unshaken, Arist.Mu.392b34; of Delos, AP9.100 ; LXXEx.13.16, al.; Act.Ap.27.41; of the sea, prob. in Plu.2.982f: metaph. of the mind, E.Ba.391 ; Pl.Ax.370d; Polystr.p.10 W.; Ep.Hebr.12.28; Hymn.Is.4; IG9.270 ;…

ἀσάμινθος.definition: bathing-tub, having made sit in it, Od.10.361; 3.468; Il.10.576, al.; Od.4.128: rare in Att., from a cup as large as a bath, Cratin.234; later, Artem.1.56, PStrassb.29.37

ἄσβεστος.definition: also Il.16.123:—unquenchable; as Subst., , unslaked lime, Dsc.5.115, Plu.Sert.17, Eum.16; Lyc. ap. Orib.8.25.16

ἄσειστος.definition: unshaken, Max.Tyr.41.4: metaph., Id.4.5, cf. D.L.8.26. Adv. unshakably, Epicur.Ep.2p.36U., Arr.Epict.2.17.33

ἄσεμνος.definition: undignified, ignoble, Arist.Mu.398b4, Ph.2.406, Hdn.2.7.1; esp. in Lit. Crit., D.H.Comp.7, al., Demetr.Eloc.189, Longin.43.1; indecent, Eust.1950.63. Adv. A.D.Conj.232.9, al.; BGU1024 vii 22

ἄσημος.definition: Dor. without mark or token; later plate, silver, LXXJb.42.11, AP11.371 ; silver-mines, Ptol.Geog.7.2.17: also, = electron, alloy of gold and silver, or an imitation thereof, Ps.-Democr.Alch.p.49 B., etc.:—masc. PLeid.…

Ἀσία.definition: Ion. Asia, Pi.O.7.18, Hdt.1.4,4.45, A.Pr.412; S.OC694, etc.:—Adj. Asian, Asiatic, Th.1.6, etc.; TheonProg.2; Str.14.1.41, Plu.Ant.2. Adv. D.C.46.30:—fem. and [the latter with freq. in A. and E., never in S., being req…

ἄσιγμος.definition: without sigma, D.H.Comp.14; name of a poem of Lasus without a sigma in it, Ath.10.455c:—hence compose such a poem, ibid

ἀσίδα.definition: = Hebr. ḥasidhah, stork, LXXJb.39.13, Je.8.7: cf. Hsch

ἀσίδηρος.definition: not of iron, E.Ba.1104; not; without sword, E.Ba.736; sham fight, Onos.10.4; Max.Tyr.36.1

ἀσινής.definition: unhurt, unharmed; less freq. of things, undamaged, . . IG3.1418, 1419; POxy.278.18 ; of ships, App.BC5.98: metaph., Ph.1.215

ἄσιος.definition: epith. of Il.2.461, prob. Asian, but also expld. as Eust.ad loc., or meadow of Asias , Str.14.1.45, St.Byz.131.7

ἄσις.definition: slime, mud, Il.21.321, Nic.Th.176; Charito2.2; cf. Hsch

ἀσκαλαβώτης.definition: spotted lizard, gecko, Platydactylus mauretanicus, Ar.Nu.170, Arist.HA538a27, 607a27; cf

ἀσκαρής.definition: not hopping or skipping, Hsch.:—also Id

ἄσκαρος.definition: a kind of castanet, Poll.4.60, Hsch.; also a kind of shoe, Id

ἀσκέπαστος.definition: uncovered, Dsc.5.114, Antyll. ap. Orib.6.23.10, Gp.7.19.3, PLond.5.1722

ἀσκεπής.definition: = foreg., Lyr.Alex.Adesp.7.17, AP5.259; not covering, Nonn.D.22.214:—also defenceless, Amynt.Epigr. in POxy. 662.37; bare-headed, Ps.-Luc.Philopatr.21

ἀσκηθής.definition: unhurt, unscathed, in Hom. of persons, Il.10.212; Od.9.79, cf. Epich.99.10, Call.Aet.3.1.69; Od.14.255 ; sound, healthy, IG4.952.109 ; Sol.19.4; unblemished, IG5.3.5 ; = Timo60, etc.; later of things, safe return, A.R…

ἄσκημα.definition: exercise, practice, Hp.Off.7, X.Cyr.7.5.79; Id.Oec.11.19, cf. PLond.3.1164i21 ; in warfare, branch of the service, arm , Arr.Tact.19.6

ἀσκίπων.definition: gen. not leaning on a staff, AP9.298 , 7.732 ; but a child too young to serve as a staff, BMus.Inscr.2.390

Ἀσκληπιός.definition: Dor. Asclepios, Il.2.731, h.Hom.16, etc.:— hence son of Asclepios, Il.4.204, al.: in pl., as a name for physicians, Thgn.432, Pl.R.405d: also in pl., Dor. guild of worshippers of A., IG2.617b, 12.162 , temple of Ascle…

ἀσκοπήρα.definition: scrip, wallet, Ar.Fr.577, Diph.55.2, prob. in Suet. Ner.45

ἀσκός.definition: skin, hide, PFay.121.9 ; but; paunch, belly, Archil.72; in oracular language, E.Med.679, Plu.Thes.3

ἀσκύλευτος.definition: not pillaged or stripped, D.H.11.27, Hld.1.1

ἄσκωμα.definition: leather padding or lining of; any swelling, such as on the female breast, Ruf.Onom.92, cf. Poll.2.163

ἄσμενος.definition: well-pleased, glad, always with a Verb, he was glad to have escaped death, Il.20.350, cf. Od.9.63, Pi.O.13.74: freq. in Trag. and Att., . . A.Pr.398; E.Hel.398; Th.6.12; Lys.1.13; Pl.R.614e: freq. in dat., glad would …

ἀσοφία.definition: folly, stupidity, Plu.Pyrrh.29, Luc.Astr.2; rejected by Poll.4.13

ἀσόφιστος.definition: not deluded by fallacies, Arr.Epict.1.7.26; J.Ap.2.41

ἄσοφος.definition: unwise, foolish, Thgn.370, Pi.O.3.45, Ep.Eph.5.15, Plu.2.330a: Comp., Them.Or.15.185a. Adv. D.S.2.29, Lib.Decl.2.27

ἀσπάλαθος.definition: Ar.Fr.749, but more commonly as; thorny trefoil, Calycotome villosa, Thgn.1193 , Arist.Pr.906b11, Theoc.4.57 , 24.89

ἀσπάλαξ.definition: elsewh. , blind- rat, Spalax typhlus, Arist.HA533a3, Antig.Mir.10, Stoic.2.51, Ael.NA17.10; Opp.C.2.612: prov., Diogenian.8.25

ἀσπαλία.definition: angling, Hsch., Suid.; perh. f.l. for

ἄσπειστος.definition: to be appeased by no libations, implacable, D.25.52; Nic.Th.367; = Plu.2.537b, cf. S.E.P.3.175

ἄσπερμος.definition: without seed, i. e. posterity, Il.20.303, Luc.Am.35: metaph., Max.Tyr.31.5:—in literal sense, opp. Arist.GA725b29; of plants, Thphr.HP7.4.4

ἄσπετος.definition: Ep. Adj. unspeakable, unutterable; mostly in sense of unspeakably great, Il.8.558, 18.403, 23.127, Od.5.101; Il.16.157; less freq. of number, countless, Od.4.75; 9.162; ye tremble unspeakably, Il.17.332, cf. Q.S.11.12…

ἀσπιδιώτης.definition: shield-bearing, a warrior, Il.2.554, 16.167, Theoc.14.67, Plb.10.29.6, AP9.116: in Pl., = Lat. scutati, Lyd.Mag.1.9:—so S.Fr.426

ἀσπίνθιον.definition: prob. a vulgar form of Hsch.:—also EM183.25

ἀσσαριαῖος.definition: at the rate of 12 asses per denarius per month, BMus.Inscr.481*.66

ἀσταθής.definition: unsteady, unstable, Phld.Ir.p.26W.; AP10.74 , cf. Nonn.D.8.140, al.; LXX3 Ma.5.39

ἀστακός.definition: the smooth lobster, Philyll.13; hollow of the ear, Poll.2.85

ἀστασίαστος.definition: not torn by faction; not liable to disturbance, Sammelb.5174 , etc

ἄστατος.definition: never standing still; unsteady, unstable, Epicur.Ep.3p.65U., cf. Phld.Rh.1.166S. , Ph.1.230, al., Diog.Oen.18, Diogenian.Epicur.2.60, Plu.2.103f; of persons, Onos.3.3; IG7.2543; Epigr.Gr.699, cf. Ph.1.651; of a house,…

ἀσταφιδίτης.definition: fem. of raisins, bunch of raisins, AP9.226

ἀστέγαστος.definition: uncovered, Gal.17.153: of a ship, undecked, Antipho5.22, cf. Apollod.Poliorc.185.10; roofless, PGen.11.7 ; from their having no shelter, Th.7.87

ἀστεῖος.definition: also Diph.73: :-of the town . II. town-bred, polite, Pl.Phd.116d; opp. Plu.Mar.3; Alc.Com.26; charming, Isoc.2.34. 2. of thoughts and words, refined, elegant, witty, opp. Ar.Fr.685; Id.Ra.901; Id.Nu.204; Pl.Phdr.227d;…

ἀστειότης.definition: prettiness, daintiness of person, Vett.Val.161.17; politeness, wit, Andronic.Rhod.p.570M., cf. Lib.Or.11.270, Sch.Ar.Pax370

ἄστεκτος.definition: insufferable, Hsch., A.Fr.224 ap.AB456 , Paul.Aeg.5.16, Dsc.Ther.13. Adv. Hsch

ἀστέλεφος.definition: leathern case for a lyre, Hsch.:—also Id

ἀστεμφής.definition: unmoved, unshaken, Il.2.344; of persons, stiff, Ar.Fr.579; unflinching, Theoc.13.37; as pr. n. of a Titan, Emp.123

ἀστένακτος.definition: without sigh or groan, S.Tr.1200, cf. 1074; E.Alc.173; a day free from groans, Id.Hec.691 , cf. Pl.Ax.370d, Mél.Nicole 308 . Adv. Plu.2.107a:—also A.Fr.307, Ar.Ec.464

ἄστηνος.definition: miserable, BCH29.410 : heterocl. pl. Hsch.; expld. in EM159.11, cf. Suid

ἀστηρίδιον.definition: Dim. of ornament in shape of star, PHamb. 10.44

ἀστήρικτος.definition: not supported by a staff, AP6.203 ; unstable, Longin.2.2, 2 Ep.Pet.3.16, Gal.UP2.15, al.; Vett.Val.242.3; not remaining still, of persons, Nonn.D.10.14, al.; of water, ib.32.8, al

ἄστικτος.definition: not marked with not tattooed; an estate not pledged or mortgaged , Lys.Fr.3S., Men.1 D., Poll.3.85

ἄστιπτος.definition: = untrodden, . . S.Ph.2, v.l. which is prob. in OGI606

ἀστοιχείωτος.definition: ignorant of the first elements, Ph.1.337

ἀστομάχητος.definition: without anger , PBaden 35.17 , Alciphr.2.2. Adv. IG14.2095

ἀστόξενος.definition: public guest of a city, A.Supp.356.—Expld. by Ael.Dion.Fr.282, Hsch., as a blood-relation, though a foreigner by birth

ἀστός.definition: townsman, citizen, Il.11.242, Od.13.192, etc.; dist. from being one who has civil rights only, one who has political rights also, Arist.Pol.1278a34; E.Med.223; the commons, opp. Pi.P.3.71, cf. Isoc.3.21; opp. Pi.O.7.9…

ἀστράγαλος.definition: one of the vertebrae; ball of the ankle joint , Hdt.3.129; in horses, X.Eq.1.15; of various animals, Hp.Int.20,30

ἀστροχίτων.definition: gen. star-clad, of night, Orph.A.513, 1028, Nonn.D.40.408

ἄστυρον.definition: Dim. of Call.Fr.19, Aet.3.1.74, Hec.1.1.6, Nic.Al.15

ἀστυφέλικτος.definition: unshaken, undisturbed, X.Lac.15.7; Call.Del.26; Epigr.Gr.540.3; AP9.764 ; Orph.Fr.168.22; Sammelb. 5829.3

ἀσύγκλωστος.definition: not interwoven, disconnected, disjointed, Cic.Att.6.1.17, cf. Porph.Abst.3.18; Herm.in Phdr.p.187A.; Porph.Chr.39; incompatible, Phlp.in Ph.34.14; Dam.Pr.5

ἀσύγκρατος.definition: incapable of blending, discordant, Plu.2.418d; of herbs, cj. ib.134d; Nicom.Harm.12

ἀσύγκριτος.definition: not comparable, Thphr.Fr.89.7; incomparable, surpassing, Ph.1.578, cf. Plu.Dio47, BGU613.20 , etc., Ath.Mitt.12.174 ; of remedies, Gal.14.112. Adv. incomparably, Hierocl.in CA3p.424M., CIG 3493.14

ἀσύγχυτος.definition: not confused, Ph.1.6,434, cf. Plu.2.735b, Procl.Inst.176; not mingled together, Arr.Epict.4.11.8. Adv. without confusion, ib.8.20

ἀσυγχώρητος.definition: forbidden, D.S.1.78; not to be conceded or admitted, Agatharch.8, S.E.M.7.380; not duly authorized, SIG793.8

ἀσύζευκτος.definition: not paired, Suid. s.v. Adv. AB456

ἀσυκοφάντητος.definition: not plagued by informers; unexceptionable, BGU1059.8 , Luc.Hist.Conscr.59, Salt.81

ἀσυρής.definition: lewd, filthy, Plb.4.4.5; Id.18.55.7; Id.38.20.6; LXXSi.23.13. Adv. Phld.Rh.1.348S

ἀσύφηλος.definition: headstrong, or perh. foolish, Il.9.647; 24.767, cf. Q.S.9.521: also in late Prose, as Eun.VSp.481B. Adv. foolishly, Dius ap.Stob.4.21.16

ἀσφάδαστος.definition: without convulsion or struggle, esp. in dying, A.Ag.1293, S.Aj.833

ἀσφαλός.definition: name of a bird, Hsch. s.v

ἀσφράγιστος.definition: not sealed, Klio 18.264 (Delph; not assigned to a BGU659 ii 9

ἀσχιδής.definition: uncloven, undivided, Arist.Pr.930b33; of animals, Id.HA499b11, cf. PA42b29; Thphr.HP3.10.1

ἄσωστος.definition: not to be saved, past recovery, Ael.NA13.7, PFay.12.24 . Adv. Dsc.2.141, Gal.15.753

ἄσωτος.definition: having no hope of safety, in; in moral sense, abandoned, S.Aj.189 ; spendthrift, Pl.Lg.743b, Arist.EN1107b12, 1120a1, al.: Sup., D.C.67.6; profligate, Vett.Val.18.2. Adv. Theopomp.Hist.217a, D.40.58, Ev.Luc.15.13: Com…

ἀταπείνωτος.definition: not humbled, Zeno Stoic.1.53, Arr.Epict.4.6.8, Plu.Cor.21

ἀταρίχευτος.definition: not desiccated, Arist.Pr.926a35; not salted, Gal.12.321

ἀτασθαλία.definition: Ion. presumptuous sin, recklessness, wickedness, Hom., always in pl.; or Il.4.409, Od.1.34, al.; 21.146; 23.67; 12.300:—after Hom. in sg., of the Titans, Hes.Th.209; ib.516; Pi.Parth.2 Fr.1.31; Simon.111.4; Hdt.2.111:…

ἀτάσθαλος.definition: reckless, presumptuous, wicked; of men's acts, words, etc., Il.13.634; Od.16.86; Alc.Supp.27.11; Hdt.7.35; Id.3.80; ib.49; Theoc.22.131.—Ep., Aeol., and Ion. word, used for comic effect by Strato Com.1.38; also in lat…

ἀταύρωτος.definition: A.Ag.245, also Ar.Lys.217:—unwedded, maiden, A. l.c.; chaste, Ar. l.c., v. Scholl.ad locc., Poll.2.173

ἄτεγκτος.definition: not to be softened by water; metaph., not to be softened, A.Fr.348: abs., hard-hearted, relentless, S.OT336, E.HF833, Ar.Th.1047, and in late Prose, D.H.5.8, J.BJ5.9.4, Plu.TG12, Luc.DMeretr.12.3, etc. Adv. Philostr.Ep.5

ἀτειρής.definition: not to be rubbed or worn away; metaph., stubborn, unyielding, ib.3.60, cf. 15.697; [Hercules] Od.11.270; Il.13.45, 17.555; Emp.86; Id.84.6; Pi.O.2.36; of persons, stubborn, Theoc.23.6; AP12.175 ; stubbornness, Pl.Cra.…

ἀτείχιστος.definition: unwalled, unfortified, Th.1.2, 8.62; not walled off, Th.1.64

ἀτεράμων.definition: gen. Att. for hard, tough, Ar.Ach.181, cf. Pl.Lg.853d, 880e, Eub.1 D.; hard to cook, Thphr.HP2.4.2, cf. 8.8.6, CP4.12.8

ἀτευξία.definition: not obtaining, privation, A.D.Synt.56.26, Dam. in AB 1345

Ἀτθίς.definition: the Attic. dialect, Str.8.1.2; history of Athens, Id.9.1.6, cf. D.H.1.8, J.Ap.1.3

Ἀτλαγενής.definition: sprung from Atlas, of the Pleiads, Hes.Op.383

Ἄτλας.definition: acc. also A.Pr.428 , cf; in hist. writers, Mount Atlas in West Africa, regarded as the pillar of heaven, Hdt.4.184, Str.17.3.2, etc.: pl, D.P.66

ἄτλας.definition: not enduring or daring, Hsch.; cf

ἄτμενος.definition: = Archil. ap. Sch.Il.Oxy.1087, Call.Fr.538, Hsch., Eust.1750.62:—as Adj., Hsch

ἀτμήν.definition: slave, servant, Call.Aet.1.1.19, Epic.inArch.Pap. 7.4, Et.Gen., Sch.Nic.Al.172,426

ἄτμητος.definition: not carved, IG1.322; Ph.2.253; indivisible, Pl.Phdr.277b, Arist.EE1230a29, Ph.1.505, al., Iamb.Comm.Math.4. Adv. HeroGeom.p.85H

ἀτμός.definition: steam, vapour, A.Eu.138; . . Arist.Pr.862a4; of incense, Pae.Delph.II: in pl., vapours, A.Fr.205; clouds of steam, Jul.Mis.341d; esp. of odours, A.Ag.1311, Arist.Pr.908a21, Ph.1.96,al., Lib.Or.12.79 , etc.; distd. fro…

ἀτρακίς.definition: name of a spinous plant, Gal.6.623

ἀτράκτιον.definition: Dim. of Epic. in Arch.Pap.7.9: pl. , POxy.1740.2

ἀτρακτυλίς.definition: or spindle-thistle, used for making spindles, Carthamus lanatus, Arist.HA627a8, Thphr.HP6.4.6, Theoc.4.52 , Dsc.3.93:—also , Hsch

ἀτραυμάτιστος.definition: not caused by a wound, Luc.Ocyp.36, cf. Aët.7.9

ἀτράφαξυς.definition: orach, Atriplex rosea, Hp.Vict.2.54, Thphr.HP7.1.2,al., Dsc.2.119, Gal.6.633. Thphr.l.c., Dsc. l.c., Hp. l.c., v.l. Dsc. l.c., Gal.11.843, cf. Hdn.Gr.1.539, 2.49,467.)

ἀτράχυντος.definition: Ion. without asperity, Aret.SD2.12; Id.CA1.10:—also Eust.340.21

ἄτρεστος.definition: not trembling, fearless, Trag., and Pl.Cra.395c: c. gen., fearless of fight, A.Pr.416 ; S.Aj.365 ; securely, Id.OT586. Adv. A.Supp.240: neut. pl. as Adv., E.Ion1198

ἀτρύγετος.definition: later IG3.900:—unharvested; metaph., of death, AP7.735

ἄτρυτος.definition: not worn, untiring, unwearied; of things, unabating: hence, limitless, Pi.P.4.178, Hdt.9.52; B.8.80; Id.5.27; S.Aj.788; Mosch.4.69; Arist.Cael.284a35; Id.EN1177b22; Ph.2.434; Chaerem. ap. Porph.Abst.4.8; of a road, we…

Ἀτρυτώνη.definition: the Unwearied, title of Pallas Athene, Il.2.157, Od.4.762, etc

ἀτρύφερος.definition: not delicate or luxurious, Eup.69; plain, simple, Ceb.20; Telesp.7H

ἀττάκης.definition: a kind of locust, LXXLe.11.22 : —also Aristeas145, Ph.1.85

Ἀτταλεῖον.definition: meeting-place of; festival at Delphi, SIG672.53

ἄττανα.definition: · Hsch.:—hence a kind of cake, coupled with Hippon.36.3:—also Hsch

ἀττελεβόφθαλμος.definition: with locust eyes, i. e. with prominent, staring eyes, Eub.107.10

ἀττικοπέρδιξ.definition: Attic partridge, nickname of an actor, Ath.3.115b

ἀτυράννευτος.definition: not ruled by tyrants, free from tyrants, Th.1.18, D.C.37.22, Chor.p.208B.:—also Phryn.PSp.30B

αὐαλέος.definition: dry, parched, withered, Hes.Op.588; of hair, rough, dub. in Simon.37.9, cf.AP7.141 ; of plants, Orph.A.246; of the mouth, Call.Cer.6; of eyes, sleepless, AP5.279 ; prob. in Timo3.— Late in Prose, Aret.SD2.2, al

αὐγοειδής.definition: of the nature of light, as the source of sight, Stoic.2.231; of the eye, Gal.UP8.6; brilliant, Plu.2.922d: metaph., ib.565d; Iamb.Myst.5.10, 3.11; luminous vehicle, Procl.in Ti.2.81 D.: Comp., Ph.1.6: Sup., ib.504, al…

Αὔγουστος.definition: Augustus, used as an Adj., = Gr; the month August, Plu.Num.19

αὐλαία.definition: curtain, Hyp.Fr.139, Thphr.Char.5.9, Men.834, Michel832.26 , Plu.Alex.49; esp. in the theatre, Men.l.c.; hunting- net, Plu.Alex.40: in pl., screens to protect a wall against missiles, Ph.Bel.95.34

αὔλειος.definition: sts. also :—of or belonging to the court, at the door of the court, i.e. the outer door, house-door, Od.11.239, cf. Pi.N.1.19, Hdt.6.69; Sol.4.28; . . Od.1.104; S.Ant.18; E.Hel.438: sg., Lys.1.17, Pl.Smp.212c, Thphr.C…

αὔλιος.definition: belonging to folds; dub. l. in Men.546; cf. Hsch

αὖλις.definition: tent or place for passing the night in, Il.9.232; to go to roost, of birds, Od.22.470, cf. h.Merc.71, E.Cyc.363, Call.Dian.87, Theoc.25.18, Arat.1027; AP6.221

αὐλίσκος.definition: small reed, pipe; generally, small pipe or tube, Arist.Ath.68.2, Plb.27.11.2, Mnesith. ap. Orib.8.38.3; catheter, Hp.Morb.1.6

αὐλουρός.definition: keeper of the court or fold, Hsch

αὐλωνοειδής.definition: full of valleys, D.S.19.17; in the shape of an Id.3.68

αὐλῶπις.definition: in Il. always epith. of helmet with a tube-like opening between the cheek-pieces to hold the Il.5.182, al.; with a socket to hold the shaft, S.Fr.1027; conical, Ath.5.189c, cf. Hsch

αὔξιμος.definition: promoting growth, Hp.Vict.2.65; intr., growing, Hp.Art.58, Vict.1.25, A.Fr.51, E.ap.Lex.Sabb.1.4, Com.Adesp.37 D

αὐξίς.definition: Byz. for or young of the tunny, Phryn.Com.56, Arist.HA571a17, Nic.Al.469

Αὐξώ.definition: goddess of growth, called to witness in an Athenian citizen's oath, Paus.9.35.2, Poll.8.106

αὐροσχάς.definition: name of a vine, Parth.Fr.17; also, = Eratosth.37

Αὐσονία.definition: poet. Italy, AP14.121 : App.Anth.2.712b.14:—Adj. AP7.343, al.: Italians, ib.363, al.:—also Arist.Pol.1329b20, IG14.1374, Ael.VH9.16 : fem. IG 14.2067, 2137

αὐσταλέος.definition: Ep. dried up, sunburnt, Od.19.327, Hes.Sc.265, Theoc.14.4, Call.Cer.16, A.R.2.200, etc

αὐταύλης.definition: soloist on the flute, condemned by Phryn.145

αὐτοματοποιητική.definition: art of making marionettes, and treatise thereupon, HeroAut.1.1

ἀφάβρωμα.definition: Megarian name of a woman's garment, Plu.2.295b; cf

Ἀφαία.definition: name of divinity in Aegina, IG4.1580; cf. Hsch

ἀφασία.definition: speechlessness, caused by fear or perplexity, E.Hel.549; Id.IA837, cf. Ar.Th.904; Pl.Lg.636e; Id.Phlb.21d; inability to say anything about it, S.E.P.2.211, cf. Dam.Pr.7

ἄφατος.definition: not uttered or named, nameless; unutterable, ineffable, E.Ion782 ; monstrous, Pi.N.1.47; AP6.112 ; untold sums, Hdt.7.190; S.OT1314 , OC1464 ; Anaxandr.41.63; IG14.2012.4 ; Phld.D.3.14; Hermog.Inv.1.4; Plot.4.8.6; . .…

ἄφεμα.definition: that which is let go: remission of tribute or taxation, LXX1 Ma.10.28 , al., PTeb.226 , PFlor.379.37

ἄφενος.definition: revenue, riches, wealth, abundance, Il.1.171, cf. 23.299, Thgn.30; Crates Theb.10.7; of the wealth of the gods, Hes.Th.112: masc. acc. v.l. in Id.Op.24: gen. Call.Jov.96, AP9.234 ; cf

Ἀφέσιος.definition: Releaser, epith. of Zeus, Arr. ap. EM176.32, Paus.1.44.9

ἀφεύρεμα.definition: deficiency, UPZ112, PTeb.8.23 , BGU 1118.14 ; loss on resale, PPetr.3p.232

ἀφέψαλος.definition: without a spark of fire, Hsch

ἀφῆλιξ.definition: Ion. beyond youth; minor, infant, in law, POxy. 487.5

ἀφηλιώτης.definition: = , IG14.1308, Apion ap.J.Ap.2.2:—hence Adj. Ptol.Geog.1.11, Gem.2.11

ἀφήμερος.definition: absent for a day, PGiss.2.27 , PTeb.104.28 , etc

ἄφημος.definition: and unknown, Hsch.: also Adv. Id., cf. h.Ap.171 ap.Th.3.104

ἀφήτωρ.definition: archer, epith. of Apollo, Il.9.404:—the Sch. gives an alternative expl., prophet , cf. Orac. in App.Anth.6.149.7; cf

ἄφθιτος.definition: not liable to perish, undecaying; of persons, immortal, of the gods, h.Merc.326; Hes.Th.389,397; of Tantalus, Pi.O.1.63; of Anacreon, Simon.184; A.Eu.724; S.Fr.278

ἄφθογγος.definition: voiceless, speechless, h.Cer.198; mutes, Pl.Phlb.18c, Cra.424c

ἄφιλος.definition: of persons, friendless, A.Ch.295; of persons and things, unfriendly, hateful, A.Th.522, S.OC186; . . Id.Aj.620; Arist.EN1101a23; unsociable, S.OC1237: perh., c. gen., hostile to, Phld.Lib.p.36O.; ib.p.20 O., cf. Carne…

ἀφίμωσις.definition: an operation connected with the manufacture of vegetable oils, PPetr.3p.315

ἄφιππος.definition: unsuited for cavalry, X.HG3.4.12; of persons, unused to riding, opp. Aeschin.Socr.Oxy.1608 Fr.1.15; ignorant of horsemanship, Pl.Prt.350a, R.335c, Luc.Nav.30

ἄφλαστον.definition: curved poop of a ship with its ornaments, Il.15.717, Asclep.Tragil.31 J., Sch.A.R.1.1089: in pl., of a single ship, Hdt.6.114

ἄφοβος.definition: without fear, and so; fearless, intrepid, Pi.I.5.40, S.OC1325, etc.; Plu.Lyc.16, Galb.23: c. gen., having no fear of, D.Chr.2.52; = Pl.La.197b. Adv. X.Hier.7.10, Pl.Lg.682c, PTeb.24.74

ἀφορία.definition: not bearing:—hence; c. gen. objecti, non-production, dearth, X.Vect.4.9; Thphr.HP9.2.4; Pl.Lg.740c ; Ph.1.430: abs., dearth, Antipho2.1.10, cf. Lycurg.84, Arist.Mete.351b14

ἄφορτος.definition: at Sparta, not having undergone the Lycurgean training, Hsch

Ἄφριος.definition: epith. of Zeus in Thessaly, also, name of month, IG9.206iiic,al

ἀφρισμός.definition: foaming, Archig. ap. Philum.Ven.14.3, Paul. Aeg.3.13, Sch.Il.9.539

Ἀφροδίτη.definition: Aphrodite, h.Hom.5; as Appellat., sexual love, pleasure, Od.22.444; Pi.O.6.35; h.Ven.1,9, etc.; a woman's form of oath, Ar.Lys.208, Ec.189, etc

ἀφρός.definition: foam, of the sea; of persons and animals, foam, slaver, froth, 20.168; Hp.Aph.2.43, cf. Ev.Luc.9.39; frothy blood, A.Eu.183, cf. Fr.372; S.Tr.702; of wine, Antiph.237; . . Theophil.2

ἀφροσύνη.definition: folly, thoughtlessness, freq. in pl., Od.24.457, cf. 16.278: in sg., Il.7.110, cf. Democr.254, Hdt.3.146, 9.82; S.OC1230 ; . . Th.1.122; opp. and Pl.Prt.332e; Arist.EN1146a27

ἄφυκτος.definition: not to be shunned; Act., unable to escape, Ar.Nu.1047; dub.l. in A.Supp.784 . Adv. LXX3 Ma.7.9: Comp. Aen.Tact.16.12.—In codd. freq. written Philem.115.4, Plu.Lys.29; IG14.803

ἀφυλλάκανθος.definition: without prickles on the leaves, Thphr.HP6.4.8

ἄφυλος.definition: without a tribe, Max.Tyr.21.4, prob. in EM178.39

ἄφυξις.definition: drawing out, ladling, dub. in Hsch., Cyr

ἀφώτιστος.definition: dark, obscure, J.AJ13.11.2, Arr.Epict.1.14.10, Plu.2.931c, Onos.10.13, S.E.M.10.164, Orph.Fr.272, etc.; unlit by the sun, Gem.11.3: metaph., Ph.1.638; Anon.in Prm. in Rh.Mus.47.608; Nonn.D.6.91; unenlightened, Plot.1.2.4

Ἀχαία.definition: Ion. epith. of Demeter in Attica; = Philet.ap. Gramm. post Orionemp.185 S

Ἀχαιΐς.definition: the Achaian land, with or without; Achaian woman, 2.235, etc.:—also 5.424, etc

ἀχαιόμαντις.definition: title of diviner in Cyprus, Hsch

ἀχάνη.definition: name of a Persian (also, Boeotian; chest, box, Phanod.25, Plu.Arat.6. Ar.Ach. ll. cc.]

ἀχανής.definition: not opening the mouth, of; yawning, Timae.28; AP9.423 , J.AJ7.10.2; without a lid, HeroAut.28.4; wide- mouthed, Diocl. ap. Orib.5.4.2, cf. Antyll.ib.44.8.12; open, D.C.37.17; open, unoccupied, of building land, POxy.1…

ἀχάρακτος.definition: not marked or branded, BGU13.8 ; not stamped, Ath.Mitt.33.384 ; of ships, without emblem or figurehead, PLille22.6; not graven or cut, Nonn.D.13.84; that cannot be cut, ib.16.158, cf. 26.242

ἀχαράκωτος.definition: not palisaded, Plb.10.11.2, Plu.Mar.20: metaph., defenceless, friendless, Philostr.VA5.35. Adv. App.BC3.70

ἀχαρνώς.definition: = a sea-fish, prob. bass, Callias Com.3: in Ath.3.286b: Arist.HA602a12; gen. ib.591b1:—also and names of fish in Hsch

Ἀχελῷος.definition: poet. Achelous, name of several; in Poets, any stream: generally, water, S.Fr.5, E.Ba.625, Ar.Fr.351, Achae.9, Ephor.27

Ἀχερόντειος.definition: of Acheron, Call.Hec.31.3:—also E.Alc.443 , Ar.Ra.471:—fem. AP5.240 : and , Th.1.46:—fem. X.An.6.2.2, Pl.Phd.113a

Ἀχέρων.definition: Acheron, river in the nether world, Od.10.513, etc.; of other rivers, Th.1.46, Str.6.1.5, etc

ἄχθος.definition: burden, load, Il.12.452, Hes.Op.692; load of grief, Hes.Sc.400; . . A.Ag.166; S.El.120 , cf. Ant.1172; E.IT710; bring or cause sorrow, X.Ep.1

ἀχίαστος.definition: not arranged chiastically, Sch.Isoc.8.102. Adv. Jo.Sic.in Rh.6.343 W

Ἀχίλλειος.definition: of Achilles, E.Tr.39, etc.; poet; a fine kind of barley, Ath.3.114f; also Hp.Morb.3.17; Thphr.HP8.10.2; cakes of fine barley, Pherecr.130.4; Ar.Eq.819; a cake of this sort, Eust.1414.33

ἄχιλος.definition: without grass, or rich in grass, both senses in Hsch. s.v

ἀχόρευτος.definition: not trained in the dance or chorus; not attended with the dance, Musae.274; esp. in bad sense, ill suiting it, joyless, S.El.1069 ; E.Tr.121 ; Telest.1.8

ἄχορος.definition: without the dance, epith. of Ares, to mark the horrors of war, A.Supp.681 ; of death, . . S.OC1222 ; v.l. in E.Andr.1037

ἄχος.definition: pain, distress, in Hom. always of mind, Il.4.169, al.; 17.591; 3.412; B.10.85; also of physical ills, Pi.P.3.50 ; A.Ch.586 ; with a play on the words, S.Tr.1035; A.Pers.573 ; Ar.Ra.1353 , cf. 1531 .— Rare in Prose, Hd…

ἄχραντος.definition: undefiled, immaculate, E.IA1574, A.R.4.1025; Mosch.2.73: c. gen., M.Ant.3.4; Philostr.VA6.11; Opp.H.2.648: metaph., Pl.Alc.1.113e; Luc.Dem.Enc.13, cf. Am.22; Jul.Or.1.9c; freq. in Pap., as POxy.59.10 ; of a cup, Ion T…

ἀχράς.definition: a kind of wild pear, Pyrus amygdaliformis, Teleclid.32, Ar.Ec.355, Dsc.1.116; used for the tree as well as the fruit, cf. Arist.HA627b17 with 595a29, Thphr.HP1.4.1 with CP2.8.2; cf

ἀχρεῖος.definition: esp. unfit for war, Hdt.3.81; the unserviceable part of an army, Id.1.191; Th.1.93, 2.6, cf. X.HG7.2.18; Th.2.44. Adv. App.BC5.84

ἀχρεοκόπητος.definition: free from debt, i.e. undiminished, PMag.Par.1.527

ἄχρονος.definition: without time, instantaneous, Gal.7.448; independent of time, S.E.M.10.225; non-temporal, Plot.4.4.1. Adv. timelessly, Alex.Aphr.in Mete.129.5, in Sens.135.14, Procl.Inst.124, Herm.in Phdr.p.159 A.; instantaneously, Ph…

ἄχωρος.definition: without resting-place, homeless, Ael.Fr.77; Tab.Defix.97.11, cf. 96.17

ἀψάλακτος.definition: untouched, unhandled, S.Fr.550; scot-free, Crates Com.46, Ar.Lys.275

ἀψάμαθος.definition: and without sand, not sandy, Hsch

ἀψηλάφητος.definition: not tried or tested, Plb.8.19.5; untouched, Hsch.; gloss on Id

ἀψόρροος.definition: back- flowing, refluent, Homeric epith. of Ocean, regarded as a stream encircling the earth and flowing back into itself, Il.18.399, Od.20.65

ἄψορρος.definition: going back, backwards, Il.21.456; 3.313; . . S.Ant.386, cf. OT431: mostly in neut. as Adv., backward, back again, . . Il.7.413; 4.152; Od.9.282; A.Pr.1021, cf. S.El.53; ; ib.1430; Id.Aj.369

ἀωΐλιον.definition: Egyptian measure of capacity, = 2 cubic PPetr. 2p.14, al. :—also ib.p.118

ἀών.definition: a kind of fish, Epich.63; a kind of garment, PAmh.2.3aii 21

ἀωρία.definition: wrong time: hence, untimely fate or death, Hld.10.16; but old age, Herod.3.29; bad condition, Procop.Arc.14: pl., bad seasons, Plu.2.371b; midnight, dead of night, Pherecr.6D., Ael.Fr.81; in full, Alciphr.3.47: metaph…

Ἀώς.definition: Dor. for c. gen., to east of, Mnemos.42.332

ἀβατόομαι.definition: Pass., to be made desert, LXXJe.29.20

ἀβλαβής.definition: without harm, i.e; Pass., unharmed, unhurt, Sapph.Supp.1.1, Pi.O.13.27, P.8.54, A.Th.68, X.Cyr.4.1.3, Pl.R.342b, etc.; S.El.650. Adv. Ion. safely, Thgn.1154; Dexipp.p.148D., cf. Arr.An.6.19.2: Sup. X.Eq.6.1:—securely,…

ἄβλαστος.definition: not growing out, of fibre, Id.HP1.2.5:—also not growing, ib.2.2.8; of seeds, not germinating, 8.11.7; of places, unfruitful, CP2.4.1; Gp.9.9.4 : metaph., Plu.2.38c; Them.Or.18.221d

ἀβλεπτέω.definition: overlook, disregard, Plb.30.6.4, Anon.ap.Suid.; Pass., Hp.Decent.13

ἀβοήθητος.definition: admitting of no help, without remedy; of persons, helpless, LXXPs.87.6, Plu.Arat.2, Epict.Ench.24; BGU970.8

ἀβούλητος.definition: not according to one's wish or will, Zeno Stoic.1.53; Phld.Mort.33. cf. Ph.2.392, Plu.2.599b

ἄβουλος.definition: inconsiderate, ill-advised, S.Ant.1026, Men.Pk.382, Anacreont.12.4; taking no thought for them, unfeeling, S.Tr.140, cf. El.546, E.Heracl.152: Comp., Th.1.120.7: Sup., Plu.Dio43. Adv. Hdt.3.71; Pherecr.143.6; Antipho1…

ἁβροβάτης.definition: softly or delicately stepping, A.Pers.1072; Subst. in B.3.48

ἁβρόβιος.definition: living delicately, effeminate, B.17.2, cf. Plu.Demetr.2 , D.P.968, Alciphr.1.12

ἁβροδίαιτα.definition: luxurious living, a faulty compd., AB322, Suid., Ael.VH12.24

ἁβροδίαιτος.definition: living delicately, A.Pers.41, cf. Epigr.ap Clearch.4: effeminacy Th.1.6, Ath.12.513c; luxurious, Diog.Oen.23. Adv. Ph.1.324

ἁβροκόμης.definition: with luxuriant foliage; with delicate hair. Orph.H.56.2, Nonn.D.13.91, al.; AP12.256 :—also Nonn.D.13.456, Man.2.446

ἀβροχέω.definition: not to be inundated, BGU973.14, PFay.33 , etc

ἀβυρτάκη.definition: sour sauce of leeks, cress, and pomegranate-seeds, Pherecr.181, Theopomp.Com.17, Alex.141.13, Nymphod.19, Polyaen.4.3.32

ἀγαθοδαιμονέω.definition: Astrol., occupy the house of III, Vett.Val.62.20, Paul.Al.O.3

ἀγαθοδαίμων.definition: the good Genius, less correct; an Egyptian serpent, Hist.Aug.Elag.28, Philum.Ven.29

ἀγαθοειδής.definition: like good, seeming good, opp; having the form of good, Plot.1.7.1, al., Jul.Or.4.135a, Procl.Inst.25: Comp., Iamb.Protr.4: Sup., Marin.Procl.27

ἀγαθοεργέω.definition: do good or well, 1 Ep.Ti.6.18: contr. Act.Ap.14.17

ἀγαθοθέλεια.definition: desire of good, Anon. ap. Suid

ἀγαθοποιέω.definition: do good, Ev.Marc.3.4, S.E.M.11.70; do good to, Ev.Luc.6.33: c. dupl. acc., LXXNu.10.32, Aristeas242: LXX2 Ma.1.2

ἀγαθοποιία.definition: = foreg., 1 Ep.Pet.4.19, al; propitious influence, Vett.Val.164.17, Ptol.Tetr.38

ἀγακλεής.definition: voc. Il.17.716, al.: Ep. gen. Il.16.738, nom. pl. Man.3.324: shortened acc. sing. Pi.P.9.106, I.1.34; dat. APl.5.377; acc. pl. Antim.Eleg.2:—very glorious, famous, in Il. always of men, as 16.738, 23.529; later of pla…

ἀγαλλίασις.definition: great joy, exultation, LXXJb.8.21, al., Ev.Luc.1.14, 44, 1 Enoch5.9, Ps.-Callisth.2.22

ἀγαλλιάω.definition: late form of rejoice exceedingly, Apoc.19.7 ; Ev.Luc.1.47, cf. POxy.1592.4 :—more common as Dep. LXXIs.12.6, al.: fut. Ps.5.11: aor. Ps.15.2, Ev.Jo.8.56; ib.5.35.—This family of words seems also to have been used in m…

ἀγαλμάτιον.definition: Dim. of IG4.1588 , Theopomp.Com.47, Polycharm.5, Plu.Lyc.25, etc

ἀγαλματοποιέω.definition: make statues, Poll.7.108: Pass., have a statue made of oneself, Steph.in Rh.280.10

ἀγαλματοφορέω.definition: carry an image in one's mind, bear impressed upon one's mind, Ph.1.16, al.; Pass., 2.136

ἀγαλματοφόρος.definition: carrying an image in one's mind, Hsch

ἀγανακτέω.definition: properly in physical sense, feel a violent; metaph., to be displeased, vexed, Ar.V.287; esp. show outward signs of grief, Pl.Phd.117d; Ar.Ra.1006, etc.; . . And.4.18:—foll. by a relat., . . Antipho4.2.1, Lys.3.3; . . …

ἀγανάκτησις.definition: physical pain and irritation; vexation, Th.2.41, cf. 2 Ep.Cor.7.11, Plot.4.4.19:—of God, wrath, Porph.Marc.7, Jul.Gal.171e

ἀγανόφρων.definition: gen. poet. Adj. gentle of mood, Il.20.467, Cratin.238; Ar.Av.1321

ἀγάπη.definition: love, LXXJe.2.2, Ca.2.7, al; esp. love of God for man and of man for God, LXXWi.3.9, Aristeas229; Ph.1.283, cf. Ep.Rom.5.8, 2 Ep.Cor.5.14, Ev.Luc.11.42, al.:—also brotherly love, charity, 1 Ep.Cor.13.1, al

ἀγάπημα.definition: darling, of a person, Crates Theb.Fr.12, cf. Suet.Gramm.3, Epigr.Gr.1023 :—generally, delight; of a dainty dish, Axionic.4.6; Lyr.Alex.Adesp.24

ἀγαπήνωρ.definition: = loving manliness, manly, epith, of heroes, Il.8.114, etc

ἀγάπησις.definition: affection, Arist.Metaph.980a22, Pl.Def.413b, Clearch.39, LXXHo.11.12,al., Aristeas44, Phld.Lib.p.38O., Plu.Per.24, etc

ἀγαυριάομαι.definition: to be insolent, LXXJb.3.14: Act., EM6.38

ἀγγαρευτής.definition: one who impresses, Hsch. s.v; impressed workman, labourer, PSI200.2 ; PIand.24.1

ἀγγαρεύω.definition: press one to serve as an generally, press into service, Ev. Matt.5.41, 27.32, OGI 665.24; PTeb.5.182, 252 , cf. PPetr.2p.64 :—Pass., to be pressed into service, Men.440: metaph., to be constrained, Procop.Arc.13

ἀγγαρήιος.definition: Ion. form of Hdt.3.126; Subst. posting-system, Id.8.98

ἀγγαροφορέω.definition: bear as an Procop.Arc.30, Aed.2.4; generally, 'toil and moil', Men.10 D

ἀγγειολογέω.definition: take up a vein and operate upon it, c. acc., interp. in Sor.1.85, cf. Paul.Aeg.6.5:—hence Subst. Antyll. or Heliod. ap. Orib.45.18.32, Aët.7.95

ἀγγελιαφόρος.definition: Ion. messenger, Hdt.1.120, Arist.Mu.398a31, Luc.Sacr.8, etc.: esp. Persian chamberlain, Hdt.3.118

ἀγελάζομαι.definition: Pass., to be gregarious, flock, Arist.HA597b7, 610b2, Nic.Dam.p.151 D.; Men.Prot.p.49 D.:—Act., Hsch

ἀγελαρχέω.definition: lead a herd or company, Ph.1.679: c. gen., 1.658, Plu.Galb.17

ἀγέλη.definition: herd, of horses, Il.19.281; elsewhere; in Crete and at Sparta, bands in which boys were trained, Ephor.64, Plu.Lyc.16, Heraclid.Pol.15, GDI4952 , etc.; Epigr.Gr.223.8 ; ib.239

ἀγελήτης.definition: belonging to a herd, Suid.; cf

ἀγενής.definition: unborn, uncreated, Pl.Ti.27c; of no family, ignoble, opp. S.Fr.84, cf. POxy.33v5.5 ; of things, Sch.Od.11.568; cf. AB336, St.Byz. s.v

ἀγένητος.definition: uncreated, unoriginated; not having happened, Gorg.Pal.23; ; S.Tr.743; Id.Fr.860; Agatho5; groundless charges, Aeschin.3.225; Alciphr.3.58; baseless dreams, Phld.D.1.22; . . was left undone, Isoc.20.8

ἀγεννής.definition: = II , low-born; of things, sordid, Hdt.5.6, Pl.Grg.465b, 513d, al.; Ar.Pax748; Dem.21.152. Adv. E.IA1458, Pl.Com.46.6.—In Pl. mostly with neg., Chrm.158c, etc

ἀγερωχία.definition: arrogance, Plb.10.35.8, D.Chr.32.9; in; revelry, LXXWi.2.9; pl., feats of mastery, Philostr.VA2.28

ἀγέρωχος.definition: poet. Adj. (used also in late; later in bad sense, arrogant, Archil.154, Alc.120, Com.Adesp.162, LXX3 Ma.1.25; Luc.Asin.40; of things, Anacreont.53.42. Adv. AP9.745 , Plb.2.8.7: Comp. Id.18.34.3

ἀγεώργητος.definition: uncultivated, Thphr.CP1.16.2, PPar.63.6 , SIG685.73 , D.S.2.36, Ph.1.564, etc

ἀγηλατέω.definition: drive out one accursed or polluted, esp. one guilty of sacrilege and murder, Hdt.5.72, S.OT402, Arist.Ath.20.3:—also EM10.34

ἀγηνορία.definition: manliness, courage, of men, Il.22.457; arrogance, pride, in pl., 9.700; sg., Nonn.D.42.384, AP10.75.7 , etc.; of a lion, Il.12.46

ἀγησίλαος.definition: leader of the people, epith. of Hades, A.Fr.406; Ion. AP7.545 ; Ep. Nic.Fr.74.72; poet. also Call.Lav.Pall.130, Epigr.Gr.195 :-the form cited in EM8.32 , etc., is corrupt. II. pr. n., esp. of the well-known Spartan ki…

ἀγησίχορος.definition: leading the chorus or dance, Pi.P.1.4: fem. as pr. n., Alcm.23.77

ἁγιστεία.definition: ritual, service, in pl., Isoc.11.28, cf. Pl.Ax.371d, Arist.Cael.268a14; later in sg., Str.9.3.7, J.Ap.1.7, Plu.Rom.22, Jul.Or.5.178d

ἀγκαλίζομαι.definition: embrace, Semon.7.77; AP12.122 , cf. Man.1.45; Lyc.142: in pass. sense, Aesop.366

ἀγκαλίς.definition: in pl., = arms, Ep. dat. pl; armful, Ar.Fr.418, Nicostr.24, Ister54 , Ph.5.147C., Plu.Rom.8

ἀγκιστρεύω.definition: angle for, entice, Aristaenet.1.5:—Med., Ph.1.344: metaph., 2.265; 1.304

ἀγκιστρόδετος.definition: with a hook bound to it, AP6.27

ἀγκιστροειδής.definition: hook-shaped, barbed, Placit.1.3.18, etc. Adv. Erot. s.v

ἀγκιστρόομαι.definition: Pass., to be furnished with barbs; to be caught by a hook, Lyc.67

ἀγκύλη.definition: properly, like bend of; bend of the knee, ham, Philostr.Im.2.6, Sch.Il.23.726

ἀγκυλίζομαι.definition: in wrestling, clasp the adversary's neck, dub. l. in Poll.1.176

ἀγκυλόγλωσσον πάθος.definition: contraction of the tongue, Orib.45.15 tit., Paul.Aeg.6.29; and one who suffers from it, Aët.8.38

ἀγκυλογλώχιν.definition: of a cock, with hooked spurs, Babr.17.3

ἀγκυλόκυκλος.definition: curved in spires, of a dragon's tail, Nonn.D.35.217

ἀγκυλοχείλης.definition: with hooked beak, Od.19.538, AP6.229 ; Il.16.428, Hes.Sc.405, Batr.294

ἀγκυλοχήλης.definition: with crooked claws, v.l. in Batr.294, Ar.Eq.197, cf. Sch

ἀγκυροειδής.definition: anchor-shaped, Dsc.3.158, Gal.2.766. Adv. Erot. s.v

ἀγκυρόμαχος.definition: a kind of ship, Isid. Etym. 19.1.16, Gloss

ἀγκυρομήλη.definition: hooked probe, Hp. ap. Erot., cf. Gal.19.69

ἀγκωνισμός.definition: a bending, reach, of an estuary, Eust.1712.29

ἀγλάϊσμα.definition: ornament, honour, A.Ag.1312; of a child, E.Hel.11, cf. 282; of the hair of Orestes placed on his father's tomb, A.Ch.193, S.El.908, cf. E.El.325; of a sarcophagus, IG12.600 .— Poet. and late Prose; of the rose, Ach.Ta…

ἀγλαόθρονος.definition: with splendid throne, bright-throned, Pi.O.13.96, cf. N.10.1, B.16.124

ἀγλαομορφέω.definition: in Pass., to be endowed with beauteous form, PLeid.W.4.16

ἀγλαόμορφος.definition: of beauteous form, AP9.524, Orph.H.14.5, al

ἀγλαοτρίαινα.definition: acc. he of the bright trident, epith. of Poseidon, Pi.O.1.40

ἁγνευτήριον.definition: place of purification, Chaerem.Hist.4, cf. AB267; sacristy, POxy.840.8

ἁγνίζω.definition: fut. LXXNu.8.6: pf. 1; cleanse, purify, E.HF1324, cf. Diph.126.1, LXXEx.19.10:—Med., purify oneself, ib.Jo.3.5, Plu.2.1105b:—Pass., Act.Ap.21.24; LXXNu.6.3

ἁγνίτης.definition: purifier, Poll.1.24; one who requires purification, Hsch., AB338, v.l. in Il.24.480

ἁγνοπολέομαι.definition: to be purified by sacrifices, Phot

ἀγνωμονέω.definition: to be act without right feeling; act ill-advisedly, Aq.1 Ki.13.13

ἀγνωμοσύνη.definition: want of acquaintance with a thing; want of sense, folly, Thgn.896, Democr.175; senseless pride, arrogance, Hdt.2.172, E.Ba.885 ; Hdt.4.93; Id.5.83; Id.9.3

ἀγνώσσω.definition: = pres. only, mostly poet., Simm.1.13, Musae.249, D.P.173, Coluth.8, Nonn.D.1.425, etc.; in late Prose, Luc.Ep. Sat.25

ἀγοράζω.definition: fut. Ar.Lys.633, LXXNe.10.31; buy in the market, Ar.Ach.625; X.An.1.5.10; generally, buy, Ar.Pl.984, etc.; farm taxes or state-contracts, PRev.Laws41.22, al.; ib.60.23:—Med., buy for oneself, X.An.1.3.14:—Pass., D.50.…

ἀγορανομέω.definition: to be Alex.247, IG12.170 ; POxy.910.2 ; at Rome, to be aedile, D.H.10.48, Plu.Caes.5, App.BC2.1, etc.: pf. D.C.52.32

ἀγορανόμιον.definition: court or office of the Pl.Lg.917e, IG2.192c11, 12.170, PHib.29.3 , AP11.17

ἀγορανόμιος.definition: of or in the forum, IGRom.4.504

ἀγορανόμος.definition: clerk of the market, who regulated; public notary, PGrenf.2.23aii 2 , POxy.99.2 , etc

ἀγορασείω.definition: Desid. of wish to buy, Sch.Ar.Ra.1068

ἀγορασία.definition: purchase, Telecl.51, Hyp.Fr.70, Inscr.Magn.116.20 , D.L.2.78 , etc

ἀγορασμός.definition: purchasing, Phint. ap.Stob.4.23.61a; purchase, LXXGe.42.19,al., OGI660.20 ; freq. of auctions, BGU1128.9 B.C.)

ἀγοραστής.definition: the slave who had to buy provisions for the house, purveyor, X.Mem.1.5.2:—generally, purchaser, Men.500, cf. Arist.Oec.1352b6, Dinon12, Ael.VH12.1, POxy.298.48

ἀγράμματος.definition: illiterate, X.Mem.4.2.20, Damox.2.12; of animals, unable to utter articulate sounds, Arist.HA488a33

ἄγραμμος.definition: not on the line, of a throw of the dice, counting nothing, Hsch

ἀγραυλέω.definition: live in the open, out of doors, Arist.Mir.831a29, Parth.29.1, Plu.Num.4, Str.4.4.3; of shepherds, Ev.Luc.2.8

ἀγρεύς.definition: hunter, epith. of Aristaeus; of an arrow, AP6.75

ἀγρευτήρ.definition: = sq., Theoc.21.6, Call.Dian.218; as Adj., Opp.C.3.456; i.e. with fishing-net, Man.5.279

ἀγρευτής.definition: hunter, epith. of Apollo as slayer of; Adj., hounds, Sol.23; a fowler's trap of reeds, AP7.171 , cf. 6.109

ἀγρευτίς.definition: fem. of prob. l. in Sch.Ar.V.367

ἀγριαίνω.definition: intr., to be or become wild, to be angered, provoked, Pl.R.493b, etc.; with one, Id.Smp.173d; Porph.Abst.3.12; of animals, Arist.HA608b31; of rivers and the like , chafe, . . Plu.Caes.38:—Pass., D.S. l. c.; of sores, …

ἀγριέλαιος.definition: = foreg., AP9.237; as Subst., = Theoc.7.18, Thphr.HP2.2.5, Ep.Rom.11.17, etc

ἀγριεύω.definition: catch by hunting or fishing, PRyl.98a7

ἀγριοδαίτης.definition: eating wild fruits, Orac. ap. Paus.8.42.6

ἀγριόω.definition: aor. E.Or.616, the act. tenses being; mostly in Pass., Hp.Aër.4: impf. E.El.1031 codd.: aor. Plu.Per.34: pf. S.Ph.1321, E.IT348, Ar.Ra.897:—grow wild; in pf. to be wild, properly of plants, countries, etc., Thphr.HP5.…

ἀγρογείτων.definition: country neighbour, Plu.Cat. Ma.25, POxy.1106.2 ; having a field adjoining his, J.AJ8.13.8

ἀγροικεύομαι.definition: to be stupid, Phld.Mus.p.95 K., cf. EM14.2, Hsch. s.v

ἀγροικία.definition: rusticity, boorishness, Pl.Grg.461c; the country, Herod.1.2, Inscr.Magn. 8, SIG344.100 , Muson.Fr.11p.60H., Plu.2.519a, Longus1.13, Aristid.Or.47.45; pl., Plu.2.311b

ἀγροικίζομαι.definition: to be rude and boorish, Pl.Tht.146a, Plu.Sull.6: aor. Aristid.1.491 J

ἀγρολέτειρα.definition: waster of land, Hsch.; epith. of Artemis, Suid

ἀγρότερος.definition: of countrymen, AP9.244 , APl.4.235; of plants, wild, AP9.384.8, cf. Nic.Th.711, Coluth.111

ἀγρότης.definition: poet. word, countryman; hunter, . . Od.16.218, cf. Alcm.23.8; to whom are offered, AP6.13 :—fem. A.R.2.509; i.e. Artemis, AP6.111 ; ib.57

ἀγρυπνέω.definition: pf. Hp.Prog.2:—lie awake, pass; metaph., to be watchful, LXXWi.6.15, Ev.Marc.13.33, Ep.Eph.6.18; Ep.Heb.13.17; LXXDa.9.14: c. inf., PGrenf.2.14a3

ἀγρυπνία.definition: Ion. sleeplessness, wakefulness, Hp.Aph.2.3, al., Pl.Cri.43b, etc.; in pl., Hp.Acut.42; Hdt.3.129, cf. IG4.952.50 , Ar.Lys.27, Pl.R.460d. II. time of watching, Pl.Ax.368b; Just.Nov.13Pr. III. of poetry, product of sle…

ἄγρυπνος.definition: wakeful, Hp.Epid.1.18, Pl.R.404a; Act., banishing sleep, keeping awake, Arist.Pr.917b1; APl.4.211 . E.Rh.2 , Theoc.24.106.]

ἀγρώστης.definition: = Subst. and Adj., S.Fr.94; wild, Babr.115.2

ἄγυια.definition: street, highway, chiefly in pl; collection of streets, city, Pi.O.9.34, N.7.92; Hymn.Is.2. Il.20.254 , cf. Pi.N.7.92 codd. vett.; Ion. and old Att. acc. to Hdn.Gr.2.613, Eust.1631.29; incorrectly, EM14.21, etc.; freq.…

ἀγυιάτης.definition: in pl., inhabitants of an IG9.241 , cf. Hsch., EM15.31

Ἀγυιεύς.definition: a name of Apollo, as guardian of the; pointed pillar, set up as his statue or altar at the street-door, Ar.V.875, Pherecr.87, Dieuchid.2; S.Fr.370

Ἀγυίηος.definition: name of month at Argos, Mnemos.44.221

ἀγυιόπεζα Κουρῆτις.definition: mystical name for Pythagorean triad, Nicom. ap. Phot.Bibl.143B

ἀγυιοπλαστέω.definition: to build in streets or rows, Lyc.601

ἀγύμναστος.definition: unexercised, untrained; unpractised, in a thing, E.Ba.491, X.Cyr.1.6.29, Pl., etc.; also or Pl.Lg.731b, 816a; Plu.2.802d, Gal.8.608; Phld.Rh.1.189 S.: c. inf., Muson.Fr.6p.23H

ἀγυρτεύω.definition: live by begging as a vagabond, Str.7 Fr.18, cf. Sch.Luc.Alex.13

ἀγχέμαχος.definition: fighting hand to hand, Il.13.5, Hes.Sc.25; X.Cyr.1.2.13, cf. Arr.Ind.24.4; APl.4.173

ἀγχίαλος.definition: also h.Ap.32, Androm. ap. Gal.14.42: :— poet. word, near the sea, of cities, Il.2.640; Androm.l.c.; B.4.14; of islands, sea-girt, as Peparethos, Lemnos, Salamis, h.Ap.l.c., A.Pers.887 , S.Aj.135 , AP9.288 ; of the fou…

ἀγχιβατέω.definition: stand by, Hsch; Ion. for Suid

ἀγχίκρημνος.definition: near the cliffs or coast, Pi.Fr.82

ἀγχίμολος.definition: coming near; Ep. word, mostly used in neut. as Adv., near, close at hand, Il.4.529, cf. Od.8.300, etc., Hes.Sc.325; Il.24.352; close behind him, Od.17.336: c. gen., cj. in Theoc.25.203

ἀγχίνοια.definition: ready wit, sagacity, shrewdness, Pl.Chrm.160a, Arist.EN1142b6, APo89b10, Zeno Stoic.1.56, Onos.Praef.9, D.S.1.65, etc.; Plb.15.34.4

ἀγχίνοος.definition: contr. ready of wit, shrewd, Od.13.332, Pl.Lg.747b, Stoic.2.39, etc.; Arist.HA587a12: Comp., Ptol.Tetr.57, S.E.P.2.41: Sup., ib.42. Adv. Aen.Tact.11.10; Id.24.11, Arist.VV1250a33, Andronic.Rhod.p.575M.: Sup. Phlp.in P…

ἀγχιστεύς.definition: mostly in pl. next of kin, of nations, Hdt.5.80:—heir-at-law, LXXRu.3.9 , Hierocl.in CA5p.428M.; Luc.Tim.51

ἀγχιστῖνος.definition: Ep. Adj. close, crowded, in heaps, Il.5.141; 17.361, cf. Od.22.118

ἄγχιστος.definition: Hom. has only neut. as Adv., nearest, Od.5.280; more commonly pl., was most nearly like , Il.2.58, 14.474; Od.13.80; 6.152, cf. Pi.I.2.10: freq. c. gen., next to Zeus, A.Supp.1035 ; Hdt.9.81; Id.1.134, al., cf. those …

ἀγχίστροφος.definition: turning closely, quick-swooping; quick-changing, changeable, Hdt.7.13; sudden change, Th.2.53; D.H.4.23:—Rhet., rapidity of transition, Longin.27.3; a style flexible in the use of the cases, D.H.Comp.22. Adv. Longin.22.1

ἀγχιτέρμων.definition: gen. near the border, neighbouring, S.Fr.384, E.Rh.426; Theodect.17, Lyc.1130.—Poet. and in X.Hier.10.7

ἀγχιτόκος.definition: near the birth, pangs of child- birth, Pi.Fr.88.2, Nonn.D.24.197; of a woman, AP7.462 ; Nonn.D.8.12

ἀγχόμορος.definition: neighbouring, c. gen., dub. in Theoc.25.203

ἀγχοτάτω.definition: Adv., Sup. of nearest, next, c. gen., h.Ap.18, Hdt.2.169, E.Fr.620; of like ness, Hdt.7.64 , 80, al.; ib.91; the nearest of kin, 4.73

ἀγωνάρχης.definition: judge of a contest, S.Aj.572; Boeotian magistrate, IG7.1817 , cf. Sch.Il.24.1

ἀγωνία.definition: contest, struggle for victory, Hdt.2.91; E.Hec.314, cf. Tr.1003; esp. in games, Pi.O.2.52, P.5.113:-also in Prose, X.Cyr.2.3.15; [D.]60.30, etc. 2. gymnastic exercise, Hp.Art.11, Pl.Men.94b, Lg.765c, etc.: generally, …

ἀγωνιάω.definition: inf. Pl.Prt.333e, part; to be distressed or anxious, be in an agony, Pl.Prt.333e; Id.Ly.210e, cf. Arist.Pr.869b8, Men.Her.2, PPetr.3p.151; Arist.Rh.1367a15: c.acc., Plb.1.20.6, al.; Plu.Caes.46; . . Plb.3.9.2, etc.; N…

ἀγωνίζομαι.definition: fut. E.Heracl.992, etc. (in pass; contend for the prize on the stage, of the rhapsode, Hdt.5.67; of the playwright, Ar.Ach.140,419; of the actor, D.19.246, cf. 250, Arist.Po.1451a8; of the choragus, D.21.66: c. acc., …

ἀγώνισμα.definition: contest, conflict: in pl., deeds done in; in sg., feat, achievement, a feather in his cap, Th.8.12, cf. 17: c. inf., Id.7.59,86; prize of sagacity, Id.3.82; issue of the curse, E.Ph.1355

ἀγωνιστής.definition: combatant, E.Ion1257; pleader, debater, Pl.Phdr.269d, Tht.164c

ἀγωνοθεσία.definition: office of direction or exhibition of games, IG2.379 , Nic.Dam.Vit.Caes.9, Plu.Ages.21, etc.: pl., prob. in Phld.Rh.2.27 S

ἀγωνοθετέω.definition: exhibit games, GDI1842 , etc; c. acc., embroil them, Plb.9.343; etc., stir up faction, war, etc., Plu.Cat.Mi.45, J.AJ17.3.1

ἀγωνοθήκη.definition: = S.Fr.975, criticized as irreg. by Poll.3.141

ἀδαήμων.definition: unknowing, ignorant, c. gen., Il.5.634; Od.12.208; Hdt.8.65, cf. MatroParod.Fr.6, Hierocl.in CA4p.425M.: abs., Ps.-Phoc.86

ἀδάκρυτος.definition: Act., tearless, Il.1.415, cf. Od.24.61; 4.186; S.Tr.1200; so that they weep not, ib.106 :—Medic., abnormally dry, Aet.7.91

ἀδαμαντοπέδιλος.definition: on a base of adamant, Pi.Fr.88.5

ἀδάμαστος.definition: unsubdued, inflexible, of Hades, Il.9.158, cf. Phld.D.1.18: later in the proper sense, untamed, unbroken, X.Eq.1.1, cf. Corn.ND20; Timo9.1

ἀδάματος.definition: = unconquered, A.Ch.54, Th.233, S.OT205, etc.: of females, unwedded, S.Aj.450; untamed, E.Ph.640.—Trag. word, always in lyr. ; restored by Elmsl. for or of codd

ἀδεισιδαίμων.definition: without superstition, Adv. D.S.38.7: Comp. Sor.1.80

ἀδελφιδέος.definition: contr. nephew, Alcm.56A, etc.; usu. brother's son, Hdt.1.65, 6.94, al., Th.2.101, etc.; also, sister's son, Hdt.4.147, Str.10.5.6, etc.:—also beloved one, LXXCa.2.3, al

ἀδελφίζω.definition: adopt as a brother, call brother, Hecat.8J., Apolloph.4, Isoc.19.30:—Pass., to be very like, Hp.Acut.9, etc.; Id.Fract.31, Art.45

ἀδέλφιον.definition: Dim. of Keil-Premerstein Zweiter Bericht 215 , POxy.1300.4
