ἀδελφοκτόνος.definition: murdering a brother or sister, Hdt.3.65 , Nic.Dam.p.142 D., Plu.2.256f, Ph.1.148

ἀδελφοκτονέω.definition: to be murderer of a brother or sister, J.BJ2.11.4, Vett.Val.74.28

ἀδελφοκτονία.definition: murder of a brother or sister, J.BJ1.31.2, Ph.1.210, al

ἀδελφομιξία.definition: marriage of brother and sister, Tz.H.1.590

ἀδελφόπαις.definition: brother's or sister's child, D.H.4.64 , cf. Just.Nov.127.1

ἄδεσμος.definition: unfettered, unbound, Lat. libera custodia, 'parole', Th.3.34, D.H.1.83, etc.; open purses, Plu.2.503c; of suppliant's wreath, E.Supp.32; unbandaged, Gal.18.505

ἀδηλία.definition: = A.D.Pron.25.18, v.l. in Corn.ND13; Iamb.Myst.10.4, cf. AP10.96

ἀδηλότης.definition: uncertainty, Protag.4, Plb.5.2.3, Ph.1.277, Corn.ND13, etc

ἀδημονέω.definition: to be sorely troubled or dismayed, be in anguish, Hp.Virg.1; Pl.Tht.175d, cf. D.19.197; X.HG4.4.3: c. dat. rei, Pl.Phdr.251d; to be puzzled by . ., Epicur.Nat.11.8; D.H.3.70; POxy.298.45 . .177), and is itself of doub…

ἀδήριτος.definition: without strife or battle, Il.17.42; uncontested, undisputed, Plb.1.2.3, Orph.A.846. Adv. Plb.3.93.1, D.S.4.14, Plu.Caes.3

ἀδηφαγέω.definition: to be greedy, Hermipp.84; of horses, S.Fr.976, Isoc.6.55

ἀδηφαγία.definition: gluttony, Call.Dian.160: pl., Arist.Fr.144, Opp.H.2.218:—personified, Polem.Hist.39

ἀδηφάγος.definition: gluttonous, greedy; metaph., devouring much money, costly, Lys.Fr.39, cf. Philist.58; of racehorses, Pherecr.197, Ar.Fr.736

ἀδιάβλητος.definition: not listening to calumny; unexceptionable, Pl.Def.412c; Plu.2.4b; App.Sam.4.4. Adv. Just.Nov.137.2

ἀδιάβολος.definition: = foreg. I, Stoic.3.153; Pass., unexceptionable, Mon.Ant. 23.60

ἀδιάγλυπτος.definition: not to be cut through, AB344

ἀδιάγνωστος.definition: indistinguishable, D.S.1.30; Antig.Mir.25; hard to distinguish or understand, Aristid. Quint.1.5

ἀδιάζευκτος.definition: not disjoined, inseparable, Corn.ND14, Iamb.in Nic.pp.15, 107P.; Procl.in Prm.p.521 S.; indistinguishable, Phld.D.1.19

ἀδιάθετος.definition: not disposed or set in order; having made no will, intestate, Plu.Cat.Ma.9, D.Chr.54.4, POxy.105.6 , al

ἀδιάκοπος.definition: unbroken, uninterrupted, Aristeas139; Herod.ap.Orib.7.8.4; Ph.1.81, cf. Porph.Plot.8. Adv. HeroDef.37, Ulp.ad D.18.308, Steph.in Hp.1.149 D

ἀδιακόσμητος.definition: not set in order, D.H.3.10; Stoic.2.189, cf. Ph.2.505; of lands, not disposed of, unassigned, J.AJ5.1.23

ἀδιάλειπτος.definition: unintermitting, incessant, Ti. Locr.98e, Ep.Rom.9.2, Hierocl.p.19.55A., Plu.2.121e, M.Ant.6.15. Adv. Metrod.Herc.831.8, Polem.Hist.30, Plb.9.3.8, Posidon.25, LXX1 Ma.12.11, Ep.Rom.1.9, PLond.3.1166.6

ἀδιάληπτος.definition: indistinct, confused, Metrod.Herc.831.11, cf. 13; Phld.Rh.2.44S.: —also of persons, confused in mind, ib.47 S., Id.Po.1676.3. Adv. opp. Id.Mus.p.32 K., al

ἀδιάλυτος.definition: undissolved: indissoluble, Pl.Phd.80b; irreconcilable. Adv. Plb.18.37.4

ἀδιανέμητος.definition: not to be divided, Longin.22.3; undivided, Timae.77

ἀδιανόητος.definition: unintelligible, Did. ap; inconceivable, Pl.Sph.238c, Epicur.Fr.606, cf. Ep.2p.43U., Phld.Sign.12, al., Arr.Epict.2.20.18, S.E.M.8.389

ἀδιάπαυστος.definition: not to be stilled, incessant, violent, Plb.4.39.10, Phalar.Ep.67.3. Adv. Plb.1.57.1, Antyll. ap. Orib.4.11.14

ἀδιάπλαστος.definition: as yet unformed, Pl.Ti.91d, cf. Suid. s.v

ἀδιαπνευστία.definition: want of perspiration or suppressed perspiration, Gal.10.763, Alex.Trall.Febr.1

ἀδιαπόρευτος.definition: that cannot be traversed, Simp.in Cat.470.2

ἀδιάπτωτος.definition: infallible, Hp.Decent.12, S.E.M.7.110; faultless, of writers, Longin.33.5; perfection of style, Id.36.4; Diog.Bab.Stoic.3.214; D.T.629.12

ἀδιάρθρωτος.definition: not jointed or articulated; confused, Arr.Epict.1.17.1, Plu.2.378c

ἀδιαρίπιστος.definition: not scattered by the winds, Hsch. s.v

ἀδιάρρηκτος.definition: not torn in pieces, gloss on EM149.12

ἀδιάσειστος.definition: not shaken about, Gal.19.81; gloss on Sch.Opp.H.4.415

ἀδιάσπαστος.definition: not torn asunder, uninterrupted, unbroken, X.Ages.1.4, Plb.1.34.5; inseparable, Dam.Pr.418, cf. Olymp.Alch.p.77B. Adv. Steph.in Hp.1.65 D., Hsch

ἀδιάστατος.definition: continuous, Antipho Soph.24; Andronic.Rhod.p.513M. Adv. without intermission, Ph.1.342,501, etc. b. without distinctions or intervals, Plot.3.7.2, Dam.Pr.105,370. 2. Gramm. of in diphthongs, inseparable, not forming a…

ἀδιάστολος.definition: Gramm., not distinguished, A.D.Pron.11.26. Adv. Phld.Rh.1.53S., cf. Phoeb.Fig.1.3, Porph.Abst.2.37

ἀδιάστροφος.definition: incapable of turning: metaph., rigid; not distorted, Arist.Pr.958a12; Plu.2.780b; Aret.SD1.12. Adv. Gal.18.334

ἀδιάτρεπτος.definition: not to be turned aside, c. gen; headstrong, LXXSi.26.10. Adv. LXX v.l. ibid., Jul.Or.6.197b

ἀδιάφθαρτος.definition: = I, Pl.Ap.34b, Lg.951c; = sq. II, Epicur.Fr.267, Gal.2.27

ἀδιάφθορος.definition: not affected by decay, Antyll. ap; of judges, incorruptible, Pl.Lg.768b; of witnesses, Arist.Rh.1376a17; of magistrates, Id.Pol.1286a39 , cf. IG2.240b13. Sup. Adv. Pl.l.c

ἀδιαχώρητος.definition: without evacuation, Hp.Acut.38; not passing through the bowels, Sor.1.125

ἀδιαχώριστος.definition: unseparated, undistinguished, EM538.34, Suid. Adv. Hsch. s.v

ἀδιάψευστος.definition: not deceitful, D.S.5.37; of Sphaer.Stoic.1.141, cf. M.Ant.4.49, Iamb.Protr.21. Adv. S.E.M.7.191, Ruf.Fr.68.10

ἀδιεξέταστος.definition: that will not stand examination, LXXSi.21.18

ἀδιεξήγητος.definition: indescribable, Ph.1.407, prob. in IG5.1359 :—inexhaustible, Dam.Pr.178

ἀδιεξόδευτος.definition: having no outlet, Eust.1688.37, cf. Sch.E.Or.25

ἀδιέργαστος.definition: not wrought out, unfinished, Isoc.12.268, Poll.6.143. Adv. ib.144

ἀδιερεύνητος.definition: uninvestigated, Ph.1.470, etc; of persons, not searched, Plu.Dio19

ἀδιευκρίνητος.definition: obscure, lacking in order, of style, Hermog.Id.2.11; Heraclit.All.48

ἀδίκιον.definition: = Hdt.5.89, cf. IG7.235 ; esp. suit for malversation, Arist.Ath.54.2, cf. Plu.Per.32; also, damage, PTaur.4.15 , cf. PPar.14.44

ἀδικομαχέω.definition: fight unfairly, esp. in the law-courts, Alciphr.3.29; dub. in Poll.3.154

ἀδικομαχία.definition: unfair fighting, Arist.SE171b23, cf. Ascl.in Metaph.243.9

ἀδικοπράγημα.definition: wrong action, Stoic. ap. Stob.2.7.11e, Phld.Piet.19G

ἀδικοπραγής.definition: Ion. acting wrongly, Perict. ap. Stob.4.28.19

ἀδιόδευτος.definition: not to be travelled through, Them.Or.16.206d, cf. Charito7.3

ἀδιοίκητος.definition: unarranged, D.24.28, cf. IG5.433 ; undigested, Gal.19.217, Hippiatr.31:—of property, = PPetr.3p.198

ἀδιόρατος.definition: not to be seen through, Poll.5.150

ἀδιόριστος.definition: in Logic, indesignate, Arist.APr.26b23; undefined, Phld.Po.1425.1, al.; indefinite, Arist.PA639a22, cf. Dam.Pr.37, al. Adv. Arist.Ph.184b11, al.; vaguely, loosely, Anon.in SE62.31

ἀδιπλασίαστος.definition: not doubled, of letters, Eust.781.15. Adv. Id.870.63

ἀδοκίμαστος.definition: not approved, Lys.14.8, 15.11, Aeschin.3.15, etc.; D.H.11.57; Onos.Praef.7

ἀδολεσχέω.definition: talk idly, prate, Eup.353, Pl.Phd.70c; generally, talk, LXXPs.68.12

ἀδολεσχία.definition: prating, garrulity, Ar.Nu.1480; keenness, subtlety, Pl.Phdr.269e

ἀδόλεσχος.definition: = Cic.Att.16.11.2, IG14.1746 ; Alciphr.3.66; S.E.M.1.141: Comp. Gal.5.315: Sup. Plu.2.509a. Adv. Phld.Ir.p.17 W., Rh.1.212 S

ἀδοξία.definition: ill repute, Hp.Lex1, Th.1.76, Pl.Phd.82c; contempt, App.Syr.41

ἄδοξος.definition: without inglorious, D.5.5; obscure, ignoble, Isoc.12.253; D.8.66, cf. Arist.Rh.1384b31; of eunuchs, despised, X.Cyr.7.5.61. Adv. Plu.Thes.35

ἄδουλος.definition: unattended by slaves; having no slaves, too poor to keep a slave, Phryn.Com.18, Plu.2.831b

ἁδρέω.definition: to be full-grown, matured, Dsc.2.85:— Pass. forms , Hsch

ἁδροκέφαλος.definition: with large head, Sor.2.63, Paul.Aeg.6.74; sens. obsc., Hierocl.Facet.251

ἁδρομερής.definition: of coarse, large grains, opp. D.S.5.26, Gal.8.336 ; coarse, of wine, Dsc.5.6: Comp. Ph.1.493. Adv. Heras ap.Gal.13.1045

ἁδρύνω.definition: ripen, mature, S.Fr.979, X.Mem.4.3.8; Thphr.HP3.1.3:—Pass., grow ripe, ripen, come to maturity, of fruit or corn, Hdt.1.193, Arist.Ph.230b2; of embrya, Hp.Septim.1, Oct.12, cf. Arist.HA565b13; of nestlings, 619b30

ἀδυναμέω.definition: to want power, be incapable, LXXSi.Prol., Simp.in Cael.139.24: c. inf., PLond.2.361r8

ἀδυναμία.definition: Ion. want of strength; generally, inability, incapacity, Hdt.8.111, Arist.Metaph.1019b15, etc.; Antipho5.2, cf. Pl.Lg.646b, etc.: pl., LXX3 Ma.2.13: c. gen., for wrongdoing, Pl.R.359b; for political action, Arist.Pol.…

ἀδυνατέω.definition: of persons, to be lack strength; of things, to be impossible, LXXJb.10.13, Phld.Ir.p.98 W., Ev.Matt.17.20, Ev.Luc.1.37, Ps.-Callisth.3.26

ἀδύνατος.definition: of persons, unable to do a thing, c. inf., Hdt.3.138, Epich.272, E.HF56, etc.; Arist.Rh.1379a2; . . Onos.1.13: Comp., Pl.Grg.483d: Sup. Eup.95

Ἀδώνιος.definition: rare form of Plu.2.756c; as Adj., of Adonis:—hence a statue of him borne in the Adonia, Suid

Ἄδωνις.definition: cuttings planted in pots for the Adonia, Pl.Phdr.276b, Thphr.HP6.7.3, cf. Theoc.15.113: prov., of any short-lived pleasure, Sch.Pl.ad loc

ἀδωροδόκητος.definition: incorruptible, Aeschin.3.82, etc. Adv. D.18.250, 19.4, IG2.114A5, Onos.1.8, D.S.39.20

ἀδωσιδικία.definition: failure to give satisfaction, P Lond.2.357.7

ἀειγενέτης.definition: only in Ep.form epith. of the gods, everlasting, used by Hom. only at the end of a line, Il.2.400, cf. 3.296

ἀειγενής.definition: eternal, Hp.Virg.1, Pl.Lg.773e; everlasting, opp. Plu.2.374d

ἀειγεννητής.definition: perpetual producer, epith. of Apollo , Macr.Sat.1.17.35

ἀείζωος.definition: Trag. contr. ever-living; evergreen, A.Fr.28, 29, cf. Gp.2.18.1: esp. houseleek, Sempervivum, Thphr.HP1.10.4, Dsc.4.88; S. arboreum, S. tectorum, ib.89; stonecrop, Sedum stellatum, Ps.-Dsc.4.90

ἀεικέλιος.definition: Od.4.244, also 19.341; poet. form of 13.402, Il.14.84; contr. Thgn.1344, E.Andr.131 : —of things, words, and actions; more rarely of persons, Od.6.242. Adv. Od.8.231, 16.109, B.3.45

ἀεικινησία.definition: perpetual motion, Inscr. Perg.333, [Gal.]19.376, Syr.in Metaph.37.13, Procl.in Prm.p.874S

ἀεικίνητος.definition: in perpetual motion, Pl.Phdr.245c, Philol.21, Ruf.Anat.27, Aen.Gaz.Thphr.p.46B. Adv. Arist.Mu.400b31

ἀειλογέω.definition: to be always talking, Hsch.; condemned by Phryn.PSp.35B

ἀείμνηστος.definition: had in everlasting remembrance, A.Pers.760; S.Aj.1166, E.IA1531 , etc.; Th.1.33; Lys.2.20: Comp., Id.26.4; Antipho5.79; Isoc.9.4; PLips.35.22 . Adv. Aeschin.2.180, PLond.3.854.12

ἀειναής.definition: = sq., Nic.Fr.78, in Ep. dat. pl

ἀειπαθής.definition: perpetually passive, Crito ap.Stob.3.3.64, cf. Philol.21

ἀειπάρθενος.definition: ever a virgin, Sapph.96 (in Aeol; in Pythag. language, of the number 7 , Ph.1.46; of the Sabbath, ib.497

ἀείφρουρος.definition: ever-watching, i.e. everlasting, Cratin.98.7; of the grave, S.Ant.892; Opp.H.4.189

ἀειφυγία.definition: exile for life, Pl.Lg.877c, IG1.9, SIG194 ; D.21.43, etc

ἀείχλωρος.definition: always green, Euph.133; used of Dsc.2.173

ἀελλόπος.definition: for :—storm-footed, storm-swift, Il.8.409, etc. ; Euph.113; dat. pl. h.Ven.217: pl. Simon.7, Pi.N.1.6, etc.: once in Trag., E.Hel.1314.—Later of the hare, Opp.C.1.413

ἀέναος.definition: Hdt., IG5.1119 ; contr. Ar.Ra.146, gen. pl. Cratin.20 D.: Trag. only in lyr.:—ever-flowing, Hes.Op.595; Hdt.1.93,145, cf. Simon.120; A.Supp.553, E.Ion1083, cf. 118; Theoc.15.102; Pi.P.1.6, cf. Call.Ap.83; Ar. l.c.; Id…

ἀεξίφυτος.definition: nourishing plants, AP9.36.3.5 , cf. Nonn.D.7.304, al

ἀέρινος.definition: aerial, like air; light blue , LXXEs.8.15; Poll.4.119; Gal.12.780

ἀεροδονέομαι.definition: to be whirled through air, Sch.A.Pr.128

ἀεροειδής.definition: Ep. and Ion. like the sky or air, Pl.Ti.78c, Arist.GC330b24, etc.:—cloudy in colour, Id.Col.794a4, cf. 797a7, BGU1207.6 .—For the Homeric usage of the word v

ἀερολέσχης.definition: man of big empty words, Hsch

ἀερόμελι.definition: oak-manna, Amynt. ap. Ath.11.500d, cf. Gal.6.739

ἀερομιγής.definition: compounded of air, Cleom.2.1, al., Corn.ND19, D.L.7.145, etc

ἀεροσκοπία.definition: divination by observing the heavens, 1Enoch8.3, cf. Sch.Il.1.62

ἀερόφοιτος.definition: roaming in air, A.Fr.282:—also Ion Eleg.10

ἀερσίνοος.definition: contr. increasing; cheering, prob.l.Ion Eleg.9; Orph.Fr.280.9

ἀερτάζω.definition: lengthd. Ep. form of lift up, Call.Fr.19, etc.: impf. AP9.12 , A.R.1.738, etc.: irreg. opt. Nonn.D.43.99:—also aor. 1 AP6.223 : pf. Pass. ib.5.229 , Opp.C.2.99

ἀέσκω.definition: Hdn.Gr.1.436, EM20.11: impf. Med. Hsch.: aor. 1 contr. inf. Od.19.342, 3.151,490, 15.40, A.R.4.884. metri gr. or by contraction, otherwise.]

ἀζαίνω.definition: dry, parch up, aor. Nic.Th.205, and v.l. in 368:—Pass., ib.339: aor. Hsch

ἀζηλοτύπητος.definition: not likely to arouse jealousy, Cic.Att.13.19.4; not exposed to jealousy, Plu.2.787d

ἀηδέω.definition: feel disgust at, v.l. for in Od.1.134, cf. Hsch., cf.EM23.26

ἀηδής.definition: distasteful, nauseous, of food; generally, unpleasant, Hdt.7.101, cf. Pl.Lg.893a, al.: freq.in Pl. of narration, or Ap.33c, 41b, Phd.84d: Comp., Hdt. l.c.: Sup. Pl.Lg.663c, Phdr.240b

ἀηδίζω.definition: disgust, S.E.P.1.92: —Pass., to be disgusted, Anon.in Rh.194.32; Alex.Aphr.Pr.2.15; PLond.1.42

ἀηδονίς.definition: = nightingale, E.Rh.550 , Call.Lav.Pall.94, Theoc.8.38; of a poet, AP7.414 ; of a girl, IG14.1942

ἀηδώ.definition: = sq., gen. S.Aj.628 , voc. Ar.Av.679 : nom. pl. Sapph.Oxy.1787.6.7

ἀηθέω.definition: to be unaccustomed, Hsch.: impf. prob.l. A.R.1.1171

ἀηθίζομαι.definition: to be unaccustomed to a thing, Posidon.26

ἀθαλάσσωτος.definition: Att. unused to the sea, a land-lubber, Ar.Ra.204, Agath.1Praef

ἀθαμβής.definition: fearless, unabashed, Ibyc.1.9, B.14.58, Phryn.Trag.2; Plu.Lyc.16

ἀθαυμαστία.definition: absence of wonder, Str.1.3.21: c. gen., 1.3.16

ἀθέλγω.definition: = Hsch.:—Pass., is drawn off or pressed out, Hp.Hum.1 .—For v

ἀθέλητος.definition: unwilling, Hsch. Adv. Aspas. ap. Ath.5.219d

ἀθεμίστιος.definition: lawless, godless, Od.18.141; freq. in phrase versed in wickedness, 9.428, etc.; Xenoph.12, Man.2.301

ἀθέμιστος.definition: or (the former in Poetry, the; of things, unlawful, freq. in neut., Hdt.7.33; X.Mem.1.1.9; Id.Cyr.1.6.6; S.Fr.742 , Din.Fr.89.4S.; 1 Ep.Pet.4.3: c. dat., PTaur.1 ii 22

ἀθεμιτουργία.definition: doing of unlawful deeds, Cat.Cod.Astr.2.178: —Adj. Hld.8.9

ἀθεραπευσία.definition: want of attendance, c. gen., neglect of a thing, Pl.R.443a; Thphr.Char.19.1, cf.Plb.3.60.3

ἀθεράπευτος.definition: uncared for, of things, X.Mem.2.4.3; incurable, PGnom. 205 , cf. Luc.Ocyp.27, [Gal.]14.689; Phld.D.1.15. Adv. Ph.2.404

ἀθέτημα.definition: a breach of faith, transgression, D.H.4.27 , LXX3 Ki.8.50 ; cancellation, annulment of grant, PTeb.124.9

Ἀθηναΐζω.definition: to be wise as Athena, Eust.1742.2

Ἀθήναιον.definition: the temple of Athena, Hdt.5.95; lecture-hall at Rome, D.C.73.17

Ἀθηναῖος.definition: Athenian, Il.2.551, etc; Dor. sc. month in Locris, IG9.385

Ἀθηνιάω.definition: long to be at Athens, Luc.Pseudol.24

ἀθήρατος.definition: not caught, or not to be caught, Opp.C.1.514, Ael.N A1.4. Longus2.4; Max.Tyr.6.3

ἀθόλωτος.definition: untroubled, of water, Hes.Op.595; of pure air, Luc.Trag.62: metaph., Them.Or.19.232d; Just.Nov.78.2.1

ἀθροίζω.definition: Att. aor. E.Ph.495, etc.: pf; in Pass. of the mind, collect oneself, Pl.Phd.83a, cf.67c; fear has gathered strength, X.Cyr.5.2.34

ἀθυμέω.definition: to be disheartened, despond, A.Pr.474; S.Aj.587; at or for a thing, Id.El.769, etc.; Isoc.4.3; Pl.Sph.264b; Th.2.88; Id.5.91; . . X.Oec.8.21; Id.An.5.4.19:—to be sore afraid lest, S.Tr.666; Id.OT747

ἀθυμία.definition: Ion. lack of spirit, Hp.Aër.16; faintheartedness, despondency, Hdt.1.37, E.HF552; or Pl.Lg.731a, Aeschin.3.177; X.Cyr.4.1.8; Lys.12.3; X.HG6.2.24; S.Ant.237; X.Mem.3.12.6: pl., Arist.Pr.954a23

ἄθυρμα.definition: plaything, toy, Il.15.363, h.Merc.40: in pl., beautiful objects, adornments, Od.18.323, Sapph.Supp.20a.9; delight, joy, of a choral ode, Pi.P.5.23; i.e. songs, B.Fr.33, cf. 8.87; pastimes of Ares, i.e. battle, 17.57; …

ἀθυρμάτιον.definition: Dim. of foreg., Philox.3.23; pet, Luc.DMar.1.5

ἀθυρονόμος.definition: making game of the laws, Hsch

αἰγιαλεύς.definition: = foreg., Nic.Th.786, Numen. ap. Ath.7.313e:—pr. n., of the inhabitants of north coast of Peloponnese, Hdt.5.68, 7.94; of the Argives, Theoc.25 174

αἰγιβάτης.definition: goat-mounting, epith. of he- goats, etc., Pi.Fr.201; of Pan, Theoc.Ep.5.6, AP6.31

Αἴγινα.definition: Aegina, Il., etc.:—hence fem. an Aeginetan, ib., etc

Αἰγιναῖος.definition: Aeginetan, Cratin.165, al.; etc., Th.5.47, etc.:—also Luc.Tim.57; statues of the Aeginetan School, Paus.1.42.5

αἰγοπρόσωπος.definition: goat-faced, Hdt.2.46; stamped with a goat's face, Aët.7.101

αἰγοφάγος.definition: goat-eating, epith. of Zeus, Nic.Fr.99; of Hera at Sparta, Paus.3.15.7

Αἰγυπτιάζω.definition: to be like an Egyptian, i.e. to be sly and; speak Egyptian, Luc.Philops.31

Αἰγυπτιασμός.definition: imitation of the Egyptians, Eust.ad D.P.391

Αἰγυπτιόω.definition: to make like an Egyptian, i.e. swarthy, Com.Adesp.9, Hsch

αἰδέσιμος.definition: exciting shame or respect, venerable, M.Ant.1.9 , Aristid.2.99J. , Hierocl.in CA13p.448M. : c. dat., Aristid.Or.37.6; as honorary title, PFlor.15.6 ; Luc.Nigr.26; holy, Paus.3.5.6. Adv. reverently, Ael.NA2.25

αἰδεσιμότης.definition: as title, Your Reverence, Your Worship, POxy.125 ,al

αἰένυπνος.definition: giving eternal sleep, epith. of Death, S.OC1578

αἰθεροβατέω.definition: = of birds, Ph.1.506: metaph. of men, 2.242, al., cf. Ps.-Luc.Philopatr.25

αἰθεροδρόμος.definition: ether-skimming, Cines. ap. Ar.Av.1393; IG12.891 , cf. 9.881.7

αἰθερόομαι.definition: to be high in air, Sch.Opp.H.1.201

Αἰθιοπίζω.definition: to speak or be like an Ethiopian, Hld.10.39

αἰθριοκοιτέω.definition: sleep in the open air, Theoc.8.78, Antyll. ap. Orib.9.3.8

αἰθροπλανής.definition: wandering in ether, a planet, ib.586

αἰκάλλω.definition: only pres. and impf., flatter, wheedle, fondle, properly of dogs , c.acc., E.Andr.630, cf. Pl.Com.21D.; Ar.Eq.48; flatter, please me, ib.211; it cheers my heart. Id.Th.869; Plb.5.36.1, cf. Axiop.3.4, Philostr.VA5.42:—…

αἰκίζω.definition: aor. Herod.2.46: pf; more freq. in Med. A.Pr.197, Isoc.4.123: impf. S.Aj.300: fut. AP12.80 , Att. E.Andr.829: aor. S.Aj.111, OT1153, Isoc.5.103, X.An.3.4.5: pf. E.Med.1130, plpf. Plu.Caes.29:—in same sense as Act., Il…

αἰκισμός.definition: = foreg., D.8.51, Ctes.Fr.29.58, etc; Medic., discomfort, Antyll. ap. Orib.6.23.13; wrench, shock, Apollon.Cit.1

αἱμάσσω.definition: Att. D.H.2.74: fut. : aor. :-Pass., aor. E.El.574, S.Aj.909 , part. A.Pers.595: pf. SIG1171 :-make bloody, stain with blood, Pi.I.8.50, cf. A.Ag.1589; Id.Th.275; Theoc.Ep.1, cf. Philostr.VA1.1; D.H. l.c.; . . S.Ph.100…

αἱματοποιέω.definition: to make into blood, Pall.in Hp.2.74D

αἱματοποσία.definition: or drinking of blood, Porph. ap. Stob.1.49.53

αἱματόρρυτος.definition: blood- streaming, a shower of blood, E.IA1515

αἱματοσταγής.definition: blood-dripping, reeking with blood, A.Ag.1309, cf. Pers.816, E.Supp.812 , Ar.Ra.471

αἱμοβόρος.definition: blood-sucking, of certain insects, Arist.HA596b13; of serpents, greedy of blood, Theoc.24.18; IG4.620.4 ; Alciphr.3.21

αἱμορραγέω.definition: have a haemorrhage, bleed violently, Hp.Acut.67; there is a violent haemorrhage, Id.Aph.4.27, cf. Sostrat.1, Zopyr.Hist.3:—impers. Hp.Aph.4.74; Id.Epid.1.12

αἱμορραγία.definition: haemorrhage, Hp.Art.69, Aph.7.21; any violent bleeding, ib.5.16; nose-bleeding, Gal.17.50, etc

αἱμορροέω.definition: to lose blood, Hp.Coac.86, 110, Aristobul.32, etc.; to have a LXXLe.15.33, Ev.Matt.9.20

αἱμόστασις.definition: styptic, Androm. ap. prob. in Ps.-Dsc.4.9

αἱμωδιάω.definition: have the teeth set on edge, Hp.Morb.2.55, Diocl.Fr.43, Arist.Pr.886b12, LXXEz.18.4 : c. acc., Hp.Morb.2.73: metaph. of one whose mouth waters, Timocl.11.7

αἰνίζομαι.definition: Dep. only pres., = Il.13.374, Od.8.487:—Act. in AP11.341

αἰνίσσομαι.definition: Act. in late Prose, Philostr.V A6.11; Pass., to be spoken darkly, aor. Pl.Grg.495b: pf. Thgn.681, Ar.Eq.196, Arist.Rh. 1405b4

αἰνόμορος.definition: doomed to a sad end, Il.22.481; of terrible doom, h.Merc.257; deadly, Q.S.9.395; Marcell. SId.14

αἰνοπαθής.definition: suffering dire ills, Od.18.201, A.R.4.1078, AP7.167 ; Anacr.36

αἰνοτόκεια.definition: unhappy in being a mother, Mosch.4.27

αἰνοτόκος.definition: unhappy in being a parent, Opp.H.5.526, IG14.1858:—but Hsch

αἵνω.definition: aor. inf. Hp. ap. Gal.19.103 , Phot.:- sift, winnow, Pherecr.183, cf. Hdn.Gr.2.930; v

αἰολίζω.definition: = metaph., trick out with false; compose in the Aeolian mode, Pratin.Fr.5; speak Aeolic, Dicaearch.3.2, Str.8.1.2, Plu.Cim.1; A.D.Synt.279.52

αἰολοβρόντης.definition: wielder of the flashing thunderbolt, Pi.O.9.42

αἰολόδειρος.definition: with sheeny neck, Ibyc.8, cf. Opp.C.2.317, Nonn.D.12.76,al

αἰολόμητις.definition: full of various wiles, like Hes.Th.511, A.Supp.1036 ; also Hes.Fr.7

αἰολομίτρης.definition: with glittering girdle, Il.5.707; with variegated mitre or turban, Theoc.17.19

αἰολόπωλος.definition: with quick-moving steeds, Il.3.185, h.Ven.137, Theoc.22.34

αἰολόστομος.definition: shifting in speech, of an oracle, A.Pr.661

αἰονάω.definition: moisten, foment, Hp.Nat.Mul.44: fut. BKT3.20: aor. 1 A.Fr.425:—Med., Lyc.1425

αἰπόλιον.definition: herd of goats, Il.11.679; goat-pasture, AP9.101

αἱρεσιάρχης.definition: leader of a school, S.E.P.3.245; Astrol., dominating the 'condition' , Paul.Al.R.3

αἱρετίζω.definition: fut. LXXGe.30.20, choose, Com. ap. Phot.p.54 R., cf. Hp.Ep.17, LXXGe.l.c., Babr.61.5; 1 Ch.28.6; ib.10; adoptive father, IPE2.299 : abs., IG3.74:—Med., LXXPs.118.30, al., Aesop.53, Ctes.Fr.29.9

αἱρετιστής.definition: one who chooses, Plb.22.6.11; partisan, Philem.131, cf. Plb.1.79.9, etc.; founder of a philosophical school, D.L.9.6; Vit.Philonid.p.12 C

αἰρολογέω.definition: clear of darnel, in Pass., IG5.514.15

αἰσθητήριον.definition: organ of sense, Hp.Vict.4.86, Arist.de An.421b32, etc.; opp. Epicur.Ep.1p.12U.; Macho2; the faculties, LXX4 Ma.2.22, cf. Ep.Heb.5.14

αἴσθομαι.definition: sometimes in good Mss. as v.l. for as Th.5.26, Isoc.3.5, Pl.R.608a

ἀϊστόω.definition: fut. Hdt.3.69 : aor. ib.127, contr. :—Med., aor. Orph.A.473:—poet. Verb, not in Il., used by Hdt., and once in Pl., make unseen, make away with, destroy, Od.20.79; . . Pi.P.3.37; A.Pr.234, cf. Pl.Prt.321a; S.Aj.515; I…

αἰσυμνάω.definition: hold office of , GDI3053 , 5632 ; at Naxos, IG12.223

αἰσυμνητεία.definition: office of II.1, = Arist.Pol.1285b25, cf. D.L.1.100

αἰσχόω.definition: = censured by Hdn.Gr.2.933, citing Eup.142; dub. in Epigr.Gr.336

αἰσχροεπέω.definition: use foul language, Ephipp.23: c. acc., Hp.de Arte1

αἰσχροκέρδεια.definition: sordid love of gain, base covetousness, Hp.Decent.2, S.Ant.1056, Lys.12.19, Pl.Lg.754e, Thphr.Char.30

αἰσχροκερδέω.definition: to be sordid, greedy of gain, Hyp.Fr.223

αἰσχροκερδής.definition: sordidly greedy of gain, Hdt.1.187, E.Andr.451, And.4.32 , cf. Pl.R.408c, Arist.EN1122a8, etc. Adv. 1 Ep.Pet.5.2

αἰσχρολογία.definition: foul language, obscenity, X.Lac.5.6; abuse, Plb.8.11.8, cf. POxy.410.77, Ep.Col.3.8, Phld.Rh.1.176S., etc

αἰσχρόμητις.definition: fostering or forming base designs, A.Ag.222

αἰσχροποιέω.definition: act filthily, Ath.8.342c; =; trans., degrade, dishonour, v.l. in Hp.de Arte1

αἰσχροπρεπής.definition: of hideous appearance, Sch.E.Hipp.75; f.l. for Ael.Fr.80

αἰσχρορρημοσύνη.definition: = D.Ep.4.11, Phld. Rh.1.175 S., Oenom. ap. Eus.PE5.32

αἰσχρουργέω.definition: contr. for act obscenely, esp. = masturbari, S.E.P.3.206 :—Pass., D.L.Prooem.5

αἰσχρουργία.definition: shameless conduct, E.Ba.1062: pl; obscenity, Aeschin.2.99, cf. Plu.2.1044b

αἴτησις.definition: request, demand, Hdt.7.32, Antipho5.4, POxy.1024.20 ; Arist.Int.20b22

αἰτητής.definition: one that asks, petitioner, POxy. 788 , D.C.Fr.66.2

αἰτιάζομαι.definition: only in Pass., to be accused, X.HG1.6.5, cf. 12, Anon.Oxy.1012 Fr.14; of a thing, D.C.38.10

αἰτιολογέω.definition: inquire into causes, reason, account for, Epicur.Ep.1p.31U., cf. Diocl.Fr.112, Plot.6.7.3, Plu.2.689b; Aenesid. ap. S.E.P.1.181, cf. Demetr.Lac.1012.68:— Pass., the conjunction indicates that the cause resides in . .,…

αἰτιολογία.definition: a giving the cause of a thing, Democr.118, Aenesid. ap. S.E.P.1.181, Phld.D.1.10, A.D.Conj.231.16; Epicur.Ep.2p.42U

αἰχμαλωσία.definition: captivity, D.S.20.61, LXXAm.1.15, al; body of captives, D.S.17.70, LXXNu.31.12,al

αἰχμαλωτεύω.definition: = sq., LXXGe.34.29, al., Ep.Eph.4.8; capture, Ps.-Callisth.3.20

αἰχμαλωτίζω.definition: take prisoner, D.S.14.37, LXX4 Ki.24.14, al.:—more freq. in Med., J.BJ4.8.1: fut. ib.2.4: aor. ib.1.22.1, D.S.13.24: pf. J.BJ4.9.8 ; also in pass. sense, SIG763

αἰχμαλωτίς.definition: captive, S.Aj.1228, E.Tr.28, LXXGe.31.26. 2. Adj. fem. of S.Aj.71

αἰχμάλωτος.definition: taken by the spear, captive; name of plasters, Aët.15.20

αἰχμοφόρος.definition: spearman, Hdt.1.103,215; esp., like of body-guards, Id.1.8, 7.40, B.10.89

ἀΐω.definition: Ep. and Lyr. word, freq. used by Trag. in; c. gen., listen to, give ear to, Hes.Op.213 ; obey, A.Pers.874, Ar.Nu.1166. [Hom. uses always in pres., so A.Pers.633, S.Ph.1410; but A.Supp.59 , S.OC181, 304: impf. Il.10.53…

αἰωνίζω.definition: to be eternal, Phot., Suid.; to be eternalized, Dam.Pr.105

αἰωνοπολοκράτωρ.definition: eternal ruler of the heavens, PMag.Berol.1.201

αἰώρησις.definition: oscillatory movement, esp. Medic., of passive exercise, Pl.Ti.89a, cf. Gal.10.710; Poll.10.51

ἀκαθαρτίζομαι.definition: to be ceremonially unclean, v.l. ib.14.36

ἀκάθαρτος.definition: uncleansed, foul; morally unclean, impure, Pl.Phd.81b, D.19.199, etc.; thou beast! Bato5; = Achae.30; LXXZa.13.2, Ev.Matt.12.43, cf. PMag.Par.1.1238. Adv. Pl.Ti.92b

ἀκαθυστέρητος.definition: lacking nothing, Vett. Val.67.18, cf. Ps.-Callisth.2.11. Adv. without delay, BGU 1126.11

ἀκαιροπαρρησιαστής.definition: one who employs ill-timed freedom of speech, Id.1857.2

ἀκακοπαθέω.definition: to be free from suffering. EM85.12. Adv. Apollon.Mir.35

ἀκαλαρρείτης.definition: soft-flowing, epith. of Ocean, Il.7.422, Od.19.434

ἀκαλλιέρητος.definition: not accepted by gods, ill-omened, Aeschin.3.131, 152

ἀκαλλώπιστος.definition: unadorned, Heraclit.92, Ph.1.1, Luc.Pisc.12, Gal.Protr.10, Max.Tyr.29.7

ἀκαμαντόπους.definition: gen. untiring of foot, Id.O.3.3; ib.4.1, 5.3

ἀκαμαντοχάρμας.definition: unwearied in fight, Pi.Fr.184, in voc

ἀκαμπής.definition: = Thphr.HP3.10.4, Orph.A.173, etc.: metaph., ib.999, cf. Ph.1.528, Plu.2.959f

ἀκάμπιος.definition: = S.Fr.988:—neut. in chariot or horse-racing, straight course, IG2.966A43, Delph.3.38,al., cf. EM45.3

ἄκαμπτος.definition: unbent, rigid, Hp.Fract.2; metaph., unbending, unflinching, Pi.P.4.72; Id.I.4.53; A.Ch.455 ; Plu.Lyc.11, Cat.Mi.4

ἀκάνθινος.definition: of thorns, Ev.Marc.15.17; metaph., thorny, Anacreont.53.12

ἀκανθολόγος.definition: gathering thorns, nickname of quibblers , AP11.20 , 347

ἀκανθόφυλλος.definition: with spinous leaves, cj. in Thphr.HP1.10.4

ἄκαρπος.definition: without fruit, barren, E.Fr.898.8; metaph., fruitless, unprofitable, B.Fr.7.5; Pl.Phdr.277a; Arist.EN1125a11. Adv. S.OT254

ἀκατάβλητος.definition: not to be thrown down, Sch.E.Hec.1

ἀκαταγγείωτος.definition: not supplied with blood vessels, Antyll. ap.Orib.45.17.8

ἀκαταθύμιος.definition: disagreeable, interp. in Artem.2.48, cf. Just.Nov.53.3.1, Eust.149.28,etc

ἀκατάκλαστος.definition: not to be broken, stubborn, Sch.Od.10.329

ἀκατάληκτος.definition: incessant, Ocell.4.2, cf; acatalectic, in prosody, Heph.4, Aristid. Quint.1.23

ἀκατάληπτος.definition: that cannot be reached or touched; not to be conquered, J.BJ3.7.7; defying suppression, Vett. Val.238.25

ἀκατάλληλος.definition: not fitting together, incongruous, Plb.6.42.3, cf. Arist.Mu.397b31, Arr.Epict.2.11.8; unsuitable, Ruf.Fr.62; inconsequent, Phld.Po.1676.8:—esp. Gramm., ungrammatical, D.H.Dem.27; lacking in concord, A.D.Synt.30.5, al.…

ἀκατάλυτος.definition: indissoluble, perpetual, D.H.10.31, Ep.Heb.7.16; LXX4 Ma.10.11; unimpaired, Jahresh.14 Beibl.135

ἀκαταμάθητος.definition: not learnt or known, Hp.Acut.7,51, Plot.3.9.3

ἀκατανάγκαστος.definition: not compulsory, Diogenian.Epicur.3.61, Porph. ap. Eus.PE5.10

ἀκατανόητος.definition: inconceivable, Ps.-Luc.Philopatr.13, Hsch. s.v. gloss on Sch.Opp.H.4.520. Adv. Suid. s.v

ἀκατάπληκτος.definition: undaunted, Epicur.Fr.37, D.H.1.81, App.BC2.142. Adv. Phld.Mort.39, D.H.1.57, App.BC1.110

ἀκαταπληξία.definition: imperturbability, as the highest good, Nausiph.3; Phld.D.3 Fr.81

ἀκατάπτωτος.definition: not liable to fall, Eustr.in EN311.18

ἀκατασήμαντος.definition: unsealed, unwritten, a commission by word of mouth, Hdn.3.11.9

ἀκατασκεύαστος.definition: not properly prepared, Thphr.HP9.16.6; unwrought, unformed, LXXGe.1.2; chaos, 1 Enoch21.1; unpolished, unartificial, Ps.-Plu.Vit.Hom.218. Adv. D.H.Is.15

ἀκατάσκευος.definition: lacking equipment, PEdgar8.4; in Lit. Crit., without artifice or elaboration, Phld.Rh.1.8S., D.H.Th.27, Philostr.V A6.11; epith. of orator, Plu.2.835b. Adv. Plb.6.4.7

ἀκατασόφιστος.definition: not to be put down by fallacies, Ap.Ty.Ep.44

ἀκαταστασία.definition: instability, anarchy, confusion; unsteadiness, Chrysipp.Stoic.3.121; Plb.7.4.8: pl., Man.5.57

ἀκαταστατέω.definition: to be unstable, Arr.Epict.2.1.12, Heph.Astr.1.1:—Pass., LXXTo.1.15

ἀκαταστέριστος.definition: not arranged in constellations, Ach. Tat.Intr.Arat.40

ἀκατάστροφος.definition: never-ending, Favor. ap. Stob.4.15.29; of a literary period, without conclusion, D.H.Comp.22. Adv. incessantly, Chrysipp.Stoic.2.273

ἀκατάσχετος.definition: not to be checked, Hipparch. ap. Stob.4.44.81, cf. Onos.1.3; D.S.17.38; of persons, uncontrollable, Phld.Piet.86, Apollon.Mir.40, Plu.Mar.44. Adv. D.S.17.34, Plu.Cam.37

ἀκατάτριπτος.definition: inexhaustible, Plb.3.89.9; not wearing out, Gal.UP1.15

ἀκαταφόρητος.definition: not to be borne, Hsch. s.v

ἀκαταφρόνητος.definition: not to be despised, X.Ages.6.8, J.AJ9.11.2, Plu.2.483a, etc. Adv. without negligence, P Lond.1.113.15

ἀκατέργαστος.definition: not cultivated, PTeb.61b32 (ii B; undigested, Arist.PA650a15, Diocl.Fr.43, etc.; indigestible, Xenocr.112, Gal.6.484

ἀκατεύναστος.definition: not put to bed, waking, Hsch., Suid., Phot

ἀκατηγόρητος.definition: not accused, PTeb. 5.47 , Sammelb.343 , D.S.11.46, J.AJ17.11.3, BGU183.8 ; blameless, Phalar.Ep.10

ἀκατονόμαστος.definition: nameless, Epicur.Fr.314, cf. D.H.Comp.21, Archig. ap. Gal.8.592; Ph.1.630, al

ἄκαυστος.definition: unburnt, Hp.Haem.2, X.An.3.5.13; incombustible, Arist.Mete.387a18, Thphr.Lap.4; unquenchable , LXXJb.20.26

ἀκενόδοξος.definition: without vain conceit, M.Ant.1.16. Adv. Sch.Od.3.411:—hence Zonar

ἀκενόσπουδος.definition: shunning vain pursuits, Antip. Tars.Stoic.3.254, Cic.Fam.15.17.4, M.Ant.1.6

ἀκεραιότης.definition: freshness, of troops, Plb.3.73.6; integrity, Just.Edict.7.8Intr

ἀκεραύνωτος.definition: not struck by lightning, Luc.J. Tr.25

ἀκεστής.definition: = Lyc.1052: Phrygian acc. to; menders of torn clothes, X.Cyr.1.6.16 , cf. Alciphr.3.27

ἀκεστορία.definition: the healing art, A.R.2.512, APl.4.272 , Max.314

ἀκεσώδυνος.definition: allaying pain, Paetus ap.Hp.Ep.2, AP9.815, IG14.1015, Men.Rh.p.443 S

ἀκήδεστος.definition: uncared for, Il.6.60; esp. unburied, AP7.686 ; unkempt, Nonn.D.10.272. Adv. without care for others, ruthlessly, Il.22.465, 24.417, cf.AP9.375

ἀκηδής.definition: Pass., uncared for: esp. unburied, Il.24.554; Od.20.130; Od.24.187, cf. 6.26, 19.18.Adv. Suid

ἀκήρατος.definition: undefiled, pure; of persons, undefiled, a virgin, E.Tr.675, Pl.Lg.84cd; E.Or.575: c. dat., untouched by woes, etc., Hipp.1113, HF1314: c. gen., without taint of ill, Hipp.949; free from throes of child-birth, A.R.1.97…

ἀκίνδυνος.definition: free from danger; Adv. E.Rh.588, Antipho2.4.7, etc.; Th.6.80; their departure without danger to us, Id.7.68: Comp. with less danger, Pl.Phd.85d: Sup. X.Mem.2.8.6

ἀκινησία.definition: absence of motion, Arist.Ph.202a5, al.; stagnancy, Hp.Vict.2.37; incapacity to move, Thphr.Fr.11; failure of mobility, Epicur.Nat.908.6; pause, intermission, of the pulse, Gal.8.510, Aret.CA2.3

ἀκινητέω.definition: to be at rest or immovable, Hp.Mul.1.11, cf. Stoic.2.161, Antyll. ap. Orib.8.6.9, S.E.M.7.188; of bones, as opp. joints, Gal.19.460

ἀκίνητος.definition: idle, sluggish, to sit in idleness, Hes.Op.750 ; a sluggish soul, Ar.Ra.899; of the Boeotians, Alex.237; untilled, Plu.2.38c

ἀκκίζομαι.definition: affect ignorance, dissemble, Pl.Grg.497a, Cic.Att.2.19.5, Luc Merc. Cond.14, Jul.Or.7.223b; I will dissemble and talk commonplaces, Men. l.c

ἀκληρέω.definition: to be unfortunate, Telesp.26 H., D.S.3.13, al.: pf. Plb.1.7.4, D.S.27.16

ἀκλήρημα.definition: loss, mishap, Dicaearch.1.25 , Telesp.25H., Agatharch.24, M.Ant.10.33,etc

ἀκληρονόμητος.definition: without heirs, Berl.Sitzb.1880.649 ., BGU868.12 , Eust.533.32:—also PLond.3.905.12

ἀκληρούχητος.definition: not having received a lot, OGI229.102

ἄκλητος.definition: uncalled, unbidden, Asius1, A.Pr.1024, Ch.838, S.Aj.289, Th.1.118, Pl.Smp.174b, Arist.EN1171b21

ἀκμάζω.definition: to be in full bloom, at the prime; of persons, Hdt.2.134, Pl.Prt.335e; X.Mem.4.4.23, Pl.Plt.310d, etc.; of cities and states, Hdt.3.57, 5.28; Arist.Rh.1390b9; = Hyp.Fr.122

ἀκμαστής.definition: = foreg.I.1, Hdn.1.17.11; gymnastic club at Thyatira, IGRom.4.1234, al

ἀκοινωνησία.definition: non-existence of community of; unsociableness, Stob.2.7.25

ἀκοινώνητος.definition: not shared with; not to be communicated, LXXWi.14.21; not to be shared, incommunicable, Ph.2.201; Alex.Aphr.Pr.2.72

ἀκολάκευτος.definition: not liable to flattery; Act., not flattering, Id.31.6; Jul.Or.2.86b; Them.Or.2.27b. Adv. Cic.Att.13.51.1, Ph.1.449

ἀκολασία.definition: licentiousness, intemperance, opp. Hecat.144, Antipho4.1.6, Th.3.37, Pl.Grg.505b, cf. Arist.EN1107b6, etc.: pl., Lys.16.11, Pl.Lg.884

ἀκολασταίνω.definition: fut. Ar.Av.1227, to be licentious, Ar. l.c., Mnesim.4.19, Pl.R.555d, etc

ἀκολάστασμα.definition: = restored by Dobree in Ar.Lys.398 ; is prob. l. for in Anaxandr.73, Alciphr.1.38

ἀκόλαστος.definition: undisciplined, unbridled; esp. incontinent, licentious, S.Fr.744; opp. Pl.Grg.507c, Arist.EN1117b32, al.; Id.HA572a12; 582a26. Adv. Pl.Grg.493c: Comp. X.Mem.2.1.1, cf. Aen.Tact.26.2, dub. in Vett.Val.153.32, 271.12

ἀκολούθησις.definition: following, Arist.Rh.1410a4; sequence in argument, with reference to the fallacia consequentis, Id.APr.52b29, SE181a23

ἀκολουθία.definition: following, attendance, S.Fr.990; sequence, succession, Chrysipp.Stoic.2.266, al.; succession of philosophers, D.L.2.47; in regular succession, Hdn.7.5.2: Lit.Crit., natural sequence of words, D.H.Comp.22, cf. Longin.2…

ἀκόλουθος.definition: following after, c. gen., . . S.OC719; following, consequent upon, in conformity with, c. gen., Ar.Ach.438, cf. Pl.Phd.111c: mostly c. dat., Id.Lg.716c, Ti.88d; D.18.257; Arist.Pol.1321b3; consistent, Demetr.Eloc.153;…

ἀκομιστία.definition: Ep. lack of tending or care, Od.21.284, Them.Or.22.274a, Max.Tyr.34.2

ἀκόμιστος.definition: slovenly, S.Ichn.143; untended, D.L.5.5, Nonn.D.40.174, al

ἀκονάω.definition: metaph., spur, goad on, D.25.46; provoke, Trag.Adesp.423, cf. X.Oec.21.3, Ph.1.469, al., Chor. in Jahrb.9.184; Demad.17:—Pass., Ph.2.178, al

ἀκονητής.definition: one who sharpens, Edict.Diocl.7.33, cf. Hdn.Gr.1.73

ἀκόντιον.definition: Dim. of , javelin, h.Merc.460; in pl., javelin-exercise, Pl.Lg.794c; also in sg., X.Eq.Mag.1.21,25

ἀκοντισμός.definition: = X.Eq.Mag.3.6, Str.11.5.1; of shooting stars, Ptol.Tetr.102

ἀκοντιστής.definition: darter, javelin-man, Il.16.328, Od.18.262, Hdt.8.90, A.Pers.52, Th.3.97, Theoc.17.55, etc

ἀκοντοβόλος.definition: dart-throwing, A.R.2.1000: as Subst. in pl., Agath.3.20

ἀκοπίαστος.definition: untiring, unwearied, Herm. ap. Stob.1.49.44. Adv. Sch.S.Aj.852

ἀκοπίατος.definition: = foreg., Stoic.1.125, cf. IG 2.630b, Vett.Val.263.17, PMag.Par.1.1127; proofs which a writer never tires of repeating, Phld.Mus.p.40 K. Adv. Id.Piet.15, LXXWi.16.20

ἀκόρεστος.definition: Act., not causing surfeit, Id.Ag.1331; X.Smp.8.15

ἀκόρετος.definition: used in Trag. for A.Ag.1117, 1143, S.El.122

ἀκορής.definition: = Them.Or.7.90d, cf. Hsch. : Sup. of a person, S.OC120

ἀκορύφωτος.definition: not to be summed, countless, Hsch.s.v

ἀκοσμέω.definition: to be disorderly, offend, S.Ant.730, Ph.387, Lys.14.13, D.24.92, Hyp.Fr.14, Arist.Ath.3.6; offend in a point, Pl.Lg.764b

ἀκόσμητος.definition: unarranged, Pl.Grg.506e; not organized as a Plot.4.3.9; Dam.Pr.205

ἀκουσείω.definition: Desiderat. of long to hear, S.Fr.991; and in Hsch. the order of words requires for

ἀκουσιάζομαι.definition: in aor. 1 Pass., sin through ignorance, LXXNu.15.28

ἄκουσις.definition: hearing, Arist.de An.426a1. al; in pl., = Plot.4.1.12

ἀκουστήριον.definition: lecture-hall, Gal.Libr.Propr.2; assembly of hearers, audience, Porph.Plot.15

ἀκουστής.definition: hearer, listener, Men.988; auditor, disciple, Scymn.20, Agathem.1.1, Phld.Rh.1.95 S., D.H.Isoc.1, etc

ἀκουτίζω.definition: make to hear, or LXXPs.50.8, Si.45.5

ἀκρατεύομαι.definition: to be incontinent, Arist.EN1145b22; 1152a28: censured by Phryn.406, who quotes however Men.989:—Act. is cj. in Plu. ap. Stob.3.6.53

ἀκρατέω.definition: to be Hp.Mul.1.25, Poll.2.154; Ep.part. Man.4.548

ἀκράτητος.definition: unsubdued, Arist.Mete.384a33: uncontrollable, Hdn.1.8.2. Adv. Orib.Syn.7.47.3; Iamb.VP20.94

ἀκρατίζομαι.definition: drink neat wine; hence, breakfast, because this consisted of bread dipped in wine , Ar.Pl.295, ubi v. Sch., Canthar.8: c. acc., to breakfast on plums, Ar.Fr.607; Aristomen.14: metaph., c. gen., Ph.2.166:—later in Act.…

ἀκράτισμα.definition: a breakfast, Arist.HA564a20, cf. Inscr.Prien.113.54, Ath.1.11d, Plu.2.726c

ἀκρατοποσία.definition: Ion. drinking of neat wine, Hdt.6.84, Hp.Aph.6.31, Satyr.1, Plu.Alex.70

ἀκρατοπότης.definition: Ion. drinker of neat wine, Hdt.6.84, Ael.VH2.41; personified as name of hero, Polem.Hist.40

ἀκρατοφόρος.definition: and vessel for pure wine, elsewh. Cic.Fin.3.4.15, Poll.6.99, 10.70, J.BJ5.13.6

ἀκραχολία.definition: passionateness, burst of passion, Hp.Epid.7.11: later Sopat. ap. Stob.4.5.56, Plu.2.454b

ἀκρέσπερος.definition: on edge of evening , hence, at nightfall, Nic.Th.25 , AP7.633 ; Arist.HA619b21, as cited by Ath.8.353b :—neut. as Adv., Theoc.24.77; but, on approach of evening, Hp.Epid.7.23

ἀκριβάζω.definition: = Aq.Thd.Pr.8.27, cf. Ps.-Callisth.3.20 :— Pass., to be proud, LXXSi.46.15; censured by Poll.5.152

ἀκριβασμός.definition: commandment, LXX3 Ki.11.34: pl., searchings of heart, ib.Jd.5.15 ; portion, gift, Aq.Ge.47.22

ἀκρίβεια.definition: exactness, precision, Hp.VM12, Th.1.22; parsimony, frugality, Plu.Per.16; is scarce, Pl.Lg.844b

ἀκριβεύω.definition: use accurately, Did.ap.Sch.Pi.N.4.3:—in Med., S.E.M.1.71:—Pass., unless I receive precise instructions from you, PAmh.2.154.7

ἀκριβής.definition: exact, accurate, precise, E.El.367; of persons, precise, strict, Th.3.46; Pl.Lg.762d; Lys.7.12; sharp-sighted, Theoc.22.194; of arguments, Ar.Nu.130; E.Supp.906, etc.; = Hp.VM9; Th.6.18: freq.in Adv. to a nicety, prec…

ἀκριβοδίκαιος.definition: precise as to one's rights, of one who strains the law, Arist.EN1138a1; but in good sense, Ph.1.672, al

ἀκριβολογέομαι.definition: to be exact or precise in language, investigation, etc., abs., Pl.R.340e, Cra.415a: c. acc. rei, weigh accurately, Id.R.403d; D.18.21; ib.240:—later in Act., D.H.Dem.26, Alex.Aphr.in Metaph.479.15

ἀκριβολόγος.definition: precise in argument, in pl., Timo25.2

ἀκριβόω.definition: fut. make exact or accurate; investigate accurately, understand thoroughly, E.Hec.1192, cf. X.Cyr.2.2.9; are you sure of . .? Pl.Chrm.156a; inquire carefully of, Ev.Matt.2.7:—Pass., Vett.Val.265.3

ἀκριτόμυθος.definition: confusedly babbling, Il.2.246; hard of discernment, Od.19.560

ἀκριτόφυλλος.definition: of undistinguishable, i.e. closely blending, leafage, Il.2.868

ἀκροάομαι.definition: abs., listen, Hp.Int.35, Ar.Lys.503, Pherecr.154, Lys.19.3; hearer, Eup.94.7; esp. of those who hear lectures, X.Smp.3.6; also, reader, Philostr.VA5.14: c. gen., Str.13.1.54, cf. Plu.Caes.3

ἀκροατήριον.definition: place of audience, Act.Ap.25.23; audience, Id.Cat.Ma.22

ἀκροβολίζομαι.definition: · aor. Hdt.8.64, Th.3.73:—throw from afar, fight with missiles, as opp. to close combat, skirmish, Th.4.34: abs., Id.3.73, X.Cyr.8.8.22: metaph., Hdt.8.64, cf. Ph.1.134:—Act. only AP7.546, Hsch

ἀκροβολισμός.definition: = Th.7.25, X.HG1.3.14, Aen.Tact.39.6, etc.; discharge of weapons by light-armed troops, Arr.Tact.15.4, 37.1

ἀκροβολιστής.definition: mounted bowman or javelineer, Ascl.Tact.7.1, Ael.Tact.2.13, Arr.Tact.4.5

ἀκρόβολος.definition: Pass., struck from afar, A.Th.158; one who throws from afar, skirmisher, IG5.1426.10 , Hsch., Suid

ἀκροβυστία.definition: foreskin, LXXGe.17.11, al., Ph.Fr.49; state of having the foreskin, uncircumcision, Ep.Rom.2.25, etc

ἀκρογωνιαῖος.definition: at the extreme angle, corner foundation-stone, LXXIs.28.16, Ep.Eph.2.20

ἀκροθιγής.definition: touching on surface, touching the lips, AP12.68 : metaph., Vett.Val.40.1. Adv. just dip in, so that it is hardly wetted, Dsc.2.83: metaph., Marin.Procl.26, cf. Vett.Val.271.11, Men.Rh.p.417 S

ἀκροθινιάζομαι.definition: take the spoils, pick out for oneself, E.HF476, cf. Dionys.Trag.1:—Act. in Hsch

ἀκροθίνιον.definition: E.Ph.282, Th.1.132, Pl.Lg.946b; mostly pl. or Pi.N.7.41, al.: acc. GDI2561 D 47 Rüsch : :—topmost or best part of heap; hence, first fruits of the field, booty, etc., offered to the gods, Simon.109, Hdt.1.86, 90, al.,…

ἀκροκνέφαιος.definition: at beginning of night, in twilight, Hes.Op.567:—also of morning twilight, Luc.Lex.11, Id.Rh.Pr.17; cf. Hsch

ἀκρόκομος.definition: with hair on crown, epith. of; with leafy crown, E.Ph.1516; esp. of palms, D.S.2.53, D.P.1010; tapering cypresses, Theoc.22.41

ἀκροκώλιον.definition: mostly pl., extremities of body, esp. of animals, snout, ears, trotters, Hp.Vict.3.75, Pherecr.108.14, Telecl.48, Ar.Fr.4, Archipp.11, Arist.Pr.935b38, etc.: sg., Antiph.126, Alex.118, Eub.7

ἀκρολοφία.definition: mountain ridge, hilly country, Aen.Tact.15.6 , Plb.2.27.5, Str.15.1.29

ἀκρόνυκτος.definition: lit. rising at sunset: hence, in opposition, Vett. Val.168.13; Ptol.Alm.10.6, Tetr.78:—as Subst., with or without opposition, Ptol.Alm.10.7, Tetr.77

ἀκρόνυχος.definition: at nightfall, Arist.Mete.367b26; Thphr.Sign.2; Procl.Hyp.5.66; Theoc.Beren.3, cf. Nic.Th.761:—neut. as Adv., Arist.Pr.942a23. .)

ἀκρόπαστος.definition: sprinkled on the surface: slightly salted, Sopat.13, Xenocr.76

ἀκρόπλοος.definition: contr. swimming at the top, skimming the surface, Hp.Morb.1.14, cf. Plu.2.591e; buoyant, Aret.SA2.11; restored for in Hp.Prorrh.2.11:—superficial, Id.Ep.18

ἀκρόπολις.definition: poet. upper or higher; esp. the Acropolis of Athens, IG1.58, al., And.1.76 ; which served as treasury, Th.2.13; hence to be entered as a state-debtor, D.58.19,48; freq. without Art., as And.l.c., D.ll. cc.; at Erythra…

ἀκροποσθία.definition: Ion. tip of fore skin, Hp.Aph.6.19, Poll.2.171, Ruf.Onom.102, Hsch

ἀκρόπους.definition: extremity of leg, i.e. foot, Ptol.Alm.7.5, al., Pall.in Hp.Fract.12.285C.: pl., PMag.Leid.W.18.37; trotters, Aret.CA1.10

ἀκρόπτερον.definition: quill, AP6.229 ; flanking men of a hunting-party, Opp.C.4.127

ἀκροσίδηρος.definition: pointed or tipped with iron, AP6.95

ἀκρόσοφος.definition: high in wisdom, Pi.O.11 .19, Lyr.Adesp.93, D.H.Dem.51

ἀκροστιχίς.definition: acrostic, D.H.4.62, Cic.Div.2.54.111:— also AP9.385 tit

ἀκροστόλιον.definition: terminal ornament of ship , crowning either the stern-post, Ptol.Alm.8.1; or more commonly, the stem-post, Callix.1, Plu.Demetr.43; taken as trophy, Str.3.4.3, D.S.18.75, Plu.Alc.32, App.Mith.25, Polyaen.4.6.9

ἀκροτελεύτιον.definition: fag-end of anything, esp. of verse or poem, Th.2.17, Phryn.Com.86: generally, Vit.Philonid. p.8 C.:—burden, chorus, D.C.63.10

ἀκροτομέω.definition: lop off corn by the ear, X.Oec.18.2, cf. PLond.2.163.21 ; saw off at end Ph.Bel.67.21:—Pass., Man.4.51: metaph., J.BJ2.10.1

ἀκρότομος.definition: cut off sharp, abrupt, of precipice, Plb.9.27.4, Ph.1.82; LXXPs.113 .8, cf.Jb.28.9, De.8.15: of a stone, sharp, Thd.Ex.4.25; smooth, J.AJ8.3.2; of ends sawn off, Ph.Bel.67.23

ἀκροφύλαξ.definition: governor of a citadel, Plb.5.50.10, BCH33.23 , IG3.3906

ἀκροχειρίζω.definition: take hold of, Aristaenet.1.4; more freq. in Med., struggle at arm's length, opp. spar, Pl.Alc.1.107e, cf. Arist.EN1111a15, Posidon.24, Philostr.Gym.36

ἀκροχειρισμός.definition: wrestling with hands, Luc.Lex.5, Gal.6.324: in pl., Hp.Vict.3.78

ἀκρόχειρον.definition: = hand, Ptol.Alm.7.5, al., Gal.UP2.2; SIG2754.6, cf. Hymn.Id.Dact.13

ἀκροχλίαρος.definition: just warm, lukewarm, Hp.Acut.58:— also Nat.Mul.53, Mul.2.201. Adv. Mul.2.204

ἀκροχορδών.definition: wart with a thin neck, Hp.Aph.3.26, Plu.Fab.1, Dsc.2.64, etc.; distinguished from Paul.Aeg.4.15 Gloss.: hence troubled with warts, D.C.Fr.47

ἀκρόψωλος.definition: only at the end, Suid. s.v

ἀκρωλένιον.definition: elbow of a net, i.e. outer angle of mesh, X.Cyn.2.6, Poll.5.29

ἀκρωμία.definition: point of the shoulder, acromion process, Hp.Art.14: in a horse, withers, X.Eq.1.11, cf. Arist.HA498b30:— Hp.Art.16, Mochl.5, Arist.HA606a16: Alciphr.Fr.5.4

ἀκρώνυχος.definition: with nails, claws, hoofs, etc., tips of fingers, AP12.82; traces of one walking on his toes, Plu.2.317e, cf. Suid

ἀκρώρεια.definition: mountain ridge, X.HG7.2.10, Theoc.25.31, Hp.Ep.10, Timae.94, Plb.24.6.5

ἀκρωτηριάζω.definition: cut off of ships; of persons, cut off hands and feet, mutilate, Plb.5.54.10, etc.; Clearch.8, Plu.Alc.18; D.S.34.8; of circumcision, Ph.2.211; Inscr. on statue, CIG6855:—so in Med., LXX4 Ma.18.20: inetaph., D.18.296; …

ἀκρωτηριασμός.definition: amputation, Dsc.Ther.Praef., Heliod. ap. Orib.47.14 tit,, Philum.Ven.7.7, Leonid. ap.Aët.16.49

ἀκταινόω.definition: lift up, raise, only aor. Anacr.137, Pl.Lg.672c, Pl.Com.180, cf. 19

ἀκτημοσύνη.definition: poverty, Crates Theb. ap. Epiph.Haer.3.2, Poll.3.111, 6.197

ἀκτήμων.definition: gen. without property, poor, in gold, Il.9.126: abs., Theoc.16.33; cf. Plu.Sol.14, Demoph.Sent.16, Alex.Aphr.Pr.1.89

ἀκτινοβολέω.definition: emit rays, Ph.1.638:—Pass; Astrol., of a planet, aspect from the left , Heph.Astr.1.16, Porph.Intr.p.189:—Pass., Vett.Val.116.22

ἀκτινοβολία.definition: shooting of rays, Plu.2.781a; Astrol., aspecting from the left, Thessal. in Cat.Cod. Astr.8.138, Porph.Intr.p.185:—also Man.1.322

ἀκτινοειδής.definition: = Ph.2.559; Horap.1.17. Adv. Gal.19.171, Steph.in Hp.1.144 D., al

ἄκυμος.definition: = foreg., Arist.Pr.931b31 : metaph., E.HF698; Plu.2.1090b; Epicur.Fr.413

ἀκύρωσις.definition: cancelling, D.H.8.21; Phld.Rh.1.276S., cf. BGU 1282.35 , POxy.266.107.5

ἀκύρωτος.definition: verb. Adj., unconfirmed, E.Ion801, PRyl.427 Fr.14

ἀλαβαστρίτης.definition: calcareous alabaster, Thphr.Lap.65, cf. Str.12.8.14, Zos.Alch.p.113 B.:—also Callix.1

ἀλαζονεία.definition: false pretension, imposture, Pl.Grg.525a, D.22.47, etc., cf. Arist.EN1127a13, Thphr.Char.23; Ar.Ra.919: in pl., Id.Eq.290,903, Isoc.12.20; boastfulness, Procop.Pers.1.11 : metaph., their over- readiness to sound, opp.…

ἀλαζόνευμα.definition: imposture, piece of humbug, Aeschin.3.238, cf. Aristid.27.29: in pl., quackeries, Ar.Ach.87, Aeschin.1.178

ἀλαίνω.definition: = wander about, A.Ag.82, E.Tr.1084, El.204,589, Cyc.79: c. acc., Id.Ph.1536.—Always in lyr., exc. Or.532

ἀλαλαγμός.definition: = Hdt.8.37, Plu.2.564b; generally, loud noise, E.Cyc.65, Hel.1352

Ἀλαλκομένιος.definition: or Boeot. month, answering to the Att. IG7.2227, al., Plu.Arist.21

ἀλάμπετος.definition: without light, darksome, h.Hom.32.5; of the nether world, S.OC1662 , cf. Epigr.Gr.264.5 ; ib.149.3 , cf. ib.241.5 Smyrna); AP9.540

ἀλαμπής.definition: = foreg., Simon.37.8; dull, not bright, v.l. in Hp.Prog.2, D.S.3.48; of colour, Arist.Col.793a12; of sound, Orib.50.51.2; out of sun’s light, S.Tr.691; J.BJ1.3.3; Epigr.Gr.431 . 2. metaph., obscure, .. Plu.Phoc.1, cf.…

ἀλαοσκοπιά.definition: Ion. blind man's watch, i.e. careless watch, Il.10.515, 13.10, Od.8.285, Hes.Th.466

ἀλάστορος.definition: under influence of an; epith. of Zeus, avenging, Pherecyd.175 J

ἀλγεσίθυμος.definition: grieving the heart, Orph.H.65, cf. PMag.Lond.121.355

ἀλγηδών.definition: pain, suffering, of body, Hdt.5.18; of mind, pain, grief. S.OC514, E.Med.56, Metrod.7 : pl., Phld.D.1.16, etc

ἄλγημα.definition: pain felt or caused, suffering, S.Ph.340, Hp.VM6, E.Fr.507, Plu.Sull.26, Plot.6.1.19; Men.667

ἀλγύνω.definition: Ion. impf. Q.S.4.416 : fut. S.OT332, etc.: aor. Id.Tr.458, etc.:—Pass., with fut. Med. Id.Ant.230, E.Med.622 : aor. v. infr.—Rare exc. in Trag., Eup.90 , Democr.223, X.Ap.8, and later Prose, as Plu.2.82c :— pain, grie…

ἀλεάζω.definition: to be warm, Arist.Pr.863b22, Resp.472b4; trans., = Gal.19.73, Hsch

ἀλεαίνω.definition: aor. Ael.VH9.30, warm, make; intr., grow warm, be warm, Ar.Ec.540, Arist.PA656a22, Pr.885b27; Men.832

ἄλειμμα.definition: anything used for anointing, unguent, fat, oil, Pl.Ti.50e, Antiph.154, Arist.Pr.884b37, etc.: pl., Hices. ap. Ath.15.689c, Diocl.Fr.141

ἀλειμμάτιον.definition: Dim. of foreg., Diog. ap. D.L.6.52

ἀλειπτήριον.definition: place for anointing in gymnasia, or; paint-brush , Hsch

ἀλειτουργησία.definition: exemption from late word for Att. Str.13.1.2-, IGRom.4.295 , POxy.1.140.10 , Sammelb.4224.15 , etc.; censured as by Poll.8.156:—also Benndorf- Niemann Reise in Lykien p.78

ἀλειτούργητος.definition: free from Decr. Byz. ap. D.18.91; Megasth. ap. D.S.2.40, cf. Din.Fr.89.5, IG22.682.17, POxy.62v ; IG7.2413 : metaph., Epicur.Ep.2p.42U

ἀλεκτορίσκος.definition: Dim. of cockerel, Babr.5.1, Aesop.341.12: as ornament, Roussel Cultes Égyptiens 230

ἀλεκτοροφωνία.definition: cock-crow, i.e. third watch of night, Str.7 Fr.35, Ev.Marc.13.35

ἀλεκτρυών.definition: cock, Thgn.864, etc., cf; or guinea-fowl, Luc.Nav.23

Ἀλεξανδρίζω.definition: to be on Alexander's side, Apolloph. ap. Phylarch.46

Ἀλεξανδριστής.definition: partisan of Alexander, Chares ap. Plu.Alex.24

ἀλέξημα.definition: defence, guard, help, A.Pr.479: c. gen., remedy for, Hp.Mul.2.212; protection against, Gal.UP12.3; Longin.17.2; D.H.7.13, Paus.10.18.3

ἀλεξήνωρ.definition: aiding man, as name of physician, Paus.2.11.6

ἀλεξητήριος.definition: able to keep off, defend, or help; remedy, medicine, Hp.Acut.54; protection, X.Eq.5.6; charm against . ., Thphr.HP7.13.4; Nic.Th.7, IG9.881.3 ; Aristid.Or.48.11

ἀλεξιάρη.definition: she that guards from death and ruin ,Hes.Op.464; wand that served as amulet, Nic.Th.861:— masc. Hsch

ἀλεξίκακος.definition: keeping off ill or mischief, Il.10.20, cf. Hes.Op.123 , Ar.V.1043, Paus.8.41.8; Euph.137; Hierocl.in CA12p.447M.: c.gen., AP6.170 : epith. of Heracles, Luc.Alex.4, etc.; of Hermes, Ar.Pax422; save the mark! Ar.Nu.1372…

ἀλεξίλογος.definition: promoting or supporting discourse, dub. in Critias2.10, cf. AB382

ἀλεξίμβροτος.definition: protecting mortals, Pi.N.8.30; sacred processions which shield men from ill, Id.P.5.91

ἀλεσούριος.definition: a fish, = EM59.52; also a shell-fish, Hsch

ἀλευρομαντεῖον.definition: divination from flour, Oenom. ap. Eus.PE5.25

ἀλευρόμαντις.definition: one that divines from flour, Hsch.; epith. of Apollo, Phot

ἀληθεύω.definition: fut. X.Mem.1.1.5, al.:—speak truth; of things, to be, prove true, Hp.Prog.25:—Pass., to be fulfilled, of conditions, X.Cyr.4.6.10, freq. in Arist.:—Act. of reasoners, arrive at truth, Id.Metaph.1062a25:—Pass., is in a…

ἀληθής.definition: Hom., opp. phrases Il.6.382, Od.13.254, 3.254, 247, al.; in Hdt. and Att. by Trag. crasis Ion. , or by crasis etc.; Hdt.1.14, etc.; 1.120; Th.1.23

ἀληθίζω.definition: dye with genuine purple, PHolm.18.6; Med. = Hdt.1.136, 3.72, Plu.2.230b, Alciphr.3.39, 59

ἀληθινολογία.definition: speaking truth, Pl. ap. Poll.2.124, Plb.12.26D.1

ἀλήθω.definition: = Att. , mostly pres. , Hp.Vict.1.20, Thphr.CP4.12.13, D.S.3.13, AP11.154 , POxy.908.26 ; prob. in Herod.2.20 : aor.part. Pass. Gp.9.19.7

ἀλημοσύνη.definition: wandering about, Man.4.34, D.P.716: in pl., A.R.2.1260 codd., Man.6.226

ἀλητεία.definition: Dor. wandering, roaming; A.Pr.900 ; E.Hel.523 , cf. 934; in later Prose, Vett.Val.4.18, prob. in Ph.1.658

ἀλητήρ.definition: name of a dance in Ithaca and at Sicyon, Aristox.Hist.Fr.50

ἀλθαίνω.definition: heal, Lyc.582, Timae.15: fut. Nic.Th.587: aor. ib.496, Al.112: aor. 2 inf. Hp. ap. Gal.19.76: —Pass., become whole and sound, pres., Hp.Morb.2.33: Ep. impf. or aor. Il.5.417; Q.S.9.475 : fut. Il.8.405: aor. Hp.Art.14:…

ἄλθεξις.definition: healing, cure, Hp.Fract.10, Art.34, cf. Aret.CA2.2:—fut. Med. = SD2.8

ἁλιάετος.definition: poet. sea-eagle, prob. osprey, E.Fr.636, Ar.Av.891, Arist.HA619a4

ἁλιβδύω.definition: expl. by Gramm. as Aeol. for sink or submerge in the sea, Call.Fr.269 : hide, aor. Lyc.351, cf. EM63.13, Hsch

ἁλίβρεκτος.definition: washed by the sea, AP7.501 , Nonn.D.1.96

ἁλίβρωτος.definition: swallowed by the sea, Lyc.760:—also Id.443

ἁλίζω.definition: aor. E.HF412, Hdt.1.77, X.Cyr.1.4.14:—Pass., aor. Emp.41, Hp. , Hdt.1.79: Ion. pf. part. Hdt.4.118, 7.172 : :—gather together, assemble, of military forces, Hdt.1.77,80,al.; collect, of fragments, ib.119, etc.; E.Hera…

ἁλίκτυπος.definition: sea-smitten, of ships, S.Ant.953 , cf. AP6.23, Nonn.D.31.113; also roaring on the sea, E.Hipp.754

ἀλινδέω.definition: later : aor. Ar.Nu.32, and pf. ib.33 :-make to roll. II. Pass., mostly in part., rolling in the dust, like a horse, Plu.2.396e; Nic.Th.156; ib.204; rolled over, overturned, Din.Fr.10; to be twirled, Call.Iamb.1.113. 2…

ἀλινδήθρα.definition: place for horses to roll in, Phryn.PSp.5B.: metaph., of Euripides' tragedies, Ar.Ra.904

ἁλίπαστος.definition: sprinkled with salt, Aristomen.6, Eub.7.10, Archestr.Fr.57.4B

ἁλίπληκτος.definition: Dor. sea-beaten, of islands, Pi.P.4.14, v.l. in S.Aj.597

ἁλιπόρφυρος.definition: of sea-purple, of true purple dye, Od.6.53, 13.108; Arion1.18 codd.; Alcm.26.4; Him.Or.16.2

ἁλίρροθος.definition: = foreg.; pathways of the roaring sea, A.Pers.367, cf.S.Aj.412 ; E.Hipp.1205, Mosch.2.132

ἁλίσμηκτος.definition: washed by the sea, Lyc.994: Hsch. has · Suid

ἁλιστέφανος.definition: sea-crowned, sea-girt, h.Ap.410; Alex. Lychn. ap. St.Byz.s.v. Nonn.D.40.521

ἀλιτήριος.definition: sinning or offending against; abs., guilty, D.19.197, Lys.13.79, And.1.130; . . Eup.146b, cf.96, Men.563

ἀλιτραίνω.definition: Ep. for , abs., sin, offend, or Hes.Op.243 ; AP9.763 ; Tryph.269

ἀλιτρόνοος.definition: wicked-minded, Maiist.56, Orac. ap. Eus.PE14.20, Epigr.Gr.1052

ἁλίτροφος.definition: sea-nurtured, i. e. fishes, Opp.H.1.76, cf. Nonn.D.5.182, al

ἁλίφλοιος.definition: sea-bark oak, Quercus Pseudosuber, Thphr.HP3.8.5, Sch.Theoc.9.20

ἀλκάζω.definition: put forth strength or prowess, EM56.11, 66.10:—Med., Hsch

ἀλλαντοποιός.definition: maker of sausages, Hsch.Mil.7 A 3, D.L.2.60

ἀλληγορέω.definition: interpret allegorically, Plu.2.363d, cf. 996b, Heraclit.All.1 :-Pass., to be spoken allegorically, Ep.Gal.4.24 ; Sch.S.Aj.186. 2. abs., speak figuratively or metaphorically, Demetr.Eloc.151,285; speak allegorically, J…

ἀλληγορία.definition: allegory, veiled language; figurative, metaphorical language, Demetr.Eloc.99, Cic.Orat.27.94, Quint.Inst.8.6.44 ; Phld.Rh.1.174 S., cf. 164 S

ἀλλήγορος.definition: allegorical, Et.Gud.515.42. Adv. allegorically, Anon. ap. Sch.A.Pr.428

ἀλληλεγγύη.definition: mutual security, PFlor.368.10 , POxy.918 ii 15 , etc.; PCair.67126.18

ἀλληλίζω.definition: lie together, sens. obsc., AB383 :—also and Hsch

ἀλληλοβόρος.definition: in pl., devouring one another, Hsch. s.v

ἀλληλοκτονέω.definition: slay each other, Hp.Ep.17, Arist.Fr.344, Ph.2.38

ἀλληλοκτόνος.definition: of things, producing mutual slaughter, Moschio Trag.6; D.H.2.24

ἀλληλοπάθεια.definition: Astrol., subjection to mutual influence, Vett. Val.5.13

ἀλληλοτυπία.definition: mutual impact, of atoms, Placit.1.12.6: pl., Ph.2.489

ἀλληλουχέω.definition: hold together, intr., Ph.1.464, 2.417 :—Pass., Nicom.Ar.1.2 ; Iamb.in Nic.p.7.13 P., cf.Simp.in Ph.711.16, Syrian.in Metaph.150.1, Dam.Pr.206

ἀλληλουχία.definition: holding together, conjunction, Longin.36.4; coherence,Epicur.Nat.2.993.5; continuity, opp. Theol.Ar.4 ; Procl.Inst.97, cf. Dam.Pr.85 ; close texture, consistency, Gal.14.12 ; Dsc.5.127 ; mutual support, of words in co…

ἀλληλοφαγία.definition: an eating one another, Hdt.3.25, Pl.Epin.975a, Athenio1, etc

ἀλληλοφονία.definition: Dor. mutual slaughter, Pi.O.2.42, Philipp. Perg. in IG4.1153 , Them.Or.6.74b, Herm. ap. Stob.1.49.44

ἀλλογενής.definition: of another race, OGI598, LXXGe.17.27, al., Ev.Luc.17.18, Agath.4.5, Ps.-Callisth.3.26

ἀλλόγλωσσος.definition: using a strange tongue, Hdt.2.154, SIG1.4 , IG12.328.20 , LXXBa.4.15

ἀλλοδημία.definition: Dor. = stay in foreign land, Hp.Int.48 ; abroad, Pl.Lg.954e; Phld.Mort.26 : pl., Iamb.VP35.252. II. concrete, foreign people, B.17.37, cf.Poll.9.21

ἀλλοεθνής.definition: of foreign nation, D.S.2.37, Nic.Dam.p.94 D., J.AJ15.11.5 ; with foreign foe, D.H.5.5, cf. LXX3 Ma.4.6

ἀλλόθροος.definition: contr. speaking a strange tongue, Od.1.183, 3.302, 15.453: generally, foreign, Hdt.1.78 ; Id.3.11 ; A.Ag.1200 ; strange, alien, S.Tr.844.—Not in Att.Prose

ἀλλοιοπροσωπέω.definition: to be separated from another planet by a distance differing from that between their two domiciles, Vett.Val.65.8

ἀλλοίωσις.definition: difference, Pl.R.454c; alteration; confusion of mind, Plb.3.81.5

ἀλλόκοτος.definition: of unusual nature or form, strange, portentous, Hp.Fract.1, Ar.V.71, Crates Com.43, etc.; unwelcome, against the grain, Th.3.49; strange, uncouth word, Pl.Tht.182a: c. gen., with purpose utterly different from . . , S…

ἀλλομορφέω.definition: disguise oneself, Ps.-Callisth.1.3; change one's shape, Sm.Ez.31.15

ἀλλοπρόσαλλος.definition: simply, transferred, coupled with Tryph.565; deceitful, Nonn.D.46.4, al.; changeful, successive, of waves, etc. , ib.3.24, al., cf. Man.5.68

ἀλλοτριάζω.definition: to be ill-disposed, Plb.15.22.1: c. gen., towards . . , ib.25.34

ἀλλοτριόγνωμος.definition: thinking of other things, absent, Cratin.154

ἀλλοτριοεπίσκοπος.definition: busybody in other men's matters, 1 Ep.Pet.4.15

ἀλλοτριομορφοδίαιτος.definition: ever changing in form, epith. of nature, Orph.H.10.23

ἀλλοτριονομέω.definition: assign things to their wrong place; adopt foreign customs, D.C.52.36

ἀλλοτριοπραγέω.definition: meddle with other folk's business: excite commotions, Plb.5.41.8; opp. Procl.in R.2.149 K

ἀλλοτριοπραγία.definition: meddling with other folk's business, Plu.2.57d, Procl.in R.1.216K

ἀλλότροπος.definition: strange, Linus ap.Stob.1.10.5; Iamb.VP25.114. Adv. Sch.E.Hec.299

ἀλλοφάσσω.definition: to be delirious, Hp.Prog.20, al., cf. Gal.18.249, prob. l. in Aret.SA2.4.—Ionic word, cf. Xenocrit. ap. Erot.Fr.1, Eust.1324.10

ἀλλοφροσύνη.definition: absence or derangement of mind, Poll.8.163

ἀλλοφυλέω.definition: adopt foreign customs or religions, LXX4 Ma.18.5

ἀλλοφυλισμός.definition: adoption of foreign customs, LXX2 Ma.4.13

ἀλλόφωνος.definition: speaking a foreign tongue, LXXEz.3.6, Hsch. s.v

ἁλμαία.definition: = brine, Ar.Fr.706, Nic.Fr.70.18: in pl., Dsc.2.174

ἁλμίζομαι.definition: to be made salt, Sch.Il.2.538, cf. Zos.Alch.p.248B

ἀλογιστέω.definition: lose one's senses, rave, Plu.2.656d, Longin.10.3, Vett. Val.130.30

ἀλογιστία.definition: Ion. thoughtlessness, Democr.289, Plb.5.15.3, Chrysipp.Stoic.3.129, Phld.Ir.p.93 W., Plu.2.466c

ἀλογοθέτητος.definition: of which no account is given, Gloss

ἀλοητός.definition: threshing, Ael.NA6.43; threshing-time, LXXLe.26.5, BGU1031.11 : perh. payment for threshing, PTeb.48.17

ἁμαξήλατος.definition: traversed by wagons: carriage-road, Aen.Tact.16.14, Poll.9.37, cf. Str.6.3.7

ἀμελετησία.definition: want of practice, negligence, Pl.Tht.153b; Id.Phdr.275a, cf. Eus.Mynd.Fr.33, Ph.1.548, etc

ἀμερσίνοος.definition: depriving of mind, maddening, Nonn.D.1.388, prob. in Ps.-Dsc.4.78

ἀμπελόπρασον.definition: wild leek, Allium Ampeloprasum, Dsc.2.150, Did. ap. Ath.9.371f

ἀμπελουργέω.definition: fut. Philostr.Im.2.17; work in or; metaph., strip, plunder, D.ap.Aeschin.3.166

ἀμφαγαπάω.definition: Ep. = foreg., aor. h.Cer.439; Hes.Op.58; Orac. ap. D.S.8 Fr.21

ἀμφάγνυμαι.definition: to be broken around, prob. l. in J.BJ4.10.5

ἀμφιγυιόω.definition: mutilate, or impale, Hsch., cf. EM89.17

ἀμφιδηριάομαι.definition: Dep., fight about, Semon.7.118: c. dat., Lyc.1437

ἀμφιδοκεύω.definition: lie in wait for, BionFr.9.6; guard, Orph.A.925

ἀμφιδύω.definition: put on, Sch.Ar.Th.1053:—Med., put on oneself, S.Tr.605

ἀμφίεσμα.definition: garment: pl., wraps, clothes, Hp.Mul.2.133, Pl.Grg.523d, R.381a; in anatomy, of membranes, Gal.2.554, al

ἀμφιέτηρος.definition: celebrated in yearly festivals, epith. of Dionysus, Orph.H.52.10

ἀμφιετίζομαι.definition: Pass., return yearly, of festivals, Hsch.,EM90.27:—also Cratin.2D

ἀμφιθαλής.definition: lit. blooming on both sides; flourishing on all sides, Poll.1.239: metaph., all-abounding, of gods, A.Ch.394; Ar.Av.1737 ; of a man, IG14.1863: metaph., abounding in . . , A.Ag.1144

ἀμφιθάλλω.definition: pf. to be in full bloom, AP9.231 , 12.96

ἀμφιθρύπτομαι.definition: to be broken up, dub. l. Aret.SD2.4

ἀμφιθρῴσκω.definition: in aor. part. leap around, Eumel.9

ἀμφικαίνυμαι.definition: in plpf. Pass. to be adorned with, Q.S.10.179, cf. 188

ἀμφίκειμαι.definition: Pass., lie round or upon, Pi.Fr.92; locked in each other's arms, S.OC1620; . . slaughter is heaped on slaughter, Ant.1292

ἀμφίκλυστος.definition: washed on both sides by waves, of a promontory, S.Tr.752, cf. 780; Str.11.4.2; App.BC5.72

ἀμφικρέμαμαι.definition: Pass., hang round, Pi.I.2.43, cf. O.7.24

Ἀμφικτυονεύω.definition: to be a member of the Amphictyonic Council, IG7.106 , SIG58 :— Pass., to be subject to the Amphictyony, Gött.Gel.Anz.1913.175

Ἀμφικτυονία.definition: or Amphictyonic League, D.5.19,11.4, cf. Did.in D.4.6; IG4.589 ; of the League of Calauria, a third share in the representation of Locri in the Amphictyony, Klio 16.163

Ἀμφικτυονίς.definition: name of Demeter at Anthela, Hdt.7.200

ἀμφικυκλόομαι.definition: Pass., encircle, surround, A.Pers.458.—Act. in Agath.3.6

ἀμφικυλίνδω.definition: aor roll about, round, or on, Pi.N.8.23

ἀμφικυρτόομαι.definition: Pass., to be gibbous, of the moon, Man.6.575

ἀμφίκυρτος.definition: convex on each side, like the moon in; doubly convex, of a curvilinear angle, opp. Procl.in Euc.Def.8 p.127F., al.; Gal.2.673; Ph.Bel.70.23

ἀμφιλάφεια.definition: or wealth, abundance, Cic.QF2.14.3, Gp.2.8.1, Hsch.,AB389

ἀμφιλαφής.definition: thickly grown, thick, Call.Cer.27, cf. Ael.NA7.6; also of hair, Philostr.Jun.Im.8, etc.; Nonn.D.5.153

ἀμφιλογέομαι.definition: Dep., dispute, doubt, Plu.Lys.22.—Act. in J.AJ8.1.4, Hsch

ἀμφιλογία.definition: Ep. dispute, doubt, Hes.Th.229; Plu.Comp.Arist.Cat.4, Ages.28, cf. App.Hann.46

ἀμφιμερίζομαι.definition: Pass., to be completely parted, AP9.662

ἀμφιμήτριος.definition: round the womb, concerning; ship's bilge, = Artem.4.30, Poll.1.87

ἀμφιμίγνυμι.definition: mix up well, aor. 2 Pass. Orph.Fr.238.12

ἀμφιπαρίσταμαι.definition: stand about and beside, Epic. ap. Afric.Cest.Oxy.412.42

ἀμφιπατάσσω.definition: strike on or from all sides, AP9.643

ἀμφιπεριπλάσσω.definition: aor. spread allround, of a drug, Hp. Steril.22

ἀμφιπεριστείνομαι.definition: Pass., to be pressed, crowded on all sides, Call.Del.179

ἀμφιπεριφρίσσω.definition: bristle all round, all over, Opp.H.4.54

ἀμφιπήγνυμαι.definition: Pass., to be fixed around, aor. 2 Opp.H.1.297; to be pierced by, 241

ἀμφιπλέκω.definition: aor. 2 part.Pass. Orph.A.881:—twine round, E.Fr.369 ; of musician, Telest.2.4; embrace, Opp.H.4.158; so in Pass., Orph.l.c

ἀμφίπλευρος.definition: with traverses on both sides, Ph.Bel.81.30

ἀμφιπολέω.definition: later form of mostly in pres; attend on, watch, guard, Id.O.12.2, cf. Theoc.1.124; Pi.N.8.6; busy oneself with, B.Fr.7.3

ἀμφίπρυμνος.definition: with two sterns, i.e. with rudder behind and before, S.Fr.131, cf.Milet.7p.60, D.C.74.11, Agath.3.21: metaph., two-edged, E.ap.Phot.p.103 R

ἀμφιρρήγνυμι.definition: rend all in pieces, aor. 2 Pass. Q.S.1.39

ἀμφισβασίη.definition: Ion. for come to controversy with one, Hdt.4.14; Id.8.81, cf. Inscr.Prien.37.129

ἀμφισβητέω.definition: abs., disagree, dispute, wrangle, Id.4.14, etc.: And.1.27, Isoc.4.19, Pl.Prt.337a; Antipho3.4.3: 3.1.1; the parties, in a law-suit, Arist.Rh.1354a31

ἀμφισβητήσιμος.definition: disputable, Antipho3.1.1, etc.; debatable ground, X.HG3.5.3, D.7.43, Hell.Oxy. 13.3, Theopomp. ap. Phot.p.104 R.; disputed property, Pl.Lg.954c; Arist.Rh.1362b29; doubtful, Pl.Smp.175e; . . Arist.Metaph.996b27; D.18.139

ἀμφισβήτησις.definition: dispute, controversy; as Att. law-term, claim to an inheritance, Lys.17.5, cf Is.6.4, D.48.26

ἀμφισμίλη.definition: and prob. ff. ll. for , Gal.2.574, 581

ἀμφιστέλλομαι.definition: Med., fold round oneself, deck oneself in, Theoc.2.74

ἀμφιστεφανόομαι.definition: Pass., . . the assembly stood all round, h.Ven.120

ἀμφιστεφής.definition: placed round like a crown, Il.11.40; brim-full, Hsch., Suid. s.v

ἀμφιστρεφής.definition: turning all ways, of a dragon's three heads, Il.11.40 :—also Diotog. ap. Stob.4.7.62

ἀμφισφάλλω.definition: treat a dislocated joint by circumduction, Hp.Art.2:—Pass., Id.Mochl.5

ἀμφιταλαντεύω.definition: cause to weigh evenly on both sides, Nonn.D.1.183, cf. 6.110

ἀμφιταράσσομαι.definition: Pass., to be troubled all round, Simon.51

ἀμφιτείνομαι.definition: Pass., to be spread round or over, Opp.H.1.163

ἀμφιτέμνω.definition: Ion. cut off on all sides, intercept and surround, in tmesi, Il.18.528; clear away, AP7.281 , IG4.823.49 ; pare all round, AP5.227

ἀμφιτιμάομαι.definition: to be disputed, of an assessment or estimate, BCH 37.184

ἀμφιτρέχω.definition: run round, surround, Archil.40; Pi.P.3.39; Semon.7.89

ἀμφιφέρομαι.definition: Pass., to be borne round, revolve, in impf., Q.S.5.10

ἀμφιφράζομαι.definition: Med., consider on all sides, consider well, Il.18.254

ἀμφιχαράσσω.definition: scratch, incise around, PMag.Par.1.2845; lance all round, Marcell.SId.89; of stars, mark the course of, Man.2.66

ἀμφιχορεύω.definition: dance around, abs., Critias19 , AP9.83 : c. dat., Opp.C.1.27

ἀμφιχρίομαι.definition: Med., anoint oneself all over, Od.6.219

ἀμφοδάρχης.definition: officer commanding troops levied in a ward, Ph.Bel.93.8: also a civil official, OGI483.82 , Wilcken Chrest.61

ἀμφοδέω.definition: miss, fail to meet, Rev.Egypt.1.208, Hsch. s.v. cf

ἀμφοτερόβλεπτος.definition: looking on both sides, circumspect, Timo59

ἀμφοτερόγλωσσος.definition: speaking both ways, double- tongued, of Zeno the inventor of dialectic, Id.45, cf.Eust.1440.35

ἀμφοτεροδύναμος.definition: with power for good or ill, of Zeus, Eust.1363.29

ἀμφοτερόπλοος.definition: money lent on bottomry, when the lender bore the risk of the outward and homeward voyage, D.34.6, etc.; Ael.Ep.18; opp. q.v

ἀναβαθμός.definition: flight of steps, stair, Hdt.2.125, Arist.Oec.1347a5, D.C.65.21; by degrees, Ph.2.557

ἀναβάθρα.definition: = sq., CIG4436b; flight of steps, Str.7.2.3

ἀναβακχεύω.definition: rouse to Bacchic frenzy, madden, E.HF1086; intr., break forth in Bacchic frenzy, Id.Ba.864, Plu.Crass.33, Lib.Or.40.23

ἀναβαστάζω.definition: raise or lift up, carry, J.AJ19.3.1, Luc.Anach.24

ἀναβάτης.definition: poet. one who mounts, one; fire-brand, Sch.Ar.Ach.321

ἀναβιβάζω.definition: fut. Ph.Bel.97.43 : aor; draw a ship up on land, Id.HG1.1.2

ἀναβιβρώσκω.definition: aor. gnaw through, Nic.Th.134: aor. Pass. to be corroded, Philostr.Im.2.17; to be eroded, of ulcers, Gal.8.392

ἀναβιόω.definition: Arist.Mir.832b6 is the common pres.): aor. 2 , Luc.Hist.Conscr.40; later aor. 1 Arist.HA587a24, Thphr.HP4.14.12: also aor. Med. Lib.Or.12.50: pf. E.ap. Phot.p.107 R., Luc.Nec.1:—come to life again, Ar.Ra.177; And.1.12…

ἀναβίωσις.definition: return to life, LXX2 Ma.7.9, Plu.Luc.18, App.Gall.1.3, etc

ἀναβιώσκομαι.definition: causal of bring back to life, Pl.Cri.48c: aor. inf. Phd.89b: fut. Ael.NA2.29: later in Act., Them.Or.8.115c, Sch.E.Alc.1; Act. only interpol. in Polyaen.6.38.2

ἀναβλαστάνω.definition: fut. v.l. in Hdt.3.62: aor; trans., put forth, Ph.1.304, cf. 1.118; Eun.Hist.p.235D

ἀναβλέπω.definition: c. acc., look up at, E. l. c.: c. dat., Ion1467; Supp.322 codd

ἀνάβλησις.definition: putting off, delay, Il.2.380; 24.655; Call.Ap.45: abs., AP12.184

ἀναβλύζω.definition: poet. AP9.374, Orph.A.1130: fut; intr., gush forth, Arist.Mu. l. c., IG14.889 , Heliod. ap. Orib.46.11.9, etc.; Theoc.17.80

ἀναβλυστάνω.definition: = Str.Chr.16.22, Procop.Aed.2.3, al.:— also Sch.Pl.Ti.22e: or Eup.105, cf. Eust.1095.8, EM200.52

ἀναβλύω.definition: Ep. impf. A.R.3.223, = boil over, Hp.Mul.1.78; gush out, Plb.34.9.7, Str.3.5.7, Nonn.D.48.878 A.R. l. c.: c. acc. cogn., spout out, Nonn.D.9.31, 6.255:—spurt foam from the mouth, Hp.Morb.Sacr.7

ἀναβόησις.definition: shouting, calling, D.H.9.10; invocation, Sch.S.OT80; Paul. Aeg.3.13

ἀναβοθρεύω.definition: dig up, force up, AB389, Suid., Hsch

ἀναβολάδιον.definition: Dim. of I.2, mantle, Aq.Is.61.3, POxy.109, Isid.Etym.19.25.7:—also Sm.Is.3.22, Edict.Diocl.26.78,93

ἀναβολεύς.definition: groom who helps one to mount; stirrup, Eust.1406.5, Suid

ἀναβρασμός.definition: prop. boiling up; hence kind of earthquake, Suid. s.v. metaph., 'réchauffé', rehash, Olymp.in Mete.230.11

ἀνάβραστος.definition: boiled, Ar.Ra.553, Aristomen.8; Pherecr.130.10, cf. 108.23; Dsc.3.83

ἀναβρέχομαι.definition: Pass., become wet again, v.l. Arist.Pr.927b6

ἀναβροχισμός.definition: extraction of eye-lashes by a loop, an operation for trichiasis, Paul.Aeg.6.13, cf. Gal.15.918:— 14.784

ἀναβρύω.definition: = Ael.VH3.43, f.l. in Ph.1.477: c. acc., Nonn.D.7.346

ἀνάβρωσις.definition: corrosion or erosion, Sor.2.40, Gal.1.154,239, Antyll. ap. Orib.44.32.11

ἀναγαργαρίζω.definition: gargle, Hp.Morb.2.26,27, Aff.4:— so also in Med., Mul.2.185, IG4.955.30 , Archig. ap. Gal.12.976

ἀναγελάω.definition: laugh loud, X.Cyr.5.1.9, Plu.Arat.6, Philostr.VA5.7; at one, X.Cyr.6.1.34

ἀναγκάζω.definition: c. acc. pers. only, constrain a person, E.Andr.337; esp. by argument, opp. Pl.Grg.472b; I was constrained, tortured, S.El.221, cf. X.Hier.9.2; under compulsion, Th.6.22, 8.99; And.1.2; D.18.19

ἀναγκαίη.definition: Ep. and Ion, for Il.6.85, Tyrt.6, Sol.36.8, Hdt.1.11, etc

ἀναγκαῖον.definition: place of constraint, prison, X.HG5.4.8; = Artem.1.45, Eust.1968.39, Cat.Cod.Astr.8.133

ἀναγκαῖος.definition: in Att. also Th.1.2; Act., constraining, applying force, a word of force, Od.17.399; urgent necessity, Il.8.57; day of constraint, i.e. life of slavery, 16.836; a doom imposed by fate, or fateful chance, S.Aj.485, cf.…

ἀναγκοθέτησις.definition: compulsion, coined by Oenom. ap. Eus.PE6.7 as a parody on

ἀναγκόσιτος.definition: eating perforce, i. e. getting what one can, epith. of parasites, Crates Com.44, Nicostr.Com.32

ἀναγκοφαγέω.definition: = Arr.Epict.3.15.3, Philostr.VS2.17: metaph., stomach, Theopomp.Hist.282, Philostr.Gym.44

ἀναγκοφαγία.definition: strict diet, of athletes, Arist.Pol.1339a6, Them.Or.15.185d

ἀναγκοφορέω.definition: bear on compulsion, apptly. f.l. for D.H.10.16

ἀνάγλυφος.definition: wrought in low relief, Ps.Callisth.3.28; AP3 tit.: LXX3 Ki.6.18

ἀναγλύφω.definition: aor. carve in relief, Keil- Premerstein Dritter Bericht No.37 , J.AJ12.2.9, Gal.UP16.11: plpf. Pass. J.AJ12.2.10

ἄναγνος.definition: unclean, unholy, defiled, A.Ag.220, Ch.994, S.OT823; Antipho2.1.10; Ph.1.156. Adv. Id.1.2, Poll.1.32

ἀναγνωρίζω.definition: recognize, Pl.Plt.258a, Prm.127a; in a tragedy, recognize or come to the knowledge of a person or thing, so as to produce a dénouement, Arist.Po.1452a36, al

ἀναγνώρισις.definition: recognition, Pl.Tht.193c; in Tragedy, recognition, as leading to the dénouement , Arist.Po.1452a29, 1454b19

ἀνάγνωσις.definition: recognition, Hdt.1.116; reading, Pl.Euthd.279e, Arist.Po.1462a17 , Rh.1414a18, etc.: pl., Aristeas283

ἀναγνώστης.definition: reader, slave trained to read; secretary, Inscr.Prien.111.194; Inscr.Cos238

ἀναγόρευσις.definition: public proclamation, Decr. ap. D.18.118; freq. in Inscrr., as GDI3502.4 : = Lat. renuntiatio, Plu.Marc.4, etc

ἀναγόρευτος.definition: not to be spoken or told, Sch.S.Tr.1093

ἀναγραμματίζω.definition: write the letters of a name in direct; transpose the letters of one word so as to form another, Eust.46.2, 488.12 ; e. g

ἀναγραμματισμός.definition: transposition of this kind, Artem.4.23, Sch.Lyc.p.5 S., Eust.45 fin

ἀναγράφω.definition: contr. IG7.8, Tab.Heracl.1.126: (v; of a person, register or record his name, Isoc.16.9:—Pass., to be inscribed or entered in a public register, Hdt.6.14, cf. 8.90; to be registered as a benefactor, as was the custom …

ἀναγχιππέω.definition: to be forced to serve as knight, Eup.394:—Subst. Phot.p.109 R

ἀνάγωγος.definition: ill-bred, Timo51 , Plu.2.147f; Phld.Vit.p.27 J.; D.S.34/5.2.35; tasteless, Longin.34.2; D.H.Orat.Vett.1; unlearned, Plb.12.25.6; dissolute, Plu.2.140b; of horses and dogs, ill-broken, unmanageable, X.Mem.3.3.4, 4.1.3:…

ἀναγώνιστος.definition: without contest or conflict, Th.4.92 ; never having contended for a prize, X.Cyr.1.5.10; failing in the race of virtue, Pl.Lg.845c

ἀναδάκνω.definition: stimulate, of salt applied to roots, Thphr.CP3.17.4; Xenocr.25: generally, irritate, Ruf. ap. Orib.8.39.3, Hippiatr.33; Dsc.5.136

ἀναδασμός.definition: redistribution, partition of land, among colonists, Hdt.4.159, 163; as a revolutionary measure, freq. coupled with Pl.R.566a, D.17.15, Jusj. ap. eund.24.149, SIG526.22

ἀναδατέομαι.definition: divide anew, redistribute, Th.5.4:—Pass., to be distributed, Orac. ap. Hdt.4.159: aor. Plu.Agis8

ἀνάδειγμα.definition: image for show, Hsch; mouthpiece worn by public criers to serve the purpose of a speaking-trumpet, Epigr. ap. Poll.4.92, Hsch

ἀναδείκνυμι.definition: also Plu.2.417e: Ion. aor; notify, esp. proclaim any one as elected to office, Plb.4.48.3; make him the greatest man, 22.4.3; Ev.Luc.10.1:—Pass., SIG630.23

ἀναδενδρομαλάχη.definition: hollyhock, Alcea rosea, Gal.10.960, Orib.14.38.13, cf. 15.1.4

ἀναδεσμεύω.definition: tie up, suspend, D.S.18.42, cf. Mnesith.Cyz. ap. Orib.inc.15.16:—also Gp.4.7.3, cf. Sch.A.Pers.191: metaph., of religious scruples or taboos, Lyd.Ost.16

ἀναδίδωμι.definition: poet. fut. etc.:—give up; deliver, Plb.29.10.7, D.S.11.45, cf. IG14.830; OGI437.78

ἀνάδικος.definition: 343 B2), tried over again, And.1.88, Pl.Lg.937d, cf. D.40.39, etc.; render subject to appeal, Id.24.191

ἀναδινέω.definition: intr., of the eyes, roll, Hp.Mul.1.36:—also and Hsch

ἀναδιπλόω.definition: double, fold, Sor.1.84:—Pass., to be made; Gramm., of a word or syllable, reduplicate, Phryn.PSp.32 B.:—Pass., TryphoFr.21, cf. EM98.38

ἀναδίπλωσις.definition: repetition, duplication, Ph.2.56, Phlp.in Mete.103.37; esp. in Rhet. , Demetr.Eloc.66, al., Alex Fig.2.2, etc

ἀνάδοσις.definition: sending up, presentation of names, POxy.82.2; distribution, Posidon.17; J.Ap.2.39

ἀνάδοχος.definition: taking upon oneself, giving security; as Subst., security, surety, D.H.6.84, Plu.Dio18; PGrenf.1.1; Phalar.Ep.22,38

ἀναδύομαι.definition: shrink back, withdraw, Od.9.377; Il.7.217; hesitate, shirk, Ar.Ra.860, cf. Lys.16.15, X.Smp.5.2, D.8.50, 19.210, Men.Epit.205; of rivers, fail, Plu.Thes.15

ἀνάζεσις.definition: boiling up, of fire, Arist.Mir.833a22, Sch.Il.Oxy.221 xiv 18

ἀναζεύγνυμι.definition: and yoke or harness again; abs., break up, shift one's quarters, mostly in part., Th.8.108, cf. X.An.3.4.37, Ph.Bel.103.15; Plu.Pomp.42; march through . . , Id.Ant.84; Chron.Lind.D.43

ἀναζήτησις.definition: investigation, Pl.Criti.110a: search for, Memn.41; inspection, in pl., Just.Nov.26.4Intr

ἀναζυγόω.definition: push back the bolt , unbolt, Ar.Fr.654; open, unfasten a casket, Hsch

ἀναζωγραφέω.definition: paint completely, delineate, Str.8.3.30; picture to oneself, Ph.2.59, Arr.Epict.2.18.16, S.E.M.7.222:—Pass., to be painted on, Ph.2.591; to be represented, Diog.Oen.7

ἀναζωγράφημα.definition: memory-image, Peripatetic word, Alex.Aphr.de An.60.6, al

ἀναζωόω.definition: recall to life, Ph.1.643, cf. Sch.E.Med.9, Aq.Ho.6.2, Sm.Ps.29.4, al

ἀναζώωσις.definition: recalling to life, Eustr.in EN71.25, Sch.E.Or.288

ἀναθάλπω.definition: warm again, cherish, Anacreont.31.21, J.AJ17.6.5, Plu.2.600b

ἀναθαρσέω.definition: Att. regain courage, Ar.Eq.806, Th.6.63, 7.71; at a thing, Id.6.31; Plu.Alex.31

ἀναθάρσησις.definition: Att. recovery of courage, Onos.14.1, Eust.1267.22

ἀναθεματίζω.definition: devote to evil, LXXNu.21.2, Jo.6.20; intr., curse and swear, Ev.Marc.14.71

ἀναθεματισμός.definition: a cursing, Just.Nov.42.1.1: pl., Cod.Just.1.3.38, Just.Nov.146.1.2

ἀναθερίζω.definition: reap again, Ph.2.390; glean, Hsch. s.v

ἀναθερμαίνω.definition: warm up, heat again, AP11.55:—Pass., become warm again, Hp.Epid.1.2, cf. Arist.HA569b11: Hp.Prog.17

ἀναθεώρησις.definition: close examination, D.S.13.35; attention attracted by an event, magnam res habet Cic.Att.14.5.1, cf. ib.9.19.1, 14.6.2

ἀναθορυβέω.definition: cry out loudly, commonly in applause, Pl.Prt.334c, cf. X.An.5.1.3; ib.6.1.30, cf. Pl.Smp.198a: abs., Euthd.276b

ἀναθρηνέω.definition: lift up one's voice in wailing, D.C.74.13, Sch.E.Or.1335

ἀναθρύπτομαι.definition: indulge in affectation, pf. inf. Pass. Poll.6.185

ἀναθυάω.definition: to be again at heat, of swine, Arist.HA546a28, 573b8; prov., Diogenian.4.10, cf. Phot.p.118 R., and prob. in Pherecr.35

ἀναιρέτης.definition: destroyer, murderer, Sch.Ar.Pl.1147; Astrol., Anareta, a planet cutting short human life, Balbill.inCat.Cod. Astr.8.236

ἀναισθησία.definition: lack of sensation, Pl.Ti.74e; mental obtuseness, D.22.64

ἀναισθητέω.definition: lack perception, D.18.221; to be without sense of weariness, J.AJ11.5.8; BJ4.3.10: abs., Epicur.Ep.1p.21U., Sor.2.49, prob. in Porph.Abst.1.39

ἀναίσθητος.definition: without sense or feeling; without perception or common sense, wanting tact, stupid, Th.6.86; those blockheads . . , D.18.43, cf. Phld.Rh.1.215S.: = Th.1.69. Adv. Phld.Rh.1.227S

ἀναισιμόω.definition: impf. : aor. subj. : pf. v.l. in X.Cyr.2.2.15:—Pass., aor. pf. up, use, spend, consume, . . he used up the earth, Hdt.1.185; 3.150:—Pass., 2.60; 1.72, cf. 2.11, 5.53: often to be used for a purpose, or spent upon a th…

ἀναισχύντημα.definition: impudent act or speech, Hyp.Fr.226, Gal.UP10.9

ἀναισχυντία.definition: shamelessness, impudence, Ar.Th.702, D.20.166, etc.; Pl.Smp.192a

ἀναιωρέω.definition: lift up, . . . . Coluth.155: plpf. Pass. Nonn.D.16.342

ἀνακαγχάζω.definition: burst out laughing, Hp.Ep.17; Pl.Euthd.300d; R.337a

ἀνακαθαίρω.definition: clear out, clear completely; Med., clear or sweep away, Pl.Mx.241d ; Plb.10.30.8; Plu.Alex.17

ἀνακάθαρμα.definition: rubbish, lumber, dub. in Hsch. s.v

ἀνακαθίζω.definition: set up: whence Med., sit up; intr., sit up, Hp.Prog.3, Aen.Tact.27.8; Theol.Ar.48; of a hare listening, X.Cyn.5.7

ἀνακαινίζω.definition: renew, Plu.Marc.6, cf. App.Mith.37: Hsch.Mil.4.33; revive legend, Str.2.1.9: metaph., Ep.Hebr.6.6:—Pass., Isoc.7.8; Just.Nov.111.1

ἀνακαινόω.definition: in Pass., to be renewed, 2 Ep.Cor.4.16, Col.3.10:—in Med., renew, Heliod.in EN221.13

ἀνακαλπάζω.definition: trot, gallop , A.Fr.145 A, S.Fr.1007, Ar.Fr.48 D., Pl.Com.25 D.; prob. in Ar.Th.1174

ἀνακαλύπτω.definition: Dor. uncover, IG4.952.62; remove a covering, Arist.Sens.444b25, cf. 2 Ep.Cor.3.14

ἀνακάπτω.definition: gulp down, Hdt.2.93, Ar.Av.579, Arist.HA541a13, al
