ἀνάκειμαι.definition: poet. serving as Pass. to; to be set up as a statue in public, D.19.251, cf. IG14.1389i8; Theoc.10.33, cf. Lycurg.51

ἀνακέομαι.definition: repair, IG11.203A56 ; cf. make good, Ael.NA5.19; D.C.52.37

ἀνακεράννυμι.definition: and mix up or again, Od.3.390; Ar.Ra.511: metaph., Plu.Cat.Mi.25; D.H.1.60:—Pass., Pl.Criti.121a: aor. Id.Ti.87a, part. Plu.Rom.29

ἀνακεφαλαιόομαι.definition: sum up the argument, of an orator, D.H.Lys.9; Arist.Fr.133:—Pass., to be summed up, Ep.Rom.13.9

ἀνακηρύσσω.definition: Att. proclaim by voice of; c. acc. pers., proclaim as conqueror, Ar.Pl.585:—Pass., Hdt.6.103, cf. Th.5.50; of slaves, GDI3600

ἀνακινδυνεύω.definition: run a further risk, D.C.41.25, 42.1 ; generally, run risks, c. inf., Hdt.8.100: c. dat., c. part., Id.9.26

ἀνακινέω.definition: stir up, awaken, S.Tr.1259; of cocks or quails, stir them up , Pl.Lg.789c; Plu.Luc.5; Pomp.16:—Pass., Pl.Men.85c, cf. Pherecyd.102 J

ἀνακίρναμαι.definition: as Pass., tempered by . . , Pl.Ax.371d: mingle with, Iamb.in Nic.p.73 P.:—Act., Ph.1.284, part. 1.153:—Pass., Id.Fr.74 H. , cf. Alex.Trall.1.13

ἀνακλάζω.definition: aor. 2 E.IA1062, Call.Hec.1.1.10: aor. 1 Ael.NA12.33:—cry aloud, scream out, E.l.c.; of a dog, bark, bay, X.Cyr.1.4.15; of geese, cackle, Ael. l. c

ἀνακλαίω.definition: Att. fut. Telecl.1; c. acc., weep for, Hdt.3.14: so in Med., . . S.Ph.939; Antipho2.4.1

ἀνάκλασις.definition: a bending back, flexure; reflection of light or reverberation of sound, Arist.AP0.98a29, Sens.437b10, al., Stoic.2.199; so of the wind, Arist.Pr.945a7; of water, have its course turned, Plb.4.43.9; make it elastic, Ar…

ἀνακλασμός.definition: = foreg. I, Heliod. ap.Orib.46.12.1; in metre, overlapping, cf. II.2, Sch.Heph.12

ἀνακλέπτω.definition: steal, prob. l. in h.Merc.515, cf. GDI1586 , Theoc.5.9:—Pass., steal away, retire, Hsch

ἀνάκλητος.definition: called back to service, Lat. evocatus, D.C.45.12; Id.55.24, 78.5

ἀνακλιντήριον.definition: head-rest of a couch, Erot. s.v. Poll.6.9; condemned by Phryn.130

ἀνάκλιτος.definition: for reclining, Hp.Superf.8, Aret.CA1.4; = Plu.Rom.26; Ps.-Callisth.3.22

ἀνακλύζω.definition: fut. wash up against, A.R.2.551; abs., boil as with waves, Plu.2.590f:—causal, stir up, Sch.Nic.Al.165

ἀνακλώθω.definition: of the Fates, undo the thread of one's life, change one's destiny, Luc.Hist.Conscr.38; IG 14.1188

ἀνακναδάλλω.definition: excite by scratching, of quails, Poll.7.136, 9.108, Hsch

ἀνακογχυλιασμός.definition: gargling, Ath.5.187a, Antyll. ap.Orib.5.28.3; and , gargle, Pl.Com.196

ἀνακογχυλίζω.definition: = Eup.275, Ruf. ap. Aët.2.92, Poll.6.25, Gal.11.769

ἀνακοινέω.definition: = sq., only in Med. imper. Thgn.73

ἀνακοιρανέω.definition: rule or command in a place, Posidipp. ap. Ath.7.318d

ἀνακολλάω.definition: glue on or to, glue together, Dsc.2.133:—Pass., Lyd.Mag.2.13

ἀνακόλλησις.definition: sticking up or out of in-growing eyelashes with an adhesive, Gal.6.627, Dsc.1.71

ἀνακολουθία.definition: Rhet., inconsequence, esp. employed with humorous effect, Demetr.Eloc.153; generally, Demetr.Lac.Herc.1012.63, Corn.Rh.p.368 H., Diogenian.Epicur.3.26

ἀνακόλουθος.definition: inconsequent, Epicur.Ep.2p.41U; Gramm., anomalous, of inflexions, A.D.Pron.66.1, al.; also of changed constructions, D.H.Th.41,42. Adv. Id.Rh.8.13, Sch.Il.2.469, EM722.2

ἀνακολυμβάω.definition: come up after diving: trans., bring up from the bottom, Thphr.HP4.6.5:—Pass., Hsch

ἀνακομβόομαι.definition: gird oneself up for action, Gp.10.83.1

ἀνακομίζω.definition: poet. carry up, X.HG2.3.20:—; bring back, recover, v.l. in X.Mem.2.10.1:—Med. , bring or take back or away with one, Hdt.5.85, Th.6.7:—Pass., to be brought back, Hdt.3.129, etc.; and of persons, return, come or go bac…

ἀνακοσμέω.definition: adorn anew, restore, IGRom.4.468.14 , v.l. in Aristid.Or.26.98

ἀνακουφίζω.definition: lift or raise up, S.Fr.23; E.Or.218; of a horseman mounting, X.Eq.7.2; of the ship of state, S.OT23; Arist.Pr.939a35:—Pass., feel lightened or lifted up, E.Hipp.1392; to be relieved in mind, X.HG5.2.28

ἀνακρήμνημι.definition: = shore up, J.BJ5.11.4; undermine, App.Mith.75:—also prob. in J.BJ2.17.8, AJ7.10.2

ἀνακρίνω.definition: examine closely, interrogate, esp; inquire into, Antipho2.3.2; Phld.Po.994 Fr.21, cf. Lib.p.21 O.:—Med., what remedy there shall be, Pi.P.4.63

ἀνακροτέω.definition: lift up and strike together, Ar.Pl.739; Aeschin.2.226; Plu.Mar.44: abs., applauded vehemently, Ar.Eq.651, V.1314, cf. J.AJ12.4.9, Alciphr.1.39: aor. part. cj. in Hexam. ap. Diogenian.3.67

ἀνακτάομαι.definition: refresh, revive, Id.3.60.7, 87.3; D.H.2.42; . . Dsc.3.31; J.AJ9.6.4, Arr.Epict.3.25.4, etc

ἀνάκτησις.definition: regaining, Hierocl.in CA24p.474M., Herm. ap. Stob.1.41.44, Dam.Pr.75; PTeb.378.12; a recovery of strength, etc., Thphr.Fr.166, Porph.Marc.4, f.l. in Hp.VM4

ἀνακτίζω.definition: rebuild, Str.9.2.5, D.Chr.2.79: fut. prob. l. for in App.Anth.6.75:—Pass., CIG8646 , al

ἀνακυκάω.definition: stir up and mix, mix up, , Ar.Ach.671, Pl.302, cf. Thphr.CP6.1.5: metaph., Ph.1.690

ἀνακυκλέω.definition: turn round again, E.Or.231; intr. in Act., come round in a circle, Arist.GC338a4; Id.Mete.339b29:—so in Pass., Pl.Ti.37a; Arist.EN1100b3

ἀνακυκλόω.definition: = v.l. in AP9.342 , in Pass.—The Act. perh. in Jul.Ep.180p.394c

ἀνακύκλωσις.definition: = Ptol.Tetr.87; wheeling about, Hdn.4.2.9; cycle of constitutions, Plb.6.9.10

ἀνακυλίω.definition: roll up, Luc.Luct.8, cf. D.H.Comp.20; overturn, Plu.2.304f: metaph., Alex.116.7; roll away or back, Ev.Marc.16.4

ἀνακύπτω.definition: come up out of the water, pop up, Ar.Ra.1063; Pl.Phd.109d; opp. Id.Tht.171d, cf. Phdr.249c

ἀνακωδωνίζω.definition: try by the sound, ring, Ar.Fr.303

ἀναλαλάζω.definition: raise a war-cry, X.An.4.3.19; E.Ph.1395: generally, cry aloud, Id.Supp.719

ἀναλαμβάνω.definition: fut. Ion. pf.inf.Pass; suspend in a sling, Hp.Art.22

ἀναλάμπω.definition: flame up, take fire, X.Cyr.5.1.16; shine out; metaph., break out, as war, Plu.Sull.6, cf. 7

ἀναλδήσκω.definition: grow up, A.R.3.1363; spring up afresh, Opp.C.2.397

ἀναλειψία.definition: neglect of anointing, Sm.Ps.108.24; lack of oil, CPR57.16

ἀνάλημμα.definition: that which is used for repairing; any high erection or embankment, esp. of substructures or retaining-walls, SIG2587.20, SIG290 , 813A5 , IG11.163A38 , cf. 165.33, D.S.17.71: pl., Id.20.36, D.H.3.69, IG4.203.21; LXX2 …

ἀναληπτήρ.definition: bucket, J.AJ8.3.7; ladle or bowl, LXX2 Ch.4.16

ἀναληπτρίς.definition: suspensory bandage, Gal.18.323; analemptris, = prob.l. in Ov.AA3.273

ἀνάληψις.definition: receiving back into a family, Luc.Abd.5; acquirement of knowledge, etc., Phld.Rh.1.31 S., al., Ti.Locr. l.c., S.E.P.1.73, D.S.1.1; Plu.2.351e

ἀναλίσκω.definition: metaph., hast wasted words, S.Aj.1049, cf. E.Med.325; Pl.R.369e; Th.2.64; Pl.Mx.247b; waste time in sleep, Pi.P.9.27; diem eximere dicendo, Plu.Aem.30

ἄναλκις.definition: acc. Il.8.153, etc., but Od.3.375, A.Ag.1224: :—without strength, impotent, feeble, of unwarlike men, Il.2.201, cf. 9.35; 8.153, 14.126; of the suitors, Od.4.334; of Aegisthus, 3.310, cf. A.Ag.1224; of Aphrodite, Il.5…

ἀναλογίζομαι.definition: reckon up, sum up; foll. by a Conjunction, . . calculate or reflect that, Th.8.83, X.HG2.4.23, etc.; take into account, Phld.Herc.1251.5

ἀναλογισμός.definition: reconsideration, Th.3.36; reckoning; according to proportionate reckoning, Docum. ap. D.18.106; S.E.P.1.147

ἀναλωμάτιον.definition: Dim. of foreg., slight loss; trifling expenditure, PFlor.131.3

ἀναμανθάνω.definition: inquire closely, Hdt.9.101; learn afresh, Hsch.; simply, learn, D.S.34.17, Ph.1.406

ἀναμαντεύομαι.definition: take the auspices a second time; unmake a prophecy, Phryn.PSp.45B

ἀναμαρμαίρω.definition: move quickly, of a smith's bellows, A.R.3.1300

ἀναμάρτητος.definition: making no mistake, unerring; in moral sense, blameless, Hp.Fract.16 , cf. Antipho3.2.10, Men.Epit.487, Phld. Sto.Herc.339.17; sinless, Ev.Jo.8.7, cf. Aristeas252, Muson.Fr.2p.6H.; a faultless form of government, Arist…

ἀναμαστεύω.definition: · Hsch.; make a search , Men.Prot.p.131 D

ἀναμείγνυμι.definition: join company, D.54.8; have social intercourse, Plu.Num.20

ἀναμέτρησις.definition: measurement, Str.1.1.20; estimate, Plu.Sol.27, cf. Hierocl.in CA19 p.461M

ἀναμετρητής.definition: official in charge of land-survey, Wilcken Chrest.229.3

ἀναμηλόω.definition: examine with a probe, h.Merc.41 , Hsch

ἀναμηρυκάομαι.definition: or chew the cud, Ath.9.390f, Luc.Gall.8

ἀναμηρύομαι.definition: wind up, draw back, as a thread, Plu.2.978d

ἀναμίσγω.definition: poet. and Ion. for Od.10.235; Tim.Fr.7:—Med., have intercourse with, Hdt.1.199:—Pass., Call.Aet.Fr.7.3 P

ἀναμισθόομαι.definition: Dor. Pass., to be let anew, Tab.Heracl.1.111

ἀναμίσθωσις.definition: renewal of lease, re-letting, LW483 , BGU1122.32

ἀνάμνησις.definition: calling to mind; memorial sacrifice, LXXNu.10.10, cf. Ev.Luc.22.19

ἀναμοχλεύω.definition: raise by a lever, force open the gates, E.Med.1317; Luc.Cont.4: metaph. of dislocated limbs, Gal.18 .403

ἀναμύω.definition: open the eyes, opp. AB391, Hsch

ἄνανδρος.definition: = husbandless, of virgins and widows, A.Supp.287, Pers.289 , S.OT1506, etc., and in Prose, as Hp.Mul.1.4, Pl.Lg.930c

ἀνανεάζω.definition: become young or new again, Ar.Ra.592, LXX4 Ma.7.14, Sm.Jb.29.20, Phyrn.PSp.59B., Suid. s.v. Corn.ND33

ἀνανεόομαι.definition: fut. Plb.22.7.1, al.: aor; revive them, prob. for S.Tr.396, cf. E.Hel.722, Plb.5.36.7.—Act. freq. in LXX,Jb.33.24, al., IG14.1078a, Delph.3 No.60, cf. SIG478.503 , Dam.Pr.391:—Pass., Ep.Eph.4.23

ἀνανέωσις.definition: revival of a suspended ceremony or office, OGI764.25 , POxy.1252v16

ἀνανήχομαι.definition: = swim, Arist.Resp.475b1; swim up-stream, Opp.H.1.120:—Act. form Hsch.; cf. , Id

ἀνανταπόδοσις.definition: suppressed apodosis in a conditional sentence, Anon.Figp.157 S

ἀνανταπόδοτος.definition: without apodosis: hypothetical proposition wanting the consequent clause, Sch.Ar.Pl.469

ἀναντίβλεπτος.definition: what one dares not face, Plu.2.67b: metaph., irrefragable, Procl.in Alc.p.201 C

ἀναντίθετος.definition: not to be contradicted, Olymp.in; without contrary or opposite, Dam.Pr.26, Anon.in Cat.23.21

ἀναντίλεκτος.definition: undisputed, PHib.95.13; incontestable, Cic.QF 2.8.1, Luc.Eun.13; not to be opposed J.AJ19.1.4. Adv. Aen.Tact.31.9, Str.13.3.6, Luc.Cal.6

ἀναντίρρητος.definition: not to be opposed, Plb.6.7.7, 28.13.4; undeniable, Act.Ap.19.36; S.E.M.8.160. Adv. without opposition, by consent, Plb.22.8.11; incontrovertibly, OGI335.138 , Aët.15.15; without gainsaying, Act.Ap.10.29

ἀναξαίνω.definition: tear open, Babr.12.24, Antyll. ap. Orib.44.23.4, Them.Or.7.98c; Phld.Ir.p.60 W. :—Pass., of evils, break out afresh, Plb.27.7.6; Plu.2.610d, cf. Dem.17: but of those whose appetite is stimulated afresh, Alciphr.Fr.6.18

ἀναξηρασμός.definition: drying up, Sor.2.10, Leonid. ap. Aët.16.44, Herod.Med.inRh.Mus.58.90

ἀναξίαλος.definition: lord of the sea, epith. of Poseidon, B.19.8

ἀναξιβρέντας.definition: lord of the thunder, epith. of Zeus, Id.16.66; cf

ἀναξίμολπος.definition: queen of song, epith. of Urania, B.6.10

ἀναξιοπάθεια.definition: unworthy treatment, or rather, just indignation thereat, J.AJ15.2.7, Hp.Ep.17

ἀναξιοπαθέω.definition: to be indignant at unworthy treatment, Str.8.4.7 , D.H.4.11, J.AJ15.3.2

ἀναξιόπιστος.definition: unworthy of credit, Eudem. ap. Simp.in Ph.115.35, Alex.Aphr.in Metaph.317.15

ἀνάπαιστος.definition: hammered, forged; struck back, rebounding: —as Subst., anapaest , D.H.Comp.25, Heph.8, etc.; dactyl, Aristid.Quint.1.15

ἀναπαλαίω.definition: retrieve by contest, J.BJ4.1.6; retract, Sch.Od.8.567

ἀναπαλινδρομέω.definition: to be brought back again to the same spot, of a bandage, Hp.Fract.4

ἀνάπαυλα.definition: c. gen. rei, rest from a thing, S.El.873, cf. Ph.878; Th.2.38; Pl.Phlb.30e

ἀναπαύσιμος.definition: of or for rest, Eust.1260.53, al

ἀνάπαυσις.definition: poet. repose, rest; c. gen. rei, rest from a thing, Th.4.20; X.Hier.2.11; Epicur.Ep.3p.61U.; PFlor.57.56

ἀναπείθω.definition: persuade, convince; persuade, move to do a thing, c. acc. pers. et inf., Hdt.1.124,156, etc.; foll. by Conj., . . Id.1.123; . . 1.37: c. dupl. acc., persuade one of a thing, Ar.Nu.77, cf. AP9.438

ἀνάπειρα.definition: trial, proof, Plb.25.4.8, cf; in pl., exercises, Plb.1.59.12

ἀναπειράομαι.definition: try or attempt again: generally, make a trial, essay, Plb.25.4.9; make trial of a new ship, prove her, D.51.5; also of the ship herself, ibid.; esp. as a naval term, manœuvre, exercise, Hdt.6.12, Th.7.7,12,51

ἀναπεμπάζομαι.definition: count again, count over, Pl.Ly.222e; think over, ponder over, Id.Lg.724b, Plu.2.605a, Ath.6.263b, al.; Aret.CA2.3, etc.:—Act. later in same sense, Lyc.9, 1470, AP11.382.12 , Hld.3.5, etc

ἀναπέμπω.definition: poet. send up, A.Ch.382; send up to higher ground, Id.Cyr.7.5.34; esp. from the coast inland, into Central Asia, Th.2.67, cf. Isoc.8.98; to the metropolis, Plb.1.7.12, etc

ἀναπέτομαι.definition: poet. IG14.1934f, late; metaph., to be on the wing, S.Aj.693; Id.Ant.1307.—Cf

ἀναπηρόομαι.definition: Pass., to be maimed, Pl.Plt.310e, Arist.Pr.960b37:—Act., prob. l. in Plu.2.373d

ἀνάπηρος.definition: maimed, mutilated, Hermipp.35, Lys.24.13, Pl.Cri.53a, etc.; Id.R.535d; Id.Alc.2.149a, cf. Arist.PA773a13, al. Adv. Zonar

ἀναπίεσμα.definition: a kind of trap-door on the stage, Poll.4.127, 132

ἀναπιεσμός.definition: = foreg., HeroSpir.1.28; reduction of hernia, Heliod. ap. Orib.50.42.6

ἀναπίμπρημι.definition: blow, swell up, in Pass., Nic.Th.179: aor. Hp.Nat.Mul.41

ἀναπιπράσκω.definition: sell again, Poll.7.12:—Pass. in aor. 1 part. IPE12.32A53

ἀναπίπτω.definition: poet. fall back, A.Ag.1599; metaph., fall back, give ground, Th.1.70; flag, lose heart, D.19.224; D.H.5.53

ἀναπλάσσω.definition: Att. form anew, remodel; simply, model, mould, fashion, . . Ar.Nu.995, cf. AP7.410 , al.; Pl.Alc.1.121d: metaph., Demad.11; make up, Dsc.1.8, al

ἀναπληρόω.definition: fill up a void, Pl.Ti.81b, cf. 78d; make up, supply, Pl.Smp.188e; Arist.Pol.1318b22; . . compensates them, Id.Fr.101:—Med., fill their houses, E.Hel.907

ἀναπλήρωσις.definition: filling up, means of filling up; satisfying, Arist.Pol.1267b4; satisfaction of the wants and appetites, Id.EN1173b8

ἀναπνοή.definition: poet. recovery of breath; respiration, breathing, Pi.P.3.57, Ar.Nu.627, Pl.Ti.33c, etc.; including and Arist.Resp.471a7; = breathe, live, S.Aj.416; strangle, Plu.Rom.27; in a breath, Plb.10.47.9

ἀναπόβλητος.definition: not capable of being lost, S.E.P.3.238, cf. Cleanth.Stoic.1.129, Alex.Aphr.Quaest.121.16

ἀναπόγραφος.definition: not registered in the custom-house books, contraband, Poll.9.31; unregistered mines, Hyp.Eux.34; not registered in the census, PLond.2.260.29 ; BGU338ii6

ἀναπόδεικτος.definition: not proved, undemonstrated; of first principles, indemonstrable, Pl.Def.415b, Arist.APr.53b2, 57b33, al.; of syllogisms, Chrysipp.Stoic.2.79, al. Adv. S.E.P.1.173, Gal.17.160

ἀναπόδοτος.definition: not given back, not returned; = Sch.Ar.Av.7, cf. Simp.in Ph.45.11

ἀναπόδραστος.definition: unavoidable, not to be escaped; Act., unable to run away, AB392, Alb.Intr.6

ἀναποιέω.definition: make up, prepare a medicine, Hp.Nat.Mul.36; make fresh, vamp up, Sch.Ar.Pl.1063

ἀναπόλαυστος.definition: not to be enjoyed, Plu.2.829d; Act., not enjoying, Phld.Mort.13; Heph.Astr.1.1, Hsch

ἀναπολέω.definition: poet. properly, turn up the ground again : hence, go over again, repeat, Pi.N.7.104; S.Ph.1238; Pl.Phlb.34b, cf. Vett.Val.242.20:—aor. 1 Pass., J.AJ13.5.8

ἀναπόλησις.definition: repetition, A.D.Synt.29.10, al., Plot.2.9.12; reconsideration, recalling to mind, Id.4.6.3, Hierocl.in CA19p.461M

ἀναπολόγητος.definition: inexcusable, Plb.12.21.10, Ep.Rom.1.20, 2.1; undefended, D.Chr.2.39, cf. Eun.VSp.489 B.; without making a defence, D.H.7.46

ἀναπόμπιμος.definition: sent back, Luc.Luct.10, D.C.62.2; of; of trials, referred to a higher court, Luc.Eun.12, D.C.52.33, etc

ἀναπομπός.definition: one that sends up or back, epith. of; distributor of bread to soldiers, POxy.1115.2

ἀναπόρριφος.definition: not liable to be rejected, free from blemish, PLond.2.282.13 , etc

ἀναπόσπαστος.definition: inseparable, Dam.Pr.113. Adv. Simp.in Epict.p.6 D

ἀναπόστρεπτος.definition: not to be turned away, Sm.Jb.9.13

ἀναπότευκτος.definition: unerring in its aim, Arr.Epict.2.8.29; of persons, 1.4.11, al. Adv., Comp. 4.6.26

ἀναποφέρω.definition: bring back again, in aor. 1 Med. PCair.Preis.32.12

ἀναπράσσω.definition: Att. contr. exact, levy money or debts, Th.8.107, Lys.16.6; IG9. 694.58 ; demand back, of loans already repaid, OGI669.20 ; exact the fulfilment of a promise, Th.2.95, cf. Ar.Av.1621; distrain upon, SIG554.16 :—Med., …

ἀναπτερόω.definition: prop. raise its feathers, of a bird: hence; metaph., set on the wing, put on the tiptoe of expectation, excite, Hdt.2.115, cf. Pl.Phdr.255c; . . E.Or.876; Id.Supp.89, cf. S.Fr.355; Ar.Av.1449, cf. Men.Epit.510: —Pass.…

ἀναπτέρωσις.definition: clamour, clamorous words, LXXSi.31.1, cf. Pr.7.11

ἀναπτερύσσομαι.definition: to be furnished with wings, Sch.Ar.Eq.1341

ἀναπτοέω.definition: poet. scare exceedingly, Mosch.2.23, Opp.C.1.107, etc.:—Pass., to be scared, Plu.Pel.16; to be in great excitement, Id.2.261a, etc

ἀνάπτυξις.definition: opening, gaping; explanation, Id.Rh.Al.1435b18, cf. Plu.2.382d, Ath.1.1a

ἀναπτύσσω.definition: pf. inf. Pass. E.El.357: aor; cut open, of freshly killed animals, Pherecyd.97 J., Philum.Ven.17.3, PMag.Leid.V.10.1, etc

ἀναπτυχή.definition: = . . oh wide expanse of heaven! E.Ion1445; S.Fr.956; the sun's unclouded orb, E.Hipp.601; El.868

ἀναπτύω.definition: spit up or out, Hp.Aph.5.13; Plb.12.13.11: abs., sputter, Nic.Al.211; . . S.Ant.1009:—Pass., Gal.16.210

ἀναπυνθάνομαι.definition: inquire closely into; abs., discover by inquiry, Hdt.5.57; also, learn by inquiry, X.An.5.7.1 codd.; Pl.Hp.Mi.363b; ask of a person, Ar.Pax693

ἀναπωλέω.definition: put up for sale again, PPetr.3p.109 ; sell again, Poll.7.12:—Pass., prob. in CIG2266.11

ἀναράομαι.definition: recall a curse, Callisth. ap. Suid., Poll.5.130

ἀνάργυρος.definition: without silver: without money; not bought with silver: incorruptible, Poll.6.191

ἀναρίθμητος.definition: not to be counted, countless; unregarded, E.Ion837, Hel.1679

ἀναριστέω.definition: take no breakfast, v.l. in Hp.Acut.28

ἀναρίστητος.definition: not having breakfasted, Eup.68, Ar.Fr.454, Gal.15.562

ἀναρμοστέω.definition: not to fit or suit, Pl.R.462a; Id.Sph.253a; of musical instruments, to be out of tune, Id.Grg.482b

ἀναρμοστία.definition: discord, of musical sounds, Id.Phd.03c, 03e, al.: metaph., Dam.Pr.341

ἀνάρμοστος.definition: not fitting, of dress, X.Mem.3.10.13; unfitted, unprepared, Th.7.67

ἀναρραΐζω.definition: recover from a bad illness, Poll.3.108, Hsch

ἀναρριχάομαι.definition: impf. Ar.Pax70, Aristaenet.1.20: fut. Poll.5.82: aor. D.C.43.21:—in Suid. and EM the augm. tenses are written cf. clamber up with the hands and feet, scramble up, Hellanic.197 J.; Ar.l. c.; also in late Prose, Philost…

ἀναρροθιάζω.definition: dash up, of the sea, dub. cj. in Eup.324

ἀναρροπία.definition: motion upwards, Hp.Hum.1, cf. Epid.2.1.6; elevation, Gal.10.318

ἀναρροφέω.definition: = Cratin.7 D., Arist.Mete.356b13, Placit.3.5.2, Luc.VH1.30; gulp down, D.C.71.10

ἀναρρόφησις.definition: sucking up through a tube, Sch.Opp.H.4.462

ἀνάρρυσις.definition: rescuing, Phot.Bibl.p.2 B; name of second day of festival Ar.Pax890, ubi v. Sch., cf. AB417

ἀναρρώννυμι.definition: aor. strengthen afresh; intr. in Act., Pherecyd.33 J.; Plu.Pomp.57, cf. 2.182b

ἀναρύτω.definition: aor. 1 Hsch., draw as from a well, Plu.2.949f: metaph., Cratin.36

ἀνασαλεύω.definition: shake up, stir up, Luc.Astr.29; Alciphr.1.39

ἀνασειράζω.definition: draw back with a hawser, A.R.1.391; draw off the right road, E.Hipp.237; draw away, c. gen., Nonn.D.39.355

ἀνασείω.definition: brandish at one, threaten with, D.25.47; Ar.Ach.347; shake out, IG2.104a36 ; shake out every reef, Ph.1.327, al.; Philostr.VA6.12, cf. VS2.32; Poll.1.214; Philostr.Im.1.6

ἀνασθμαίνω.definition: breathe with difficulty, Q.S.4.244, cf. Opp.H.5.212

ἀνασιλλιάομαι.definition: wear the hair bristling up, Hsch

ἀνάσιμος.definition: snub-nosed, Ar.Ec.940; generally, turned up at end, of the elephant's tusks, Arist.HA501b33; Id.Pr.932a18; of a horse's neck, curved up, SimonEq.6

ἀνασιμόω.definition: turn up the nose, sniff, esp. of male animals following the females, Hsch

ἀνασκαίρω.definition: Ep impf. hop or skip up, Q.S.8.321

ἀνασκαλεύω.definition: scrape up, Hsch., Zen.1.27:—Med., clean; metaph., ransack, PMag.Par.1.186

ἀνασκάπτω.definition: dig up, Str.9.3.8; extirpate, of plants, Thphr.HP3.18.5 ; raze to the ground, of buildings, Plb.16.1.6, IG12.526a4

ἀνασκεδάννυμι.definition: or dissipate, Hp.Liqu.1; scatter abroad, Plu.Pyrrh.22:—Pass., v.l. in Polyaen.1.40.2

ἀνασκευή.definition: opp. pulling down: suppression; refutation of arguments, S.E.M.6.4, cf. Quint.Inst.2.4.18, Hermog.Prog.5; negative mood, proof by denial or argument from non- existence, Phld.Sign.31, al.; removal, cure, Dsc.3.137; Ar…

ἀνασκησία.definition: want of practice or exercise, Eus.Mynd.39, Muson.Fr.4p.15H., Poll.1.159

ἀνάσκητος.definition: unpractised, unexercised, X.Cyr.8.8.24, Plb.1.61.4, Onos.10.3, Plu.Cam.18, etc. Adv. Id.2.112e

ἀνασκινδαλεύω.definition: or = Att. Hsch., EM100.51, Phryn.PSp.48 B

ἀνασκιρτάω.definition: leap, skip with joy, D.S.19.55; but of wounded horses, Plu.Crass.25; of athletes, Philostr.Gym.39: pf. part. Pass. Eup.22

ἀνασκολοπίζω.definition: —Pass., with fut. Med. Hdt.3.132, 4.43, but Pass. Luc.Prom.7: aor. ib.2,10: pf. Id.Peregr.13:—fix on a pole or stake, impale, Hdt.1.128, 3.159, al.; in 9.78 it is used convertibly with asin Ph.1.237,687, Luc.Peregr.11

ἀνασοβέω.definition: scare and make to start up: generally, rouse, Pl.Ly.206a; Plu.2.44d; Chor.p.206 B.: —Pass., with ruffled hair, Luc.Tim.54; Id.JTr.30

ἀνασπαστήριος.definition: fitted for drawing up: a machine for raising a portcullis, App.BC4.78

ἀνασπάω.definition: poet. draw, pull up; draw, suck up greedily, A.Eu.647; Hp.VM22; Arist.HA495a26, PA661a19; draw water, Th.4.97

ἀνασπογγίζω.definition: sponge clean, sponge well, Hp.Ulc.4; soak up drugs, . . Id.Nat.Mul.32, cf. 74

ἀναστατέω.definition: carry off, or perh. seduce, POxy.1836

ἀνάστατος.definition: made to rise up and; of cities, ruined, laid waste, Hdt.1.155,178, And.1.108, etc.; S.Tr.240; Id.Ant.673; Th.8.24; Isoc.6.66, cf. Alex.1 D., Men.Inc.2.30 Körte

ἀναστατόω.definition: unsettle, upset, LXXDa.7.23; Act.Ap.17.6, cf. 21.38, PMag.Par.1.2244; of the mind, Ep.Gal.5.12; he upsets me, POxy.119.10 ; destroy, Asp.in EN61.28; drive out, BGU1079.20 :—Pass., Harp. s.v. Aq.Ps. 10.1

ἀνασταυρόω.definition: = foreg., Hdt.3.125, 6.30, al.; identical; in Rom. times, affix to a cross, crucify, Plb.1.11.5, al., Plu.Fab.6, al

ἀνασταχύω.definition: shoot up with ears, A.R.4.271, Procl.H.5.10: metaph., A.R.3.1054; trans., cause to spring up, Nonn.D.25.199

ἀναστέλλω.definition: send up, raise, Arat.417:—Med., gird; draw back, e.g. the flesh in a surgical operation, Hp.VC14; push back or up, Arist.HA632a17:—Pass., to be turned up, of the foot, Hp.Mochl.24

ἀναστενάζω.definition: = Hdt.1.86, 6.80, Ev.Marc.8.12; c. acc. pers., groan for, lament, A.Ch.335, E.HF118

ἀναστέφω.definition: crown, wreath, E.Fr.243; ib.362.48; Call.Hec.1.1.15:—Pass., I have my head wreathed with leaves, E.Hipp.806; but also Epigr.Gr.786

ἀναστηλόω.definition: set up as or on a monument, Lyc.883, Plu.2.1033e

ἀναστήλωσις.definition: setting up of a monument, Ptol.Heph. ap. Phot.Bibl.p.147B

ἀναστοιχειόω.definition: resolve matter into its elements, Chrysipp.Stoic.2.188, cf. Ph.1.501,477 , Gal.1.508

ἀναστοιχείωσις.definition: dissolution, Alex.Aphr.Pr.1.79, Lyd.Mens.4.26, cf. 40; of the body, Gal.7.251

ἀναστομόω.definition: furnish with a mouth, open up; clear; of one sea opening into another, Arist.Mu.303a22; . . D.S.3.38, cf. Ph.2.475, Hld.1.29

ἀναστόμωσις.definition: outlet, opening, Plu.2.590f; patency, Cels.4.5, Gal.7.31

ἀναστρατεύω.definition: enlist again, App.BC3.66:—Med., serve again, of soldiers, D.C.41.35

ἀναστροφή.definition: turning upside down, upsetting; turning back, return, S.Ant.226; of a hunter, making many casts backward, X.Cyn.6.25; wheeling round, of a horse, Id.Eq.Mag.3.14; of soldiers in battle, whether to flee or rally, Id.Cyr…

ἀναστρόφιος.definition: converse, of mathematical proportions, Papp.210.15, al

ἀνασύνταξις.definition: reassessment of war-tax levied on property, Poll.6.179, Suid

ἀνασφάλλω.definition: fut. J.AJ17.6.5 , intr., rise from a fall or illness, recover, Pl.Ax.364c; Nic.Dam.p.98D., cf. Babr.75.9; Id.78.3, cf. D.Chr.34.5; Luc.Abd.32: abs., J.l.c

ἀνασφίγγω.definition: bind tight up, Nonn.D.42.51: aor. 1 part. IG12.11

ἀνασχίζω.definition: rip up, Hdt.1.123, cf. 124, 3.35; Arist.EN1148b20; Theoc.25.277, cf. IG4.952.32 ; plough up, Pi.P.4.228 :—Pass., track opened up, Plu.2.161f

ἀνασωφρονίζω.definition: reduce to sobriety, in Pass., Hsch. s.v

ἀναταράσσω.definition: Att. stir up the mud; rouse to frenzy, S.Tr.218; confound, Pl.Phd.88c:— Pass., march in disorder, X.An.1.7.20

ἀνατείνω.definition: poet. lift up, in; stretch forth, so as to threaten, X.Cyr.4.1.3:— Med. , Simon.8; hold out any alarming threat, D.19.153: abs., threaten, Plb.5.55.1: c. dat., 4.82.8: c. fut. inf., 4.18.10

ἀνατειχίζω.definition: rebuild, X.HG4.4.18:—in Med., build up, J.BJ5.5.1

ἀνατιμάω.definition: raise in price, Hdt.9.33; D.C.38.5:—Med., Poll.3.125

ἀνατινάσσω.definition: fut. shake up and down, brandish, E.Ba.80: also of the wind shaking about a sail, Id.Or.341 , cf. Gal.14.638

ἀνατιτράω.definition: bore through, bore, Dsc.1.66 , TryphoFr.112 V. ; part. Gal.UP16.11, etc., Orib.46.11.10

ἀνατοιχέω.definition: roll from side to side, esp. of sailors in a storm: metaph., Arr.Epict.3.12.7; is preferred by Phryn.139, Poll.1.114

ἀνατολμάω.definition: regain one's courage, Plu.Luc.31, Ant.50; f.l. in E.Alc.277

ἀνατρέφω.definition: bring up, cherish, educate, A.Eu.523; feed up, opp. Hp.Art.33,50: metaph., Ar.Ra.944:—Pass., convalesce, Hp.VM14; of fish after milting, Arist.HA608a2

ἀνατριαινόω.definition: shake as with a trident, Amphis14.8

ἀνατριχόομαι.definition: Pass., have one's hair grow again, Suid

ἀνατροπεύς.definition: overturner, destroyer, Antipho2.2.2; Plu.2.5b; subverter, D.Chr.37.32

ἀνατροπή.definition: overthrow, ruin, A.Eu.355, Pl.Prt.325c; Clearch.10; pouring out, of drink, LXXHg.2.15

ἀναυξής.definition: not increasing, Thphr.CP4.6.3; intr., not waxing or growing, Hp.Art.53, Mochl.24,al., Arist.HA569a30, Cael.270a13

ἀναύξητος.definition: = Arist.Cael.270a25, Sor.1.47; without augment, Eust.19.29. Adv. Greg.Cor.180

ἀναφάλαντος.definition: forehead-bald, LXXLe.13.41, freq. in Pap., PPar.5.1.5 , PPetr.1p.54 , etc

ἀναφεύγω.definition: flee up, X.An.6.4.24, Plu.Crass.29, al.: c; escape, X.HG6.5.40, cf. 2.3.50: metaph., retreat, Plot.6.7.28

ἀναφθέγγομαι.definition: call out aloud, Ph.1.74, al., Plu.Thes.24, Caes.46, etc.: c. acc., Plb.18.5.6; Ph.2.177

ἀνάφθεγξις.definition: mode of utterance, ib.618, cf. Diog.Oen.10

ἀναφλέγω.definition: light up, rekindle, E.Tr.320; inflame, Ph.2.48; Plu.Alc.17:—Pass., to be inflamed with anger, Pl.Ep.349a; Conon23.1; to be inflamed, AP12.80 ; to be excited, Plu.2.798f; Ael.NA15.2; Plu.Dio4; Id.Ant.47, etc.; Jul.Or.2…

ἀναφόριον.definition: Dim. of petition, proposal, etc., BGU 1123.3, POxy.294.13, etc

ἀναφράσσω.definition: or barricade again, block up; remove barriers, Hsch

ἀναφρίσσω.definition: bristle up, with . ., Opp.H.4.599; of hair, Poll.2.25

ἀναφρόδιτος.definition: without not enjoying her; insensible to love, Plu.2.57d,Jul.Mis.347c

ἀναφρονέω.definition: come back to one's senses, X.An.4.8.21, D.C.60.14; Hsch

ἀναφυράω.definition: mix up well, Hp.Mul.2.157, Thphr.Od.25; IG14.966.8

ἀναφυσάω.definition: blow away, Hp.Mul.1.78; blow up or; abs., of the elephant going through water, blows upward, Id.HA497b30; of whales, Id.PA669a7; of Tritons, Philostr.Im.1.25

ἀναφύσησις.definition: upward blast, of volcanoes; prelude in flute-playing, Hsch. s.v. Eust.1406.50

ἀναφωνέω.definition: call aloud, shout, Plb.3.33.4, LXX1; proclaim, Id.Demetr.18: c. dat., decree, PFay.14.2

ἀναφώνησις.definition: vocal exercise, Sor.1.49; ejaculation, Plu.Brut.24; utterance, Demetr.Lac.Herc.1012.70; appellation, Phld.Rh.1.75 S

ἀναχαιτίζω.definition: of a horse, throw the mane back; c. acc., throw a rider, of a branch, E.Ba.1072: metaph., overthrow, upset, Id.Hipp.1232, cf. Tim.Pers.18; D.2.9; of wine, Anaxandr.3; Epicur.Sent.Vat.57

ἀναχαίτισμα.definition: = foreg., dub.l. in Plu.2.611f:—also = foreg., Lyd.Mag.2.15,3.52

ἀναχάσκω.definition: only pres. and impf., Ar.Av.502, Fr.68, Luc.VH2.1; poet. Pherecr.196:—other tenses from pres. fut. Hp.Superf.29: aor. 2 pf. the mouth, gape wide, Ar.Eq.641; Hp.Nat.Mul.45

ἀναχαυνόω.definition: Pass., to be puffed up, Arist.VV1251b18

ἀναχελύσσομαι.definition: cough up, Hp. ap. Sch.Nic.Al.81; expl. as = Erot

ἀναχρέμπτομαι.definition: cough up, D.L.2.75:—Act. in Suid., Zonar

ἀναχρονίζομαι.definition: Pass., to be an anachronism, Sch.E.Hipp.231, Ph.854, Eust.1404.29:—Act. c. part., to be late in doing, PTeb.413.14

ἀναχρονισμός.definition: anachronism, Sch.A.Pr.846; exchange of the quantity of two syllables, Eust.1704.8

ἀναχρώννυμι.definition: colour anew, discolour, Plu.2.93of:—Pass., v.l. in Thphr.Sud.12: metaph., to be defiled with, Eust.122.26

ἀναχωματισμός.definition: the throwing up a mound, Sch.A.Pers.646, BGU199, etc

ἀναχωνεύω.definition: smelt over again, Str.9.1.23, cf. PHolm.2.8, PLeid.X.6

ἀναχώννυμι.definition: heap up into a mound, AP7.537 :—in Pass., v.l.Th.2.102 ; raise a road by throwing down rubbish, D.55.28, cf. PPetr.2p.43 , 3p.111; Luc.Tox.43

ἀναχωρίζω.definition: make to go back or retire, X.Cyr.7.1.41, An.5.2.10; having drawn it back, Tab.Heracl.1.56, 59

ἀναψαθάλλω.definition: touch up, work up, Phryn.PSp.12B., cf. Hsch

ἀναψάω.definition: wipe up, Ctes.Fr.57.28; clean out, PLond.1.131r631:—Pass., aor. BGU530.17

ἀναψηλάφησις.definition: close search, Eust.254.31; re-examination, retrial, Cod.Just.7.62.35, cf. 12.37.19, Just.Nov.82.12,al

ἀνάψυξις.definition: cooling, Posidon.72; exposure; drying up, Str.10.2.19

ἀναψυχή.definition: relief, respite, Id.Smp.176a, PLond. 1.42.19; from misery, E.Supp.615; Id.Ion1604

ἀνδραγαθέω.definition: pf. D.S.11.25: aor. Plb.6.39.2: :—later form of behave in a manly, upright manner, Id.1.45.3, al., SIG785.14 , BGU1207.11 , Onos.34.2:—Pass., opp. Plu.Fab.20

ἀνδραγάθημα.definition: brave, manly deed, Str.1.2.8, Plu.Sert.10,IG14.951,Jul.Caes.329c, etc

ἀνδραγαθία.definition: Ion. bravery, manly virtue, Hdt.1.99,136, al., Th.2.42; the character of an upright man, Ar.Pl.191, Phryn.Com.1; Hyp.Lyc.6

ἀνδραγαθίζομαι.definition: aor. App.BC5.101:—act uprightly, if any one thinks to sit at home and play the honest man, Th.2.63; Id.3.40, cf. Arist.VV1250b4

ἄνδραγχος.definition: throttler of men: executioner, Eust.1833.54, 1858.57: Hsch

ἀνδράδελφος.definition: husband's brother, brother-in-law, Suid.:—fem. husband's sister, Eust.392.2

ἀνδρακάς.definition: Adv. man by man, Od.13.14, Cratin.19, cf. Plu.2.151e; apart, A.Ag.1595, cf. Hsch

ἀνδραποδίζω.definition: pres. Act. first in Alciphr.3.40: Att; less freq. of individuals, kidnap, Pl.Grg.508e, X.Mem.4.2.14, Smp.4.36

ἀνδραποδισμός.definition: selling into slavery, enslaving; of individuals, kidnapping, whether of free men or other people's slaves, liable to action for kidnapping, Pl.Lg.879a, 955a

ἀνδραποδιστής.definition: slave-dealer or kidnapper, Ar.Eq.1030, Pl.521, Lys.10.10, etc., cf. Poll.3.78; coupled with etc., Pl.R.344b: metaph., one who sells his own independence, X.Mem.1.2.6

ἀνδραποδωνία.definition: Ion. tax on sale of slaves, SIG4.8

ἀνδρείκελον.definition: image of a man, App.BC2.147; flesh-coloured pigment, Pl.R.501b, Cra.424e, X.Oec.10.5, Arist.GA725a26, Thphr.Lap.51

ἀνδρειφόντης.definition: man-slaying, epith. of Il.2.651, etc.; but the metre requires cf

ἀνδρηλατέω.definition: banish from house and home, A.Ag.1419, cf. Eu.221; Ag.1586, cf. S.OT100, Pl.R.565e, etc.:—Pass., D.C.47.19

ἀνδρηλάτης.definition: he that drives one from his home, dub.l. in A.Th.637, cf. Hsch

ἀνδριαντίσκος.definition: = foreg., statuette, IG22.47.5,20 , 11.161B17,60 , GDI5702 ; puppet, Plu.Thes.20

ἀνδριαντοποιΐα.definition: the sculptor's art, statuary, Pl.Grg.450c, X.Mem.1.4.3

ἀνδριαντοποιός.definition: sculptor, Pi.N.5.1, Pl.R.54cc, etc.; statuary in bronze , opp. Arist.EN1041a11

ἀνδρόβιος.definition: living like a man, Anon. ap. Suid. s.v

ἀνδρόβουλος.definition: of manly counsel, man-minded, like A.Ag.11, cf. Phryn.PSp.31B.: opp

ἀνδρογένεια.definition: of descent by the man's side, Hp.Ep.27; SIG1044.20 , cf. 1106.25

ἀνδρόγυνος.definition: man-woman, hermaphrodite, Pl.Smp.189e; womanish man, effeminate person, Hp.Vict.1.28, Hdt.4.67, Aeschin.2.127, Plu.2.219f, cf. LXXPr.18.8; Eup.3D

ἀνδροκμής.definition: man-wearying, A.Supp.678, Eu.248; man-slaying, Id.Ch.889; E.Supp.525

ἀνδροκοιτέω.definition: sleep with a man, BGU 1058.30, Aët.1.142

ἀνδροκόρινθος.definition: a Man-Corinth, in allusion to the lewdness of the men of Heraclea and the women of Corinth, Stratonic. ap. Ath.8.351c

ἀνδροκτασία.definition: slaughter of men in battle, mostly in pl., . . Il.5.909; 7.237, etc.: personified, Hes.Th.228: in sg., by reason of sad homicide, Il.23.86, cf. Hes.Oxy.1359.1.17, A.Th.693

ἀνδροκτάστης.definition: prob. f. l. for Vett. Val.237.7

ἀνδρολήψιον.definition: right of seizure, D.23.83, cf. 6.217; generally, seizure, arrest, App.BC4.6, Philostr.Ep.50

ἀνδρονομέομαι.definition: to be imperious, dub. in M.Ant.10.19 codd

ἀνδροσάθων.definition: obscene epith. of Priapus, Phot.p.127 R., Eust.1968.43, AB394 , Suid.:—also ABl.c., Hsch

ἀνδρόστροφος.definition: after the manner of men, Man.4.358

ἀνδροσώτειρα.definition: saviour of men, title of lsis, POxy.1380.55

ἀνδροφάγος.definition: eating men, Od.10.200; a people north of the Scythians, Hdt.4.18,106, cf. Palaeph.7

ἀνδροφονέω.definition: slay men, Str.4.6.8: c. acc., H.Ep.17:—Pass., Ph.2.314

ἀνδροφονία.definition: slaying of men, Arist.EN1107a12, Epicur.Fr.237 , D.H.4.24 , Plu.Rom.22

ἀνδροφόνος.definition: man-slaying, Homeric epith. of Hector; of women, murdering their husbands, Pi.P.4.252

ἀνδρόω.definition: change into a man, Lyc.176,943; rear up into manhood, AP7.419 , Plu.2.490a:—Pass., become a man, reach manhood, Hdt.1.123, 2.32, Hp.Art.58, E.HF42, Ant.Lib.13.3, etc.: metaph., Macho ap.Ath.8.341c: also in Med., = Hsch

ἀνδρωνυμικόν.definition: name transferred from an animal to a man, e.g. Sch.Il.18.319

ἀνδρῷος.definition: late form of Muson.Fr.3p.17H., Gal.2.888, Sch.Ar.Ra.47, Aspasia ap. Aët.16.18; distinguished by Sch.Lib.Or.64.54

ἀνέγερσις.definition: raising up, Plu.2.156b; waking up, ib.378f

ἀνέγερτος.definition: not broken by waking, Arist.GA779a3, EE1216a3

ἀνεθίζομαι.definition: become used to a thing, D.L.2.96

ἀνειδωλοποιέω.definition: represent in imagery, of poets, Plu.2.1113a; form a mental image of, imagine, Ph.2.59, cf. S.E.P.3.155:—Med., Placit.5.2.3:—Pass., patterns conceived in the mind, Longin.14.1

ἀνείλησις.definition: = foreg., Hp.Epid.3.8; penning up, confinement, Epicur.Ep.2p.44U

ἀνείρω.definition: fasten on or to, string, Hdt.3.118; fasten upon a spit, Pl.Com.201; IG11.161 B61 ; twine or wreathe them, Ar.Ach.1006; D.C.51.14

ἀνεισφορία.definition: exemption from taxation, SIG612B3 , Jahresh.14 Beibl.126 , Plu.Eum.4, IPE2.36.2, BGU 1074.4 , etc

ἀνείσφορος.definition: exempt from taxation, D.H.5.22, cf. Plu.Cam.2, IG14.951, J.AJ13.6.7

ἀνεκβίαστος.definition: not to be overpowered, Chrysipp.Stoic.2.64, v.l. in Gell.1.2.7

ἀνέκδαρτος.definition: not skinned, and Adv. both in Suid

ἀνεκδιήγητος.definition: indescribable, ineffable, 2 Ep.Cor.9.15, Hsch., v.l. in Aristeas99

ἀνεκδίκητος.definition: unavenged, J.AJ20.3.1; unpunished, PGoodsp.15.5; Just.Nov.77.1.1, cf.137Pr

ἀνεκθέρμαντος.definition: not warmed or to be warmed, Gal.7.189, Orib. ap. Phot.Bibl.p.175B. Adv. Antyll. ap. Orib.9.25.27

ἀνεκκλησίαστος.definition: not used for assemblies of the people, Posidon.41; unchallenged, of a

ἀνέκκλιτος.definition: not to be evaded, Hsch. s.v. Sch.Il.2.797. Adv. unavoidably, ibid

ἀνεκλάλητος.definition: unutterable, ineffable, 1 Ep.Pet.1.8; not capable of expression or calculation, Dsc.Eup.Praef.; Heliod. ap. Sch.Orib.45.2

ἀνέκλειπτος.definition: incessant, uninterrupted, Hyp.Epit.20; in Alchemy, of the asem alloy, PHolm.2.17, PLeid.X.7 and 39

ἀνεκπίμπλημι.definition: fill up or again, f.l. in X.An.3.4.22

ἀνέκπληκτος.definition: undaunted, intrepid, Pl.Tht.165b; Act., making no impression, Plu.2.7a

ἀνεκποίητος.definition: not alienated, of property, Just.Nov.22.20.2, cf. 22.39

ἀνεκπύητος.definition: not suppurating, Hp.Aph.5.20, Ruf. ap. Orib.7.26.21; exuding serum instead of pus, Hp.Fract.25

ἀνέκφευκτος.definition: not to be escaped, inevitable, D.S.20.54, Plu.2.166e, Corn.ND13, Phld.Ir.p.79 W

ἀνεκφοίτητος.definition: not proceeding or emanating: hence, inseparable from . ., Procl.in Ti.1.6 D., in Prm.p.634 S.; Dam.Pr.289; ib.59; ib.66; Eustr.in EN40.8

ἀνέλεγκτος.definition: not cross-questioned, safe from being; not refuted, Id.Grg.467a; irrefutable, Id.Ap.22a, cf. Ti.29b. Adv. without refutation or reply, Plu.CG10

ἀνελευθερία.definition: illiberality of mind, servility; esp. in money matters, stinginess, X.Cyr.8.4.32, Arist.EN1107b10, 1121b13, etc

ἀνελεύθερος.definition: not free, of a slave, Pherecr.8; of actions, servile, mean, Lys.10.2, cf. Pl.Tht.182c; Arist.EN1121b33; Pol.1336a29

ἀνελκόομαι.definition: Pass., suppurate afresh, Hp.Mul.2.122, Morb.1.21, Cass.Pr.9

ἀνέλπιστος.definition: unhoped for, Heraclit.18; of persons, having no hope, hopeless, Hp.Aph.7.47, Prog.19; Theoc.4.42: c. inf., Th.8.1; not expecting that . ., Id.3.30; X.Cyn.7.9; Th.6.17; . . Id.3.46. Adv. he is in despair, Pl.Phlb.36b

ἀνέμετος.definition: or without vomiting, Hp.Prorrh.1.85, Epid.2.3.1. Adv. Coac.546

ἀνεμίζομαι.definition: Pass., to be driven with the wind, Ep.Jac.1.6, Sch.Od.12.336: Act. in Hsch. s.v

ἀνέμιος.definition: f.l. for in Ph.1.96, cf. Hsch

ἀνεμόστροφος.definition: whirling with wind, prob. for in Anacreont.36.14

ἀνεμοτρεφής.definition: fed by the wind, Il.15.625; a spear from a tree reared by the wind, i.e. made tough and strong by battling with the wind, 11.256 cf. Philostr.Im.2.3

ἀνεμόφθορος.definition: blasted by the wind, LXXHo.8.7, Ph.2.431

ἀνεμοφόρητος.definition: carried by the wind, of rumours, Cic.Att.13.37.4; of delicate vessels, Luc.Lex.7; dub. sens. in Sammelb.4324.8 ,14

ἀνεμπόδιστος.definition: not obscured, clear, Procl.Hyp.4.92. Adv. ib.88; Act., offering no impediment, Arist.PA663b11

ἀνέμπτωτος.definition: not falling into, Pl.Def.412c: abs., D.L.7.117

ἀνέμφατος.definition: v.l. for foreg., Procl.in Prm. l.c., cf. eund.in Ti.3.1 and 12 D.; without a tinge of, Eliasin Cat.20.26: abs., lacking in expression, of melody without rhythm, Aristid.Quint.1.13; Aristid.Rh.2p.434S. Adv. Hermog.Id.2…

ἀνεμώλιος.definition: windy, Hom., but only metaph., talk words of wind, Il.4.355, Od.11.464; are like the winds, i.e. empty boasters, Il.20.123; why bear thy bow in vain? 21.474; of a trial, Maiist.38; . . Theoc.25.239; the empty fool! AP…

ἀνενδοίαστος.definition: unhesitating, Ph.1.440, 2.36; indubitable, Id.1.302, al., Luc.Herm.67; unambiguous, Anon.in SE61.15: Gramm., unquestionably correct, A.D.Synt.21.1. Adv. 218.19; without doubt, Ph.2.319; unhesitatingly, unequivocally, …

ἀνένδοτος.definition: unyielding, rigid, Antyll. ap. Orib.9.14.5; not giving way, Ph.1.154, al.: metaph., Hierocl.p.57.3A., Orib.Fr.55; Herod.Med.in Rh.Mus.58.89. Adv. Ph.2.66, cf. Eustr.in EN297.23

ἀνενεργησία.definition: want of exercise, Sor.1.106; inactivity, Alex.Aphr.de An.74.27; as criticism of Sceptics by Stoics, Stoic.2.36

ἀνενέργητος.definition: inefficacious, inactive, Ruf.Anat.30; not possessing an of the Good, Plot.5.6.6

ἀνεννόητος.definition: without conception of; inconceivable, Cleom.2.1; Dam.Pr.7

ἀνενόχλητος.definition: undisturbed, Hdn.5.7.2, Hld.5.19; of a sepulchre, CIG2845.9 , BGU935.3 . Adv. Ruf. and Aspasia ap.Aët.16.50, Sch.E.Or.630, Simp.in Ph.1176.24

ἀνέντροπος.definition: not heeding or respecting a thing, Hsch.; Eranos 13.87

ἀνεξάλειπτος.definition: indelible, Isoc.5.71, Plu.2.1b, PHolm.22.43, cf. 1.12. Adv. Hsch

ἀνεξαλλοτρίωτος.definition: unalienated, BGU1151.43 , PLond.2.360.9, etc., cf. Ath.Mitt.3.58

ἀνεξαπατησία.definition: freedom from deception or mistake, Arr.Epict.3.2.2

ἀνεξαπάτητος.definition: infallible, not to be deceived, Arist.Top.132a32; in a thing, Id.Pol.1338a42, cf. Hierocl.in CA23p.470M., al. Adv. Ph.1.483, Poll.8.11

ἀνεξαρίθμητος.definition: not to be counted or told, Id.3.88, 4.162

ἀνεξέλεγκτος.definition: incapable of disproof or criticism, Th.1.21; Arist.SE176b24; difficult to disprove rather than credible, D.S.1.40, etc.; leaves their courage without any real test or proof, Th.4.126; unrefuted, Gal.15.547. Adv. X.Oec…

ἀνεξέλικτος.definition: whose development cannot be fully exhausted, Dam.Pr.177. Adv. dub. l. S.E.M.7.191

ἀνεξέργαστος.definition: not worked out, unfinished, Luc.Fug.21, Gal.Nat.Fac.2.3

ἀνεξερεύνητος.definition: not to be searched out, Heraclit.18, Ep.Rom.11.33, D.C.69.14

ἀνεξέταστος.definition: not searched out, not inquired into; without inquiry or investigation, Pl.Ap.38a. Adv. Ph.1.550, Plu.2.94d, etc

ἀνεξεύρετος.definition: not to be found out, Th.3.87, cf. Hellanic.194 J., Arist.Mu.392a17, Plu.2.964a

ἀνεξήγητος.definition: not to be told, Hsch. s.v; unexplained, Gal.UP2.7, Simp.in Ph.241.21, Sch.Pi.N.9.95

ἀνεξικακία.definition: forbearance, Plu.2.90e, Luc.Par.53, Hld.10.12; patient endurance under . ., Hdn.3.8.8, cf. Eun.Hist.p.258D

ἀνεξίκακος.definition: enduring pain or evil, Herod.Med. ap. Orib.5.30.7, Luc.Jud.Voc.9, Vett. Val.38.21, Gal.5.38, Them.Or.15.190a , Aret.SA2.6 ; forbearing, long-suffering, 2 Ep.Ti.2.24. Adv. Luc.Asin.2

ἀνεξόδευτος.definition: with no issue or outlet, IGRom.4.743

ἀνέξοιστος.definition: not to be expressed, ineffable, ib.728d, Gorg.ap.S.E.M.7.82, Jul.Or.5.158d

ἀνεόρταστος.definition: without holidays or festive joy, Democr.230, cf. Plu.2.1102b

ἀνέορτος.definition: without festival, Alciphr.3.49; festivals unkept, D.H.8.25, but, impious festivals, Ph.2.320: c. gen., without share in festal rites, E.El.310

ἀνεπάγγελτος.definition: not announced, a war; uninvited, Cratin.44

ἀνεπαίσθητος.definition: unperceived, imperceptible; Act., not perceiving, Plb.28.1.6, Longin.4.1. OGI194 Adv. Ph.Fr.70H., Hippiatr.38, Syrian.in Metaph.100.38, Simp.in Ph.1198.39

ἀνεπαίσχυντος.definition: having no cause for shame, 2 Ep.Ti.2.15; J.AJ18.7.1

ἀνεπάνακτος.definition: not to be brought back, Ph.1.139, cf. 2.338

ἀνεπανόρθωτος.definition: irreparable, J.AJ16.11.3; not to be amended, perfect, Ph.2.614

ἀνεπέκτατος.definition: not lengthened, A.D.Synt.110.14, al.; of declensions, parisyllabic, D.T.632.10

ἀνεπεξέργαστος.definition: not wrought out, imperfect, Simp.in de An.4.13, Eust.499.2

ἀνεπηρέαστος.definition: free from injury or insult, unmolested, D.S.31.8, Memn.2.3, J.AJ14.10.6, PFlor.91.17 , cf. BGU1022.24: Medic., uninjured, Archig. ap. Orib.8.1.6, Id. ap. Aët.8.73. Adv. J.AJ16.2.5

ἀνεπιβάρητος.definition: unburdened, IGRom4.219 , cf. IG 7.2711, SIG799.16 , Ath.Mitt.33.382

ἀνεπιβασία.definition: prohibition of traffic or intercourse, IG4.752.6 , Heraclit.Ep.9.8

ἀνεπίβατος.definition: not to be climbed, Str.12.3.11; inaccessible, Plu.2.228b

ἀνεπιβούλευτος.definition: without plots, and so; Act., not plotting, the absence of intrigue, Th.3.37; not insidious, Aristid.Rh.2p.445S

ἀνεπίβουλος.definition: not exposed to treachery, PSI1.96.3 . Adv. without treachery, Eust.905.57

ἀνεπίγνωστος.definition: not distinctly known, Herm. ap. Stob.1.41.44; J.AJ12.2.11:—Act., not knowing distinctly, Simp.in de An.299.37. Adv. not noticeably, Plb.18.18.16

ἀνεπίγραφος.definition: Dor. Tab.Heracl.1.84; unregistered: hence, free of charge, of a harvest, PGnom.234 (ii A.D., cf. Plb.8.31.6, D.S.1.64, etc.: metaph., without distinguishing marks, Luc.Nec.15; unmarked, Cat.25

ἀνεπιδάνειστος.definition: no which no money has been borrowed, not mortgaged, IG12.515 , BGU193.19 , Sch.Luc.JTr.48

ἀνεπιδεής.definition: = v.l. in Pl.Lg.947e, cf. Chrysipp.Stoic.3.16; Ph.1.334, al., Luc.DMort.26.2

ἀνεπίδεκτος.definition: not accepting or admitting, Phld.Rh.1.383S.; S.E.M.9.33, cf. D.L.3.77, Alex.Aphr.in Metaph.393.13, Id.in Top.210.16

ἀνεπίδετος.definition: not bandaged, Hp.Fract.20; not requiring a bandage, of plasters, Dsc.5.85, Damocr. ap. Gal.13.915

ἀνεπίδικος.definition: without the process of by which claims to inheritance or guardianship were enforced, Is.3.59; Id.8.34 ; D.46.22, cf. Poll.3.33

ἀνεπίδοτος.definition: not growing or sprouting, Thphr.HP7.4.8, CP4.6.3

ἀνεπιεικής.definition: unreasonable, unfair, Th.3.66, Ar.Fr.50D., Phld.Ir.p.57W., Alex.Aphr.in Top.208.9: neut. as Adv., without consideration, PGiss.39.3 : regul. Adv. Arr.An.7.29.1, Poll.8.13

ἀνεπιζήτητος.definition: leaving nothing to be desired; v.l. for uninvestigated, Gal.15.14

ἀνεπιθεώρητος.definition: Astrol., not overlooked, or controlled, Gal.19.548

ἀνεπικέλευστος.definition: not under orders, metaph. of untilled land, Ph.2.207. Adv. 1.115

ἀνεπικούρητος.definition: without succour, Philem.213.2; without dominant planet, Vett. Val.151

ἀνεπικώλυτος.definition: unhindered, J.AJ18.6.4, Onos.35.2. Adv. without let or hindrance, IPE2.52 ; without restraint, D.S.17.116, Decr. ap. J.AJ19.5.3, Alciphr.3.8

ἀνεπίληπτος.definition: not open to attack, Th.5.17; not censured, blameless, v.l. in E.Or.922, X.Cyr.1.2.15; perfect, Ph.1.15; less open to criticism, Pl.Phlb.43c; not subject to control, D.H.2.14; unassailable, not subject to cancellation,…

ἀνεπίληστος.definition: not to be forgotten, Aristaenet.2.13, Hsch. s.v. Adv. Sch.Od.14.174

ἀνεπιλόγιστος.definition: unable to consider, c. gen., Diogenian.Epicur.3.25; inconsiderate, thoughtless, Epicur.Sent.Vat.63, Sor.1.48; Phld.Ir.p.24W., Mitteis Chr.361 . Adv. Pl.Ax.365d, 369e:—Subst. Sch.Od.15.225:—Verb Phld.Ir.p.19 W

ἀνεπίλυτος.definition: unbandaged, Crito ap.Gal.13.708; unsolved, Olymp.in Cat.111.15

ἀνεπίμικτος.definition: avoiding contact, Epicur.Sent.39; not mixing with others, unsocial, Plu.2.438c; Id.Rom.3; = Str.8.1.2: of a country, unfrequented, unvisited, D.S.5.21, cf. Plu.2.604b; ib.989c; to make it alien from oneself, D.S.5.17,…

ἀνεπιμιξία.definition: want of intercourse or traffic, Plb.16.29.12, App.Mith.93

ἀνεπινόητος.definition: Act., having no experience of, D.S.2.59; = sine adinventione, Just.Nov.59.7

ἀνεπίξεστος.definition: not polished, not finished, Hes.Op.746, Them.Or.26.388b

ἀνεπίπλαστος.definition: not plastered over: metaph., unaffected, D.L.2.117

ἀνεπίπλεκτος.definition: without connexion with others, isolated, Str.2.5.8, al

ἀνεπίπληκτος.definition: not liable to be reproved, Eup.397; in bad sense, not reproved, licentious, Pl.Lg.695b, cf. Eus.Mynd.62

ἀνεπιπρόσθητος.definition: not occultable, Procl.Hyp.5.12, cf. Eustr.in APo.192.33: metaph., the material forms no obstacle to the incorporeal, Porph.Sent.27. Adv. Eust.1138.59

ἀνεπισήμαντος.definition: undistinguished; without an attack of , Gal.14.277

ἀνεπίσκεπτος.definition: inattentive, inconsiderate; Pass., not examined, unregarded, X.Mem.2.4.3; unobserved, Anon.in SE12.27

ἀνεπισκίαστος.definition: not in the shade, Alex.Aphr.in Mete.19.15

ἀνεπισκότητος.definition: not obscured or overclouded, Gal.UP10.2, Ptol.Tetr.100, Heph.Astr.1.25; and so prob. Procl.Par.Ptol.144

ἀνεπιστάθμευτος.definition: exempt from billeting, Plb.15.24.2:—also OGI262.13 , PTeb.5.168

ἀνεπιστασία.definition: inattention, thoughtlessness, Pl.Ax.365d; distraction, insensateness , Phld.Ir.p.33 W.; want of reflection, Simp.in Cael.163.35,al

ἀνεπιστάτητος.definition: without inspector, without tutelary genius, Max.Tyr.14.8, cf. Hsch

ἀνεπίστατος.definition: inattentive, Plb.5.34.4; Pass., not attended to, unregarded, Ptol.Alm.10.6, cf. Simp.in Cael.163.35. Adv. Porph.in Cat.65.22

ἀνεπιστημοσύνη.definition: want of knowledge, ignorance, unskilfulness, Th.5.7; of bees, Arist.HA626b4; Pl.R.560b: want of science, opp. ib.350a,al., Plot.6.1.10: pl., X.Oec.20.21; of Chrysipp.Stoic.3.60

ἀνεπιστήμων.definition: Dor. Archyt.3, gen; without knowledge, unintelligent, Pl.R.350b, etc.; less intelligent, Hdt.2.21

ἀνεπιστρεπτέω.definition: to be indifferent, pay no heed, D.L.6.91, Arr.Epict.2.5.9, Vett.Val.43.27, Artem.3.42, POxy.486.10

ἀνεπίστρεπτος.definition: prop. without turning round: hence metaph., indifferent, heedless, Phld.Herc. 1251.17, cf. Artem.2.37. Adv. Arr.Epict.2.9.4, PMag.Par.1.45: also or Ph.1.90 , Plu.2.46e, 418b, PMag.Lond.121.439

ἀνεπιστρεφής.definition: = foreg., careless of, Placit.1.7.7; inexorable, Corn.ND21

ἀνεπίσχετος.definition: not to be stopped, J.Vit.51; Aret.SD2.5; Aristaenet.2.5; of persons, Ph.2.268. Adv. Id.1.296, Plu.Ages.27

ἀνεπίτακτος.definition: subject to no control, Th.7.69, cf. Plu.2.987b. Adv. without orders or command, J.AJ19.2.2, D.L.5.20

ἀνεπίτατος.definition: not to be extended farther; not capable of opp. Porph.Intr.20.4; in Cat.138.5. Adv. without augmentation or intensification, Procl.Inst.52; without stress, opp. Ammon.in Int.11.26

ἀνεπιτηδειότης.definition: unfitness, inconvenience, inaptitude, Ph.1.191,521, M.Ant.5.5, Procl.Inst.143

ἀνεπιτήδευτος.definition: made without care or design; unpractised, untried, Plu.Alc.23. Adv. Philostr.VA7.27

ἀνεπιτίμητος.definition: not to be censured; unpunished, Plb.35.2.8, Onos.Praef.6, Ph.1.219

ἀνεπίτμητος.definition: subject to no deduction or restriction, Hsch

ἀνεπιτρόπευτος.definition: without guardian, Ph.1.219: metaph., ib.696, cf. Gal.Nat.Fac.2.3:— also Phryn.PSp.12 B

ἀνεπίφαντος.definition: without ostentation, Ph.2.76, Vett.Val.16.21; insignificant, Paul.Al.F.1. Adv. M.Ant.1.9

ἀνεπίφατος.definition: unexpected, Ph.2.533 , Hsch. Adv. Ph.2.521, Suid

ἀνεπίφθονος.definition: without reproach, S.Tr.1033 ; it is no reproach to any one, Th.6.83, cf. Pl.R.612b, Epicur.Fr.161; . . least invidious, D.18.321; ungrudging, Onos.Praef.10. Adv. so as not to create odium, Th.6.54, cf. Plu.Cam.1; Isoc…

ἀνεπόπτευτος.definition: not admitted among the Hyp.Fr.174, cf. Poll.8.124

ἀνεποργίξομαι.definition: to be roused by anger, Phld.Lib.p.41 O

ἀνέραστος.definition: loveless, D.Chr.7.133, cf; not loved. Luc.DMort.6.3

ἀνέργαστος.definition: not thoroughly wrought, imperfect, Arist.Metaph.1048b4; unwrought, D.S.14.18; untilled, dub. l. in Luc.Prom.11; raw, J.BJ5.10.2: - of a subject, not thoroughly handled or treated, Plb.10.43.1

ἀνερεθίζω.definition: provoke, stir up, excite, J.AJ19.7.1, Plu.Thes.6:—Pass., to be in a state of excitement, Th.2.21, X.An.6.6.9, Plu.Pyrrh.11; Dam.Pr.150

ἀνερέπτομαι.definition: Pass., the stomach drawn up spasmodically so as to cause vomiting, dub. l. in Nic.Al.256, cf. AB401

ἀνερευνάω.definition: search out, examine, investigate, Pl.Phd.63a; POxy.146818 :—in Med., Pl.Lg.816c, J.AJ19.1.15:—Pass., BJ2.8.6

ἀνερεύνητος.definition: not investigated, Pl.Hp.Ma.298c; that cannot be searched or found out, v.l. in Pl.Cra.421d; harass oneself about inscrutable things, f.l. in E.Ion255

ἀνέρπω.definition: creep upwards, E.Ph.1178: aor. Ar.Pax585, Luc.Nec.22, etc.; ofivy, E.Fr.88; spring up, of water, Call.Ap.110; Arist.PA688a10; Hp.Vict.3.76

ἀνερυθριάω.definition: begin to blush, blush up, Pl.Chrm.158c, X.Smp.3.12

ἀνερύω.definition: Ion. and Dor. draw up, Od.9.77, 12.402; = Hdt.9.96, cf. A.R.2.586; Theoc.14.35:—Med., AP6.300

ἀνετάζω.definition: inquire of, LXXSu.14; examine documents, POxy.34i13; examine by torture, Act.Ap.22.24, cf. 29

ἀνεύρεσις.definition: discovery, E.Ion569, v.l. in D.H.11.27, cf. Ph.1.285, Plu.Thes.12, etc

ἀνευρίσκω.definition: fut. aor. later; think out, invent, Antiph.113, cf. Timocl.37, Pl.Phdr.273c; Philem.88.10, etc

ἀνευρύνω.definition: dilate, Hp.Superf.29, Placit.5.16.2; Philostr.Her.19.9; Aët.8.69; esp. of arterial aneurism, Antyll. ap. Orib.45.24.1; broadens out, Arist.Mu.393b6: metaph., Ph.1.249, cf. Dam.Pr.74

ἀνεύρυσμα.definition: aneurism, Ruf. ap.Aët.14.51, Antyll. ap. Orib.45.24.1, Gal.7.725, 10.335

ἀνεύφραντος.definition: joyless, Secund.Sent.9, cf. Annales du Service 22.9 , Ptol.Tetr.158, Suid

ἀνεφέλκομαι.definition: Med., draw up for oneself, Man.5.279

ἀνεψιαδοῦς.definition: first cousin's son, Pherecr.203, Hermipp.86, D.44.26, Is.11.12; also, of second cousins, acc. to Poll.3.28, but this rests on a misinterpretation of D.45.54

ἀνεψιός.definition: first cousin, or generally, cousin, Il.9.464, Hdt.5.30,7.82, A.Pr.856, Com.Adesp.58D., etc., v. esp. And.1.47; Is.11.2; Theoc.22.170: comically, Stratt.39. Il.15.554, = cf. Q.S.3.295.]

ἀνέψω.definition: boil again, Arg.E.Med. ; f.l. for in Carm.Pop. ap. Sch.Ar.Eq.725

ἀνέω.definition: = Ar.Fr.694 , Ath.10.4553, Paus.Gr.Fr.21, prob. in Poll.7.24 . Cf

ἄνηβος.definition: not yet come to man's estate, opp. Heraclit.117, cf. Leg.Gort.11.19, Lys.14.25, Theoc.8.3; pueri, CIG2034 , cf. SIG1028.32 ; impotent, Arist.HA581b22; of a girl, Pl.Lg.833c

ἀνήθινος.definition: made of dill, Theoc.7.63; Dsc.5.65; Id.1.51, cf. Aret.CA1.2; cf

ἀνήκοος.definition: without hearing, Arist.Pr.903b38; of the dead, Mosch.3.103; Lyc.1451. 2. c. gen., not hearing a thing, never having heard or learnt it, Pl.Phdr.261b, X.Mem.2.1.31: hence, ignorant of it, Aeschin.1.141; with no ear for…

ἀνηλεής.definition: = without pity, unmerciful, Men.Epit.478, Call.Del.106, Parth.14.2, App.Mith.38; poet. acc. Epigr.Gr.418 ; gen. Man.1.263; is dub. in Alcm.81, cf.An.Ox.1.60. Adv. Hp.Aff.40, And.4.39

ἀνηλέητος.definition: unpitied, Lycurg.148; unmerciful, Aeschin.2.163, Eub.1 D. Adv. Pl.Lg.697d, Ar.Fr.51D

ἀνηλιάζω.definition: place in the sun, f.l. in Protagorid.4

ἀνήμερος.definition: not tame, wild, savage, of persons, Anacr.1.7; A.Pr.716, cf. Carneisc.Herc.1027.16, 2 Ep.Ti.3.3, Arr.Epict.1.3.7; of a country, A.Eu.14; E.Hec.1078; Plu.2.86d; Phld.Ir.p.57 W., cf. p.85: Sup., Clearch.37. Adv. D.S.13.23

ἀνθαιρετιστής.definition: of planets, belonging to the opposite 'condition', Jul.Laod.inCat.Cod.Astr.5.183.21, cf. 192.36

ἀνθαλίσκομαι.definition: to be captured in turn, i.e. after one has captured others, A.Ag.340; to be convicted in turn, D.C.36.40

ἀνθαμιλλάομαι.definition: vie one with another, be rivals, Pl.Lg.731a; race, of triremes, X.HG6.2.28:—Act., part. Hp.Ep.17

ἀνθάπτομαι.definition: Ion. lay hold of in return; simply, lay hold of, grapple with, engage in, c. gen., Hdt.7.138; Th.8.97; Pl.R.525c: generally, reach, attain, E.Med.1182

ἀνθαρμόζω.definition: fit one thing to another, Sch.Pi.P.4.65

ἀνθεμόρρυτος.definition: flowing from flowers, i.e. honey, E.IT634

ἀνθεμόστρωτος.definition: strewn with flowers, Id. ap. Phot.p.138R

Ἀνθεστηριών.definition: the month Anthesterion, eighth of the Attic year, answering to the end of February and the beginning of March, in which the Anthesteria were celebrated, Th.2.15, etc.; also in Ionic cities, as Tenos, IG 12.872.48

ἀνθεσφόρος.definition: bearing flowers, flowery; women celebrating the Anthesphoria, Poll.4.78

ἀνθηρογραφέω.definition: write in a florid style, Eust.991.8:—Pass., to be embellished, Cic.Att.2.6.1

ἀνθησσάομαι.definition: give way or yield in turn, Th.4.19, D.C.49.44

ἀνθησυχάζω.definition: to be quiet in turn, App.BC2.93

ἀνθίζω.definition: strew or deck with flowers, E.Ion890; colour, dye, stain, Arist.HA547a18:—Pass., Hdt.1.98; . . . . thus disguised or with silvered hair, S.El.43; meat browned at the fire, Epicr.6; wine flavoured with flowers, Gal.19.81

ἀνθιππασία.definition: sham fight of horse, X.Eq.Mag.1.20, IG2.1291, cf. 1305b

ἀνθιστάω.definition: later form of dub. in Hermog.Stat.2:—also PPetr.2p.120

ἀνθοβαφής.definition: bright-coloured, Antyll. ap. Orib.9.14.7, cf. Ph.2.274; S.E.P.1.148; Luc.Am.41; IG7.1802

ἀνθοβάφος.definition: dyer in bright colours, Id.2.830e, Man.2.326

ἀνθολκή.definition: pulling in the contrary direction, retraction, Aret.CA1.4; revulsion in venesection, Antyll. ap. Orib.7.11.1; means of drawing back, D.C.35.5; counterpoise, Plu.2.20c; resistance, countercheck, Id.Luc.11

ἀνθολογέω.definition: gather flowers, Plu.2.917f: c.acc., Hp.Ep.16,Porph.Abst.2.6:—Med., of bees, gather honey from flowers, Arist.HA628b32:—Pass., Gp.11.26.2

ἀνθολόγιον.definition: collection of extracts, Suid. s.v. cf. eund. s. vv

ἀνθομολογέομαι.definition: make a mutual agreement or covenant; confess freely and openly, D.S.1.70; J.AJ8.10.3; Plb.15.25.4: abs., 30.8.7

ἀνθομολόγησις.definition: mutual agreement, Plb.31.24.12; confession, admission, testimony, S.E.M.7.184,8.453

ἀνθοπλίζω.definition: arm against, E.Supp.666; X.Oec.8.12:—Med., arm oneself, Id.HG6.5.7

ἀνθορίζω.definition: make a counter-definition, in Med., Sch.D.21.28, PLond. 2.355.4 ; define terms by their mutual relations, Eliasin Cat.138.9

ἀνθορισμός.definition: counter-definition, Hermog.Stat.4, Inv.3.14, cf. Sch.D.21.28; alternative definition, Eliasin Cat.205.25

ἀνθοσμίας.definition: redolent of flowers, almost always of wine, with a fine bouquet, Hp.Steril.235, Ar.Pl.807, Ra.1150, Pherecr.108.30; also X.HG6.2.6, Luc.Sat.22:—in Id.Lex.2 as a pedantic phrase:—also Sch.Ar.Ra.1150

ἀνθρακεύς.definition: charcoal-maker, Aesop.59, Cic.Att. 15.5.1 , Them.Or.21.245a, App.BC4.40:—also And.Fr.4, Ael.NA1.8

ἀνθρακίας.definition: burnt to a cinder, Luc.Icar.13, cf. DMort.20.4,al

ἀνθράκιον.definition: Dim. of a stone of which; Dim. of II.1, IG11.161B82 ; of II.2, Cass.Fel.22

ἀνθρακίτης.definition: name of a gem, Plin.HN36.148; fem. a kind of coal, ib.37.99

ἀνθρακοειδής.definition: like, or of the colour of, coal, Ph.1.383

ἀνθρωπάριον.definition: Dim. of manikin, Eup.26D., Ar.Pl.416, Demad.51 , Arr.Epict.1.3.5

ἀνθρωπέη.definition: contr. , man's skin, like etc., Hdt.5.25 codd., Poll.2.5

ἀνθρώπειος.definition: human, suited to man, within man's powers, Hdt.1.5; not for man to attempt, Pl.Prt.344c; in all human probability, Id.Cri.47a; Th.1.22

ἀνθρωπεύομαι.definition: act as a human being, as opp. both to gods and beasts, Arist.EN1178b7; a human soul, Herm. ap. Stob.1.41.68

ἀνθρώπινος.definition: also Pl.Lg.737b:—of, from; human, suited to man, fallible, human understanding, Pl.Sph.229a; super-human, monstrous folly, Id.Lg.737b, etc.; D. 21.41; Arist.EN1177b32; Men.482; X.Cyr.5.4.19

ἀνθρωπίσκος.definition: Dim. of manikin, E.Cyc.316, Pl.R.495c; with a shade of contempt, Id.Phdr.243a, cf. Luc.Pisc.17; Ar.Pax751

ἀνθρωπόγλωσσος.definition: Att. speaking man's language, of the parrot, Arist.HA597b27

ἀνθρωπογναφεῖον.definition: a place for fulling men, comic name for a bath, ap.Clem.Al.Paed.3.9

ἀνθρωπογονία.definition: begetting of men, title of play by Antiphanes, POxy.427; origin of man, J.Ap.1.8

ἀνθρωποδαίμων.definition: man-god, i.e. deified man, E.Rh.971; semi-devil, Procop.Arc.12

ἀνθρωπόδηκτος.definition: bitten by a man, Dsc.1.125, Antig. ap. Philum.Ven.5.1

ἀνθρωποειδής.definition: like a man, in human shape, Hdt.2.86; ib.142; Phryn.PSp.6B.; Arist.Metaph.997b10, Phld.Piet.15, al.; Arist.HA502a24; of zodiacal signs, Ptol.Tetr.145. Adv. D.L.10.139

ἀνθρωποθῦμος.definition: bold as a man, opp. Plu.2.988d

ἀνθρωποθυσία.definition: human sacrifice, ib.857a, al.: in pl., ib.417c, Str.4.4.5, Pallas ap.Porph.Abst.2.56

ἀνθρωποκτονέω.definition: v.l. for E.Hec.260; offer human sacrifice, Phylarch.63:—Subst. Porph.Abst.2.55, Hld.10.7

ἀνθρωποκτόνος.definition: murdering men, homicide, E.IT389, 1; proparox., feeding on slaughtered men, E.Cyc.127

ἀνθρωπόλιχνος.definition: greedy of human flesh, Herm. ap. Stob.1.41.68

ἀνθρωπολογέω.definition: describe or represent in the form of man, Ph.1.282:—Pass., ib.181

ἀνθρωπομάγειρος.definition: one who cooks human flesh, Luc.Asin.6

ἀνθρωπόμορφος.definition: of human form, Epicur.Fr.353, cf. Str.17.1.28, Ph.1.15, Corn.ND27, Procop.Arc.18; Ptol.Tetr.79,181

ἀνθρωπόνοος.definition: contr. with human understanding, intelligent, Ael.NA16.10: Sup. Str.15.1.29

ἀνθρωποποιέω.definition: make, form man or men, Simp.in Cat.333.6

ἀνθρωποποιΐα.definition: making of man or men, Luc.Prom.5,17

ἀνθρωπορραίστης.definition: title of Dionysus at Tenedos, Ael.NA12.34

ἀνθρωποφαγέω.definition: eat human flesh, Hdt.4.106, Porph.Abst.2.57; of carnivora, Arist.HA594a29

ἀνθρωποφαγία.definition: cannibalism, Arist.Pol.1338b20, Phld.Sto. Herc.339.14, Porph.Abst.2.57: in pl., Plu.Luc.11

ἀνθρωποφάγος.definition: man-eating, Antiph.68.12, Arist.HA501b1, Heraclit.Incred.31:—esp. of cannibal tribes, Str.4.5.4, etc

ἀνθρωπόχειρον.definition: herb of mercury , Cat.Cod. Astr.8.162:—also ib.7.234

ἀνθυπαλλαγή.definition: Rhet., substitution of one case for another, Demetr.Eloc.60, A.D.Synt.204.27, al

ἀνθυπαλλάσσω.definition: Att. substitute, esp. in Rhet., substitute one case for another, Demetr.Eloc.59, cf. A.D.Synt.232.2; of interchange of moods, in Pass., ib.211.19:—Med., receive in exchange, Ph.2.440

ἀνθυπατεία.definition: proconsulate, CIG 3841f , BCH 11.110 , Hdn.7.5.2, Just.Nov.8.1: pl., ib.26.5Intr

ἀνθυπατεύω.definition: to be proconsul, Plu.Comp.Dem.Cic.3, Act.Ap.18.12, Hdn.7.5.2

ἀνθύπατος.definition: proconsul, Lat. pro consule; as Adj., proconsular, D.H.9.16; Id.11.62

ἀνθυπείκω.definition: yield in turn or mutually, Plu.Cor.18, D.C.45.8

ἀνθυπόδεικτος.definition: brought forward as an instance in opposition, Phld.D.1.16

ἀνθυποκρίνομαι.definition: put on or pretend in turn, Luc.Dom.30

ἀνθυπολείπω.definition: leave on the other side, f.l. in Ph.2.505

ἀνθυπόμνυμι.definition: make a counter-affidavit, in Med., D.48.25,58.43

ἀνθυποπτεύω.definition: suspect mutually, D.C.45.8: abs., Aen. Tact.24.11 :—Pass., . . he is met by the suspicion that . ., Th.3.43

ἀνθυποστρέφω.definition: recur, of an illness, Poll.3.107; return, Olymp.in Mete.148.1, Pall.in Hp.Fract.12.276C.; turn round upon, Ps.-Callisth.2.29; turn back, ib.31, al

ἀνθυποτείνομαι.definition: maintain by way of rejoinder, Ulp. ad D.23.88

ἀνθυπουργέω.definition: Ion. return a kindness, Hdt.3.133; S.Fr.339; E.Hipp.999; Corn.ND15

ἀνθυπουργία.definition: service done in return, Anon.in Rh.109.1

ἀνθυποφορά.definition: reply, opp. D.H.Dem.54; esp; reply, A.D.Synt.72.26

ἀνθυποχωρέω.definition: give place in turn, Dam.Pr.303, Steph.in Hp.2.279D

ἀνθυφίσταμαι.definition: Pass., with aor. 2 undertake for another, undertake to serve as choragus in rivalry with another, D.21.68:—later in Act., imply reciprocally, Dam.Pr.72

ἀνθωροσκοπέω.definition: to be in a diametric aspect with the horoscope, Ptol.Tetr.200, Vett.Val.135.3

ἀνίδρωτος.definition: without having sweated or exercised oneself, Id.Cyr.2.1.29: not accompanied by perspirations, Hp.Judic.9

ἀνιερόω.definition: dedicate, devote, Arist.Oec.1346b5; Plu.Cor.3:—Pass., PTeb.60.10 , BGU1202.5 , etc.: used of persons invoking the wrath of the gods upon themselves or others in case of breach of faith, SIG1179

ἀνιέρωσις.definition: consecration, D.H.5.35, cf. SIG563.9,16 , IG9.278 ; dedication of a manumitted slave, Boeot. IG7.3315

ἀνικμάζω.definition: draw up, Sch.Nic.Al.524:—Pass., evaporate, Dsc.4.64:—hence Philum.Ven.16.6

ἀνίλλω.definition: = Phryn.PSp.31 B., Olymp.in Phlb.p.240 S.:— Pass., shrink back, of the soul, Plot.1.6.2, cf. Porph.Plot.14

ἀνιλυσπάομαι.definition: Dep., wind one's way or struggle upwards, Hsch.; wrongly written

ἀνίμησις.definition: drawing up, of water, Simp.in Ph.571.6, Suid

ἀνισάζω.definition: equalize, Hp.Vict.3.85, Arist.IA708b14, Cael.293a2:— Pass., ib.297b12

ἀνισοβαρής.definition: unequal in weight, Simp.in Cael.225.34, Alex.Aphr.in Top.166.24, 173.18

ἀνισοδιάστατος.definition: having their three dimensions unequal, ibid

ἀνισοκρατέω.definition: to be unequal in strength, S.E.M.10.28

ἀνισοπαχέω.definition: to be of unequal thickness, HeroStereom.2.59.4

ἀνισοπληθής.definition: unequal in number, of polygons, Papp.308.6

ἀνισόρροπος.definition: unequally balanced, unfair, Plu.Nob.6, Phlp.in Ph.677.25

ἀνισοσκελής.definition: with uneven legs, Sch.D.P.175; with tails of unequal length, of a bandage, Heliod. ap. Orib.48.63 tit

ἀνισοταχής.definition: unequally rapid, Ph.2.637; Theo Sm.p.189H. Adv. Alex.Aphr.in Mete.39.17, Them.in Ph.133.11, Procl.Hyp.2.14

ἀνισόχρονος.definition: of unequal duration, Herodic. ap. Orib.8.4.6; in Metric, composed of unequal times, Aristid.Quint.1.24

ἀνιστορέω.definition: make inquiry into, ask about, S.OT578: c. acc. pers. et rei, ask a person about a thing, kei/nwn a A.Pr.963, cf. S.OC991, Ph.253; . . E.Supp.110; Id.Hipp.92; investigate, Thphr.CP1.5.5

ἀνιστόρητος.definition: ignorant of history, uninformed; uninvestigated, Ph.Bel.78.36; unrecorded, Phld.Mus.p.28K., Plu.2.731c; Agatharch.58,84

ἀνίσχυρος.definition: not strong, without strength, Str.2.1.36, v.l. in D.H.4.54, Sch.Theoc.14.15: Comp., Hp.Flat.8; invalid, of a document, PSI183.9 , Just.Nov.72.5

ἀννωνεύομαι.definition: Pass., to have as an allowance , OGI200.20

ἀννώνη.definition: = Lat. annona, CIG4447 , OGI200.16 , POxy.1192.4 , al

ἀνοδύρομαι.definition: break into wailing, E.Hyps.Fr.1 iv 7, X.Cyr.5.1.6, Plu.2.123c

ἀνοησία.definition: want of understanding, Suid. s.v; opp. un-knowing, i.e. mystical vision, Porph.Sent.25

ἀνοηταίνω.definition: to be devoid of intelligence, Pl.Phlb.12d, Henioch.5, Plot.5.5.1; opp. 2.9.1:—also Sch.Ar.Nu.1480

ἀνοιδαίνω.definition: blow up, inflate, Poll.4.179: aor. inf; intr., = Nic.Fr.68.7

ἀνοίκειος.definition: not of the family, S.E.P.1.67: Comp; unfitting, unseasonable, Cic.Att.16.11.4, D.S.3.56, Plu.2.102a: c. gen., foreign to, incongruous with, Epicur.Ep.3p.60U., Plb.6.10.1, 24.5.13, D.S.12.21: c. dat., dissimilar to, Pl…

ἀνοικείωτος.definition: not to be adapted, alien, M.Ant.12.30

ἀνοικισμός.definition: = foreg., Str.9.2.17, prob. in; rebuilding, restoration, Hdn.3.6.9

ἀνοικοδεσπότητος.definition: Astrol., without a dominant planet, Vett. Val.134.17, 151.5

ἀνοικοδομέω.definition: wall up, Ar.Pax100; Lycurg.128; dub.l. in D.S.11.21; build again, rebuild, Th.1.89, cf. Jusj. ap. Lycurg.81, X.HG4.4.19, etc.; occupy again with buildings, D.S.15.66:—Pass., metaph., to be exalted, LXXMa.3.15

ἀνοικοδομή.definition: rebuilding, restoration, PLond.2.216.18, PAmh.93.19 ; Dor. IG12.9

ἀνοικονόμητος.definition: not set in order, unarranged, Macho; Act., managing badly, Plu.2.517e, v.l. in Gell.12.12.4

ἀνοιμώζω.definition: wail aloud, A.Pers.465, Th.3.113, Telecl.1 D

ἀνοιστέος.definition: one must carry back or report, S.Ant.272, E.HF1221:—one must refer, Plu.Phoc.5; Thphr.CP4.11.8

ἀνολοφύρομαι.definition: bewail aloud, Th.8.81, X.Cyr.7.3.14, J.AJ2.6.4: c. part., . . Pl.Prt.327d

ἀνομβρία.definition: want of rain, Arist.HA606b20, D.S.1.29, J.AJ8.13.2, Ph.2.383: metaph., Antipho Soph.60

ἀνομέω.definition: to be act lawlessly; Pass., to be unlawfully used, POxy.1465.9

ἀνόμημα.definition: transgression of the law, Lys. ap. Phot.p.143 R., LXXLe.20.14, al., Stoic.3.136, D.S.17.5

ἀνομογενής.definition: of different kind, ibid. , Chrysipp.Stoic.2.81, Arr.Epict.1.20.2, Alex.Aphr.in Top.116.10, al., S.E.M.8.229

ἀνομοειδής.definition: differing in species, Plot.4.3.2, Iamb.Myst.1.19, Dam.Pr.34; v.l. for Arist.EN1163b32. Adv. Dam.Pr.37

ἀνομοιογενής.definition: of different kind, Ph.2.307. Adv. in a different gender, Sch.rec.S.Ant.74

ἀνομοιοειδής.definition: of unlike kind, heterogeneous, Arist.EN1163b32, cf. Dam.Pr.440:—hence Subst. A.D.Pron.101.22

ἀνομοιόπτωτος.definition: with unlike inflexions, Eust.1228.62. Adv. Id.631.27

ἀνομοιοσχήμων.definition: gen. of unlike form, Gal.18.774, Procl.Inst.210, Phlp.inPh.677.2

ἀνομοιότροπος.definition: differing in modality (including quantity and quality, Eustr.in APo.52.17

ἀνομοιόχρονος.definition: in Metric, of dissimilar quantity, Eust.13.7

ἀνομολογέομαι.definition: agree upon a thing, come to an; recapitulate, sum up one's conclusions, Pl.Smp.200e

ἀνομολογία.definition: verbal agreement, Hsch; disagreement, Str.2.3.3, Plu.Comp.Nic.Crass.1

ἀνομόλογος.definition: not agreeing, incongruous, S.E.M.8.331, cf. Harp. s.v. Apollon.Cit.3: c. dat., Alex.Aphr.in Top.548.17. Adv. Porph.Abst.2.40

ἀνομολογούμενος.definition: not agreeing, inconsistent; not admitted, not granted, Arist.Rh.1396b28, cf. 1400a15:—Adj., compd. of priv. and for a Verb disagree with, does not occur. Adv. Gal.5.470

ἀνοργάζω.definition: lit. knead up: in Pass; toss, dandle, Hsch

ἀνορεκτέω.definition: have no appetite, Antyll. ap. Orib.5.29.8, Sor.2.43

ἀνορθόω.definition: aor. EAlc.1138, Isoc.5.64, etc; restore to health or well-being, S.OT46: Pl.Lg.919d

ἀνόρθωσις.definition: restoration, PRyl.157.13 ; = Ph.Fr.54 H.; f.l. in Plb.15.20.5, Corn.ND16

ἀνορμάομαι.definition: Pass., start up, try eagerly to do a thing, c. acc. cogn., Opp.H.3.105.—Hsch. has the Act. in neut. signf., and so Ruf. ap. Orib.45.30.40, mount, of a disease

ἀνόρνυμι.definition: fut. rouse, stir up, Pi.N.9.8; A.R.4.1352:—Pass., up he started, Il.23.812, cf. Od.8.3; A.R.1.349

ἀνορχέομαι.definition: leap up and dance, E.Supp.719; of the soul, Ph.1.379

ἀνοσιουργέω.definition: act impiously, wickedly, Pl.Lg.905b, Ph.2.128, D.C.56.5,77.12

ἀνόσφραντος.definition: that cannot be smelt, Arist.de An.421b6:—also Alex.Aphr.de An.52.15

ἀνοτοτύζω.definition: break out into wailing, A.Ag.1074, E.Hel.371

Ἀνουβιδεῖον.definition: sanctuary of A., Roussel Cultes Égyptiens 224 :— also ib.229, 231

ἀνοχλίζω.definition: heave up, A.R.1.1167, Opp.H.5.128, Hsch; heave out of the way, A.R.3.1298

ἀνταγανακτέω.definition: to be indignant in turn, Oenom. ap. Eus.PE6.7

ἀνταγαπάω.definition: love in turn or return, in Pass., Ph.2.8, Them.Or.4.55d

ἀνταγωνίζομαι.definition: struggle against, prove a match for, esp. in war, Hdt.5.109, Th.6.72, X.Cyr.1.6.8, etc.; D.43.81; Inscr.Prien.17.15, cf. Ep.Hebr.12.4

ἀνταγωνιστής.definition: opponent, competitor, rival, Dialex.2.7, X.Cyr.1.6.8, 3.3.36, Alex.272; X.Hier.4.6, etc.; a rival in love, E.Tr.1006, cf. Pl.R.554e, al.; Isoc.4.75; opponents of their system of education, Arist.Pol.1338b37; Plb.2.45.5

ἀνταγώνιστος.definition: in Poll.3.141, is interpreted, contending as an adversary;—but is f.l. for in Lib.Decl.15.21

ἀνταδικέω.definition: injure in return, retaliate upon, Pl.Tht.173a, cf.Cri.49b, 49c, Max.Tyr.18.5

ἀντᾴδω.definition: sing in answer, esp. of the partridge, answer when another calls, Arist.HA614a11, cf. Mir.845b25, Ael.NA4.16; Luc.Pisc.6; Plu.2.794c; cry out at one, Ar.Ec.887:—Pass., Poll.4.112

ἀνταίρω.definition: Ion. , raise against; intr., rise up or rebel against, withstand, Pl.Euthd.272a, D.2.24; or Id.6.5, Plu.Pyrrh.15, D.H.6.48:—so in Med., Luc.Herm.33, JTr.34

ἀνταισχύνομαι.definition: to be ashamed in turn, Ach.Tat.8.4

ἀντακολουθέω.definition: to be reciprocally implied, of the virtues, Chrysipp.Stoic.3.72, cf. S.E.P.1.68 ; Anon.in Tht.11.16; Hermog.Id.1.10, cf. Them.in Ph.150.29

ἀντακολούθησις.definition: reciprocal implication, of the virtues, Stoic.3.76, Procl.in Alc.p.319C

ἀντακόλουθος.definition: reciprocally implied, Eustr.in EN311.15: abs., corresponding, dub. in Phld.Rh.1.27S

ἀντακούω.definition: fut. S.Aj.1141, hear in turn, Id.OT544; E.Heracl.1014 ; Id.Supp.569; S.Aj.1141: abs., listen in return, A.Eu.198, cf. Crates Com.5D.: also in Prose, X.An.2.5.16, Lib.Decl.5.89

ἀνταλαλάζω.definition: return a shout, of friendly armies, Plu.Pyrrh.32, Flam.4; of an echo, A.Pers.390

ἀντάλλαγμα.definition: that which is given or taken in exchange, for a friend, E.Or.1157, cf. LXXJb.28.15, al.; Ev.Matt.16.26, cf. Ph.Fr.110H

ἀνταλλάσσω.definition: Att. exchange one thing with; more freq. in Med., take in exchange, A.Ch.133; take one thing in exchange for another, E.Hel.1088, etc.; D.16.5; interchange in thought, Pl.Tht.189c; shall receive death in exchange, i.e…

ἀνταμελέω.definition: in fut. Pass. neglect in turn, Ph.2.275

ἀνταναβιβάζω.definition: make go up in turn, X.HG3.2.15

ἀνταναγιγνώσκω.definition: read and compare, Cratin.386; D.20 Arg.ii 8, cf. PPetr.3p.50

ἀνταναιρέω.definition: strike out of an account, D.18.231:—Pass; kill in return, Ph.2.321

ἀντανάκλασις.definition: reflection of light; bending back, Sch.Opp.H.1.216

ἀντανακλάω.definition: reflect, v.l. in Plu.2.696a:—Pass; of sound, in Pass., to be reflected or echoed, LXXWi.17.19, Placit.4.20.2

ἀντανάλυσις.definition: counteraction, incongruity of position, Vett. Val.186.28, Antioch.Astr.inCat.Cod.Astr.8.107

ἀνταναπίμπλημι.definition: fill in return, v.l. in X.HG2.4.12

ἀνταναπληρόω.definition: fill up, A.D.Synt.14.1; Ep.Col.1.24; put in the poorest so as to balance the richest, D.14.17

ἀντάνειμι.definition: rise so as to balance, Th.2.75

ἀντανίστημι.definition: set up against or in rivalry; Pass., with aor. 2 Act., rise up against, S.Tr.441, cf. Plu.Sull.7; rise one against another, Id.2.723b

ἀντανίσωσις.definition: balancing, equalizing, Boethus ap. Porph. ap. Eus.PE11.28, DavidProll.214.11, Simp.in Cael.458.2

ἀνταπαιτέω.definition: demand in return, Th.3.58, 5.17, Plu.Sol.3:—Pass., to be called on for a thing in turn, Id.Cat.Mi.53

ἀνταπειλέω.definition: threaten in turn, Ph.2.469, cf. Them.Or.7.95b

ἀνταποδείκνυμι.definition: or prove in return or; appoint instead, D.C.49.43

ἀνταποδίδωμι.definition: give back, repay, tender in repayment or; take vengeance, LXXDe.32.35, al., Ep.Rom.12.19

ἀνταπόδομα.definition: repayment, requital, whether of good or evil, LXXSi.12.2, 14.6, al., Ev.Luc.14.12, Ep.Rom.11.9

ἀνταπόδοσις.definition: giving back in turn, opp; turning back, opposite direction or course, of a current, Plb.4.43.5, etc., cf. Plu.2.136b

ἀνταποθνήσκω.definition: die or am killed in requital, Antipho5.10; Ph.1.94

ἀνταποκατάστασις.definition: renewal by substitution; of planets, the opposite position to Doroth.ap.Cat.Cod.Astr.2.196.19

ἀνταποκρίνομαι.definition: Med., answer again, LXXJb.16.8; correspond to, Nicom.Ar.1.8.10, 11

ἀνταποκτείνω.definition: kill in return, Hdt.7.136, A.Ch.121, E.Hec.262, Ar.Ach.326, X.HG2.4.27, etc

ἀνταπολαμβάνω.definition: receive or accept in return, Pl.Ti.27b; D.20.46

ἀνταπόλλυμι.definition: destroy in return, E.Ion1328, Pl.Cri.51a; Pass. and Med., with pf. 2 Act., perish in turn, E.Hel.106, cf.IT715; Hdt.3.14

ἀνταπολογέομαι.definition: speak for the defence or in reply, Is.5.17, D.C.50.2

ἀνταποστέλλω.definition: send in exchange, Plb.21.43.22; send backwards and forwards, D.C.50.2, cf. Aen.Tact.31.9 ; refer one back again, S.E.M.8.86; of an echo, Plu.2.248c

ἀνταποταφρεύω.definition: cut off in turn by trenches, App.BC2.61

ἀνταποτειχίζω.definition: wall off, fortify on the other side, D.C.43.7

ἀνταποφαίνω.definition: show on the other hand, Th.3.38,67

ἀνταποφέρω.definition: catch in turn, of a ball, Poll.9.107

ἀνταρκέω.definition: hold out against, Th.7.15; abs., hold out, persist, Ar.Eq.540, Isoc.6.79, 19.26: c. part., . . D.C.68.25

ἀντασπάζομαι.definition: welcome, greet in turn, X.Cyr.1.3.3; return greeting, Hierocl.Facet.7; receive kindly, X.Cyr.5.5.42, Pl.Com.12D., Plu.Tim.38

ἀντατιμάζω.definition: requite with dishonour, prob. cj. in S.Aj.1339

ἀνταυγασία.definition: reflection of light, Gloss.:—also or Placit.2.20.12, X.Cyn.5.18, Plu.2.921b, Ps.-Hp.Hebd.1.52; Onos.29.2; from the snow, D.S.17.82; shining in one's face, Ascl.Tact.12.10

ἀνταυγέω.definition: reflect light, Hp.Carn.17, Arist.Pr.932a27, Chaerem.14; Emp.44; flashes back murder, E.Or.1519; gleam, glitter, Eub.56

ἀνταυγής.definition: reflecting light, sparkling, Sannyr.1D.; Ar.Th.902; D.S.17.82: pr. n. of the sun, Orph.Fr.237

ἀνταφίημι.definition: let go in turn, let the tear; send back, Poll.9.107

ἀντεγκαλέω.definition: make a counter-claim, D.40.14; bring a countercharge, Isoc.17.12, D.H.8.64, Plu.Ant.55, etc.; Hermog.Stat.3

ἀντεικάζω.definition: fut. Pl.Men.8cc: aor. Ar.V.1311, subj. Pl. l.c.:—compare in return, Ar. l.c.: c. acc., Pl. l.c.:—hence Sch.Ven.Il.8.560

ἀντείρομαι.definition: Ion. aor. Att. in turn, Hdt.1.129, 3.23, X.Cyr.2.2.22: in part., Plu.2.739b

ἀντεισβάλλω.definition: intr., make an inroad in reprisal, D.C.48.21

ἀντεισέρχομαι.definition: enter in turn or instead, Aristid.Or.37.27, HeroSpir.2.36, Them.in Ph.113.26

ἀντεισκρίνομαι.definition: to be introduced in place of, HeroSpir.1.3

ἀντεισοδιάζω.definition: bring in, introduce in turn, Sch.D.T.p.72H

ἀντεκβάλλομαι.definition: to be produced in an opposite direction, Theol. Ar.26; to be correspondingly projected, Anon.in EN224.24

ἀντεκκομίζω.definition: carry out or away in return, in fut. Hsch

ἀντεκκόπτω.definition: knock out in return, D.24.140; Arist.MM1194a38, cf. D.S.12.17

ἀντεκτίθημι.definition: set forth or state instead, Plu.Arat.1; contrast with, S.E.M.1.251

ἀντελαττόομαι.definition: to be worsted in turn, D.C.44.27

ἀντελπίζω.definition: hope instead or in turn, Th.1.70; Lib.Decl.26.28

ἀντεμβάλλω.definition: intr., make an inroad in turn, X.HG3.5.4, Plb.5.96.3; attack in turn, Plu.Phil.18

ἀντεμβιβάζω.definition: put on board instead, Th.7.13, cf. D.4.37

ἀντεμβοάω.definition: shout at a person in answer, AB85, Eust.855.21

ἀντεμπήγνυμαι.definition: aor. 2 Pass., to be plunged in in revenge, Ar.Ach.230

ἀντεμπίπλημι.definition: fill in turn, X.HG2.4.12; fill in return, by way of compensation, Id.An.4.5.28:—Pass., to be filled with in exchange, Pl.Lg.705b

ἀντεμπίπρημι.definition: set on fire in return, Hdt.5.102

ἀντεμπλέκομαι.definition: Pass., to be entwined together, Dsc.4.75, cf. Poll.1.184; of crossed or reversed bandaging, Sor.Fasc.12.513C.:—return one's embraces or salutation, J.AJ16.2.5

ἀντεμπλοκή.definition: mutual entwining, M.Ant.7.50; crossing of veins, Gal.in Pl.Ti.7; complication, confusion, M.Ant.6.10

ἀντέμφασις.definition: difference of appearance, Str.2.4.8; also pl., ibid.; opposition, antithesis, S.E.M.1.57; distinction, Hdn.Gr.1.941, A.D.Adv.159.19

ἀντεναντίωσις.definition: Rhet., positive statement made in a negative form, as for Alex.Fig.2.23, Zonae.Fig.22

ἀντενδείκνυμαι.definition: give contrary indications, of symptoms, Gal.10.626

ἀντενδίδωμι.definition: give way in turn, of sawyers, Ar.V.694

ἀντενέχυρον.definition: counter-pledge, Sch.A.R.1.1355:—hence take a counter-pledge, Hsch. s.v

ἀντενίστημι.definition: insert instead, prob. rest. in IGRom.4.293 i37

ἀντεντίθημι.definition: insert in turn or instead, Nicom.Ar.2.27

ἀντεξανίσταμαι.definition: Pass., with aor. 2 Act., rise up against, Hld.7.19

ἀντεξελαύνω.definition: charge against, attack, Plu.Phil.18, al., D.C.47.43

ἀντεξετάζω.definition: try one by the standard of another, Aeschin.1.8,37, Arr.Epict.2.18.21; Plu.Caes.3, cf. Gal.18.229; Them.in Ph.52.20; compare, Luc.Herm.30, cf. Aps.p.247 H., etc.:—Pass., to be measured or compared, or Plu.Tim.36, 2.65…

ἀντεξέτασις.definition: comparison, A.D.Synt.161.10; term of comparison, of an integer compared with the sum of the preceding integers, Theol.Ar.10

ἀντεξήγησις.definition: counter-explanation, title of work by Didymus, Ath.14.634c

ἀντεξόρμησις.definition: sailing against, v.l. in Th.2.91; countercharge, Plu.Pomp.69

ἀντεπαινέω.definition: praise in return, X.Cyr.8.3.49; Pass., to be extolled in comparison with, Luc.Pr.Im.19

ἀντέπειμι.definition: rush upon, meet an advancing enemy, Th.4.33,96, etc.; Id.7.6, cf.Lib.Decl.37.15, Onos.8.2; Id.21.8

ἀντεπεισάγομαι.definition: to be carried in or enter instead, Ti.Locr.102a; f.l. for sq., Placit. 4.22.1

ἀντεπέκτασις.definition: stretching in the opposite direction, Hsch. s.v

ἀντεπεκτείνω.definition: stretch in the contrary direction, Gal.18.213

ἀντεπεξάγω.definition: intr., sail or march out against, Th.8.104, Luc.Bacch.3: c. acc., J.AJ6.9.1, 8.14.4:—also in Med., D.C.50.31

ἀντεπέξειμι.definition: march out to meet an enemy, Th.7.37: abs., X.Cyr.3.3.30, etc

ἀντεπέρχομαι.definition: march against in return, Aristid.1.150J., cf. D.C.36.51
