ἀντεπερωτάω.definition: ask a question in turn, PLond.1.118.70

ἀντεπιγράφω.definition: write something instead, D.22.72:—Med., put their own names instead of the other party to the victory, i.e. claim it, Plb.18.34.2

ἀντεπιδείκνυμι.definition: exhibit in turn, Pl.Tht.162b: c. part., contrast, X.Ages.1.12:—Med., exhibit oneself in competition, Plu.2.674b: also c. acc. rei, display a fine sight in rivalry with, Id.Ant.23; also Id.Alex.21

ἀντεπιθυμέω.definition: desire a thing in rivalry with, And.4.28:—Pass., and have one's company desired in turn, X.Mem.2.6.28

ἀντεπικηρύσσω.definition: put a price on one's head in return, Poll.4.93

ἀντεπικρατέω.definition: get the upper hand in turn, Str.16.1.19, D.C.44.27

ἀντεπιλαμβάνομαι.definition: lay hold on the other side, Luc.Symp.43

ἀντεπιμελέομαι.definition: or attend or give heed in turn, v.l. X.Cyr.5.1.18; to one, Id.An.3.1.16

ἀντεπινοέω.definition: devise in turn, Ael.NA6.23, J.AJ10.8.1: c. inf., App.BC4.109

ἀντεπιπλέω.definition: sail against in turn, Th.1.54 and prob. in 1.50, Poll.1.124

ἀντεπισπάω.definition: gloss on Hsch.:—Med., Ph.1.247; absorb nutriment, Gal.17 .312

ἀντεπιστέλλω.definition: write an answer, CPR20ii5 : c. inf., J.AJ15.6.2,al.; Luc.Sat.19:—Pass., Paus.4.22.6, etc

ἀντεπιστρέφω.definition: turn against, retort, Plu.2.810e; turn round and back, of a needle, Gal.10.418

ἀντεπιστροφή.definition: turning back upon, Placit.4.14.3; Ruf. ap. Orib.49.35.4

ἀντεπιτειχίζω.definition: raise a counter-work: metaph., Him.Or.7.13: so as Dep. with pf. Pass., establish a fort in the enemy's country, Th.1.142

ἀντεπιτίθημι.definition: put on in exchange, D.C.58.7; give a letter in answer, Th.1.129, Is.Fr.49, cf. J.AJ17.5.1

ἀντεπιτρέχω.definition: · Suid.; turn and attack, of animals at bay, Ph.2.354

ἀντεπιχειρέω.definition: make a counter-attack, Str.5.2.2, cf; make attempts to prove the contrary, Arist.Top.160b10; controversial efforts to prove or disprove, S.E.M.9.191

ἀντεργολαβέω.definition: compete with, in a thing, Posidipp.3.1

ἀντερείδω.definition: set firmly against; intr., stand firm, resist pressure, offer resistance, opp. X.Cyr.8.8.16, cf. Cyn.10.16, Pl.Ti.45c, Arist.MA698b18, Epicur.Fr.76 bis; exert counter-pressure, Hp.Fract.14; offers resistance in the di…

ἀντερίζω.definition: strive against, contend, Philostr.Her.12b, cf. Hsch

ἀντερῶ.definition: fut. without any pres. in use: pf. S.Ant.47 :—speak against, gainsay, S.l.c.; A.Ag.539; Ar.Nu.1079; Ach.701; Pl.R.580a:—Pass., no denial shall be given, S.Tr.1184; Gal.5.477

ἀντερωτάω.definition: question in turn, Pl.Euthd.295b, cf. Aeschin.3.226, Aen.Tact.24.16, Plu.Cor.18

ἀντευεργέτης.definition: one who returns kindnesses, Asp.in EN113.14, Sch.A.R.2.321

ἀντεφεστιάω.definition: entertain in return, Ph.2.139, Philostr.VS2.5.3, Ael.NA9.45, 15.7; as f.l. for Pl.Ti.17b

ἀντεφήδομαι.definition: aor. inf. exult over in turn, Ph.2.313

ἀντεφοδιάζομαι.definition: Pass., to be furnished instead of provisions: metaph. in J.AJ15.9.1

ἀντεφορμάω.definition: rush against, attack, Hld.8.16: abs., Ph.2.122

ἀντηχέω.definition: Dor. Theoc.Ep.4.11 :—sing in; abs., sound responsively, of a musical string, Arist.Pr.919b16; of bronze vessels, Aen.Tact.37.7, Plb.22.11.12; resound, Hp.Morb.4.56, cf. Carn.18, Luc.VH1.38; echo, Plu.2.414c

ἀντιβαδίζω.definition: go against, the contrary way, Phot. s.v

ἀντιβάκχειος.definition: the foot – – ;⏑, Diom.1.513 K., al.: —also Ter.Maur.1411

ἀντιβάλλω.definition: throw against or in turn, Th.7.25 (the acc; put one against the other, compare, collate, of Mss., Str.13.1.54, 17.1.5, POxy.1479 ; match, compare with, Opp.C.1.68; exchange words in conversation, Ev.Luc.24.17; weigh w…

ἀντιβασιλεύω.definition: reign as a rival king, J.BJ4.7.1

ἀντιβιάζομαι.definition: use force against, AP12.183 : abs., Ph.1.295,al.:—Pass., 2.423

ἀντιβιβρώσκω.definition: fut. Pass. eat in turn, Ath.7.343c

ἀντιβλασφημέω.definition: retaliate with abuse, Sch.Aristid. p.673 D

ἀντιβλέπω.definition: fut. D.25.98:—look straight at, look in the face, c. dat. pers., X.HG5.4.27; Com.Adesp.22.41 D.; or X.Mem.4.7.7, Thphr.Sens.18: metaph., Plu.Comp.Dem.Cic.3: c. acc., Men.586: abs., part., . . facing one another, Arist…

ἀντίβλεψις.definition: looking in the face, look, X.Hier.1.35, Plu.2.681b

ἀντιβοάω.definition: return a cry, of an echo, Bion1.38; call aloud in answer, J.BJ3.5.4: c. acc., prob. in Euph.80; Him.Ecl.2.4

ἀντιβοηθέω.definition: help in turn, Th.6.18,7.58, Pl.R.559e, X.HG7.4.2

ἀντιβομβέω.definition: return a humming sound, Ach.Tat.3.2, cf. Eust.1885.19

ἀντιγενεηλογέω.definition: Ion. form, give a different pedigree, Hdt.2.143

ἀντιγεννάω.definition: generate in rivalry, Lync. ap. Ath.7.285f; or in return, Ph.1.89

ἀντιγηροτροφέω.definition: support in old age in turn, Lesb.Rh.2.10

ἀντιγνωμονέω.definition: to be of a different opinion, D.C.46.44; think that a thing is otherwise, X.Cyr.4.3.8

ἀντιγραφεία.definition: office of PPetr.3p.162, PTeb.5.85 , cf. Inscr.Prien.108.222

ἀντιγραφεῖον.definition: office whence were issued, Jahresh.7 Beibl.44 , cf.ib.18 Beibl.286

ἀντιγραφεύς.definition: checking- or copying-clerk, a public officer, Aeschin.3.25. cf. IG2.408, al., cf. 575 , SIG364.22 , etc., Plb.6.56.13, PRev.Laws 12.1; one who keeps a check upon their accounts, D.22.70

ἀντίγραφος.definition: copied, in duplicate; as Subst., transcript, copy, Decr. ap. And.1.79, Lys.32.7, D.25.47, Arist.Pol.1309a11; esp. of copies of a book, copies of an edition issued by Atticus, Harp. s.v. al.; certified copy of official…

ἀντιγράφω.definition: write against or in answer, write back; Med., with pf. Pass. , as law-term, put in as an plead against, Is.11.17, cf.D.48.31; also c. inf., plead against another that such is the case, Lys.23.5, D.44.39:—also, bring a…

ἀντίγραψις.definition: putting in of an v.l. in Lys.23.10

ἀντιδάκνω.definition: fut. Muson.Fr.10p.55H.: the aor. dub. in Luc.Ocyp.27:—bite in turn, Hdt.4.168, Ael.NA4.19, Muson. l.c

ἀντιδαπανάω.definition: or spend in turn upon, Lib.Ep.843

ἀντιδεξιόομαι.definition: give the right hand in turn, return one's salute, X.Cyr.4.2.19, D.Chr.38.47, Luc.Laps.13

ἀντιδέχομαι.definition: receive in return, A.Ch.916; Cat.Cod. Astr.2.211; E.IA1222

ἀντιδημιουργέομαι.definition: Med., manufacture in competition, Lync. ap. Ath.11.469b

ἀντιδιαβαίνω.definition: cross over in turn, X.Ages.1.8, dub.l. J.AJ13.1.3

ἀντιδιαγράφω.definition: pay in money instead of kind, PPetr.2p.102 :—Med., Inscr.Magn.103.68 :—hence Ostr.1509, al

ἀντιδιαζεύγνυμαι.definition: pair off with, in dichotomy, S.E.M.11.15; to be subjoined in turn, A.D.Synt.126.10

ἀντιδιαίρεσις.definition: in Logic, division by; in Surgery, counter-incision, Paul.Aeg.4.48

ἀντιδιάκειμαι.definition: to be different, of mixed stuffs, Aq.De.22.11

ἀντιδιακοσμέω.definition: arrange or array in opposition, of troops, App.BC2.75

ἀντιδιαλέγομαι.definition: reply to, answer in discussion, in Pass., title of work by Chrysipp., D.L.7.202

ἀντιδιαλλάσσομαι.definition: Med., exchange prisoners; of historians, differ in an account, Id.1.84

ἀντιδιαστέλλω.definition: distinguish, discriminate, Str.10.2.17; contrast, oppose, S.E.P.1.9; D.H.Th.32; Alex.Aphr.in Metaph.400.17:—Pass., A.D.Synt.14.24

ἀντιδιατάσσομαι.definition: Med., oppose, Arr.Epict.3.24.24; S.E.M.7.159: abs., ib.8.126

ἀντιδιατίθημι.definition: retaliate upon a person, D.S.34.12; Eust.546.28:—Med., offer resistance, Longin.17.1; opponents, 2 Ep.Ti.2.25

ἀντιδιδάσκω.definition: inform, instruct in turn or on the other; of dramatists, etc., contend for the prize, Ar.V.1410, cf. Satyr.Vit.Eur.Fr.38.19, D.Chr.37.40

ἀντιδίδωμι.definition: give in return, repay, Hdt.1.70; give for or instead of, E.Alc.340, IT28; Ar.Pax1251

ἀντιδιηγέομαι.definition: introduce a counter narration; relate in turn, X.Eph.5.10

ἀντιδικέω.definition: impf. Lys.6.12, but; Pass., to be an object of dispute, Phot.p.147R

ἀντιδικία.definition: litigation, contention, Plu.2.483b; the opponent in a process, Mitteis Chr.88.14 ; Astrol., opp. Ptol.Tetr.191

ἀντίδικος.definition: opponent or adversary in a suit, Aeschin.2.165, cf. Pl.Phdr.273c: fem., POxy.37i8 : properly, the defendant, Antipho1.2; but also, the plaintiff, Lys.7.13; Antipho1.5:—generally, opponent, adversary, A.Ag.41; [Heracli…

ἀντιδιορίζω.definition: define in turn, give a counter-definition, Gal.18.837

ἀντιδοκέω.definition: think oneself equal to, LXX2 Ma.9.8

ἀντιδοξάζω.definition: to be of a contrary opinion, Pl.Tht.170d, Epicur.Nat.14.8, Phld.Sign.19, cf. 31, D.L.9.18

ἀντιδοξέω.definition: = foreg., or Plb.2.56.1,16.14.4; D.S.2.29: abs., Boeth.Stoic.3.267

ἀντίδοξος.definition: of a different opinion or sect, Luc.Herm.17, Aristaenet.1.10; Luc.Par.29

ἀντιδυσχεραίνω.definition: to be angry in turn, M.Ant.6.26

ἀντιδωρέομαι.definition: present in return, one with a thing, Hdt.2.30; a thing to one, E.Hel.159, cf. Pl.Euthphr.14e; offer instead Arist.EN1159b14

ἀντίζηλος.definition: rival, adversary, LXXLe.18.18, Si.26.6: as Adj., controversial, in rivalry, Vett.Val.198.11: Astrol., Porph. in Ptol.Tetr.186

ἀντιθεραπεύω.definition: take care of in turn; court in return, in Pass., J.AJ17.2.4, Max.Tyr.20.6

ἀντίθεσις.definition: opposition, Pl.Sph.257e,258b; in Logic, opposition of propositions, in pl., Arist.Int.19b20, Top.113b15, Metaph.1054a23

ἀντιθυμόομαι.definition: show anger in turn, Ael.NA17.13 codd

ἀντικαθαιρέω.definition: pull down or destroy in turn, D.C.46.34

ἀντικάθημαι.definition: Ion. properly pf. of; mostly of armies or fleets, lie over against, so as to watch each other, Hdt.9.39, cf. 41, Th.5.6, X.Eq.Mag.8.12, etc.: metaph., S.E.M.1.145

ἀντικαθίζομαι.definition: Act., place or settle instead of another, LXX4 Ki.17.26

ἀντικαθίστημι.definition: set against, oppose, Th.4.93; establish as a counterpart, Pl.R.591a

ἀντικαλλωπίζομαι.definition: adorn oneself in rivalry with, Plu.2.406d

ἀντικαταδύομαι.definition: stoop down in turn or in opposition, Ach Tat.6.18

ἀντικατάδυσις.definition: setting in the opposite quarter, in pl., Hipparch.2.1.14, 2.2.1

ἀντικαταθνῄσκω.definition: aor.2 die or be slain in turn, A.Ch.144

ἀντικατακλείω.definition: in Pass., to be enclosed in turn, Ruf.Oss.38

ἀντικαταλαμβάνω.definition: take possession of in turn; occupy in opposition, D.C.36.47, cf. 42.31

ἀντικαταλέγω.definition: enroll instead, soldiers or senators, Id.40.65, 54.14

ἀντικαταλείπω.definition: leave in one's stead, Pl.R.540b, Pyth.Sim.36

ἀντικαταλλαγή.definition: exchange, Plu.2.49d, cf. PFlor. 47.15 ; requital, Sch.Opp.H.2.687

ἀντικαταλλάσσομαι.definition: give one thing for another, Lycurg.88; Isoc.5.135; receive one thing in exchange for another, Id.6.109, Aeschin.3.92, D.Chr.40.30

ἀντικαταμετρέω.definition: assign land in compensation or exchange, PTeb. 61b111,72.39

ἀντικαταμύω.definition: shut one's eyes in turn, Poll.9.113

ἀντικαταρρέω.definition: flow down, drip in turn, Olymp.in Mete.80.36, al., Steph.in Hp.1.130D., al.; run back again, Gal.8.285

ἀντικατασκευάζω.definition: establish instead, D.H.1.5; 'paint in the opposite colours', J.AJ16.7.1

ἀντικατάστασις.definition: being confronted with one another, Plb.4.47.4; opposition, J.AJ16.2.5; Decr.ib.14.10.21, cf. SIG785.7

ἀντικατατείνω.definition: make counter-extension, Hp.Fract.14; metaph., if we speak setting speech directly in contrast with speech against him, Pl.R.348a, cf. Plu.2.669e

ἀντικαταφέρομαι.definition: to be carried down again, Gal.17.57

ἀντικατηγορέω.definition: accuse in turn, recriminate upon; Pass., in Logic, to be convertible, Arist.Top.102a19, al.; reciprocate, of cause and effect, Id.APo.73a16, cf. 78a28

ἀντίκειμαι.definition: to be opposite to, of places, Hp.Aër.4; Str.2.5.15; of things, to be opposite or opposed, Pl.Sph.258b; in a circle, Arist.Cael.277a23, al. Adv. PA654a11

ἀντικηδεύω.definition: mind, tend instead of another, E.Ion734:—also Poll.5.142

ἀντικηρύσσω.definition: proclaim in answer to, E.Supp.673; in opposition to, Lib.Decl.39.45

ἀντικίνησις.definition: contrary motion, Corp.Herm.2.6, Simp.in Ph.677.20, Id.in Cael.366.8,395.29

ἀντικλαίω.definition: Att. weep in return, Hdt.3.14 , Eust.37.14

ἀντικομίζω.definition: bring back as an answer, Plu.Lys.26:—Med., receive in exchange, J.BJ2.8.4, App.BC4.70

ἀντικοπή.definition: beating back, hindrance, check, Epicur.Ep.1p.10U.; resistance, Id.Nat.Herc.908.4; Plu.2.77a; clashing, of streams meeting, Str.5.2.5

ἀντικορύσσομαι.definition: Med., take arms against, AP7.668 , Ath.15.701b

ἀντικοσμέω.definition: arrange in turn, Plu.2.813d; adorn in turn, ib.828a :—Pass., Aristid.Or.25 .33:—Subst. Suid

ἀντικοσμήτης.definition: IG3.1120, al.:— hence discharge this office, ib.1126

ἀντικράζω.definition: pf. to shout in return, J.BJ6.2.3

ἀντίκρουσις.definition: abrupt close, in a rhetorical period, Arist.Rh.1409b22; hindrance, check, Plu.2.721b; dub. sens. in Aeschin.1.168, perh. repartee

ἀντικρούω.definition: strike or clash against, come into; in a physical sense, . . Arist.Cael.313b2: abs., Id.PA642a36, al., cf. Pl.Lg.857c; Lib.Decl.37.8

ἀντικτυπέω.definition: aor. ring in response, AP14.10.3; clash against, APl.4.221 : abs., Procop.Goth.2.23

ἀντικυμαίνομαι.definition: Pass., boil with conflicting waves, dash hither and thither, Plu.2.897c; of wind in a cul-de-sac, surge back, Orib.9.20.3

ἀντικωμάζω.definition: celebrate by a festival in turn, Sch.Pi.P.9.156

ἀντιλαγχάνω.definition: pf. D.40.3:—as law-term, move for; enter an exceptive plea, Id.37.33

ἀντιλάζομαι.definition: or poet. and Dor. Prose for take hold of, hold by, c. gen., E.IA1227; Theag. ap. Stob.3.1.67, cf. Archyt.ib.117; take a share of, partake in, E.Or.452, etc. 2. c. acc., to receive in turn, to be repaid, . . Id.Supp.36…

ἀντιλακτίζω.definition: kick against, Ar.Pax613; kick back in return, Plu.2.10c

ἀντιλαμβάνω.definition: receive instead of; mostly in Med., with pf. Pass. Lys.28.15, Pl.Prm.130e: c. gen., lay hold of, Thgn.1362; Pl.La.184a, cf. Prt.317d,al.; ib.335d; gain or reach it, Th.7.77, cf. Ar.Th.242: abs., Th.3.22. b. metaph.c.g…

ἀντιλάμπω.definition: inf. Sapph.Supp.3.6:—light up in; intr., reflect light, shine, X.Cyn.5.18; Plu.Arat.21; of the rainbow, Anaxag.19

ἀντιλέγω.definition: Hdt., Com., and Att. Prose; c. acc. rei, S.OT409; Lys.8.11; tell one tale in reply to another, Ar.Lys.806; Men.Epit.8:—Pass., to be disputed, questioned, X.HG6.5.37; of a place, counter-claimed, ib.3.2.30; D.27.15; po…

ἀντιλημματίζω.definition: set off in accounts, deduct, POxy.1577.11 , cf. 1578.17

ἀντιλήπτωρ.definition: later helper, protector, LXX2 Ki.22.3, BGU1139.17 , Eustr.in APo.93.19; UPZ14.18

ἀντιλόβιον.definition: upper edge of the ear, opp. Gal.14.701, Poll.2.86

ἀντιλογέω.definition: = deny, S.Ant.377; = Ar.Nu.321,al.:—in Med., Democr.85, Antipho Soph.98

ἀντιλογία.definition: contradiction, controversy; later, quarrel, dispute, PPetr.2p.56 , PGrenf. 1.38.8 , Ep.Hebr.12.3, etc

ἀντιλογίζομαι.definition: count up or calculate on the other hand, Antipho2.2.8; . . X.HG6.5.24. .)

ἀντιλοιδορέω.definition: rail at or abuse in turn, PPetr.3p.48 , Plu.2.88f , 1 Ep.Pet.2.23:—Med., c. acc. rei, Luc.Symp.40

ἀντιλύπησις.definition: vexing in return, Arist.de An.403a30, Plu.2.442b

ἀντιμαίνομαι.definition: pf. part. to be filled with; rage against, APl.1.30

ἀντιμανθάνω.definition: learn in turn or instead, Ar.V.1453

ἀντιμαρτυρέω.definition: appear as witness against, Ar.Fr.437; contradict, Plu.2.418a; opp. Polystr.p.10W.; esp. in Epicurus' Logic, disprove by fact or experience, Ep.1p.10U., al.; so Plu.2.447c: abs., Id.Alc.21, cf. Gal.4.735: c. acc., Plot…

ἀντιμαρτύρησις.definition: counter evidence, Id.Fr.247: in pl., Id.Nat.28Fr.7, Plu.2.1121e

ἀντιμαρτύρομαι.definition: protest on the other hand, Luc.Symp.47

ἀντιμάχομαι.definition: fight against one, Th.4.68: abs., D.S.22.10

ἀντιμεγαλοφρονέω.definition: vie in pride or boasting with, Eust.676.5

ἀντιμεθέλκω.definition: drag different ways, distract, Ph.1.231, cf. APl.4.136 , 139 , in Pass.; AP10.74

ἀντιμεθίστημι.definition: move from one side to the other; Pass., with aor. 2 and pf. Act., exchange places, Arist.Ph.209b25, cf. 211b27, Mete.366b20; Jul.Or.8.241a

ἀντιμέμφομαι.definition: blame in turn, retort upon one, . . Hdt.2.133

ἀντιμερίζομαι.definition: impart in turn, AP6.209 (Antip; distinguish, Hsch

ἀντιμεσουρανέω.definition: to be in the opposite meridian, as the sun at midnight, Plu.2.284e, Ptol.Tetr.33, Vett. Val.116.5,al., Man.4.613

ἀντιμεσουράνημα.definition: opposite meridian, S.E.M.5.12, Ptol.Tetr.201; name of the fourth in a 'nativity', Paul.Al.L.3

ἀντιμεσουράνησις.definition: occupation of the opposite meridian, Heph.Astr.1.2

ἀντιμεταβάλλω.definition: meet one change with another, Hp.Acut.26

ἀντιμεταβολή.definition: transposition, as a figure of speech, as in 'non ut edam vivo sed ut vivam edo', Quint.Inst.9.3.85, cf. Alex.Fig.2.22, Phoeb.Fig.2.4

ἀντιμετάγω.definition: countermarch, Onos.33.6; press in contrary direction, Heliod. ap. Orib.49.8.20

ἀντιμετακλίνω.definition: turn aside or the opposite way, Ph.1.678

ἀντιμεταλαμβάνω.definition: assume in turn or in exchange; receive back in return, Phld.Oec.p.65J., cf. Piet.113

ἀντιμετάληψις.definition: partaking of the opposite; double reflex movement, Heliod. ap. Orib.8.28.28,29

ἀντιμεταρρέω.definition: flow off in turn or back, Placit.4.22.2, but is prob

ἀντιμετασπάω.definition: draw off in a different direction, J.AJ13.5.3

ἀντιμετάστασις.definition: counter-change, reciprocal replacement, Arist.Ph.208b2; reverse movement, D.H.3.19, Simp.in Ph.1352.14

ἀντιμετατάσσω.definition: change the order of battle so as to meet the enemy, in Med., D.H.3.25

ἀντιμετατίθεμαι.definition: to be changed, replaced, J.AJ16.7.6, cf. Numen. ap. Eus.PE14.5

ἀντιμεταχωρέω.definition: go away to the other side, make room for new hope, J.AJ15.2.2

ἀντιμετειλέομαι.definition: to be unrolled in reverse direction, of cables, Orib.49.22.14

ἀντιμηχανάομαι.definition: contrive against or in opposition, Hdt.8.52, cf. E.Ba.291; Th.7.53: abs., Arist.HA613b27; X.HG5.3.16

ἀντιμηχάνημα.definition: counter-engine or device, Polyaen.4.2.20, cf. Ath.Mech.9.1

ἀντίμιμος.definition: closely imitating, of an echo; = Dsc.4.75; = Ps.-Dsc.4.28

ἀντίμισθος.definition: as a reward, in compensation, A.Supp.270

ἀντιμυκάομαι.definition: low in answer, D.H.1.39; roar against, of sea and lake, Procop.Aed.4.8

ἀντινικάω.definition: conquer in turn, A.Ch.499, cf. D.C.48.21

ἀντινομία.definition: conflict of laws, Quint.Inst.7.1.15, Hermog.Stat.2, D.22 Arg.ii 12; to be in a strait between two laws, Plu.Caes.13; ambiguity in the law, Id.2.742a

ἀντινομίζομαι.definition: Pass., prob. laws enacted against one, Archyt. ap. Stob.4.1.132

ἀντινομοθετέω.definition: make laws in rivalry with, Plu.2.1044c, etc

ἀντιοστατέω.definition: = to be contrary, of a wind, S.Ph.640

ἀντιπαθέω.definition: have an aversion, Alex.Aphr.Pr.Prooem; to be opposed, reversed in metric, as lambus or trochee, Sch.Heph.p.115C

ἀντιπαθής.definition: in return for suffering, A.Eu.782; felt; of opposite feelings or properties, Plu.2.664c; ib.940a. Adv. Gp.5.11.4, Alex.Trall.8.2

ἀντιπαιδεύω.definition: teach as a rival master, Suid. s.v

ἀντιπαίζω.definition: play one with another, X.Cyn.5.4, Pl.Erx.395b

ἀντιπαιωνίζω.definition: or sing the battle song against, Max.Tyr.32.2. cf. Aen.Tact.27.4

ἀντιπαλαίω.definition: wrestle against, POxy.1099, Sch.Ar.Ach.570, Eustr.in EN117.34

ἀντιπαραβάλλω.definition: place side by side so as to compare or; contribute instead, X.Lac.5.3

ἀντιπαραβολή.definition: reply by comparison or contrast, Arist.Rh.1414b10, 1419b34, Plu.2.40f, Longin.Fr.11, Ruf. ap. Orib.49.30.9

ἀντιπαραγγελία.definition: competition for a public office, Plu.Arat.35

ἀντιπαραγγέλλω.definition: give orders, command in turn; compete for a public office, Plu.Caes.7; Id.Mar.29; with one, Id.Cat.Mi.49

ἀντιπαραγράφω.definition: add or insert on the other side, Ptol.Geog.8.1.3:—Med., as law-term, reply to a remancipo, Gloss

ἀντιπαραγωγή.definition: flank march, Id.9.3.10; metaph., machinations, UPZ20.44

ἀντιπαραδέχομαι.definition: admit instead or in place of; receive in turn, BGU977.15 ; dub. sens. in Ph.2.508

ἀντιπαραδίδωμι.definition: deliver up in turn, J.AJ15.3.1, cf. PFlor.384.74

ἀντιπαράδοσις.definition: mutual accommodation, of heavenly bodies, Vett.Val.162.31

ἀντιπαράθεσις.definition: comparison, contrast, J.Ap.2.33, A.D.Synt.49.21, al., Herm.in Phdr.p.183 A

ἀντιπαραθέω.definition: run parallel to a thing, Plot.6.5.11

ἀντιπαρακαλέω.definition: summon in turn or contrariwise, Th.6.86, cf. X.Cyr.2.2.24, Pl.Grg.526e; change one's attitude and petition, J.BJ1.25.5

ἀντιπαράκειμαι.definition: lie just opposite, Plb.3.37.7; Gramm., correspond with, to be correlative to, A.D.Adv.155.1, al.; to be opposed, Synt.118.23

ἀντιπαρακελεύομαι.definition: exhort in turn or contrariwise, Th.6.13, cf. X.Cyr.3.3.42 and 59

ἀντιπαραλαμβάνω.definition: compare by contrasting, Gal.14.221; Astrol., take a function in exchange, Vett.Val.174.7

ἀντιπαραλλάσσω.definition: pass from side to side, Sor.1.103

ἀντιπαραπέμπομαι.definition: to be cheered on one's way [to death] by the remembrance, Plu.2.1099d

ἀντιπαραπήγνυμι.definition: set up as a standard of comparison or reference, A.D.Synt.37.22

ἀντιπαραπλέω.definition: sail along on the other side, Th.2.83

ἀντιπαρασκευάζομαι.definition: Med., prepare oneself in turn, arm; later, in Act., instigate in return, D.C.38.14

ἀντιπαράστασις.definition: as a figure of speech, counter-objection, rejoinder, retort, Hermog.Stat.3, al., Aps.p.270 H., Olymp.in Cat.78.26, Alex.Aphr.in Metaph.518.28; indirect reply, Procl.in Alc.p.303C.:—Adj. Hermog.Inv.3.6. Adv. ibid., Eus…

ἀντιπαράταξις.definition: hostile demonstration, Id.6.22; stubborn determination to resist, J.AJ18.8.5

ἀντιπαρατάσσομαι.definition: Act., = Med., is dub. l. in Plb.9.26.4

ἀντιπαρατείνω.definition: stretch side by side so as to compare; intr., extend beside, Anon.Geog.Comp.7; and Pass. in same sense, ib.21

ἀντιπαρατίθημι.definition: contrast and compare, Pl.Ap.40d, cf. Men.325.15, Phld.Po.2.28, Hom.p.12O., Jul.Gal.99d

ἀντιπαραχωρέω.definition: yield, give up in turn, Phlp.in Ph.553.20; give place in turn, Gal.19.474: Astrol., yield to adverse influence, Vett.Val.125.10; return a pledge, BGU1158.6

ἀντιπαραχώρησις.definition: making way for each other, Simp.in Cael.459.16; mutual concession, Eust.445.11: Astrol., yielding to adverse influence, Vett.Val.274.19

ἀντιπάρειμι.definition: march on opposite sides of a river or entrenchments, X.An.4.3.17, HG5.4.38

ἀντιπαρεισαγωγή.definition: introduction of a second soul, Plot.2.9.5

ἀντιπαρέκτασις.definition: interpenetration of two or more bodies in Chrysipp.Stoic.2.153

ἀντιπαρεκτείνομαι.definition: to be reciprocally interpenetrated; Act., extend in line with, J.BJ3.7.24

ἀντιπαρεξαγωγή.definition: a means of attack in controversy, S.E.M.7.150

ἀντιπαρέξειμι.definition: proceed in a parallel; make hostile demonstrations, Id.Cic.43

ἀντιπαρέρχομαι.definition: pass by on the opposite side; come up and help, as against an enemy, LXX.Wi.16.10

ἀντιπαρήκω.definition: = Chrysipp.Stoic.2.153,230; stretch parallel to, c. dat., Arist.Mu.393a31, Str.2.5.28; outflank, Paus.8.10.6

ἀντιπαρίστημι.definition: Rhet., retort, Aps.p.270 H., Ps.-Alex.Aphr.in SE102.15 :—Pass., Aps.p.271 H.; correspond, Ptol.Geog.8.1.14

ἀντιπαρονομάζομαι.definition: to be opposite in expression, Iamb.in Nic.p.29 P

ἀντιπαρῳδέω.definition: write a parody against, Str.9.1.10:—Subst. Steph.in Rh.319.19

ἀντιπαρωνυμέομαι.definition: Pass., to be opposite in name or expression, Nicom.Ar.1.8:—Act. in same sense, Iamb.in Nic.p.18 P., al.:—Subst. ib.p.13 P., al.; and Adj. Nicom.Ar.2.3

ἀντιπαταγέω.definition: rattle so as to drown another sound, Th.3.22; Dam.Isid.63

ἀντιπελαργέω.definition: cherish in turn, Iamb.VP5.24, Zen.1.94; cherish in place of another, of a sister acting as parent, Aristaenet.1.25:—Subst. Com.Adesp.939

ἀντιπεραίνομαι.definition: accomplish in turn, sens. obsc., AP12.238

ἀντιπέραιος.definition: lying over against, the lands lying over against, Il.2.635:—in late Ep. also fem. A.R.2.351, D.P.962, Nonn.D.24.148:—also Tz.H.1.896

ἀντιπεριάγω.definition: bring round, Arist.Mir.844b27; of the corvus employed on the Roman ships, Plb.1.22.8; Ph.1.311

ἀντιπεριαγωγή.definition: contrary revolution, Ptol.Alm.5.2; in midwifery, rotatory movement used in extracting the afterbirth, Sor.1.73

ἀντιπεριβάλλω.definition: put round in the other direction, e.g; embrace in return, Ach.Tat.5.8:—Pass., to be clothed about, LXXSi.23.12

ἀντιπεριειλέομαι.definition: to be rolled in the contrary direction, Orib.49.22.24

ἀντιπερίειμι.definition: come round as in a cycle, Aret.SA2.2

ἀντιπεριέλκω.definition: draw round to the other side, S.E.M.7.189

ἀντιπεριΐστημι.definition: oppose by surrounding, compress; Pass., to be replaced by another substance, ib.382a14; change places with, Id.Resp.472b16, cf. Gal.17.292

ἀντιπεριπλέω.definition: sail round on the other side, Str.1.1.8

ἀντιπεριποιέομαι.definition: express reciprocal action, of certain verbs, A.D.Synt.429.3

ἀντιπερισπάω.definition: draw off, divert, D.S.3.37; esp. as; divert, distract, Iamb.VP5.24

ἀντιπερίστασις.definition: surrounding so as to; reciprocal replacement, interchange, Id.Ph.215a15, 267a16 , Mete.348b2, Thphr.Ign.18, Sud.23

ἀντιπεριστροφή.definition: turning round to the other side, Placit.4.14.2

ἀντιπερισχίζομαι.definition: to be broken up and return, of sputum, Steph.in Hp.1.174D

ἀντιπεριχωρέω.definition: move round in turn or in opposition, Plu.Ages.39

ἀντιπεριψύχω.definition: cool or chill in turn, Plu.2.691f

ἀντιπέσσομαι.definition: Att. Pass., of food, to be quite digested, Arist.Pr.884a2

ἀντιπηρόομαι.definition: Pass., to be blinded in return, Ph.2.332

ἀντιπίνω.definition: drink to, pledge in turn, Sch.Opp.H.3.226

ἀντιπίπτω.definition: collide, Arist.Pr.915b18; fall upon; resist, resisting body, Arist.Pr.961b3; Act.Ap.7.51; without demur, UPZ36.21 ; A.D.Adv.123.5; POxy.1473.20 , cf. Aët.16.73; an objection, Phlp.in Mete.58.3; Aps.p.238H

ἀντιπλαγιάζομαι.definition: to be placed athwart, of bars in lattice-work, Lyd.Mag.3.37

ἀντιπλεονεκτέω.definition: have equal precedence or privilege, Simp.in Cael.515.5; have respective advantages over each other, Id.in Cat.335.1, Eliasin Cat.98.1:—hence Simp.in Cat.341.2

ἀντιπληρόω.definition: fill in turn or against, man them; fill up by new members, X.Cyr.2.2.26; replenish after exhaustion, Thphr.CP1.13.3

ἀντιπλήσσω.definition: strike in turn, in Pass., Arist.EN1132b29, MM1194a33

ἀντιπνέω.definition: of winds, blow against; to be adverse or contrary, Ph.1.593, Plu.Cic.32, Luc.Nav.7: metaph. of fortune, Plb.25.3.9, Clitomachus ap. Stob.4.41.29: c. dat., Luc.Tox.7

ἀντίπνοια.definition: conflicting wind; contrary wind, Ph.1.352, Hdn.5.4.11

ἀντίπνοος.definition: contr. caused by adverse winds, . . A.Ag.147 ; Id.Pr.1087 . Adv. Tz. ad Lyc.739

ἀντιποιέω.definition: do in return, Pl.Cri.50e; Med. , c. gen., exert oneself about a thing, seek after it, Isoc.1.2; lay claim to, Th.4.122; Isoc.6.7; Pl.Men.90d, Phlb.23a; D.10.52; Antiph.190.11; D.Chr.11.62; Arist.Po.1448a30: also c. in…

ἀντιποίησις.definition: laying claim to, D.H.11.30, cf. S.E.M.6.27, PLond.2.251.25

ἀντιπολεμέω.definition: wage war against, Th.3.39: c. dat., Pl.Criti.112e, X.Cyr.7.2.24: c. acc., LXXIs.41.12:—Pass., to be warred against, D.C.38.40

ἀντιπολίζω.definition: build up as an opposing city, J.BJ5.2.4

ἀντιπολιορκέω.definition: besiege in turn, Th.7.28; Plu.Marc.7:— Pass., J.BJ3.7.19

ἀντιπολιτεία.definition: political opposition; in pl., opposite parties, Plb.11.25.5

ἀντιπολιτεύομαι.definition: to be a political opponent, Arist.Pol.1274a14; the opposite party, Din.1.97: in sg., political opponent, Cic.Att.7.8.5: metaph., Aristonym. ap. Stob.3.38.36; Plu.Them.19, Per.8

ἀντίπραξις.definition: counteraction, resistance, Plb.6.17.8, D.H.11.53, Plu.Publ.11, Demetr.Lac.Herc.1012.71

ἀντιπράσσω.definition: abs., act in opposition, D.32.14; = Hdt.1.92; oppose in any way, X.HG2.3.14; Arist.Rh.1379a13; conflict with, tell against a theory, Demetr.Lac.Herc.1055.20:—Med., X.Hier.2.17

ἀντιπρεσβεύομαι.definition: Med., send counter-ambassadors, Th.6.75, Luc.Peregr.16: c. dat., Paus.7.9.5:—Act. in Aristid.1.372J., App.Mith.87

ἀντιπροβάλλομαι.definition: propose instead of another, Pl.Lg.755d:—Act., Gal.19.64

ἀντιπρόειμι.definition: come forward against or to meet, Th.6.66: abs., App.Pun.107

ἀντιπροηγέομαι.definition: precede instead of following, EM462.35, Hdn.Gr.2.394

ἀντιπροΐσχομαι.definition: hold out before one, present, as weapons, Them.Or.32.357b:—Hsch. has the Act

ἀντιπροκαλέομαι.definition: Med., retort a legal challenge , D.37.43; challenge in turn, c. acc. et inf., D.H.15.8

ἀντιπροσαγορεύω.definition: return salute, Plu.Crass.3 :— but in earlier Prose, aor. 2 Thphr.Char.15.3:—Pass., X.Mem.3.13.1

ἀντιπροσαμάομαι.definition: Med., heap in turn, scrape up new soil upon, X.Oec.17.13

ἀντιπροσβάλλομαι.definition: Pass., to be impinged upon in return, Hierocl.p.23A

ἀντιπροσελαύνω.definition: intr., charge against, of cavalry, D.C.46.37

ἀντιπροσκρίνω.definition: join instead, Alex.Aphr.de An.134.32:—Pass., to be added to in exchange, c. dat., Id.in Sens.57.2

ἀντιπροσκυνέω.definition: fall down and worship in turn, Plu.2.1117c

ἀντιπρόσοψις.definition: appearing instead, glossed by Suid., Zonar

ἀντιπροτείνω.definition: hold out in turn, X.HG4.1.31; propose in turn, D.C.48.11

ἀντιπροτίθημι.definition: publish, post up in opposition, D.C.65.1

ἀντιπροφέρω.definition: in Med., adduce in reply, Demetr.Lac.Herc.1012.49

ἀντίπτωμα.definition: stumble against, LXXSi.34.29; accident, Ptol.Tetr.116, Paul.Al.N.3b

ἀντίπτωσις.definition: opposition, resistance; Gramm., interchange of cases, Priscian. Inst.17.155, Sch.Ar.V.135

ἀντιρρέπω.definition: counterpoise, balance, A.Ag.574; Hp.Art.4: metaph., vacillate, Ph.2.170, etc

ἀντίρρησις.definition: gainsaying, altercation, Plb.2.7.7; controversy, Gal.Phil.Hist.24 D.; refutation of, D.S.1.38, J.Ap.2.1, Hermog.Id.1.8, Gal.1.131; counter-statement, POxy.68.11 ; reply, Phld.Rh.1.384S., al., Sign.7, cf. II

ἀντισάζω.definition: to be equal with, compensate, c. gen., Sch.E.Alc.859

ἀντισεμνύνομαι.definition: Med., meet pride with pride; Act., extol in return, Eust.1563.40

ἀντισημαίνω.definition: give a countersign, J.AJ19.1.10; give hostile signs, Paus.10.23.1

Ἀντισθενισμός.definition: a way of life according to the teaching of Antisthenes, Jul.Or.6.187c

ἀντισιωπάω.definition: to be silent in turn, Ar.Lys.528

ἀντισκευάζομαι.definition: Med., furnish for oneself in opposition, X.Ages.8.6:—Pass., Ph.Bel.92.11

ἀντισκώπτω.definition: mock in return, Plu.Tim.15, Ant.24:—Pass., take a gibe in return for one's own, D.C.66.11

ἀντισόομαι.definition: Pass., oppose on equal terms, Th.3.11

ἀντισοφιστεύω.definition: = foreg., Id.1.449, cf. Numen. ap. Eus.PE14.8

ἀντισοφιστής.definition: one who seeks to refute, c. gen., Luc.Alex.43, cf. Cal.16

ἀντίσπασις.definition: revulsion, esp. of bodily humours, Hp.Hum.1, Vict.2.56, Gal.10.315, etc

ἀντίσπασμα.definition: in war, distraction, diversion, Plb.2.18.3, D.S.20.86, J.AJ17.2.4

ἀντισπασμός.definition: convulsion, Ar.Lys.967; counter-movement , of the sea, Placit.3.17.7

ἀντισπεύδω.definition: oppose eagerly, contend against, Antipho1.7; D.C.59.13

ἀντίσταθμος.definition: counterpoising, balancing, Pl.Sph.229c; D.S.5.29: metaph., in compensation for, S.El.571

ἀντιστασιάζω.definition: form a party against, X.An.4.1.27; = Id.Cyr.7.4.3; to offer opposition to . ., D.C.37.54

ἀντιστάσιος.definition: of equal weight: metaph., Max.Tyr.4.1; Id.39.1

ἀντίστασις.definition: counter-faction; opposition, Ph.1.577; J.AJ17.11.2; Plu.Aem.36; in pitched battle, Hdn.5.4.4; weigh equally, Arist.Mu.397a1

ἀντιστασιώτης.definition: one of the opposite faction or party, Hdt.1.92, 4.164, X.An.1.1.10, Aen.Tact.11.7, etc

ἀντιστατέω.definition: = resist, oppose, esp. as a political partisan, Hdt.3.52; Pl.Grg.513c, J.AJ18.9.2, cf. Ph.1.205, al.; Plu.2.802b; trans., Lib.Vit.1.7

ἀντιστήριγμα.definition: a prop or support, Hp.Art.9,16: metaph., support, stay, LXXPs.17.18

ἀντιστηριγμός.definition: blocking the way, resistance, D.H.Dem.38; Id.Comp.16

ἀντιστηρίζω.definition: press against, Hp.Art.47; offer resistance, Democr.9, Arist.Pr.940a11

ἀντιστοιχείωσις.definition: change of a letter, e.g. for Sch.Il.12.29

ἀντίστοιχος.definition: ranged opposite in rows or pairs; standing over against, E.Andr.745; . . corresponding with, D.H.Rh.9.7

ἀντιστορέννυμι.definition: aor. 1 inf. lay paving instead, SIG2 587.48

ἀντιστρατεύομαι.definition: take the field, make war against, X.Cyr.8.8.26:—later in Act., D.S.22.15, J.AJ2.10.1 : metaph., Aristaenet.2.1

ἀντιστρατηγέω.definition: act against as general or make war against, D.H.11.37; J.Vit.55, cf. Max. Tyr.41.3

ἀντιστρατοπέδευσις.definition: an encamping opposite, the position of two armies in sight of one another, D.C.78.26

ἀντιστρατοπεδεύω.definition: encamp over against; more freq. in Med., Hdt.1.76: abs., Th.1.30: so pf. Pass., Id.4.124, X.HG7.4.13

ἀντιστρεπτέος.definition: in Logic, to be converted; one must reverse, Plot.5.5.11

ἀντιστροφή.definition: a turning about; in choruses and dances, strophic correspondence, D.H.Comp.25; in later writers, = , Sch.Ar.Nu.595,al

ἀντίστροφος.definition: turned so as to face one another; in Logic, converse, Phld.Rh.1.179S. Adv. Id.Sign.6: also in Math., converse, Papp.970.20; the converse proposition, Apollon.Perg.Con.4.55. Adv. conversely, ib.1.38, Max.Tyr.34.4

ἀντισυγκρίνω.definition: compare one with another, Nicom.Ar.1.13:— Pass., ib.20, Charito6.1

ἀντισυμμαχέομαι.definition: Pass., to be helped in return, Longin.17.1

ἀντισυμποσιάζω.definition: write a Symposium in rivalry of Plato, Luc.Lex.1

ἀντισυνάπτω.definition: meet in opposite directions, dub. in Gal.18.727

ἀντισφίγγω.definition: form an obstacle by tension, Hp.Art.3

ἀντισχηματίζω.definition: meet one figure by another, D.H.Rh.9.14

ἀντισχηματισμός.definition: the use of such figures in turn, ibid

ἀντισχυρίζομαι.definition: Med., to be stiff in maintaining a contrary opinion, Th.3.44; Plu.2.535e

ἀντισχύω.definition: fut. repel by force, LXXWi.7.30, D.C.48.11

ἀντισῴζω.definition: preserve in turn, Anon. ap. Suid. s.v. Aristid.1.418J

ἀντίταγμα.definition: opposing force, D.S.11.67, Plu.Cleom.23; of a person, 'a political force', Nic.2, Luc.38

ἀντιταλαντεύω.definition: = APl.4.221 ; put into the opposite scale, Lib.Decl.43 Intr.2

ἀντιτάσσω.definition: Att. set opposite to, range in; Med., set oneself against, meet face to face, E.Ph.622, cf. Th.4.55, etc.; D.3.27:—Pass., to be drawn out in array against, Hdt.4.134, X.HG3.1.6; Hdt.7.103; X.Cyr.3.1.18, etc.; Id.HG4.2…

ἀντιταφρεύω.definition: dig a trench in opposition, Ph.Bel.93.26

ἀντιτειχίζω.definition: erect counter-fortifications, J.AJ14. 16.2; trans., fortify instead, Id.BJ5.8.2: metaph., Ph.1.426

ἀντιτεχνάζω.definition: use art in turn, D.H.Rh.9.5:—also in Med., J.AJ1.19.8

ἀντιτεχνάομαι.definition: contrive in opposition, counter-plan, Hdt.5.70; Max.Tyr.32.9: abs., Plu.Sert.18; J.AJ14.16.2

ἀντιτεχνέω.definition: to be a rival in art, Sch.Ar.V.1402

ἀντίτεχνος.definition: rival in an art or craft, Ar.Ra.816, Pl.R.493a, etc.; Id.Phd.60d, cf. Lg.817b; D.Chr.12.46: c. gen., Luc.Alex.43

ἀντιτίθημι.definition: set against so as to balance, contrast, or compare, Hdt.1.207, cf. 8.66; E.Or.551: also c. gen., Th.2.85, cf. 3.56: with a Prep., D.21.175:— Pass., to be contrasted, or Pl.Sph.257d,258e

ἀντιτιμωρέομαι.definition: avenge oneself on, E.IT357, Th.3.82, Plb.1.81.9: abs., revenge oneself, take vengeance, Ar.Pax134,626:—a fut. Pass. occurs in Sch.Lyc.1337

ἀντιτιτρώσκω.definition: wound in turn, Sch.E.Hipp.507: plpf. Pass. Hld.7.27

ἀντιτολμάω.definition: dare to stand against another, abs., Th.2.89; Id.7.21

ἀντιτονέομαι.definition: or Pass., to have a different accent from, Eust.1025.4

ἀντιτοξεύω.definition: shoot arrows in return, X.An.3.3.15, Philostr.Im.1.6

ἀντιτραχύνομαι.definition: Pass., to be exasperated in turn, Eust.467.9

ἀντιτυμπανίζω.definition: beat drums in rivalry with, prob. cj. in Anon.Vat.42

ἀντιτυπέω.definition: strike against, esp. of a hard body, Arist.Mete.370b18; resist, Phld.Sign.18; Luc.Dom.10; Ach.Tat.2.38: abs., Hp.Mul.2.177; Pl.Cra.420d:—also in Med., Hp.Mul.1.61

ἀντίτυπος.definition: rarely v. infr.II.1a; corresponding, as the stamp to the die, figuring or representing the true, Ep.Hebr.9.24, cf. 1 Ep.Pet.3.21; IG14.1320; resembling, c. dat., Nonn.D.26.327; ib.8.23: hence, feigned, counterfeit, 1.…

ἀντιτυπόω.definition: express as by a figure, . . AP1.36

ἀντιτύπτω.definition: fut. Ph.Bel.85.10, beat in turn, Ar.Nu.1424, Antipho4.4.3; Pl.Cri.51a

ἀντιφάσκω.definition: contradict, Olymp.in Mete.181.11; to be in contradiction, Simp.in Ph.1155.28; contradictories, Id.in Cat.44.21, cf. 19.21; the opponent in argument, Phld.Po.2.54

ἀντιφθέγγομαι.definition: return a sound, echo, repeat; speak against, contradict, J.AJ18.7.2, Luc.Salt.23, Pisc.31, S.E.M.7.332, al

ἀντίφθογγος.definition: of answering sound, concordant, c. gen., Pi.Fr.125; imitative, AP7.191

ἀντιφιλέω.definition: love in return, Pl.Ly.212d, Theoc.12.16; kiss in return, AP5.284

ἀντιφιλονεικέω.definition: strive jealously against, Id.3.103.7; 32.3.16: abs., J.AJ2.9.1

ἀντιφιλοσοφέω.definition: hold contrary tenets, Luc.Bis Acc.21; LXX4 Ma.8.15

ἀντιφιλοτιμέομαι.definition: Pass., to be moved by jealousy; Medic., set up a vicious circle with, Sever.Clyst.4

ἀντιφιλοφρονέομαι.definition: receive kindly in turn, J.AJ14.11.5; also, rival, Plu.Sert.20

ἀντιφορτίζω.definition: take in a return-cargo, Str.5.3.5; in Med. also, import in exchange for exports, X.Vect.3.2; take as return-freight, Arist.Mir.844a18

ἀντιφράζω.definition: translate, Gal.11.793; express by antithesis or negation, TryphoTrop.2.15

ἀντιφράσσω.definition: Att. barricade, block; c. dat., stand in the way of, Arist.Juv.470a13, cf. Pr.929a38; esp. of a body intercepting the sun's light, . . Id.Mete.345a29: c. acc., Id.Cael.293b25. abs., X.Smp.5.6, Thphr.Ign.49; Arist.AP0.…

ἀντιφυλακή.definition: a watching against one another, Th.2.84: pl., D.C.77.2, Luc.Hist.Conscr.28

ἀντιφυλάσσω.definition: Att. watch in turn, Pl.Lg.705e:—Med., to be on one's guard in turn, X.An.2.5.3, cf. Plu.Demetr.36

ἀντιφύω.definition: in pf. part. to be of contrary nature, Hsch

ἀντιφωνητής.definition: one who answers for, is responsible for another, POxy.136.39

ἀντιφωτίζομαι.definition: to be directly exposed to light, Dam.Pr.29

ἀντιχαλεπαίνω.definition: to be embittered against, D.H.17.5, Plu.2.468b

ἀντιχαρίζομαι.definition: show kindness in return, Hdt.7.114, X.Cyr.4.1.20, Ph.2.26, etc

ἀντίχαρις.definition: acknowledgement of a favour, Heliod.in EN95.18, Lib.Decl.43.29

ἀντιχειροτονέω.definition: vote against, abs., Th.6.13,24, Ar.Ec.423; . . D.59.5; Max.Tyr.17.5

ἀντιχορηγέω.definition: to be a rival choragus, And.4.42; furnish in return, J.BJ2.20.8

ἀντιχρηματίζομαι.definition: transact business instead of another, PFlor.382.59

ἀντιχρονία.definition: use of one tense for another, Sch.E.Or.82

ἀντιχώννυμι.definition: raise an embankment against, Amynt. ap. Ath.12.529e

ἄντλημα.definition: bucket for drawing water, Plu.2.974e, Sch.Ar.Ra.1332, Ev.Jo.4.11

ἄντλησις.definition: drawing up or emptying, Ruf. ap. Orib.5.3.1, POxy.971 , Ael.VH1.24

ἀντλητήρ.definition: one who draws water, Poll.10.31; ladle, Ath.10.424a

ἀντλητήριος.definition: of or for drawing up: bucket, D.C.50.34

ἀντλήτρια.definition: she who draws up, priestess at the Thesmophoria, Sch.Luc.DDeor.2.1

ἀντοικοδομέω.definition: build or fortify against, Plb.1.42.12, D.S.16.49; App.BC2.61:—Med., Arr.An.1.21.4: metaph., Ael.VH4.9

ἀντοίομαι.definition: aor. to be of contrary opinion, Pl.Tht.178c

ἀντόμνυμι.definition: swear in turn, swear on the other part, in; as Att. law-term, make an affidavit, both of the accuser and the defendant , Antipho1.18, Is.9.1, D.43.3, etc.:—in Med., Is.5.16

ἀντονομασία.definition: use of an epithet, patronymic, or; nomination of his successor by retiring official, POxy.1642.15

ἀντοργίζομαι.definition: to be angry in turn, M.Ant.6.26, Gal.19.211

ἀντορύσσω.definition: dig a countermine, Hdt.4.200, Aen.Tact.37.7: metaph., Paus.3.14.10

ἀντορχέομαι.definition: imitate one's dancing, Arist.HA597b24, cf. Metrod.Sceps.13

ἀντοφθαλμέω.definition: look in the face, meet face to face, Plb.18.46.12: hence, defy, withstand, and Id.1.17.3, 2.24.1, etc., cf. LXXWi.12.14; of a ship, Act.Ap.27.15; Longin.34.4

ἀντοφθάλμησις.definition: looking straight in the face: hence, straightforward dealing, IG5.1114.17

ἀντόφθαλμος.definition: looking in the face, Hsch. s.v

ἀντοχέομαι.definition: drive or ride against, f.l. in Mosch.2.119

ἀντροδίαιτος.definition: living in caves, Orph.H.32.3; of Pan, ib.11.5

ἀντροχαρής.definition: cave-haunting, epith. of nymphs and Pan, Orph.H.11.12, 51.5

ἀντῳδή.definition: in Comic Parabasis, lyric passage responding to Sch.Ar.V.1091, Nu.298

ἀντωθέω.definition: push in the contrary direction, Hp.Fract.39, cf. Ph.2.354:—Pass., Arist.GA768b19, cf. Mech.851a3:— Med., push one against another, Theopomp.Hist.283

ἀντώθησις.definition: counter-thrust, Gal.18.324, Phlp.in Ph.646.19; prob. cj. for in Paul.Aeg.6.117

ἀντωνέομαι.definition: buy instead, X.Oec.20.26, Men.438.3; bid against, And.1.134; Lys.22.9; rival bidder, D.18.239

ἀντωνυμία.definition: pronoun, D.H.Comp.6, Plu.2.1009c, etc; interchange of names, Dam.Pr.73

ἀντωφελέω.definition: assist or benefit in turn, X.Mem.2.10.3:—Pass., derive profit in turn, ib.2.8.3, Cyr.1.6.11

ἀνυγραίνω.definition: moisten, Hp.Int.51, Thphr.CP2.6.1; metaph., melt, soften, Plu.2.156d:—Pass., ib.566a

ἀνυδρεύομαι.definition: draw up from a well, Pherecr.76

ἀνυδρία.definition: want of water, drought, Hp.Aër.12, Th.3.88, PPetr.2p.22; lack of irrigation, PLond. ined.2179

ἀνυμνέω.definition: proclaim by an oracle, E.El.1190; celebrate in song, D.H.Rh.2.1, cf. Jul.Or.5.172d, Chor.p.127 B., Procop.Gaz.Ep.52, Ps.-Luc.Philopatr.4 : Orac. in App.Anth.6.261.18, Nonn.D.24.328

ἀνύπαρκτος.definition: non-existent, unreal, Epicur.Fr.27, Zeno Stoic.1.19, Phld.Mus.p.65K., Ph.2.307, Plu.2.1124a, PGiss.7.8 , etc

ἀνυπέρβατος.definition: impassable, D.Chr.64.21; not to be overcome, unsurpassable, S.E.M.9.153; Phld.Vit.p.12J

ἀνυπερθετέω.definition: do immediately, to be hasty, ib.77.21

ἀνυπέρθετος.definition: immediate, Ph.2.58,al; unsurpassed by, c. dat., Democr.275; incomparable, [Philol.]21

ἀνυπεύθυνος.definition: not liable to a not; of things, beyond human control or criticism, Hp.Praec.7; Epicur.Ep.3p.65U.; unchartered freedom, Phld.Herc.1251.3

ἀνυπηλιφής.definition: EM61.6, or Phryn.PSp.34 B., not anointed with pitch

ἀνυπηρέτητος.definition: hyperdor. without attendance, Euryph. ap. Stob.4.39.27

ἀνυπόδικος.definition: not liable to action, Plu.Cat.Mi.11; GDI1685, al. , cf. 5170

ἀνύποιστος.definition: insupportable, Timae.60, D.H.7.15; Act., impatient, Ptol.Tetr.159

ἀνυπομενετέος.definition: not to be sustained, Stob.2.6.6:—also ibid

ἀνυπονόητος.definition: unsuspected, in a thing; unexpected, Id.2.57.6. Adv. Id.1.84.9

ἀνυπόστατος.definition: not to be withstood, irresistible; without sure foundation, Plb.1.5.3, cf. 12.25f.4; D.L.9.99, cf. Ath.3.98c

ἀνυπόστολος.definition: using no concealment, frank, fearless, Poll.4.21; J.AJ16.3.1. Adv. D.Chr.13.16, Phld.Rh.1.109S., Alciphr.3.39, etc

ἀνυπόστρεπτος.definition: unreturning, Suid. s.v. Adv. without turning back, Pythag. ap. Phlp.in de An.116.32

ἀνυπόστροφος.definition: from which none return, Orph.H.56; of diseases, without relapse, Hp.Epid.6.3.4

ἀνυπότακτος.definition: of persons or things, not made; not to be classified under heads, confused, Plb.3.36.4; irregular, of dithyrambs, Demetr.Lac.Herc.1014.12, Zen.2.15

ἀνυφάντης.definition: one who weaves anew, Suid.:—fem. Eust.1764.60

ἀνυψόω.definition: raise up, exalt, LXXPs.112.7, al., PGen.51.27 :—Med., AP7.748 :—Pass., Lyd.Mag.2.16

ἀνώϊστος.definition: unlooked for, unexpected, Il.21.39; Hom.Epigr.5; Mosch.2.75; Epic.Anon.Oxy. 214.1. Adv. A.R.1.680

ἀνωμαλία.definition: unevenness, irregularity, Pl.R.547a; Astron., irregular motion, anomaly, Gem.1.20, cf. Ptol.Alm.3.3, etc.; of the moon's orbit, Plu.Aem.17

ἀνώμαλος.definition: uneven, irregular; of conditions, fortune, and the like , E.Fr.684; Pl.Lg.773b, Mx.238e; Plot.6.7.34. Adv. Hp.Prog.3, Isoc.7.29; fall into precarious health, Prisc.p.333 D

ἀνωφέλητος.definition: unprofitable, useless, to one; helpless, Eup.377; Stratt.9 D

ἀξιάγαστος.definition: worth admiring, admirable, X.Lac.10.2, Ael.Fr.116, Jul.Or.6.190d

ἀξιαφήγητος.definition: Ion. worth telling, Hdt.1.16,177 , J.AJ15.11.5 , Arr.An.1 Praef.1

ἀξιέπαινος.definition: praiseworthy, Id.Cyr.3.3.6, D.61.15; of a dead ox, Ael.NA2.57, etc.: Sup. X.HG4.4.6. Adv. Apollon.Vit.Aeschin.11

ἀξιέραστος.definition: worthy of love, X.Cyr.5.2.9, Chrysipp.Stoic.3.181, Plu.Comp.Thes. Rom.1, Luc.DMar.1.2, Aristaenet.1.27; PMag.Par.1.2010: Comp., X.Smp.8.14

ἀξινοκράτημα.definition: helve of an axe, Zonar. s.v

ἀξινόπληκτος.definition: struck by an axe, An.Par.3.114, Sch.Il.1.1

ἀξιοζήλωτος.definition: = foreg., Phld.Piet.66; worthy of emulation, Dsc.Praef.4

ἀξιοθέατος.definition: Ion. well worth seeing, Hdt.1.14,184, al., X.Smp.1.10, Corn.ND17: Comp. Plu.Demetr.43: Sup. Hdt.2.176, X.Lac.4.2

ἀξιοθριάμβευτος.definition: worth being led in triumph, Suet.Cal.47

ἀξιοκοινώνητος.definition: worthy of our society, Pl.R.371e; worthy to share in, Lg.961a

ἀξιόκτητος.definition: worth getting, X.Cyr.5.2.10, Paus.1.9.5, Philostr.Ep.9; Aristid.Quint.3.18

ἀξιομακάριστος.definition: worthy to be deemed happy, X.Ap.34

ἀξιόμαχος.definition: a match for another in battle or war; c. inf., sufficient in strength or number, Hdt.6.89; . . Id.7.138, cf. 101; D.C.43.4. Adv. Plu.Sull.19

ἀξιομίμητος.definition: worthy of imitation, Ecphant. ap. Stob.4.7.65

ἀξιομνημόνευτος.definition: worthy of mention, Pl.Prt.343a, Smp.178a, X.HG4.8.1, etc

ἀξιόνικος.definition: worthy of victory, worthy of being preferred, X.Cyr.1.5.10: c. inf., more worthy to hold this supremacy, Hdt.7.187, cf.9.26: Sup., Luc.Anach.36

ἀξιοπιστεύομαι.definition: to be worthy of belief, Phld.Po.1676.11

ἀξιοπιστία.definition: trustworthiness, Hipparch.1.1.7; plausibility, J.BJ1.32.2; credibility, Alex.Fig.1.17

ἀξιόπιστος.definition: trustworthy, Pl.Alc.1.123b; of evidence, trustworthy, Arist.GA741a37. Adv. 741a34

ἀξιοσέβαστος.definition: worthy of reverence, worshipful, Eust.ad D.P.p.72.22

ἀξιοσπούδαστος.definition: worthy of zealous endeavours, X.Lac.10.3 , Plu.2.5d

ἀξιοστράτηγος.definition: worthy of being general or worthy of a great commander, X.An.3.1.24 , D.C.36.24 codd. :— is found as v.l. in Arr.An.4.11.9 and D.C.41.55, and Id.45.42

ἀξιοτέκμαρτος.definition: worthy of being brought in evidence, credible, deeds are stronger proof than words, X.Mem.4.4.10

ἀξιοτίμητος.definition: highly prized, valuable, Ph.1.461:—also Nic.Dam.p.94 D., X.Ep.2.3 , App.BC3.19

ἀξιόω.definition: pf. Isoc.18.24:—Med., v. infr; c. acc. et gen., whether in good sense, think worthy of a reward, E.Med.962; X.An.3.2.7; or in bad, of a punishment, Hdt.3.145; Philipp. ap. D.18.166; Pl.Ap.38a:—Pass., Hdt.9.111; . . de…

ἀξόνιον.definition: Dim., small bolt or pin, HeroSpir.1.30, Poll.10.31; of bolts used in twisting the strands of torsion-engines, HeroBel.82.7:—also Id.Spir.2.32, Ph.Bel.76.24

ἀξυλία.definition: Ion. want of wood, Hes.Fr.206, Str.15.2.10 = sq. I, Hsch

ἄοινος.definition: without wine, offered to; of men, having no wine, sober, X.Cyr.6.2.27; also of a place, having none, ib.26

ἀοκνία.definition: not shrinking from, c. gen., Hp.Epid.6.4.18; censured by Poll.3.120

ἄοκνος.definition: without hesitation, resolute, Hes.Op.495; S.Aj.563; Th.1.70; Cleanth.Stoic.1.118; Epicur.Ep.3p.64U.; Plu.Pel.3; pressing, present mischief, S.Tr.841. Adv. without hesitation, Hp.Art.38, Pl.Lg.649b, Orib.Syn.Praef.: Su…

ἀορασία.definition: inability to see, blindness, Plb.12.25g.4, LXXGe.19.11, al., IG12.955.8, 1179.26 ; failure to observe, Inscr.Magn.114.4

ἀόργητος.definition: not irascible, Arist.EN1108a8:—in good sense, Phld.Ir.p.71 W., Plu.2.10c, Luc.Herm.12, Aret.CD1.4, etc. Adv. Phld.Lib.p.7 O., Arr.Epict.3.18.6, Hierocl.in CA12p.447M

ἀορισταίνω.definition: = sq., Procl.Inst.124, Phlp.in GA191.34; make Iamb.in Nic.p.78 P

ἀοριστέω.definition: to be indeterminate, Arist.Pr.941b26; to be without definite ideas, uncertain, Phld.Mus.p.48K., cf. S.E.P.1.28, Porph.Sent.33, Asp.in EN74.27

ἀοριστόω.definition: in Pass., to be indefinite, ib.70.4, al

ἀορτή.definition: in pl., = Hp.Loc.Hom.14; the arteries springing from the heart, i.e. aorta and pulmonary artery, Hp.Cord.10; esp. in sg., the aorta, Arist.HA496a7, 513b4, etc.: in pl., arteries, Poll.2.205

ἀοσσητήρ.definition: assistant, helper, aider, Il.15.254,22.333, Od.4.165, A.R.1.471, etc

ἀόχλητος.definition: undisturbed, calm, D.H.1.8: an Epicurean term, Epicur.Sent. Vat.79, cf. Luc.Par.11; Alciphr.3.55. Adv., Comp. Gal.13.597: Sup. Id.15.707

ἀπαγγελία.definition: report, e.g. of an ambassador; narrative, recital, description, . . Th.3.67; lyric poetry is said to be Pl.R.394c, cf. Phld.Po.5.1425.2; dramatic poetry is expressed by action Arist.Po.1449b26, cf. ib.II, D.H.Comp.20

ἀπαγγελτήρ.definition: one who reports, messenger, Phryn. Trag. ap.Phot.p.154 R.: metaph. of a cork, AP6.5

ἀπαγκωνίζομαι.definition: bare the elbows, aor; Act. in Eust.1221.58, bind one's hands behind him

ἀπαγλαΐζω.definition: deprive of ornament, AP5.219; honour to the full, IG.12.292

ἀπαγόρευσις.definition: failure of strength, exhaustion, Luc.Anach.37, Plu.Ant.45

ἀπαγχονάω.definition: = sq. in Pass., D.C.72.7:—also in Pass., Steph.in Hp.2.334 D

ἀπαδικέω.definition: with hold wrong fully; wrong, PLond.2.354.7

ἀπᾴδω.definition: fut. Pl.Ti.26d:—sing out of tune; metaph., dissent, Pl.Lg.662b; Plu.Lyc.27: c. gen., Luc.Anach.6; to be at variance with, Ph.1.235; fall short of, HeroBel.112.16

ἀπαθανατίζω.definition: aim at immortality, Pl.Chrm.156d, v.l; trans., deify, D.S.2.20, Vett.Val.150.17; Inscr. ap. Str.15.1.73; represent it as immortal, Ascl.in Metaph.90.26; make perpetual, Ph.1.9; Porph.Abst.2.5:—Pass., become immortal, …

ἀπάθεια.definition: impassibility, of things, opp; of persons, insensibility, apathy, Arist.EN1104b24, de An.429a29; insensibility to . ., Thphr.HP9.15.1; Arist.APo.97b23, Rh.1383b16

ἀπαιγειρόομαι.definition: to be changed into a poplar, Str.5.1.9

ἀπαιδευσία.definition: Ion. want of education; stupidity, Pl.Grg.527e, al., Aeschin.1.144; from bigotry of passion, Th.3.84

ἀπαιδευτέω.definition: to be A.D.Conj.235.19, Iamb.in Nic.p.9P.; to be foolishly said, Id.Comm.Math.7

ἀπαίδευτος.definition: boorish, rude, Pl.Grg.510b, etc.; Id.Phdr.269b; Alex.284; Philem.213.11; clumsy evidence, Aeschin.1.70; 2 Ep.Ti.2.23: Comp., Nicoch.3

ἀπαιθύσσομαι.definition: flare, stream, of a torch, D.S.2.53.—Act. in EM233.34, intr., of the eyes

ἀπαιτήσιμον.definition: list of lands subject to dues; demand for services, POxy.136.17

ἀπαίτησις.definition: demanding back, Hdt.5.85; name of a play by S.; make a formal demand, D.33.26, cf.POxy.272.13 ; claim, right to demand a thing, IG9.61

ἀπαιωρέομαι.definition: hang down from, hover about, Hes.Sc.234; to be uplifted, Luc.Astr.19

ἀπακοντίζω.definition: shoot away like a javelin, shoot off, Arist.HA501a32 ; spirt out blood, Antyll. ap. Orib.7.10.2; dart forth, Nonn.D.40.414

ἀπακριβόομαι.definition: to be highly wrought or finished; Med., finish off, make perfect, of sculpture, APl.4.172 , cf. 5.342; Luc.Im.16

ἀπακταίνω.definition: to be unequal to violent exercise, Hsch

ἀπαλγέω.definition: put away sorrow for, Th.2.61; generally, to be despondent, Plb.9.40.4; D.C.48.37: abs., Plb.1.35.5, Ep.Eph.4.19

ἀπαλέξησις.definition: defence, against a thing, Phot., Suid

ἀπαλεξίκακος.definition: = f.l. in Orph.H.67.5, dub. in IG12.253 ; Porph. ap. Eus.PE3.11

ἀπαλλαγή.definition: deliverance, release, relief; abs., divorce, in pl., E.Med.236, 1375: sg., PRyl.154.29 , etc

ἀπάλλαξις.definition: = III, Hdt.9.13, Porph.Marc.9; loss of colour, Hp.Hum.5, cf. Epicur.Nat.139 G

ἀπαλλάσσω.definition: Att. fut. Isoc.5.52: pf; put away from, remove from, as E.Med.27, Hipp.774 ; IT994; Hec.1222; take away or remove from one, Ar.Ec.1046; D.C.43.32

ἀπαλλοτριόω.definition: pf. Aeschin.2.194:—estrange; of property, alienate, Arist.Rh.1361a22, IPE12.32B68 :—Pass., PLond.3.1157v iii3

ἁπαλοκροκῶδες.definition: name of an eye-salve, Sichel Pierres sigillaires p.59

ἁπαλοπλόκαμος.definition: with soft tentacles, of cuttlefish, Philox.2.14

ἁπαλόστομος.definition: delicate to the mouth, Hsch. s.v

ἁπαλότης.definition: softness, tenderness, Hp.VM22, Pl.Smp.195d, X.Mem.2.1.22; Arist.Pol.1336a10

ἁπαλοτρεφής.definition: well-fed, plump, Il.21.363; rich pastures, IG14.1389 ii 11

ἁπαλόχροος.definition: contr. with heterocl. gen. dat. acc. h.Ven.14, Hes.Op.519, Thgn.1341, E.Hel.373 :—also Phryn.PSp.30B

ἁπαλύνω.definition: make tender or delicate, X.Lac.2.1:—Pass., to be softened, metaph., LXX4 Ki.22.19, Ps.54.21

ἀπαμαλδύνω.definition: bring to naught, plunge into obscurity, AP9.24 ; quench, Nonn.D.33.24; turn pale, Q.S.8.209

ἀπαμβλύνω.definition: fut. , blunt or dull; mostly metaph., Pi.P.1.82 ; of a person, A.Th.715; Herod.1.67; Opp.H.4.525; tone down, take the edge off a phrase, Plot.3.6.12:—more freq. in Pass., to be blunted, lose its edge or force, Hom.Epi…

ἀπαμείρω.definition: deprive one of share in a thing, A.R.3.186:— Med., Nonn.D.29.158:—Pass., to be bereft, of a thing, prob.l. in Hes.Th.801, cf. Op.578; v.l. for Od.17.322

ἀπαμελέομαι.definition: Pass., to be neglected utterly, Hdt.3.129,132, S.Ph.652

ἀπαμέργομαι.definition: Med., only pres. and impf., take or carry off for oneself, Nic.Th.861, Al.306

ἀπαμφιέννυμι.definition: strip off garments; strip off, Plu.2.516f, cf. Ph.1.117

ἀπαναγκάζω.definition: force away, Hp.Art.2; opp. ib.14; simply, = ib.58, cf. Str.2.1.31, PFay.122.18 :—freq. as f.l. for as Plb.4.46.6, 5.24.1, Them.Or.33.367a

ἀπαναιδεύομαι.definition: Dep., = mentioned by Thom.Mag.p.21 R. as an Att. word

ἀπαναισχυντέω.definition: behave with effrontery, c. acc. cogn., Pl.Ap.31b; c. inf., Alex.Aphr.in Top.524.5: abs., D.29.20, cf. 54.33; put away shame, Hld.8.5

ἀπαναλίσκω.definition: fut. Alciphr.3.47: pf; spend from a given sum, IG1.32.26

ἀπανάλωσις.definition: consumption, D.S.1.41, Sor.1.42, Antyll. ap. Orib.6.10.18

ἀπαναστομόω.definition: = for which it is v.l. in D.H.3.40

ἀπαναχωρέω.definition: pass away, Olymp.in Grg.p.367 J.; v.l. for J.BJ2.21.5:—Subst. v.l. for D.S.25.6

ἀπανδρόομαι.definition: become a man, come to maturity, E.Ion53, Luc.Am.26; viro maturae factae sunt, Aret.SD1.6

ἀπανθίζω.definition: pluck off flowers: metaph; Pass., to be withered, Phryn.PSp.9 B

ἀπανθρακίζω.definition: broil on the coals, roast, Ar.Ra.506, cf. Av.1546, Ph.1.665, Philostr.VA5.25

ἀπανθρακίς.definition: cake baked on coals, Diocl.Fr.116 , cf. Hsch

ἀπανθρακόω.definition: burn to a cinder, Luc.DMort.20.4:—Pass., Id.DMar.11.1, Peregr.1

ἀπανθρωπέομαι.definition: shun like a misanthrope, rejected by Poll.2.5, but used by Hp.Ep.12 cf. Tz.H.7.880, 885

ἀπανθρωπία.definition: unfitness for social intercourse, J.BJ2.17.3; unsociability, moroseness, Hp.Coac.472 ; inhumanity, POxy.298.52 , J.AJ17.11.2

ἀπανθρωπίζομαι.definition: become a man, opp. a beast, Herm. ap. Stob.1.49.69

ἀπαντάω.definition: impf. Th.4.127, Dor. 3sg; mostly of persons, move from a place to meet a person, and generally, meet, encounter, Hdt.8.9, E.Supp.772, etc.; Pl.Lg.893e; encounter, fall in with them, D.60.20: abs., any one that meets y…

ἀπάντησις.definition: meeting in argument, reply, Arist.SE176a23, Metaph.1009a20, cf. Phld.Sign.19,28; to reply, Plb.5.63.7; in conversation, Id.10.5.6, cf. Phld.Vit.p.13J., Id.Herc.1457.4, Plu.2.803f

ἀπαντιάζω.definition: meet, Archyt.1; v.l. for in Procop.Goth.3.6

ἀπάντομαι.definition: entreat one not to do a thing, E.Rh.901; poet., = Phryn.254

ἀπαράβατος.definition: inviolable, PRyl.65.18 , cf. PGrenf.1.60.7; permanent, perpetual, Ep.Hebr.7.24

ἀπαράβλαστος.definition: not branching laterally, Thphr.HP1.2.5, CP1.1.3; not budding laterally, Id.HP3.17.2

ἀπαράβλητος.definition: incomparable, PLond.2.232.5 , f.l. for in Ph.2.509

ἀπαράβολος.definition: without deposit made; Adv. without danger, Sch.Il.13.141

ἀπαράδεκτος.definition: inadmissible, Phld.Sign.17; Act., not receiving or admitting, c. gen., Memn.2.2; Phld.D.3 Fr.42 ; Ph.1.311; Stoic.3.153; esp. in Gramm., A.D.Synt.16.18,al

ἀπαραδίσκευτος.definition: not defeated in discus-throwing, Ephes.2 No.72

ἀπαράθετος.definition: not padded out with quotations, D.L.7.181: hence in Gramm., words or phrases without quoted authority, prob. for Et.Gud. s.v

ἀπαράθραυστος.definition: unshaken, not to be shaken, Olymp.in Phlb.p.274S., Eustr.in EN297.26

ἀπαράκλητος.definition: unsummoned, volunteering, Th.2.98; not to be consoled, Sch.A.Pr.185

ἀπαραλόγιστος.definition: not to be deceived; Act., not deceiving, Hsch. s.v

ἀπαράμονος.definition: not abiding, transient, Secund.Sent.14, Vett.Val.39.30, al

ἀπαραμύθητος.definition: not to be persuaded or; incorrigible, in Adv. Pl.Lg.731d

ἀπαράμυθος.definition: = foreg., inexorable, A.Pr.185 ; restive, E.IA620. [In A. metri gr.]

ἀπαραπόδιστος.definition: free from embarrassment or interference, Arr.Epict.1.1.10, al., BGU 1124.44 ; Hld.3.13; clear, Hices. ap. Ath.15.689c. Adv. Arr.Epict.2.13.21, S.E.M.1.178, PLond.3.1168.12 , Gal.4.725

ἀπαρασήμαντος.definition: unnoticed, LXX2 Ma.15.36, Mon.Ant.23.61 , cf. Michel 546.21

ἀπαράσημος.definition: not counterfeit, Hsch; with no defendant named, Antipho2.1 tit

ἀπαρασκεύαστος.definition: = sq., X.An.1.5.9, 2 Ep.Cor.9.4, J.AJ4.8.41. Adv. Arist.Rh.Al.1430a3

ἀπαράσκευος.definition: without preparation, unprepared, Antipho5.18 , Th.2.87; X.Cyr.7.5.25; D.40.30; Plb.1.49.4: c. gen., unprovided with, J.BJ3.7.32; also of things, Th.3.13: Sup., X.An.1.1.6. Adv. Plb.1.45.7, 14.10.7

ἀπαράστατος.definition: not having appeared in person, PLond.2.260.128

ἀπαρασχημάτιστος.definition: not parallel in formation, EM13.33: c. dat., having no corresponding neuter, Eust.94.30

ἀπαράτιλτος.definition: with hairs not pulled out, Ar.Lys.279, Luc.Salt.5

ἀπαραφύλακτος.definition: not to be guarded against; careless, heedless, Sch.E.Hipp.657

ἀπαραχάρακτος.definition: not counterfeit, Damocr. ap. Gal.14.135, Hsch. s.v

ἀπαράχυτος.definition: without anything poured in, unmixed, Gal.13.721, cf. 10.832; Hld.5.16: generally, pure, Plu.2.968c

ἀπαραχώρητος.definition: not giving ground, staunch; refusing to retire, unyielding, D.H.10.19; 10.54, cf. Plu.2.10a

ἀπαργυρισμός.definition: selling for ready money, Gloss; = Lat. adaeratio, PFlor.377.4 , Just.Nov.43.1 Intr., 130.4

ἀπαρέγκλιτος.definition: direct, Gal.UP15.8; inflexible; straight, Phlp.in Mete.21.10, cf. Ammon.in Porph.9.1. Adv. Gal.18.726; not diverging from the perpendicular, Eustr.in EN74.9

ἀπαρεγχείρητος.definition: not to be tampered with, inviolable, Ti.Locr.95a, Arr.Epict.4.1.161, J.AJ15.8.1. Adv. inimitably, perfectly, D.S.4.78

ἀπαρεμπόδιστος.definition: = , Sor.1.3; Chrysipp.Stoic.297, cf. S.E.M.1.147. Adv. Aët.16.61, Hdn.Fig.p.96S., Alex.Aphr.in Top.46.3

ἀπαρέμφατος.definition: not determinative or; the infinitive mood , D.H.Comp.5, A.D.Synt.226.20, Ps.-Alex.Aphr.in SE34.28; S.E.P.1.204. Adv. in the infinitive mood, take as an infinitive, A.D.Synt.76.16

ἀπαρενθύμητος.definition: not considering, carelessly, M.Ant.10.8. Adv. Id.6.53

ἀπαρενόχλητος.definition: undisturbed, Phld.Ir.p.78 W.; BGU1140.24 , cf. IGRom.4.2927 , PTeb.41.24, Plu.2.118b

ἀπαριθμέω.definition: count over, take an inventory of; reckon or pay back, repay, X.Cyr.3.1.42, D.H.4.10,etc

ἀπαρίθμησις.definition: counting over, Th.5.20, cf. Alex.Aphr.in Top.425.8, Procl.in Prm.p.908 S., in Ti.1.15 D., al.:—Adj. Sch.Hermog.Id.in Rh.7.1027 W

ἀπαρκέω.definition: suffice, be sufficient, Sol.5; to be contented, acquiesce, A.Ag.379 :—Pass., Cerc.18 ii 13, Lyc.1302

ἀπαρνέομαι.definition: fut. Pl.Grg.461c; in Logic, opp. deny, Arist.APr.41a9:—Pass., ib.63b37

ἀπαρτίζω.definition: fut. Mitteis Chr.88 iii 13 (ii A; generally, get ready, complete, Plb.31.12.10; finish, Iamb.in Nic.p.35 P.; dispose of, Mitteis Chr.l.c., cf. Charito6.1; educate an apprentice thoroughly, POxy.724.11 :— Pass., to be …

ἀπαρτιλογία.definition: Ion. an even number or sum, Hdt.7.29, Lys.Fr.28 S., Antipho Soph.99

ἀπαρτισμός.definition: completion, Ev.Luc.14.28; rounding off, Antyll. ap. Orib.50.3.1

ἀπαρχαΐζω.definition: compare to something ancient; assign antiquity to, Gal.14.683; Sch.Pi.N.3.27

ἀπαρχαιόομαι.definition: Pass., to be or become ancient, old-fashioned songs, Antiph.85; D.H.Th.24, Aristid.Rh.2p.508J

ἀπασβολόομαι.definition: turn to soot, become sooty, Dsc.5.76

ἀπασκαρίζω.definition: fut. Men.839:—struggle, be convulsed, like a dying fish, Ar.Fr.495; Men. l. c.; gave up the ghost, prob. for AP11.114

ἀπασπάζομαι.definition: take leave of, Act.Ap.21.6, v.l. in LXXTo.10.13; Him.Ecl.11.1

ἀπαστράπτω.definition: flash forth, Arat.430, Opp.C.1.220; J.AJ3.8.9: c. acc. cogn., Ph.1.150, al.; Opp.C.3.479; Procl.H.7.31, cf. Luc.Gall.7, Iamb.Myst.2.3

ἀπασφαλίζω.definition: make secure, fasten or shut up, Ps.-Porph. in Bentley Epistola ad Millium p.303 , Sch.E.Or.1108

ἀπατεών.definition: cheat, rogue, Hp.Art.42, Democr.63, Pl.R.451a, X.Cyr.1.6.27, Epicur.Fr.236, etc.:—as Adj., Max.Tyr.2.1

ἀπάτη.definition: trick, fraud, deceit; guile, treachery, A.Supp.111, cf. S.OC230; A.Fr.301, cf. Pers.93; S.Ant.617; Antipho6.7, etc.; opp. Th.4.86; 2.39; a being cheated out of the marriage, S.Ant.630; 'without fraud or covin', Hdt.1.…

ἀπαύγασμα.definition: radiance, effulgence, of light beaming from a luminous body, LXXWi.7.26; Ep.Hebr.1.3, cf. Ph.1.337, al., Hld.5.27, Dam. ap. Simp.in Ph.775.15

ἀπαυθαδίζομαι.definition: speak or act boldly, Pl.Ap.37a; freq. in late Prose, in bad sense, Ph.2.441; J.BJ3.7.11, cf. Plu.2.766c, Them.Or.10.131d,135a, 23.290c

ἀπαυθημερίζω.definition: do on the same day; esp. go or return the same day, X.An.5.2.1; Ael.VH9.2

ἀπαυλίζομαι.definition: aor. sleep or live away from, D.H.8.87; Poll.3.39

ἀπαυλιστήριος.definition: belonging to the a garment presented on this day, Poll.3.40

ἀπαυξάνομαι.definition: pf. part. in 'irrational' proportion to the Gal.8.913

ἀπαυτοματίζω.definition: do a thing of oneself, Plu.2.717b; produce spontaneously, Ph.1.36:—Pass., Id.2.182:—Act., intr., occur spontaneously, Id.1.571; ib.387; of the menses, Orib.7.20.1

ἀπαυτομολέω.definition: go of one's own accord, desert, Th.7.75; D.H.Orat.Vett.2; D.C.36.17

ἀπαυχενίζω.definition: cut off by the neck, D.S.34.2.22; tame a bull by forcing back his neck, Philostr.Her.12b, cf. Philostr.Jun.Im.2

ἀπαφρίζω.definition: skim, esp. of honey, Gp.8.29 and 32, Orib.5.33.4:— Pass., Gal.6.283, Gp.8.27.2, Philagr. ap. Orib.5.21.1

ἀπεθίζω.definition: disaccustom, Aeschin.1.58: c. inf., accustom or teach not to do something, ib.152; Philostr.VS1.25; Epicur.Fr.458, cf. Gal.16.141: pf. part. Plu.Alex.40:—Pass., J.BJ5.13.4

ἀπειδοποιέω.definition: construct according to a pattern, Inscr.Milet. , in form but more prob. from make flat, smooth

ἀπειθαρχία.definition: disobedience to command, Antipho Soph.72, D.C.Fr.57.17

ἀπείθεια.definition: disobedience, X.Mem.3.5.5, D.H.9.41, Arr.Epict.3.24.24; Ep.Eph.5.7; later BGU 747ii14 , etc., Gloss

ἀπεικάζω.definition: fut. X.Mem.3.11.1; express by a comparison, S.Fr.149.2, cf. Pl.Tht.169b; Id.Smp.221c; the word seems to express the growth . ., Id.Cra.414a; to express by the sound of ib.426e:—Pass., to be copied or expressed by like…

ἀπεικονίζω.definition: represent in a statue, AP12.56; Med., reflect, symbolize, Procl.in Alc.p.25 C., cf. Inst.209, Aristaenet.2.5

ἀπεικόνισμα.definition: = Socr.Ep.20, Ph.1.4, al., BMus.Inscr.481*.24 , Phlp.in Ph.316.24

ἀπειλητήρ.definition: threatener, boaster, Il.7.96, Call.Del.69, AP6.95 : as Adj., Nonn.D.4.378,al.:—fem. ib.2.257

ἀπειράγαθος.definition: unacquainted with goodness, foolish, LXXEs.8.13. Adv. D.S.15.40

ἀπειρόγαμος.definition: unwedded, Eub.35; of Athene, Nonn.D.47.416, Cat.Cod.Astr.7.227

ἀπειροδύναμος.definition: of infinite potentiality, Porph.Sent.37, cf. Procl.Inst.84, Id.in Prm.p.642 S., Dam.Pr.117, al., Simp.in Ph.608.36:—Subst. infinite potentiality, Procl.in Prm.p.873 S., Simp.in Ph.1329.10

ἀπειροειδής.definition: resembling the infinite, Procl.Inst.159, Dam.Pr.210, Simp.in Ph.528.13

ἀπειροκαλία.definition: ignorance of the beautiful, want of taste, Pl.R.403c; ib.405b; vulgar extravagance, Arist.EN1107b19; of literary style, D.H.Dem.23: in pl., vulgarities, X.Cyr.1.2.3

ἀπειρόκαλος.definition: ignorant of the beautiful, tasteless, vulgar, Pl.Lg.775b, cf. D.H.Pomp.2, etc.; Plu.2.44d; Ael.Tact.1.2; = X.Mem.3.10.5. Adv. Pl.Phdr.244c, etc.; foolishly, rashly, Onos.11.4

ἀπειρολογία.definition: interminable argument, S.E.P.2.151 , prob. l. in Phld.Rh.1.7S

ἀπειρομάχας.definition: unused to battle, untried in war, Pi.N.4.30

ἀπειροπλασίων.definition: gen. infinitely more, many thousand-fold, Phlp.in Mete.17.15, Eust.89.8

ἀπειροπληθής.definition: infinitely great or numerous, Id.562.37, Sch.Nic.Th.310:—Subst. or Eust.202.43

ἀπειροπόλεμος.definition: inexperienced in war, App.Mith.51; D.H.8.37. Adv. App.BC2.71

ἀπεκδίδωμι.definition: relet , CIG2266 ; simply, contract for, Michel468.72 ; ib.481.31

ἀπέκδοσις.definition: contract, Milet 6.36 , cf. PPetr.2p.34; performance of work contracted for, PSI4.352.5

ἀπεκλέγομαι.definition: pick out and reject, Dsc.1.7, Antip.Stoic.3.252, Arr.Epict.4.7.40

ἀπεκλογή.definition: rejection, opp. Diog.Bab.Stoic.3.219, cf. S.E.M.11.133: pl., Ph.Fr.8H

ἀπέκτασις.definition: spreading out, LXXJb.36.29, Gal.19.447; f.l. for in Ph.Bel.72.28:—also Anon.in Rh.146.1

ἀπελαύνω.definition: also as imper. from pres; lead away an army, Hdt.4.92: freq. abs. like march, depart, Id.1.77, cf. 5.25, etc.; Id.8.102; also ride away, X.Smp.9.7, etc

ἀπελέγχω.definition: strengthd. for convict, expose, refute, Antipho5.19; Ph.1.205; ib.193; . . M.Ant.8.36: abs., procure a conviction, CIG4325k ; vindicate, Jul.Or.2.81d:—Pass., to be convicted, of having persuaded, Antipho5.21

ἀπελευθερία.definition: Ion. enfranchisement of; status of a freedman, Poll.3.83

ἀπελευθεριάζω.definition: to be free, act freely, Ph.1.419, cf. 277; in bad sense, Id.2.31

ἀπελεύθερος.definition: restored to freedom, S.Ichn.193; emancipated slave, freedman, Pl.Lg.930d; Lys.7.10; opp. and X.Ath.1.10, Arist.Pol.1278a2; Aeschin.3.41: metaph., 1 Ep.Cor.7.22:—fem. Ion. Hp.Epid.5.75, Is.6.19, D.59.18, Men.436

ἀπελευθερόω.definition: emancipate a slave, Pl.Lg.915a sq., POxy.722.18 :—Pass., Pl.Lg.915b; Arist.Rh.1408b25

ἀπελευθέρωσις.definition: emancipation, D.17.15, cf. Plu.Publ.7, PGnom.60 , BGU96.10

ἀπελλάζω.definition: Lacon. for Plu.Lyc.6.—Hsch. writes but quotes IG5.1144.21, 1146.41

ἀπελπίζω.definition: Att. fut. D.S.19.50: pf; despair of, Plb.1.55.2, al.; to be confident of, Gal.8.365; D.S.2.25

ἀπεμπολάω.definition: sell, E.Ion1371; to sell for a thing, Id.Cyc.257; X.Smp.8.21, cf. Herod.7.65; Luc.Merc.Cond.23; sell, i.e. betray, E.Tr.973; barter your lives, Id.Ph.1228; dost thou smuggle her out of the country? Id.IT1360; Procop.P…

ἀπενθής.definition: free from grief, A.Pr.956; B.12.87; Fr.7.2, cf. Plu.Flam.11, Tryph.599

ἀπενιαύτησις.definition: banishment for a term of years, ib.868e

ἀπεξαρτάω.definition: hang out, Anon. ap. Suid. s.v

ἀπεξινόω.definition: purge, prob. in Timocl.39; also aor. Med. Hsch

ἀπεραντολόγος.definition: talking without end, Thal.4 Bgk., cf. Ph.1.216: Comp. Gal.18.254

ἀπεργάζομαι.definition: pf. sts. Act., Pl.Lg.704c; of a painter, fill up with colour, represent in a finished picture, opp. , Pl.R.548d

ἀπερεύγομαι.definition: belch forth, disgorge, Hp.Morb.2.60, Nic.Al.380, etc.; of a river, empty itself, D.P.693,981

ἀπερημόομαι.definition: to be left destitute of, Pl.Plt.274b; to be isolated, Id.Sph.237d; in isolation, Plot.6.6.11

ἀπερίβλεπτος.definition: not looked at from all sides: hence; Act., regardless, Phryn.PSp.10B

ἀπεριγένητος.definition: not to be overcome, D.S.3.30; Corn.ND31

ἀπερίγραφος.definition: not circumscribed, Ph.1.5, al., Procl.Inst.93, Dam.Pr.71; undetermined, of time, Chrysipp.Stoic.2.67

ἀπερίεργος.definition: not over-busy, artless, simple, Hp.Decent.3; Gal.13.168; of things, Dsc.Eup.1.35, Sor.2.11; Ath.6.274a: Sup., ib.b; simplicity, Plu.2.1144f, Ach.Tat.5.27. Adv. Ceb.21, D.H.Dem.9, Sor.1.46, S.E.P.1.240, Ael.VH12.1

ἀπεριήγητος.definition: not traced out, Pl.Lg.770b; innumerable, Simp.in Ph.178.29

ἀπερικάλυπτος.definition: uncovered, exposed, in Adv. undisguisedly, Hld.8.5

ἀπεριλάλητος.definition: not to be out-talked or without skill in circumlocution, Ar.Ra.839:—cf. Hsch

ἀπερίληπτος.definition: uncircumscribed, absolute power, Plu.Pomp.25; indeterminate, Theol.Ar.58; not to be embraced or comprehended, Ph.2.24; Iamb.VP29.159: abs., Plot.6.9.6, cf. Procl.Inst.150; incomprehensible, Iamb.Myst.1.7, Dam.Pr.7; Ga…

ἀπερίλυτος.definition: not annulled or cancelled, valid, BGU1170.58 , POxy.713.39

ἀπερινόητος.definition: inconceivable, i.e. indefinitely short, Epicur.Ep.1p.10U; unintelligent, Eust.644.43

ἀπερίοπτος.definition: unregarding, reckless of, Th.1.41, J.AJ19.1.11: abs., Onos.1.22. Adv. Poll.3.117

ἀπερίπνευστος.definition: sheltered from wind, Agathin. ap. Orib.10.7.16

ἀπερίπτωτος.definition: not liable to, or; not stumbling, of the Stoic sage, Arr.Epict.1.1.31, al. Adv., Comp. 4.6.26

ἀπερισάλπιγκτος.definition: not surrounded by the sound of trumpets, Pyrrhus ap.Stob.4.13.60

ἀπερίσπαστος.definition: not drawn hither and thither, not; uninterrupted, free from digressions, D.H.Th.9; the fact of power not passing from hand to hand, Plu.Arist.5. Adv. continually, Ath.1.10c

ἀπερίστικτος.definition: not dotted round, opp. Sch.Il.p.xliii Dind., etc.; Gal.19.750

ἀπερίτμητος.definition: uncircumcised, LXXGe.17.14, al; not clipped or circumscribed, Plu.2.495c

ἀπερίτρεπτος.definition: not to be turned or moved, immutable, Sm.Ps.95.10, Plu.2.983c. Adv. S.E.M.1.53

ἀπερίψυκτος.definition: free from chill, Gal.11.475, cf. Sor.2.14

ἀπέρρω.definition: go away, be gone, E.HF260; away! begone! Ar.Nu.783, Ec.169; Cratin.123

ἀπεσχαρόω.definition: remove a scab, Zopyr. ap. Orib.14.61.2:—Pass., Eust.1575.43

ἀπευθανατίζω.definition: die well or happily, LXX2 Ma.6.28

ἀπευκταῖος.definition: = Pl.Ax.369b , Plu.2.289b; CPHerm. 119riv 16 , cf. A.D.Synt.252.10. Adv. to the loss of our hopes, POxy.1114.24

ἀπευτακτέω.definition: deliver or pay regularly, Str.4.6.9:— Pass., Id.7.4.6, UPZ42.15

ἀπεχθήμων.definition: gen. worse form for sq., Poll.8.153

ἀπηγορέομαι.definition: Med., defend oneself, like Arist.Pr.951a23:—Act., defend, Simp.in Cat.17.2

ἀπηλιώτης.definition: east wind, Hdt.4.22, 7.188, E.Cyc.19, Th.3.23; opp. Arist.Mete.363b13, cf.Mu.394b23, Vent.973a13, al.—The Ion. form is retained in Att., and appears on the Tower of Andronicus Cyrrhestes, CIG 518; on a later table of …

ἀπιάλλω.definition: fut. Hsch., Dor. for Th.5.77; keep them off, Archestr.Fr.29

ἀπισόω.definition: make equal, in reference to Procrustes, Plu.Thes.11, cf. Luc.Pr.Im.13:—Pass., to be made equal, to their value, Hdt.4.196, cf. Sch.Il.Oxy.1086i 22

ἀπισχναίνω.definition: make lean or thin, Philem.98.7, Arist.HA574b6

ἀπισχνόω.definition: in Pass., shrink, Hp.Int.3, Morb.Sacr.8, cf. Sor.1.53

ἀπισχυρίζομαι.definition: oppose firmly, give a flat denial; set oneself to affirm, maintain a thing, ib.28.342c, Eust.1278.53, etc

ἀπιχθυόομαι.definition: Pass., to become a fish, Herm. ap. Stob.1.49.69

ἀπλανής.definition: not wandering, steady, fixed; Astron. of stars,fixed, opp.planets, ib.40b, cf.Arist.Mete.343b9, Metaph.1073b10, Arat.461, AP9.25 ; Corp.Herm.2.6

ἀπλάνητος.definition: that cannot go astray or err, LXXJb.12.20, Babr.50.20, POxy.237 vi30

ἀπληστεύομαι.definition: to be insatiable, in a thing, Hipparch. ap. Stob.4.44.81; LXXSi.34.17

ἀπληστία.definition: insatiate desire, greediness, whether of; c. gen. rei, insatiate desire of, Pl.R.562b, Lg.831d; E.Andr.218; referring to Midas, Arist.Pol.1257b16; Ph.1.12

ἄπληστος.definition: insatiate, greedy, Thgn.109, S.El.1336; Adv. Pl.Grg.493c, al.; or X.Cyr.4.1.14, Isoc.5.135, 8.7: also neut. pl. as Adv., CIG2240

ἁπλοΐζομαι.definition: behave simply, deal frankly, X.Mem.4.2.18; to be simple in habits, D.C.65.7; to be reduced to simplicity, Dam.Pr.32.—Act. in same sense, Sch.Od.6.187

ἁπλοτομία.definition: simple incision, Antyll. ap. Orib.44.8.6, Gal.14.781

ἅπλωμα.definition: that which is unfolded, expanse, Sch.Ar.Av.1218

ἀπνεύμων.definition: gen. without breath or life, Simp.in Epict.p.6 D., Orac. ap. Dam.Pr.453, Tab.Defix.Aud.22.8

ἀποβάλλω.definition: throw away, h.Merc.388, Hdt.3.40, etc.; Ar.V.22, And.1.74, Lys.10.9, etc.; reject him, E.Tr.663, cf. Pl.Tht.151c, etc.; cast, shed, Arist.HA500a10, 604a15,al.:—Med., Pl.Lg.802b; jettisons cargo, Arist.EN1110a9; Theoc.…

ἀποβάπτω.definition: dip, plunge, Hdt.2.47; draw water, LXX2 Ma.1.21

ἀποβατήριος.definition: of Zeus, as protector of persons; offerings made on landing, St.Byz. s.v. Poll.2.200

ἀποβάτης.definition: one that dismounts; but in usage, one who rode several horses leaping from one to the other, Plu.Phoc.20, cf. IG2.966,al., D.H.7.73, AB198,426, EM124.31, Suid

ἀποβήσσω.definition: cough up, Hp.Aph.5.11, Prog.23: fut. Id.Mul.1.41

ἀποβιάζομαι.definition: force away, force back; treat with violence, Plb.16.24.5: abs., 33.9.5, cf. SIG629.20 , Wilcken Chr.11 A30 : metaph., Phld.Oec.p.59J

ἀποβιβάζω.definition: causal of B, make to get off, esp. from a ship, disembark, put on shore, Th.6.97, etc.; Hdt.8.76, Pl.Grg.511e; Ar.V.1163; X.HG7.4.3:—Med., cause them to be put on shore, Hdt.9.32

ἀποβιβρώσκω.definition: eat off, in aor. Pass. AP7.294

ἀποβίωσις.definition: ceasing to live, death, Plu.2.389a, CIG4253 ,al

ἀποβλάπτω.definition: ruin utterly, Pi.N.7.60, Pl.Lg.795d:-Pass., to be robbed of a friend, S.Aj.941

ἀποβλαστάνω.definition: shoot forth from, spring from, S.OC533, cf. Plu.2.954c, Hierocl.in CA17p.459M., Iamb.Myst.3.20

ἀποβλάστησις.definition: shooting forth, growth, Hp.Art.45, cf. Gal.UP8.6; of roots, Dsc.2.183

ἀπόβλεπτος.definition: gazed on by all, admired, E.Hec.355, Procop.Arc.9,al

ἀποβλέπω.definition: fut. Luc.Somn.12, etc., but HeroSpir.2.34: Antip.Stoic.3.254 codd. Stob.:-Med., pres., Luc.VH2.47 : aor., Sch.Od.12.247:-Pass., Ar.Ec.726:-look away from all other objects at one, gaze steadfastly, Hdt.7.135; E.Andr.2…

ἀποβλήσιμος.definition: fit to be cast away, CPHerm.119rvi5

ἀποβοόομαι.definition: Pass., of Io, become a cow, Eust.278.32

ἀπόβρασμα.definition: that which is thrown off, Alex.Trall.Febr.6; scum, Hsch.; chaff, Id., Suid

ἀποβράσσω.definition: Att. Poll.6.91: mostly in aor; metaph., ib.354

ἀπόβρεγμα.definition: infusion, Agatharch.61, Str.16.4.17, Dsc.4.81, Aret.CA1.1, Plu.2.614b

ἀποβρέχω.definition: steep well, soak, Thphr.CP2.5.5, IG4.955.9 : metaph., Zeno Stoic.1.67, cf. Suid. s.v. aor. part. Thphr.HP5.9.5; Dsc.1.110: metaph., Philostr.VA7.22

ἀποβροχίζω.definition: ligature, Sor.1.80, Gal.14.784; bind tightly, AP9.410

ἀποβροχισμός.definition: making a ligature, Antyll. ap. Orib.45.24.3

ἀπογαλακτίζω.definition: wean from the mother's milk, Diph.74, LXXGe.21.8, Sor.1.116, POxy.37i22 , PLips.31.20

ἀπογαλακτόομαι.definition: Pass., to become milky, Antyll. ap. Orib.4.11.6

ἀπογαληνόομαι.definition: calm down, of physical disturbances, Sor.1.46

ἀπογεισόω.definition: crown with a cornice, IG22.463.71,cf. BCH35.12 : metaph., make to jut out like a cornice, X.Mem.1.4.6:—Pass., jut out like a cornice, Arist.GA781b13

ἀπογεμίζομαι.definition: Pass., of a ship, discharge her cargo, D.H.3.44; to be emptied of contents, Ps.-Luc.Philopatr.24

ἀπογεόομαι.definition: Pass., to be changed into earth, Ph.2.508

ἀπογεύω.definition: give one a taste of, AP4.3.39 ; opp; Med., take a taste of, Hp.Epid.7.2, cf. Pl.R.354b, Tht.157d, X.Cyr.1.3.4, Plb.3.57.8; Eub.42, cf. Antiph.326: metaph., Ph.2.338

ἀπογηράσκω.definition: grow old, Thgn.821, Hp.Aph.2.20; part. dub. l. Alex.278; inf. of senile dementia, Gal.16.696; Thphr.HP7.13.6; of vines, . . fail from old age, Tab.Heracl.1.170

ἀπογίγνομαι.definition: Ion. and later Att. fut; abs., to be taken away, opp. Zeno Eleat.2, Pl.Ti.82b, Lg.850a; . . Th.2.98: generally, to be away, absent, Antipho2.3.5, Pl.Phd.69b, D.8.35: Aeschin.2.126; of diseases, opp. Hp.Morb.Sacr.1

ἀπογιγνώσκω.definition: Ion. and later Att. fut; c. gen. rei, despair of, Lys.2.46; Men.131; D.Chr.32.97; Jul.Or.2.61c: abs., despair, D.4.42 , Babr.43.18: c. fut. inf., Arr.An.3.20.3; Luc.Icar.10: c. aor. inf., Arr.An.1.5.8, cf. D.Chr.32.9

ἀπογλαυκόομαι.definition: Pass., suffer from of the; become grey-blue, of the pupil, Dem.Ophth. ap. Aët.7.53; to be dyed blue, PHolm.26.32

ἀπογλαύκωσις.definition: formation of a Dsc.1.54, Ptol.Tetr.149 , Orib.Syn.3.151

ἀπογλάφομαι.definition: scrape off from oneself, obliterate, . . Com.Adesp.574, cf. Paus.Gr.Fr.109

ἀπογλυκαίνω.definition: sweeten, D.S.1.40, cf. Ruf. ap. Orib.8.47b7; Diph.Siph. ap. Ath.2.55f

ἀπογλύφω.definition: scrape or peel off, Aret.CD1.2, Alciphr.3.60; scrape thin, Heliod. ap.Orib.48.33.3; carve, of sculpture, Rev.Phil.44.251

ἀπογλωττίζομαι.definition: Pass., to be deprived of tongue, Luc.Lex.15

ἀπογραφή.definition: register, list, of lands or property; register of persons liable to taxation, Ev.Luc.2.2, J.AJ18.1.1; PLond.2.260.79 , etc.; of the Roman census-lists, Plu.Cat.Ma.16 ; muster-roll of soldiers, Plb.2.23.9

ἀπόγραφος.definition: copied:—as Subst., a copy, D.H.Is.11, D.L.6.84; Cic.Att.12.52.3

ἀπογράφω.definition: write off, copy, and in Med., have a thing; enter in a list, register, Hdt.7.100:—Pass., to be registered, Pl.Lg.914c, cf. Men.272; Is.6.44:—freq. Med., register as one's own property, POxy.246.10 ; declare as liable …

ἀποδάκνω.definition: bite off a piece of; abs., bite, gnaw, Cratin.164, cf. X.Smp.5.7, Tab.Defix.Aud.237.18 :—Pass., have one's tongue bitten, as by a pungent substance, Arist.Pr.958b7

ἀποδαρθάνω.definition: aor. inf. Them.Or.7.91a; wake up, Ael.NA3.13

ἀποδαψιλεύομαι.definition: to be liberal of a thing, Gloss

ἀποδέδεγμαι.definition: pf. of also Ion. for pf. Pass. of

ἀποδείκνυμι.definition: point out, display, make known, whether by deed or word, Hdt.1.171,al.; Th.1.26; A.Ag.727; Hyp.Epit.29; Hp.Praec.9; proclaim, GDI l. c.;—Pass., SIG134b22

ἀποδεικτικός.definition: affording proof, demonstrative; in which the facts are regularly set forth and explained, Plb.2.37.3, 4.40.1, cf. Plu.2.243a. Adv. Sch.Iamb.in Nic.p.129 P

ἀποδεισιδαιμονέω.definition: brood over with superstitious fear, Sch.Th.7.50

ἀποδεκατόω.definition: tithe, take a tenth of, LXX1 Ki.8.16; pay tithe of, LXXGe.28.22, Ev.Matt.23.23, etc

ἀποδέκτης.definition: receiver: in pl., financial officials, established by Cleisthenes, IG2.38, D.24.162, Arist.Ath.48, Pol.1321b33, Harp.: also at Thasos, IG12.608; in Egypt, Ostr.1217; POxy.43riii 8 , cf. Poll.8.114; Jahresh.21/2 Beibl.…

ἀποδενδρόομαι.definition: Pass., grow into a tree, Thphr.HP3.17.2, cf. 1.3.2; to be turned into a tree, Luc.VH1.8, Heraclit.All.36

ἀποδερματίζω.definition: flay, strip, Androm. ap. Gal.12.991, Sch.Nic.Al.301, Hsch

ἀποδερματόομαι.definition: Pass., of shields, to have their leather covering destroyed, Plb.6.25.7: —late in Act., flay, Zos.Alch.p.108 B

ἀποδεσμέω.definition: = foreg., Pherecyd.119J., Tim.Gaz. ap. Ar.Byz.Epit.143.14, Olymp.in Mete.96.7

ἀπόδεσμος.definition: band, breastband, girdle, Ar.Fr.320.13; bag, case, receptacle, Plu.Dem.30, Paul.Aeg.3.41; sachet, LXXCa.1.13
