ἀποδέχομαι.definition: accept as a teacher, follow, X.Mem.4.1.1,etc.; Pl.Prt.323c; admit to one's presence, Plb.21.35.5; 21.22.1, cf. 3.66.8

ἀποδέω.definition: bind fast, tie up the navel, Pl.Smp.190e; generally, bind, LXXJo.9.4, J.AJ4.8.21:—Pass., Pl.Erx.400a, cf. Arist.HA587a14, Erasistr. ap. Gal.11.148

ἀποδημέω.definition: Dor. pf. dub. in; go abroad, to visit him, Hdt.3.124; go abroad to Aegina to fetch the Aeacidae, Id.8.84; Pl.Cri.53e; Id.Ap.40e; Lycurg.21,57 ; X.HG4.7.3; Ar.Ra.48; Pl.Lg.579b; Id.Phd.61e

ἀποδημία.definition: Ion. going or being abroad, Hdt.6.130, cf. Lys.3.10; Pl.Cri.52b; Id.Lg.949e, cf. 950a; And.4.30; as to my life in that foreign land, i.e. beyond the grave, Pl.Phd.61e, cf. 67c, Ap.41a ; from a long journey, X.Cyr.3.1.7

ἀπόδημος.definition: Dor. away from one's country, abroad, Pi.P.4.5, cf. Plu.2.799f, etc.; from abroad, CIG3344 A ; Luc.Am.6: metaph., Hp.Ep.17:—less Att. than Moer.143, cf. Poll.1.177

ἀποδιαγράφω.definition: order payment to be made, SIG976.30 , PTheb.Bank 12.7

ἀποδιαιρέω.definition: distribute, v.l. in LXXJo.1.6; divide off, distinguish from, Jul.Or.5.165b; Eust.1221.36:—Pass., PStrassb.92.6

ἀποδιαλαμβάνω.definition: set apart, Syrian.in Metaph.64.40; discuss separately, Dex.in Cat.59.16, Herm.in Phdr.p.115A., etc

ἀποδιάληψις.definition: division into parts, Iamb.Myst.1.9, Procl.in Prm.p.674S.; abstraction, Dex.in Cat.40.9

ἀποδιαστέλλω.definition: divide, PTaur. 8.22.48 , LXXJo.1.6 :—Pass., to be set apart, forbidden, ib.2 Ma.6.5

ἀποδιατρίβω.definition: waste time, Aeschin.2.49; spend; c. acc. pers., detain, D.C.44.19; defer, App.BC2.20: abs., delay, ib.13

ἀποδιδύσκω.definition: = Artem.2.69:—Med., Parth.15.3; cast off, slough off, Artem.2.13,14

ἀποδιΐστημι.definition: intr., to be distant, Lib.Descr.8.1, cf. Paul.Al.F.1

ἀποδικάζω.definition: acquit, opp. Antipho6.47, Arist.Pol.1268b18; Critias71 D., PPetr.3p.44

ἀποδικέω.definition: defend oneself on trial, X.HG1.7.21, Antiph.313

ἀποδιοπομπέομαι.definition: fut. (in pass. sense; generally, set aside, waive, Ath.9.401b, cf. Theo Sm.p.200H

ἀποδιοπόμπησις.definition: offering of an expiatory sacrifice, Pl.Lg.854b

ἀποδιορίζω.definition: mark off by dividing or defining, Arist.Pol.1290b26; Ep.Jud.19

ἀποδισκεύω.definition: throw like a discus, in Pass., Eust.1591.31

ἀποδιφθερόομαι.definition: Pass., to be covered with hides, Lyd.Ost.45

ἀποδιωθέω.definition: thrust away, Hices. ap. Ath.3.87d, cf. Hp.Mul.2.201, Aspasia ap.Aët.16.72:—Med., Ar.Byz.Epit.10.9

ἀποδίωγμα.definition: pursuit, a ceremony performed at the Thesmophoria, Hsch.s.v

ἀποδιώκω.definition: fut. chase away, Th.3.108, 6.102; Arist.HA614a16; take yourself off, Ar.Nu.1296; Men.410; intr., move, Olymp.in Mete.43.2:—Pass., to be ridden at full speed, of a horse, Aët.3.7

ἀποδίωξις.definition: expulsion, Antyll. ap. Orib.6.36.4, cf. Gp.13.1.1

ἀποδοκιμάζω.definition: reject on scrutiny or trial, reject a; generally, reject as unworthy or unfit, Pl.Tht.181b; X.Eq.Mag.1.13; Id.Mem.4.4.14; Thphr.Char.4.11; Arist.Pol.1341a26, cf. 37 ; Id.HA618a17; Timocl.8.12; X.Cyr.8.1.47: c. inf., P…

ἀπόδοσις.definition: payment, IG1.32 A 5, etc.; Th.8.85; Luc.VH1.36: generally, giving, Pl.Lg.807d; rendering, i.e. performance, Dam.Pr.64

ἀποδοχεῖον.definition: storehouse, LXXSi.1.17; cistern, ib.50.3; also PHib.1.85 , BCH1.55

ἀποδοχεύς.definition: keeper of archives, IGRom.4.1248 , Jahresh.21/2 Beibl.255

ἀποδραπετεύω.definition: run away from, Tz. in An.Ox.4.80

ἀποδρεπανίζω.definition: prune, lop with a Suid. s.v

ἀποδρέπω.definition: pluck off, pluck and take them home, Hes.Op.611; pluck off hair, Hp.Mul.2.106: metaph., Pi.P.9.110, cf. O.1.13; Archipp.2 D.:—Med., Pi.Fr.122.8, cf. AP6.303 , Plu.2.79d

ἀποδυσπετέω.definition: desist through impatience, Arist.Top.163b19; Plu.2.502e; Luc.Rh.Pr.3; Alciphr.3.74

ἀποδυτήριον.definition: undressing room in the bath, X.Ath.2.10, Pl.Ly.206e, etc.; in the palaestra, Id.Euthd.272e

ἀποζεύγνυμι.definition: separate, part, Man.3.85; mostly in Pass., aor. , also E.El.284, AP12.226 :—to be loosed from the yoke, Babr.37.6; but usually metaph., to be parted from, E.HF1375, cf. Med.1017; if I were free from . ., Id.Supp.791; …

ἀποθαρρέω.definition: and take courage, have full confidence, X.Oec.16.6: c. inf., to have the boldness to . ., Longin.32.8, J.AJ15.7.3: c. acc., Paus.10.19.5: c. dat., use rashly, Aët.12.23

ἀποθαυμάζω.definition: Ion. or marvel much at a thing, Od.6.49; Hdt.1.11,30; Id.2.79: abs., wonder much, Id.1.68, X.Oec.2.17, Luc.Am.13, POxy.1242 iii 53 : c. part., Hdt.1.88; folld. by wonder that . ., Aeschin.1.94, 119.—Rare in Trag., A.A…

ἀποθεόω.definition: deify, Pteb.5.78 , Plb.12.23.4; in magic, drown a sacred animal and thus liberate its divine element, PMag.Berol.1.5, PMag.Lond.121.629 ; Afric.ap. Sch.Tz.H.9.161

ἀποθεραπεία.definition: regular worship; restorative treatment after fatigue, Antyll. ap. Orib.6.21.1, Gal.Thras.47

ἀποθεραπεύω.definition: treat with attention and honour; cure, Hp.Praec.5; Plu.2.118c; apply to, Antyll. ap. Orib.7.16.10, Gal.6.201

ἀποθερίζω.definition: poet. aor. :—cut off, Archil.138; E.Or.128, cf. Hel.1188, AP6.107 , etc.; Dsc.3.70; of persons, Nonn.D.48.96; regul. form in Ael.NA1.5, Apollod.1.9.22; LXXHo.6.6:—Med., aor. AP5.236 ; of the tonsure of monks, Procop.A…

ἀποθεσπίζω.definition: utter as an oracle, Str.9.3.5, cf. Plu.Luc.2; prophesy, D.H.6.43

ἀπόθετος.definition: laid by, stored up, Dsc.5.9; hidden, secret, mysterious, Pl.Phdr.252b; D.H.11.62, cf. Philostr.Im.1.10, 2.16, Plu.Crass.16

ἀποθεωρέω.definition: = Arist.Mir.839b3, Plb.27.4.4, D.S.4.38, Polycharm.1; observe, Plu.Lyc.25; examine, consider, Phld. Rh.2.116 S., cf. Oec.p.74J

ἀποθεώρησις.definition: serious contemplation, Plu.Pel.25; wide view, D.S.19.38

ἀποθηλασμός.definition: sucking, sucking out, Erasistr. ap. Dsc.Ther.Praef., Sor.1.77, Paul.Aeg.3.35

ἀποθηριόω.definition: change into a beast; make quite savage, Plu.2.995d; exasperate, Plb.1.79.8:—Pass., to become or be so, ib.67.6; D.S.17.9; of wounds, Plb.1.81.5

ἀποθηρίωσις.definition: changing into a wild beast, Hsch; fury or rage against any one, D.S.34/5.20

ἀποθησαυρίζω.definition: store, hoard up, LXXSi.3.4, D.S.5.40, Luc.Alex.23; 1 Ep.Ti.6.19:—Pass., J.BJ7.8.4, Vett.Val.16.21

ἀποθινόομαι.definition: Pass., to be silted up, Plb.1.75.8

ἀποθρασύνομαι.definition: to be very courageous, dare all things, D.61.20:— later Diog.Ep.32.3

ἀπόθραυσις.definition: breaking, fracture, Paul.Aeg.6.89,117; Sor.Fract.10. II. breaking up, Arist.Mu.394a33

ἀποθραύω.definition: break off, A.Pers.410; D.H.4.56: metaph., Jul.Mis.356b; Dam.Pr.51:—Pass., to be broken off, Arist.Pr.967b5, Arr.Tact.2.4: metaph., to be broken off from one's fair fame, make shipwreck of it, Ar.Nu.997

ἀποθυννίζω.definition: dismiss as worthy of a tunny, in Pass., Luc.JTr.25, cf. Eust.1720.63

ἀποθυρίζω.definition: put out of doors, Gloss.:—also Hsch

ἀποθύω.definition: fut. IG4.951.45 :—offer up as a votive sacrifice, X.An.3.2.12; 4.8.25; Diph.43.10; IG l.c

ἀποθωρακίζομαι.definition: put off one's coat of mail, Procop.Goth.4.32

ἀποικεσία.definition: = esp. of the Captivity, LXX4 Ki.24.15, al

ἀποικέω.definition: go away from home, esp. as a colonist, settle; dwell afar off, Th.3.55; X.Oec.4.6; E.HF557, cf. IA680; Arist.Pol.1272b1; Philostr.Im.1.9: c. acc., live a long way off a person, Theoc.15.7 :—Pass., . . Corinth was inha…

ἀποίκησις.definition: = sq., emigration, Hsch., Suid.; dub. in D.H.2.36

ἀποικισμός.definition: settlement of a colony; = LXXJe.26.19, al

ἀποικιστής.definition: leader of a colony, IG1.31.4, Men.Rh.p.356 S

ἀποικονομέω.definition: manage so as to get rid of a thing, Antyll. ap. Orib.6.6.1:—Med., get rid of them by one's manner of life, Hierocl.p.51A., cf. Plot.1.4.6,5.9.1, Procl.in Prm.p.497 S.:—Pass., to be removed, Herod.Med. ap. Orib.10.37.17

ἀποικονόμησις.definition: getting rid of a thing, Cass.Pr.70

ἀποικονόμητος.definition: to be got rid of, Arr.Epict.4.1.44

ἀποικτίζομαι.definition: complain loudly of a thing, . . Hdt.1.114

ἀποιμώζω.definition: bewail loudly, A.Ag.329, S.Ph.278; A.Fr.138, Antipho5.41; E.Med.31; D.H.5.8

ἀποιωνίζομαι.definition: shun as an ill-omen, Lat.abominari, Gloss

ἀποκαθαίρω.definition: aor. inf. Gal.11.129, but subj; refine metal by smelting, Str.9.1.23; purified, Dsc.1.25: metaph., to be pure in dialect, Luc.Hist. Conscr.21

ἀποκάθαρμα.definition: that which is cleared off, excretion, Arist.PA677a29, cf. HA546b24; by-product, dross, 624a15; dregs, Jul.Or.5.170d; offscourings, slops, St.Byz. s.v

ἀποκάθαρσις.definition: purging: hence, of dross; cleansing, Gp.12.22.11; sifting of grain, PRev.Laws 39.10 , PLond.ined.2361r

ἀποκαθιστάνω.definition: = sq., SIG2588.56 , Plb.3.98.9, D.S.18.57: —also v.l. in Arist.Metaph.1074a3

ἀποκαθίστημι.definition: fut. aor. later; pay what is due, LXXGe.23.16

ἀποκαλαμουργέω.definition: free from reeds, in Pass., PLond.3.1003.7

ἀποκαλλωπίζω.definition: strip of ornament, esp. of foliage, Poll.1.236

ἀποκαλύπτω.definition: aor. 2 Pass. CPR1.239.5 (iii; disclose, reveal, Pl.Prt.352a; Id.Grg.455d, cf. 460a:—Med., reveal one's whole mind, Plu.Alex.55,2.880e:—in Pass., LXX1 Ki.2.27, al.; let one's designs upon a thing become known, D.S.17.6…

ἀποκάλυφος.definition: uncovered, Ph.1.141 ; land cultivable only when the water receded, BGU640, CPR 32.7 ; CPHerm.45.6

ἀποκάλυψις.definition: uncovering, of the head, Phld.Vit.p.38J.; disclosing, of hidden springs, Plu.Aem.14: metaph., Id.2.70f; revelation, esp. of divine mysteries, Ep.Rom.16.25, etc.; of persons, manifestation, 2 Ep.Thess.1.7, etc.; title …

ἀποκαραδοκέω.definition: expect earnestly, c. acc., Plb.16.2.8, al., Aq.Ps. 36.7, J.BJ3.7.26

ἀποκαρδιουργέω.definition: extract the heart of a victim, Hsch. s.v

ἀποκαρπίζω.definition: gather fruit:—Pass., to be stript of; metaph. in Med., reap the fruits of, enjoy, c. acc. rei, IG 14.1934 fi 12

ἀποκαρπόω.definition: throw off, send out, Hp.Oss.17:—Med., enjoy the fruits of, PAmh.2.142.15

ἀποκαρτερέω.definition: kill oneself by abstinence, starve oneself to death, Hp.Acut.56; title of work by Hegesias, Cic.Tusc.1.34.84, cf. Plu.Num.21, Luc.Macr.19; Phld.Mort.6; Com.Adesp.336.8; . ., Timocl.18

ἀποκαρφόομαι.definition: Pass., to be parched, dried up, Sever.Clyst.p.12D

ἀποκατάστασις.definition: restoration, re-establishment, Arist.MM1205a4; ib.1204b36, 1205b11; return to a position, Epicur.Ep.1p.8U.; esp. of military formations, reversal of a movement, Ascl.Tact.10.6, etc.; generally, Act.Ap.3.21; of the sou…

ἀποκατατίθημι.definition: lay aside, A.R.3.1287: c. gen., ib.817

ἀποκαταφαίνομαι.definition: Pass., to be clearly visible, Aristaenet.1.3

ἀποκαυλίζω.definition: break off by the stalk: hence, break short off, E.Supp.717, Th.2.76:—Pass., to be so broken, to be fractured across, Hp.Fract.45, Art.33

ἀπόκαυμα.definition: firebrand, Sm.Ps.101 .4; blister caused by a burn, Hierocl.Facet.135, Eust.1123.24; chilblain, Id.ad D.P.916, Sch.Nic.Th.677

ἀπόκειμαι.definition: fut. used as Pass. of; abs., to be laid up in store, of money, Philetaer.7.6; D.42.6; Lys.19.22; for one's use, X.An.2.3.15; . . is laid up as a common possession, S.OC1752: hence, to be kept in reserve, X.Cyr.3.1.19,…

ἀποκενόω.definition: drain, exhaust, Hp.Nat.Puer.15; LXXJd.3.24; evacuate, Sor.1.27:—Pass., Arist.Fr.224

ἀποκεντέω.definition: pierce through, Hp.Ulc.25, LXXNu.25.8, al., D.L.9.26

ἀποκερδαίνω.definition: pf. D.C.43.18:—have benefit, enjoyment from or of a thing, c. gen., E.Cyc.432; make some small gain of a thing, And.1.134: abs., Luc.DMort.4.1

ἀποκερματίζω.definition: break into small pieces, Porph.Sent.37; metaph., dissipate one's whole substance, AP7.607

ἀποκεφαλαιόομαι.definition: Pass., to be summed up, Eust.1769.4

ἀποκεφαλίζω.definition: behead, Arr.Epict.1.1.24, LXXPs.151.7, v.l. in Artem.1.35; of a fish, Dorio ap.Ath.7.287e:—Pass., Phld.Sign.13, 29, Arr.Epict.1.1.19

ἀποκεφάλισμα.definition: dirt that comes off the head, Poll.2.48

ἀποκήρυκτος.definition: publicly renounced; of a son, disinherited, disowned, Theopomp.Hist.309, Poll.4.93, Luc.Icar.14, Hermog.Stat

ἀποκήρυξις.definition: public announcement, esp. public renunciation of a son, disinheriting, Plu.Them.2, Luc.Abd.5, Hermog.Inv.4.13

ἀποκηρύσσω.definition: Att. offer a thing for public; renounce publicly, Pl.Lg.928esq., cf. D.39.39, Luc.Abd.1:—Pass., to be disinherited, Aeschin.Socr.Oxy.1608.39

ἀποκίδναμαι.definition: spread abroad from a place, A.R.4.133, Arat.735, D.P.48

ἀποκιρσόομαι.definition: Pass., become varicose, Archig. ap. Gal.8.90

ἀποκισσόομαι.definition: Pass., develop into of; to be deprived of the ivy-wreath, IG3.80

ἀποκλαίω.definition: or bewail much, mourn deeply for, Thgn.931, A.Pr.637; Pl.Phd.117c:—Med., bewail one's woes, S.OT1467; Ar.V.564; E.Fr.563

ἀποκλεισμός.definition: exclusion, Arr.Epict.4.7.20, Artem.3.54; but, prison, Aq.Ps.141.8

ἀποκλείω.definition: fut. X.An.4.3.20: Att; shut out or exclude from, Id.1.37, etc.; D.28.17; Ar.V.601; also . . . . Id.Av.1263:—Pass., turn away from food, have no appetite, Hp.Int.1; Id.Vict.3.81, cf. D.54.11; Id.45.19; refuse, Phld.Her…

ἀποκληρόω.definition: choose by lot from a number, Hdt.2.32; allot, assign by lot, Plu.Caes.51, cf. Hld.4.2:—Pass., to be allotted, fall to one's share, Luc.Merc. Cond.32, Ph.2.577; have allotted to one, Ph.1.214

ἀποκλήρωσις.definition: selection by lot, D.C.39.7; choice by lot or chance, unreasoning choice, Plu.2.1045f: hence, absurdity, absence of reason, in the phrase . .; what is there unreasonable in . ., A.D.Synt.267.17, cf. Alex.Aphr.de An.22.…

ἀποκλίνω.definition: fut. Pass., aor. poet. Theoc.3.37:-turn off or aside, Od.19.556; Sor.1.100; turn back, h.Ven.168: metaph., Simp.in Ph.1164.39:-Pass. , slope away, of countries, D.S.13.89; of the day, decline towards evening, Hdt.3.10…

ἀπόκλισις.definition: slope, Cleom.1.1, Ph.1.459; turning off, decline, of fortune, Plu.2.611a; of disease, Gal.7.424, Herod.Med. in Rh.Mus.58.98

ἀποκναίω.definition: Att. inf. dub. l; wear one out, worry to death, Ar.Ec.1087, Pl.ll.cc., f.l. in Thphr.Char.7.4; Men.341; D.21.153, cf. D.H.Dem.20:—Pass., to be worn out, Pl.R.406b; X.HG6.2.1

ἀποκνίζω.definition: fut. nip or snip off, Hp.Steril.214, Ar.Ach.869, Sotad.Com.1.23, Thphr.HP6.8.2; Arist.HA554b5; D.S.2.4; Plu.2.977b; wring off, LXXLe.1.15; perh. f.l. for Tab.Defix.Aud.242.59

ἀποκογχίζω.definition: draw out with a I.2, Dsc.1.30

ἀποκοιμάομαι.definition: Pass. with fut. Med. sleep away; get a little sleep, esp. of troops on duty, Hdt.8.76, Ar.V.213, X.Cyr.2.4.22 and 26, Plb.3.79.10; simply, fall asleep, Polyaen.8.23.1

ἀποκοιμίζω.definition: put to sleep, Alciphr.1.39:—Pass., go to sleep: metaph., Socr.Ep.1.6

ἀποκοιτέω.definition: sleep away from one's post, Decr. ap. D.18.37, cf. PPetr.3p.204

ἀποκολούω.definition: cut short off, dub. in Hp.Nat.Mul.8, cf. Call.Jov.90 , AB435, Hsch. s.v

ἀποκολυμβάω.definition: dive and swim away, Th.4.25, D.C.49.1

ἀποκομίζω.definition: carry away, escort, X.Cyr.7.3.12; carry; carry back, A.R.4.1106:—Pass., return, Hdt.5.27

ἀποκορυφόω.definition: bring to a point, Plb.3.49.6:—Pass., rise; metaph., gave them this summary answer, Hdt.5.73; cause to culminate, Simp.in Ph.1359.8, cf. in Cael.126.3

ἀποκοτταβισμός.definition: dashing out the last drops; vomit, Herod.Med. ap. Orib.5.27.9

ἀποκουφίζω.definition: lighten, set free from, E.Or.1341, Hec.104 , cf. AP9.372; relieve, Plu.Cleom.18; lighten a cargo, Str.5.3.5

ἀποκραιπαλάω.definition: sleep off a debauch, Plu.Ant.30; waste in debauch, Theognet.2

ἀποκρέμαμαι.definition: Pass., hang down from, hang on by, Arist.HA553b3; appendages, ib.620b14; impf. Q.S.11.197; aor. Luc.DDeor.21.1; hook-nosed, Philostr.Her.3.3

ἀποκρημνίζω.definition: throw from a cliff's edge, Hld.2.8

ἀπόκρημνος.definition: sheer, precipitous, Hdt.7.176, cf.3.111; Id.8.53, cf. Th.4.31, etc.: Sup., Diog.Ep.37.4: metaph. of an advocate's case, full of difficulties, D.25.76

ἀπόκρισις.definition: separation, Anaxag.4; Medic., excretion or secretion, Hp.Genit.2, Vict.4.93, cf. Arist.HA582a4, Pr.878a23, etc.; PA681b35; Epicur.Nat.Herc.908.3

ἀπόκριτος.definition: separated, chosen, Inscr.in Sauciuc Andros130, Opp.H.3.266

ἀπόκρουσις.definition: retiring, waning, Colum.2.10.10, Alex. Trall.8.2, PMag.Leid.V.11.28, Horap.1.4, etc

ἀποκτάομαι.definition: lose possession of, alienate, Hsch; metaph., clear out of the way, refute, Gal.1.132

ἀποκτείνυμι.definition: or , = sq., Crates Com.17, Lys.12.7, Pl. l. c., X.An.6.3.5, D.20.158, etc.: —also X.HG4.4.2, 5.2.43, etc

ἀποκτέννω.definition: later form for Plb.1.69.11, AP11.395 , LXXTo.6.13

ἀποκτυπέω.definition: sound loudly from, Philostr.VS1.25.7; make a noise by striking, Suid. s.v. cf. AB208

ἀποκυβεύω.definition: run hazard or risk, D.S.17.30, Polyaen.8.14.1

ἀποκυβιστάω.definition: plunge headlong off a place, Clearch.73

ἀποκυέω.definition: bear young, bring forth, c. acc., Arist.Fr.76, interpol. in D.H.1.70, Plu.Sull.37: abs., Luc.DMar.10.1: metaph., Ep.Jac.1.15, cf. Ph.1.214:—Pass., of the child, Plu.Lyc.3. Hdn.1.5.5

ἀποκύησις.definition: bringing forth, birth, Plu.2.907c, Dsc.2.120, Ph.2.396, Sor.1.46, etc

ἀποκυΐσκω.definition: = Ael.NA9.3, D.L.8.29: metaph. in Pass., Herm.in Phdr.p.134A

ἀποκυλίω.definition: roll away, LXXGe.29.3,al., D.S.14.116, Ev.Matt.28.2, Apollod.3.15.7:—Pass., Luc.Rh.Pr.3

ἀποκυματίζω.definition: make to swell with waves, boil up, Plu.2.734e: metaph., ib.943d; D.H.Comp.23

ἀποκυρτόομαι.definition: rise to a convex shape, v.l. for Hp.Prog.7

ἀπολαγνεύω.definition: spend in debauchery, in pf. Pass., Hsch

ἀπολαγχάνω.definition: obtain a portion of a thing by lot; fail in drawing lots, Lys.4.3, cf. Plu.Cat.Mi.6, 2.102e: generally, lose one's all, be left destitute, E.Ion609

ἀπολαΐζομαι.definition: become stone, prob.l. in Hsch. s.v

ἀπολακτισμός.definition: a kicking off or away, of a violent death, A.Supp.937: Medic., of a form of haemorrhage, diapedesis, Steph.in Hp.1.124D

ἀπολαλέω.definition: blurt out, J.AJ6.9.2, cf. Luc.Nigr.22, Poll.2.127

ἀπολαμβάνω.definition: fut. in Hdt. 3.146; receive what is one's due, Hdt.8.137; X.An.7.7.14; E.Or.654; Ar.Nu.1274; Antiph.196; have them paid, And.3.15; X.Smp.3.3; Aeschin.1.196: opp. Epist. Phil. ap. D.12.14, cf. D.7.5; accept them when t…

ἀπολαμπρύνω.definition: make bright or famous, Lib.Or.64.87:—Pass., become so, by one's deeds, Hdt.1.41; Id.6.70

ἀπόλαυσις.definition: act of enjoying, fruition, Th.2.38; result of enjoying, pleasure, Arist.Pol.1314b28, cf. EN1148a5, etc.; a life of pleasure, Id.Top.102b17

ἀπολαύω.definition: c. acc. , Diph.32.6 ; Arist.Sens.443b3; abs., opp. Id.Pol.1263a13; to have less enjoyment, Id.HA584a21; Plu.2.69e

ἀπολέγω.definition: pick out from a number, and so: 1. pick out, choose, Hdt.5.110, cf. 3.14, Ar.V.580, Aen.Tact.1.5, 3.2:-freq. in Med., pick out for oneself, from the army, Hdt.8.101; Th.4.9:-Pass., picked men, Hdt.7.40; X.Eq.Mag.8.12.…

ἀπολειόω.definition: erase, CIG3966 ; Arc. dub. in IG5 p.xxxvi D 1.20

ἀπολείχω.definition: lick off, v.l. for A.R.4.478, cf. Epic. in Arch.Pap.7.6, Ath.6.250a, Sch.Il.Oxy.221ii33; lick clean, c. gen. partit., Ev.Luc.16.21

ἀπολεπτύνω.definition: fine down, esp. of reducing temperature or fever, Plu.2.695e, Alex.Trall.Febr.5:—more freq. in Pass., become quite fine or thin, being fined away, Pl.Ti.83b; Arist.HA489b33; of fever, v.l. in Hp.Epid.1.25

ἀπολευκαίνω.definition: make all white, Hp.Prorrh.2.20; Plu.Eum.16:—Pass., to be or become so, Arist.Fr.350, Archig. ap. Orib.44.26.1

ἀποληκέω.definition: snap the fingers, Hellanic.63 J., Hsch. , Suid. s.v

ἀπολιγωρέω.definition: esteem little, Sch.Th.1.140, cf. Steph.in Gal.1.285 D

ἀπολιθόω.definition: turn into stone, petrify, Arist.Pr.937a17, cf. Hellanic.191 J., Pherecyd.77 J.:—Pass., Thphr.HP4.7.2; become stone, Arist.Pr.937a14, Mir.838a14, Str.5.4.13, Palaeph.31; become hard, PHolm.4.38

ἀπολίθωσις.definition: petrifaction, Pherecyd.12 J., Thphr.Lap.50, Sch.Il.2.319: metaph., Arr.Epict.1.5.3

ἀπολιμνόομαι.definition: Pass., become a lake or pool, Eust.267.47

ἀπολιμπάνω.definition: Aeol. collat. form of Sapph.Supp.23.5, cf. Luc.Cat.7, Gal.UP4.11, POxy.1426.12 : -Pass., Plu.Them.10

ἀπολισθάνω.definition: later Poll.1.116, v.l. in; c. gen., slip away from, Ar.Lys.678; prob. in Alciphr.3.11; also, cease to be intimate with one, Plu.l.c.; Luc.Dem. Enc.12; Iamb.Myst.9.8

ἀπολιταργίζω.definition: Att. fut. hop off, pack off, . . Ar.Nu.1253

ἀπολίτευτος.definition: without political constitution; not fitted for public affairs, unstatesmanlike, Plu.Mar.31; Id.Crass.12, 2.1034b

Ἀπολλώνιος.definition: of or belonging to Apollo; name of month at Elis, Methymna, etc., Sch.Pi.O.3.35, IG12.505, etc

Ἀπολλωνίσκος.definition: Dim. of Ath.14.636f; statuette of Apollo, Roussel Cultes Égyptiens221

Ἀπολλωνιών.definition: name of month at Halicarnassus, BCH14.106

ἀπολογέομαι.definition: aor. E.Ba.41, Antipho5.13; c. acc. rei, defend oneself against, Th.8.109; defend what one has done, Aeschin.1.92

ἀπολόγημα.definition: plea alleged in defence, Pl.Cra.436c; Plu.Cim.1

ἀπολογία.definition: speech in defence, opp. Antipho6.7, Th.3.61, Pl.Ap.28a, etc.; to make a defence, Is.6.62; Lys.14.29; Hyp.Eux.31; Ep.Phil.1.16; expl. by Hsch

ἀπολογίζομαι.definition: fut. Phld.Lib.p.50 O; refer to a head or class, Pl.Phlb.25b

ἀπολογισμός.definition: giving account, statement of reasons; account kept, record, Luc.Dem.Enc.33; Klio18.276 , cf. Plu.Per.23, POxy.297.5 : in pl., Plu.2.822e

ἀπολοπίζω.definition: = skin, peel, prob.l. for Ar.Fr.135, Antiph.128, cf. Phryn.PSp.44 B

ἀπολούτριος.definition: washed off: water which has been used for washing, Ael.NA17.11:—also Sch.Ar.Eq.1401

ἀπολοφύρομαι.definition: bewail loudly, And.3.16, cf. X.HG1.1.27; Antipho Soph.54: abs., indulge one's sorrows to the full, Th.2.46, Pl.Mx.249c

ἀπολυπραγμόνητος.definition: not meddled with, prob. in SIG399.24 . Adv. Hsch. s.v

ἀπολυσίδιον.definition: order for delivery, PFlor.131.7 , al.; PFay.133.14

ἀπολύσιμος.definition: deserving acquittal; released from public service, PLond.2.445.7 ; CPR1.3

ἀπόλυσις.definition: loosing, e.g. of a bandage or cord; release, deliverance, Pl.Cra.405b, Plb.33.1.5: c. gen., as far as acquittal from a capital charge went, Hdt.6.136; Plu.Arat.54; end of mourning, OGI56.53

ἀπόλυτος.definition: loosed, free, Plu.2.426b; absolute, unconditional, Arr.Epict.2.5.24, S.E.M.8.273, Plot.6.1.18 and 22. Adv. S.E.M.8.161, Men.Rh.p.434 S., Lyd.Mens.4.7; opp. Procl.in Prm.p.733 S

ἀπολυτρόω.definition: release on payment of ransom, Men.Mis.21: c. gen. pretii, Pl.Lg.919a, cf. Philipp. ap.D.12.3; restore for a ransom, Plb.2.6.6, cf. J.BJ2.14.1:—Med., Polyaen.5.40

ἀπολύτρωσις.definition: ransoming, Plu.Pomp.24; redemption by payment of ransom, deliverance, Ev. Luc.21.28, Ep.Rom.3.24, al.; of Nebuchadnezzar's recovery, LXXDa.4.30c; in NT, redemption, Ep.Rom.3.24,al

ἀπομαγδαλία.definition: or the crumb or inside of the loaf, on which the Greeks wiped their hands at dinner, and then threw it to the dogs: hence, dog's meat, Ar.Eq.415, Alciphr.3.44, Plu.Lyc.12

ἀπομαδίζω.definition: make quite bald, Crito ap.Gal.12.454, Sch.Ar.Eq.373

ἀπομάκτης.definition: one who wipes, rubs, or cleans, Com.Adesp.589, AB431; esp. in magical rites, Poll.7.188

ἀπομαλακίζομαι.definition: to be weak or cowardly, show weakness, in a thing, Arist.HA613a1, cf. Plu.Lyc.10

ἀπομανθάνω.definition: unlearn, Pl.Phd.96c, cf. Prt.342d, X.Cyr.4.3.14, Antisth. ap. D.L.6.7: c. inf., Plu.Lyc.11

ἀπομαντεύομαι.definition: divine by instinct, presage, Pl.R.516d; ib.505e; Id.Sph.250c, cf. Plot.5.5.12, Jul.Or.4.149c

ἀπομαραίνω.definition: cause to waste away, Sor.1.30, cf. Chor.p.22 B.; Callistr.Stat.2; Philostr.VA7.4; obliterate from memory, Chor.Milt.19:—Pass., waste, wither away, die away, Pl.Tht.177b; Id.R.328d; of a tranquil death, X.Ap.7, cf. Plu…

ἀπομαρτυρέω.definition: testify, bear witness, Milet. 3 No.313 : c. acc. et inf., Plb.30.31.20; Plu.2.860c:— Pass., IG2.377.9

ἀπομάσσω.definition: wipe clean, esp. in magical ceremonies, D.18.259, cf. Luc.Nec.7, Hsch. s. vv. —Med., wipe for oneself, you wipe your hands on the finest bread, Ar.Eq.819; Ath.9.410b: abs., wipe one's mouth, Eratosth.30; of a serpent,…

ἀποματαΐζω.definition: behave idly or unseemly, euphem. for Hdt.2.162, Favor. ap. Stob.4.50.25; cf. Hsch

ἀπομάχομαι.definition: fut. fight from the walls; fight off a thing, decline it, Hdt.7.136: abs., Id.1.9; D.H.2.60

ἀπομειουρίζω.definition: or make to taper off to a point, Nicom.Ar.2.13; of a root, Herod.Med. ap. Orib.8.4.3

ἀπομείρομαι.definition: distribute, Hes.Op.578; Pass., to be parted from, Id.Th.801, Arat.522:—in each place with v.l

ἀπομελαίνομαι.definition: turn black, of grapes, Thphr.HP2.7.5; to be blackened by mortification, Hp.Art.69

ἀπομέμφομαι.definition: rebuke, E.Rh.900 ; J.BJ1.24.2, Plu.2.229b ; Oenom. ap. Eus.PE5.20

ἀπομένω.definition: dub. sens. in PFlor.378.6 ; remain behind, Alciphr.3.60, dub. l. in Polyaen.4.6.13

ἀπομερίζω.definition: divide off, separate, Pl.Plt.304a; detail for special service, Plb.8.30.1; or Id.3.101.9, 16.21.8:—Pass., Id.10.16.2; to be selected by merit, Pl.Lg.855d:—also in Act., take as one's special province, Bito56.3

ἀπομερμηρίζω.definition: aor. AB431:—sleep off care, forget one's cares in sleep, Ar.V.5, D.C.55.14

ἀπομεστόομαι.definition: Pass., become filled to the brim, Pl.Phdr.255c, Plot.2.3.18

ἀπόμετρον.definition: in pl., emoluments of a priest, IG22.1357,1363 , Leg.Sacr.2.10B10

ἀπομηκύνω.definition: prolong, draw out, Pl.Sph.217e, cf. Prt.336d, Luc.Herm.67, etc.: abs., to be prolix, Them.Or.2.39d, etc.:—Pass., to be prolonged, extended, Sor.1.57, Luc.DMar.1.2

ἀπομηρύομαι.definition: draw up from, out of, Opp.C.1.50

ἀπομιμέομαι.definition: express by imitation, copy or represent faithfully, X.Mem.3.10.3; Pl.Lg.865b; Aeschin.3.150; endeavour to express motion by the sound of i, Pl.Cra.427a sq.: pf. in pass. sense, Moschio ap.Ath.5.207f

ἀπομίμημα.definition: imitation, copy, Hp.Vict.1.22, Bato Sinop.4, D.S.16.26

ἀπομίμησις.definition: imitation, Hp.Vict.1.10, Arist.Rh.Al.1420b16, Phld.Lib.p.450., J.AJ3.7.7, Plu.Num.14

ἀπομιμνῄσκομαι.definition: fut. aor. recognize: hence, repay, Il.24.428; for benefits, Hes.Th.503; . . Th.1.137, cf. E.Alc.299

ἀπομισθόω.definition: let out for hire, Th.3.68; Lys.7.9; . . Pl.R.475d; farm out by contract, IG1.26a10, al.; Milet.7.69 , etc.: c. inf., contract for . ., Lex ap.D.43.58

ἀπομιτρόω.definition: take away the mitre, LXXLe.21.10, Ph.1.562

ἀπομνημόνευμα.definition: memorial, record, D.S.1.14, Plu.Pomp.2; memorandum, PSI1.85 : in pl., memoirs, as those of Socrates by X., D.H.Rh.9.12, Plu.Cat.Ma.9

ἀπομνημονεύω.definition: relate from memory, Pl.Phdr.228a; remember, call to mind, Pl.Plt.268e, Phd.103b, Ly.211a, D.19.13, Aeschin.3.16, etc.; keep in mind, Pl.Plt.273b,al

ἀπομνησικακέω.definition: bear a grudge against, Hdt.3.49; Eus.Mynd.45

ἀπόμοιρα.definition: portion, OGI55.15; particle of divinity, M.Ant.2.1

ἀπομοχλεύω.definition: move as with a lever, Hp.Art.70, cf. Ph.Bel.70.47

ἀπομύζουρις.definition: obscene name of a courtesan, Com.Adesp.1352

ἀπομυκτηρίζω.definition: turn up the nose at, Hsch. s.v. :—also Luc.DMeretr.7.3

ἀπομυλλαίνω.definition: make mouths at, EM125.25; of a broken jaw, in which the fractured parts override each other, Hp.Art.33

ἀποναρκόομαι.definition: become torpid, stupefied, Hp.Coac.478, cf. Acut.55; Pl.R.503d, Hp.Ep.21

ἀπονεκρόω.definition: destroy, Dsc.Eup.1.204; esp. of cold, benumb, Tz.H.1.332:—Pass., to be quite killed, be benumbed, D.S.2.12, cf. Luc.VH2.1: metaph., Arr.Epict.4.5.21; ib.1.5.4

ἀπονέμησις.definition: distribution, M.Ant.8.6; branch, Gal.4.565, Orib.22.2.6, cf. 8.62

ἀπονευρόομαι.definition: Pass., become tendinous, Gal.2.252, etc; become a nerve, Id.5.191

ἀπονήχομαι.definition: escape by swimming, swim away, Plb.16.3.14, Luc.Pisc.50: metaph., escape from . ., Plu.2.476a; J.BJ2.20.1

ἀπονίσσομαι.definition: go away, Thgn.528, A.R.3.899: aor. AP9.118

ἀπονοέομαι.definition: have lost all sense; of shame or duty, abandoned fellow, Thphr.Char.6.1, cf. Isoc.8.93, D.19.69:—later in Act., make desperate, J.AJ18.1.6

ἀπονυκτερεύω.definition: pass a night away from, Plu.Fab.20: abs., Id.2.195e

ἀποξαίνω.definition: scarify, tear, in Pass., LXX4 Ma.6.6, Asclep.Jun. ap. Gal.13.1022

ἀποξένωσις.definition: living abroad, Plu.Pomp.80; exile, Paul.Al.E.2 , al

ἀποξηραίνω.definition: generally, dry completely, lay them up, Th.7.12:—Pass., Alex.124.11, cf. Thphr.HP8.11.3

ἀποξυράω.definition: or shave clean, c. dupl. acc., Hdt.5.35; Ar.Th.215; ib.1043; Luc.Sacr.15:—Pass., Polyaen.7.35.1

ἀποξυστρόομαι.definition: Pass., become bent or blunted, Plb.2.33.3

ἀποπάλλω.definition: hurl or cast, Luc.Am.45; radiate, J.BJ5.5.6:—Pass., rebound, Epicur.Fr.293; Arist.Pr.891a3, cf. Plu.Alex.35, S.E.M.10.73, etc

ἀπόπαλσις.definition: = foreg., ib.2p.50U.; gloss on Gal.19.84; shock, Archig. ap. Orib.8.2.10

ἀποπαππόομαι.definition: Pass., become pappose, of dandelions, Thphr.HP7.11.4

ἀποπαρθενεύομαι.definition: lay aside virginity, Hp.Aër.17:—also deflower, LXXSi.20.4

ἀποπέκω.definition: shear off wool:—Pass., Hsch.:—Med., comb her hair, Call.Lav.Pall.32, cf. AP6.155

ἀποπελεκάω.definition: hew or trim with an axe, Ar.Av.1156, Thphr.HP5.5.6:—also AB438

ἀποπερατόω.definition: = foreg., Porph.in Cat.132.33, Sch.Ar.Th.1033:—freq. in Pass., Hierocl.in CA26p.478M., Paul.Aeg.6.77, Steph.in Hp.1.188D., al.; Phlp.in Mete.31.1

ἀποπεράτωσις.definition: termination of a fistula, Antyll. ap. Orib.44.22.9, Paul.Aeg.6.77: generally, completion, end, Syrian.in Metaph.49.29; final term, Procl.Inst.147 , Dam.Pr.114, al

ἀποπέρδομαι.definition: fut. Ar.Ra.10: aor. Act. Id.Eq.639, Pl.699, etc.:—break wind, Ar. ll. cc., etc.: metaph., i.e. desinit in equum, of a Centaur, APl.4.115

ἀποπερισπάω.definition: draw off, divert, Sor.1.117, cf. Sch.Ar.Nu.721

ἀποπέρνημι.definition: sell, Aeol. aor. subjunct. Schwyzer 646.13 : Ion. aor. inf. GDI 5533f2 ; 3pl. SIG45.32

ἀποπερονάω.definition: fix with a buckle or pin, Hp.Mochl.5:—Pass., Ph.Bel.66.43

ἀποπηδάω.definition: leap off, esp. of riders, dismount; start off from, turn away from, Hp.Art.47; from its natural position, of a joint, ib.61; metaph., Pl.Tht.164c; X.Mem.1.2.16: abs., leap off, Pl.R.613b; stalk off, Id.Lg.720c; Procop…

ἀποπιέζω.definition: squeeze tight, Hp.Aph.5.46, al.; press outwards or away from a spot, Id.Fract.30:—Pass., Thphr.Fr.11:—also LXXJd.6.38, Archig. ap. Orib.8.1.21

ἀποπινόω.definition: dirty, soil, prob. l. for Hsch

ἀποπλάσσομαι.definition: Med., fut. aor. or mould from a thing: hence, represent, model, portray, Plu.Aem.28, AP5.14 , 7.34 , etc.; Call.Fr.194

ἀποπληκτικός.definition: paralysed, Hp.Coac.467, cf. Arist.Rh.1411a21; apoplectic seizures, Hp.Coac.470; Arist.Pr.954b30

ἀπόπληκτος.definition: disabled by a stroke; in mind, struck dumb, astounded, Hdt.2.173, cf. S.Ph.731; Id.Fr.248; senseless, D.21.143, cf. Men.Epit.344, Phld.Ir.p.82 W., D.Chr.11.100; D.34.16; Men.Pk.246; D.Chr.11.54

ἀποπληξία.definition: of body, apoplexy, Hp.Aph.2.42, Aret.SD1.7; paralysis, Arist.Pr.905a17: in pl., ib.860a33, al

ἀποπληρόω.definition: = fill up, Hp.Art.45 (in; satisfy, Pl.R.426c, Lg.782e; satisfy an inquirer, . . Id.Chrm.169c, cf. Plt.286a; make this complete for me, satisfy me in this, Id.Prt.329c:—Pass., Arist.Rh.1369b14

ἀποπλήρωσις.definition: filling, satisfying, Plu.2.48c; accomplishment, fulfilment, Dam.Pr.64, cf. Iamb.Myst.5.26, al

ἀποπληρωτής.definition: one who completes or fulfils, Pl.R.620e, cf. Jul.Or.2.90c, Iamb.Myst.5.10,al

ἀποπνευματίζω.definition: breathe out, expire, in Pass., Hsch. s.v. also, = Sch.Ar.Pax891

ἀποπνίγω.definition: fut. Pl.Com.198, Antiph.171: aor; generally, cut off, kill, Aret.CA1.9:—Pass., Procop.Arc.26

ἀπόπνοια.definition: = foreg. I, Hp.de Arte12; = foreg. II, Thphr.CP5.12.2

ἀποποιέω.definition: unmake, Corp.Herm.9.6. 2. deduct, BGU475r5 . II. Med., put away from oneself, reject, LXXJb.14.15, Plu.2.152a; refuse, Plot.4.3.14; deny, disclaim, Max.Tyr.24.4; do away with, kill, Cat.Cod.Astr.7.135.29

ἀποπολιτεύω.definition: dissolve political community, IG9.205.16 : —in Med., ib.9.32

ἀποπομπή.definition: sending away, LXXLe.16.10. b; divorce, PSI1.36a16 , etc., Poll.8.31

ἀποπορεία.definition: return, of machinery at; departure, D.C.Fr.104.4, Agath.2.31, 3.23; retreat, Procop.Pers.1.23, al

ἀποπορεύομαι.definition: Pass., depart, X.An.7.6.33, IG; go back, return, Plb.24.7.6; of machinery , HeroAut.6.3

ἀποπρεσβεία.definition: an ambassador's report, Plb.23.9.5,al., cf. AJA 18.324f

ἀποπρεσβεύω.definition: report as ambassador, Pl.Lg941a: abs., make such a report, Plb.7.2.5

ἀποπρίω.definition: saw off, Hdt.4.65. AP11.14 ; Hp.Fract.33:—Pass., Isid.Char.20, Plu.2.924b, prob. in Archil.122

ἀποπρολείπω.definition: leave far behind, Hes.Fr.144, cf. A.R.1.1285, Hermesian.7.21,44

ἀποπρονοσφίζω.definition: Alt. fut. remove afar off, carry far away, E.IA1286

ἀποπροσποιέομαι.definition: Med., reject, Ath.9.402a, Eust.769.14; dissemble, Men.Prot.p.44D., cf.p.125D

ἀποπροσωπίζομαι.definition: Med., clean one's face, Pherecr.9: also, = Hsch

ἀποπτερυγίζομαι.definition: clap the wings vehemently, Thphr.Sign.18; spread the wings and fly away, metaph. of Eust.397.5

ἀποπτερυγόομαι.definition: lose the of a rudder, Vett.Val.287.36

ἀποπτήσσω.definition: strengthd. for f.l. for Hsch. s.v. dub. in Opp.H.4.370

ἀπόπτυστος.definition: spat out: hence, abominated, detested, A.Eu.191: abs., S.OC1383, E.Med.1373, Ar.Eq.1285, etc

ἀποπυκνόομαι.definition: Pass., to be condensed, consolidated, f.l. in Epicur.Ep.2p.49U

ἀποπυνθάνομαι.definition: inquire or ask of, . . asked of him whether . ., Hdt.3.154; J.AJ12.4.9

ἀποπυρίας.definition: a kind of toasted bread, Cratin.99, Ath.3.111e

ἀποπυριάω.definition: foment, Antyll. ap. Orib.7.22.21, Gal.13.245, al

ἀποπυρίζω.definition: roast on the fire, Epich.124, cf. Hsch

ἀποπυτίζω.definition: stronger form of Hp.Epid.7.25, Ar.Lys.205, Arist.HA527b22

ἀποργίζομαι.definition: Pass., to be angry, Men.Sam.338, LXX2 Ma.5.17

ἀπορέω.definition: Lacon. 1pl. X.HG1.1.23: aor; to be at a loss, be in doubt, be puzzled, mostly folld. by relat. clause, Hdt.1.75; Th.3.109; S.OT486 ; Th.1.107, 8.80, X.HG5.4.44; Id.Cyr.4.5.38; . . D.3.3; . . Pl.Prt.326e; . . X.Mem.1.4…

ἀπορνεόω.definition: turn into a bird, Apollod.1.7.4, Sch.Ar.Av.251:— Pass., Herm. ap. Stob.1.49.69, Apollod.1.8.3

ἀπορνέωσις.definition: being changed into a bird, Sch.Ar.Av.212

ἀπορνιθόομαι.definition: become a bird, Str.6.3.9, Heraclit.Incred.35, Sch.Ar.Av.100

ἀπόρνυμαι.definition: start from a place, Il.5.105, cf. Hes.Th.9, A.R.1.800

ἀπορραθυμέω.definition: leave off in faintheartedness or laziness, X.Mem.3.7.9: abs., Pl.R.449c, D.8.75. Adv. v.l. for Jul.Or.8.252a

ἀπορράπτω.definition: sew up again, Hdt.1.123: metaph., Aeschin.2.21, cf. Ph.1.476; Plu.2.997a:—Pass., Gal.18.671

ἀπορραψῳδέω.definition: speak in fragments of epic poetry, X.Cyr.3.3.54

ἀπορρέμβομαι.definition: wander from, c.gen., M.Ant.3.4: abs., hesitate, Id.4.22

ἀπόρρευμα.definition: that which distils, as from a tree, Theognost.Can.79

ἀπορρευματίζω.definition: v.l. for Ps.-Diocl.Epist. ad Antig. ap.Paul.Aeg.1 fin

ἀπορρέω.definition: Ep. Nic.Th.404, fut; fall off, of fruit, Hdt.1.193; feathers, Pl.Phdr.246d; leaves, D.22.70; hair, Arist.HA518a14; flesh, E.Med.1201: generally, run to waste, Plot.2.1.3; of riders, Plu.Eum.7, cf.Pyrrh.30,al

ἀπόρρητος.definition: forbidden, though it; not to be spoken, secret, make a secret of, Hdt.9.94; esp. of state secrets, Ar.Eq.648; X.An.7.6.43; Lys.12.69; Plu.Luc.17, cf. OGI 371; = a secretis, Procop.Pers.2.7; keep them secret so that yo…

ἀπορρίψιμος.definition: that should be thrown away, Artem.5.85

ἀπόρροια.definition: = foreg. 1.4, Arist.Sens.438a4, al., Epicur.Ep.1p.9U., Porph.Abst.2.46, etc.; Orph.L.173; Medic., effluvia, Gal.15.625 , etc

ἀπορροιβδέω.definition: shriek forth, of birds of prey, S.Ant.1021; Nonn.D.2.257

ἀπορφανίζω.definition: bereave, BCH46.345:—Pass., to be orphaned, A.Ch.249; to be torn away from . ., 1 Ep.Th.2.17

ἀποσάττω.definition: unsaddle, unpack, opp. LXXGe.24.32; stop up, caulk, Din.Fr.89.10; stuff with food, Diph.43.41:—Med., stuff oneself, Philem.68

ἀποσαφέω.definition: make clear, indicate, . . Pl.Prt.348b, cf. Cra.384a, Gal.8.678, Luc.Hist.Conscr.52; Jul.Gal.138a

ἀποσβέννυμι.definition: Pass., pres. in Heraclit.30, Hp.Aër.4, X.Lac.13.3, etc.:— Med., fut. Pl.Lg.805c: aor. 2 and pf. Act. intr., E.Med.1218, X.Cyr.l.c., Call.Fr.1.10 P., Theoc.4.39, etc.; X.Cyr.8.8.13, Pl.Plt.269b, etc.: aor. 1 Pass. Ar.L…

ἀποσεμνύνω.definition: extol, glorify, Pl.Tht.168d, D.S.2.47, etc. II. Pass., with fut. Med., give oneself solemn airs, Ar.Ra.703; ib.833, cf. Procop.Arc.17; of Tragedy, assumed a dignified form, Arist.Po.1449a20; Aristid.26.63. 2. c. dat.,…

ἀποσηκόω.definition: shut up in a pen, Hsch

ἀποσημαίνω.definition: announce by signs or signals, give notice; c. acc., indicate by signs or symptoms, Hp.Epid.1.9; = S.Fr.676; denote, represent, J.AJ3.7.7, Plu.Sull.7, etc.; indicate, J.AJ1.3.8, al.; declare, ib.1.8.1,al.:—Med., show b…

ἀποσημάντωρ.definition: a sealer, recorder, Eust.1590; enunciation, Phld.Po.2.16

ἀποσημειόομαι.definition: note down, make notes, Phlp.in Cat.3.29

ἀποσιτίζομαι.definition: get to eat, f.l. for Aristaenet.1.3

ἀποσιωπάω.definition: maintain silence, Isoc.12.215; trans., keep secret, Luc.Pseudol.21; leave unsaid, Id.Pisc.29; leave unnoticed, POxy. 237 vii 24

ἀποσιώπησις.definition: becoming silent, Plu.Alex.52; a rhetorical figure, when for emphasis, modesty, etc., the sentence is abruptly broken off, Quint. Inst.9.2.54, Demetr.Eloc.103, 264, Plu.2.1009e, Hermog.Id.2.7

ἀποσκάπτω.definition: fut. Pass. Polyaen.5.10.3:—cut; strengthd. for Pl.Lg.760e

ἀποσκέπτομαι.definition: not found in pres. fut. aor. Plu.3.582d, Hp.Mul.1.11

ἀποσκέπω.definition: give shelter from; strip, Hsch. s.v

ἀποσκευάζω.definition: pull off, Lycurg.128; clear away tables, Suid.; strip of furniture, LXXLe.14.36. 2. = Hsch. II. mostly in Med., pack up and carry off, SIG633.68 , cf.588.50 , Plb.2.26.6, D.H.9.23: abs., pack up and depart, Act.Ap.21.…

ἀπόσκηνος.definition: encamping apart, living and messing alone, opp. Id.Cyr.8.7.14

ἀποσκήπτω.definition: hurl from above; intr., fall suddenly, her wrath fell upon thee, E.Hipp.438; Aeschin.1.182; Arist.Mir.846a2; Plu.Pomp.19; Philostr.VA1.6; come to a sorry ending, Hdt.1.120; Cic.Att.12.5.1; D.H.7.15, Alciphr.1.37

ἀποσκίδνημι.definition: scatter, Ph.2.100:—elsewh. in Pass., Il.23.4; of soldiers, to disperse for a purpose, Hdt.4.113: abs., Th.6.98; cf

ἀποσκιρτάω.definition: skip away, Hellanic.111 J.; in Str.17.1.31 to have a bout of skipping or capering: metaph., to be restive or rebellious, Luc.Merc.Cond.23, Them.Or.7.87b

ἀποσκληρύνω.definition: harden, Hp.Coac.515:—Pass., Arist.Mir.836b5, Thphr.CP3.16.2; gloss on Erot

ἀποσκολοπίζω.definition: remove stumbling-blocks, Aq.Is.57.14, al; skin, strip off, Archil.124 , S.Fr.423; also = Hsch., Ael.Dion.Fr.432

ἀποσκοπεύω.definition: = sq., LXXLa.4.17, Ph.1.677 codd., etc.; cf

ἀποσκοπέω.definition: look away from other; c.acc., look to, regard, E.Hec.939 , D.H.6.72, Procop.Goth.4.15:—Med., Plu.Pomp.79; Procl.in Prm.p.549 S

ἀπόσκοπος.definition: erring from the mark; beholding from afar, Hsch

ἀποσκορακίζω.definition: wish one far enough, curse, damn, LXXIs.17.13, Plu.2.740a, Alciphr.1.38, Iamb.VP25.112

ἀποσκοτόομαι.definition: to be darkened, blinded; to be shaded off, in painting, Ar.Fr.712

ἀποσκυβαλίζω.definition: treat as vile refuse, Sch.Pi.P.3.22; pollute a tomb, prob. in CIG3927 :—Pass., to be cast forth as excrement, Epict.Gnom.19:—hence Subst. Sch.Ar.Pl.1184

ἀποσκυθίζω.definition: metaph. in Pass., to be shaved bare, E.Tr.1026; Ath.12.524f

ἀποσκώπτω.definition: banter, rally, . . Pl.Tht.174a; or jeer at one, D.C.48.38, Luc.Herm.51, etc.; D.C.60.33; D.L.5.11

ἀπόσμηξις.definition: wiping, cleaning, Archig. ap. Aët.9.35, Hsch. s.v

ἀποσμήχω.definition: = Pherecyd.33 J., Sor.1.81, Paus.5.5.11, Luc.Tim.54, Them.Or.32.359c:—Pass., c. dat., to be smeared with, Gp.16.18.2

ἀποσόβημα.definition: that which averts evil, Sch.Opp.H.1.46, Sch.E.Med.1322; = sq., Sch.rec.A.Th.69

ἀποσπαργανόω.definition: take off the swaddling-clothes, Sor.1.100:—Pass., Lyd.Mens.4.26

ἀποσπασμός.definition: tearing away, severing, Plu.2.77c; being torn away, separation, severance, Str.8.3.17; D.H.5.55, cf. Phld.Lib.p.4 O.; Id.Mort.9

ἀποσπερματόομαι.definition: to be converted into semen, Steph.in Hp.1.124 D

ἀποσπογγίζω.definition: wipe off as with a sponge, Antipho5.45, Antyll. ap. Orib.6.9.1:—Med., Sch.Od.8.88

ἀποσπόγγισμα.definition: dirt wiped off, with a sponge, Rh.3.530 W

ἀποσπογγισμός.definition: sponging off, Antyll. ap. Orib.9.23.2, Sor.1.67

ἀποστάζω.definition: let fall drop by drop, distil away; intr., trickle, Hp.Coac.328; fury distils from madness, or trickles away, i.e. passes off, S.Ant.959 ; Luc.Electr.6; of grain, Herod.6.6: metaph., not a brass farthing would come of…

ἀποστάτις.definition: pecul. fem. of LXX1 Es.2.18, J.AJ11.2.1

ἀποσταυρόω.definition: fence off with a palisade, Th.4.69, 6.101, X.HG7.4.32, Plb.4.56.8, Plu.Arat.40:—Pass., Pherecr.17

ἀποστεγάζω.definition: uncover, Emp.100.14 (prob. in; take off a covering, Ev.Marc.2.4

ἀποστεγνόω.definition: cover close, Moschio ap.Ath.5.207b:—Pass., to be blocked, of the intestines, Hp.Acut.51; to be luted or sealed up close, HeroSpir.1.23, 2.10

ἀποστέγω.definition: shelter or protect; keep out or off, Arist.Pr.924a26, cf. Emp.84.10, Pl.Lg.844b; Arist.Pr.939b17; Thphr.CP3.6.3, al.; ib.4.12.2, cf. 5.12.9, Plu.2.665f: metaph., A.Th.234 ; Plb.6.23.5

ἀποστέλλω.definition: fut. aor. :—send; dispatch, on some mission or service, S.Ph.125,1297, etc.; freq. of messengers or forces, Hdt.1.46,123; Id.7.235, cf. 8.64; Id.5.32; Th.1.45: also Hdt.4.150; , Arist.Pol.1306b31; Th.3.28; X.An.2.1.5,…

ἀποστενόω.definition: poet. straiten, Thphr.Ign.54 , Alex.Aphr.Pr.1.75; Theoc.22.101; D.S.3.37: metaph. in Pass., to be contracted, Simp.in Ph.18.4; hampered, Alex.Aphr.in Top.56.3; Dam.Pr.28bis

ἀποστερεόω.definition: harden, Ph.Bel.79.4, 81.4:—Pass., become solid, Arist.Mir.837b13, 844a14: metaph., persist stubbornly in, Phld.Rh.2.31S

ἀποστερέω.definition: detach, withdraw oneself from a person or thing, . . Id.OT1381; Antipho5.78; Th.1.40; Crobyl.3; . . . . deprive them of the power of walling off, Th.7.6:—reversely, Plu.Aem.26, cf.Dem.4

ἀποστέρησις.definition: withholding what is due, Antipho Soph.107, D.24.111; in order to avoid payment of my claims, Id.30.5

ἀποστερητής.definition: one who withholds, Arist.EE1232a15; esp. one who withholds what is due, a defrauder, cheat, Pl.R.344b, POxy.745.7 ; a farm that costs money instead of bringing it in, Com.Adesp.109

ἀποστεφανόω.definition: rob of the crown, discrown, Charito1.5, etc.:— Med., aor. inf. lay aside one's crown, D.L.2.54, Max.Tyr.5.9:—Pass., Luc.JTr.10, Jul.Caes.310c

ἀποστηματίας.definition: one who has an abscess, Aret.SD1.9

ἀποστημάτιον.definition: Dim. of Gal.17.326, Heliod. ap. Orib.44.14.10

ἀποστήριγμα.definition: stay, support, Hp.Off.25, cf; determination of humours, Hp.Flat.9

ἀποστηρίζομαι.definition: Med., fix firmly; support oneself firmly, throw one's weight upon, Arist.Pr.882b30: Id.IA705a8, cf. MA699a5

ἀποστήριξις.definition: fulcrum or rest for a lever, Hp.Mochl.42

ἀπόστιλψις.definition: emission of light, Sch.A.R.3.1377 , Hsch. s.v

ἀποστλεγγίζω.definition: scrape with a , Philostr.Gym.18,51: —Med., scrape oneself clean, X.Oec.11.18; pf. part. Pass. scraped clean, fresh from the bath, Ar.Eq.580; Arist.Pr.867b4; censured as archaic by Luc.Rh.Pr.17

ἀποστολεύς.definition: one who dispatches; at Athens, magistrate who had to fit out a squadron for service, D.18.107, 47.26, Aeschin.2.177, Philoch.142, IG2.809b20

ἀποστολιμαῖος.definition: sent off, missive; connected with dismissal, Eust.790.44

ἀπόστολος.definition: messenger, ambassador, envoy; commander of a naval force, Hsch

ἀποστοματίζω.definition: teach by word of mouth, teach; interrogate, catechize, as a master his pupil, Ev.Luc.11.53, cf. Pl. ap. Poll.1.102

ἀποστομίζω.definition: deprive of an edge; = foreg. II, Hsch

ἀποστρακίζω.definition: bake to a hard crust, of a quick fire; banish by ostracism, Hsch., Suid

ἀποστρακόομαι.definition: become dry like a potsherd, Hp.VC16, Dsc.2.4, Hippiatr.25; to be ossified, Phlp.in GA113.1

ἀποστρατεύομαι.definition: to be discharged from military service, App.BC5.26

ἀποστρατοπεδεύομαι.definition: remove one's camp from, encamp away from, X.An.3.4.34; encamp at a greater distance, ib.7.7.1

ἀποστρεβλόομαι.definition: Pass., to be horribly tortured, LXX2 Ma.9.7

ἀποστροφία.definition: she that turns away, epith. of Aphrodite, Paus.9.16.3

ἀποστρυθάομαι.definition: perh. = disturb, move, dub. in IG5.1155.2

ἀποστυγέω.definition: aor. 1 S.OC692 Opp.H.4.370: aor. 2 Call.Aet.1.1.11, Del.223, Nic.Al.406, Parth.36.2: pf. with pres. sense, Hdt.2.47:—hate violently, abhor, Hdt.l.c., S.OC186,692, E.Ion488 ; Melanipp.4; Call.Aet.l.c.: c. inf., Hdt.6.129

ἀποσυλάω.definition: strip off spoils from a person: hence, strip off or take away from, Pi.P.4.110. II. rob, defraud one of a thing, . . S.OC1330; Is.5.30; E.Alc.870 , X.An.1.4.8:-Pass., A.Pr.172 ; Jul.Or.7.228b. III. carry off, Luc.Tox.2

ἀποσυμβαίνω.definition: to be absent, of an accidental quality, S.E.M.7.282; negative symptoms, e.g. absence of pain, Gal.18.86

ἀποσυμβιβάζω.definition: make good a deficiency, POxy.136.25 :— hence ib.2035

ἀποσυμβουλεύω.definition: metaph., divert, of a stream of blood meeting another, Hp.Loc.Hom.3

ἀποσυνάγω.definition: recover a man from, LXX4 Ki.5.3

ἀποσυνάγωγος.definition: expelled from the synagogue, Ev.Jo.9.22, etc

ἀποσυνεθίζω.definition: wean one from, Sor.1.116:— Pass., ibid

ἀποσυνεργέω.definition: thwart, oppose, ib.27, al., S.E.P.1.212; of planetary influence, Ptol.Tetr.3

ἀποσυνίστημι.definition: appoint a representative; recommend, introduce one person to another, c. acc. et dat., Phamb.27.1, AB436

ἀποσυριγγόω.definition: make a channel for, Hp.Oss.18:—Pass., Id.Loc. Hom.12

ἀποσύρω.definition: tear away, S.Fr.416, EM127.19; Philum.Ven.33.3; torn flesh, Gal.13.457, cf. Orib.44.18.2 ; Th.7.43; but Plb.10.15.1; lay bare, strip, Theoc.22.105, Plb.34.10.10; skim off, Sor.2.13

ἀποσφάζω.definition: in Att. Prose Lys.13.78, Pl.Euthphr.4c, etc.: plpf. D.C.78.7:—Pass., aor. Hdt.4.84: fut. Ar.Th.750:—cut the throat of a person, so that the blood runs into a pail, Hdt.4.62: generally, slay, Ar.Ach.327, Th.7.86, Pl.l.…

ἀποσφαιρίζομαι.definition: Pass., to be thrown off like a ball; later in Act., jerk away like a ball, Tz.ad Lyc.17

ἀποσφενδονάω.definition: hurl from or as from a sling, D.S.2.50, Luc.JTr.33:—Pass., LXX4 Ma.16.21, Plu.2.1062a

ἀποσφενδόνητος.definition: driven away by the sling, ib.293b

ἀποσφήνωσις.definition: impaction of an infant in childbirth, Paul.Aeg.3.76

ἀπόσφιγξις.definition: squeezing tight, Hp.Fract.11 , Art.69 :—in form ligature above a poisonous bite, Philum.Ven.22.4, cf. Leonid. ap. Orib.45.23.78, Antyll.ib.7.9.2

ἀποσφράγισμα.definition: impression of a seal; sealed copy, IG12.237.69

ἀποσφραίνω.definition: make to smell, he gives himself a whiff of pennyroyal, AP11.165 , cf. Sor.2.85, Orib.8.6.1:—Pass., when smelt at, Dsc.1.54

ἀπόσχασις.definition: opening of a vein, Hp.Epid.7.66; letting go, in an engine, Ph.Bel.74.51

ἀποσχεδιάζω.definition: = make off hand; act off hand or at random, Jul.Ep.89a, cf. Sch.Ar.Pax990, etc

ἀποσχηματίζω.definition: shape, fashion, in Pass., Socr.Ep.28, cf. Philostr.VS1Praef

ἀποσχίζω.definition: split, cleave off; sever, detach from, Hdt.6.9; part them off, separate them, Pl.Plt.262e; M.Ant.4.29:— Pass., . ., of a river being parted from the main stream, Hdt.2.17, 4.56; of a tribe detached from its parent sto…

ἀποσχοινίζω.definition: separate by a cord: hence generally, bar, exclude, D.25.28: abs., Plu.2.443c; Ph.1.205; ib.219, cf. Lib.Decl.23.45

ἀποσῴζω.definition: save or preserve from, S.Ph.1379; keep safe, Pl.Phlb.26c, Lg.692c, IG2.268; keep them in mind, remember, E.Fr.362.2

ἀποσωρεύω.definition: heap up, accumulate, AB432, Hsch. s.v

ἀπότακτος.definition: set apart for a special use; settled, appointed, Critias6.27 D.; fixed, PTeb.42.12 ; POxy.280.17 , etc.:—Subst. fixed rent, ib.1124.9 ; prescribed sum, PFay.39 , Porph.Abst.4.17; imperial assessment, POxy.1662.14

ἀποταμιεύομαι.definition: lock up, keep, Ael.VH1.12, cf. PSI4.428.28

ἀποταφρεύω.definition: fence off with a ditch, X.An.6.5.1, HG5.4.38; for defence or offence, D.H.2.37, 3.41

ἀποτείνω.definition: extend, prolong, of the line of an army, X.HG5.2.40 ; extend rewards much further, Pl.R.363d; esp. of speeches, Id.Grg.466a; to make long speeches, Id.Prt.335c, al.; Id.Grg.465e; Id.R.605d; of brazen vessels, Id.Prt.3…

ἀποτειχίζω.definition: by way of fortifying, Hdt.6.36:—Pass., Id.9.8; keep off by fortification, Plu.Per.19

ἀποτεκμαίρομαι.definition: draw signs or proofs from a thing, conclude, c.acc. et inf., A.R.4.1538

ἀποτεκνόομαι.definition: Pass., to be deprived of children, LXXGe.27.45

ἀποτέλειος.definition: title of a magistrate of the Achaean League, Plb.16.36.4: in pl., Id.10.23.9; subordinate commander, IG5.293

ἀποτέλεσμα.definition: full completion; event, result, Plb.2.39.11, D.S.1.89, Phld.Rh.1.129 S. , Antyll. ap. Orib.45.26.4, M.Ant.6.42, etc.; effect, opp. Stoic.2.118, al., Herm. ap.Stob.1.41.6, Procl.Inst.18

ἀποτελεσματογραφία.definition: nativity plan, Vett.Val.29.10, Paul.Al.L.1, Porph.in Ptol.201

ἀποτελευτάω.definition: intr., end, Hp.Aër.10, cf. Alex.Aphr.Pr.2.57; Pl.Prt.353e, 354b; at last, Id.Plt.310e; Arist.Metaph.983a18; Id.Pol.1305b11

ἀποτελεύτησις.definition: ending, Hp.Loc.Hom.3; result, Pl.Sph.264a; completion, accomplishment, Dam.Pr.67,113

ἀποτελέω.definition: fut. Att. bring to an end; produce, Pl.Ti.84c, cf. Epicur.Ep.1p.20U., M.Ant.10.26, etc.: —Pass., Arist.Cael.268b26

ἀποτελωνέομαι.definition: get discharge from the customs, PLond.ined.2092

ἀποτερατεύομαι.definition: Pass., to be astonished as by a prodigy, Ps.Callisth.3.17

ἀπότευγμα.definition: failure, Arist.VV1251b20, Phld.Rh.1.67S., Vit.p.35J., D.S.1.1, Cic.Att.13.27.1, etc

ἀποτεφρόω.definition: reduce to ashes, Dsc.5.81, Poll.1.167:—Pass., Lyd.Mag.3.70

ἀποτηγανίζω.definition: eat off the gridiron, eat broiled, Pherecr.123, Phryn.Com.57, Macho ap.Ath.13.582e; written in Sotad.Com.1.1

ἀποτήκω.definition: meltaway from, meltaway a part of . ., Pl.Ti.65d; reduce them, Dsc.5.99: metaph., Plu.2.451f:—Pass., Hdt.1.50, cf. Epicur.Ep.2. p.49U.; , Luc.DMort.28.2

ἀποτίκτω.definition: bring to the birth, Pl.Tht.150c, 182b, Arist.HA544a3, al.:—Pass., ib.10, Philostr.VA1.5, Iamb.Comm.Math.4; IG9.882.5

ἀποτιλάω.definition: pass, of excrement, Hippiatr.75; defile, Suid

ἀποτίλλω.definition: fut. Cratin.123: aor; pull the hair off, pluck bare, Ar.Lys.578, cf. Luc.Gall.28; Cratin. l.c.:—Pass., Ar.Av.806, cf. Ec.724

ἀποτίμημα.definition: mortgaged property, security, Lys.Fr.84S., Is.6.36, D.30.7, IG2.1059.4

ἀποτίμησις.definition: pledging of a property; = Lat. census, Plu.Crass.13, J.AJ18.2.1

ἀποτινάσσω.definition: shake off, E.Ba.253:—Med., Gal.6.821; has got rid of it, LXX1 Ki.10.2

ἀποτίνυμι.definition: cf. sq.], Dor. inf. Supp.Epigr.1.410.9 ; 3sg. imper. GDI5100.11 , SIG2680.8 :—later inf. part. Them.Or.23.289c, 3.40d, imper. J.AJ4.8.36, SIG1109.79 :—also LXXGe.31.39, al., Ph.2.596; PAvrom. 1 A 26:—for Med. v. sq. II.1

ἀποτολμάω.definition: make a bold venture upon, Th.7.67: c. inf., Lys.7.28; Aeschin.3.131, cf. Plb.2.45.2, Ph.1.233, etc.:—pf. part. Pass. in act. sense, too presumptuous liberty, Pl.Lg.701b, cf. Plu.Galb.25: in pass. sense, Pl.R.503b: abs…

ἀποτομάς.definition: pecul. fem. of abrupt; as Subst., split or hewn piece of wood, J.AJ3.1.2; javelin used in athletic games, Poll.10.64, Hsch

ἀποτομή.definition: cutting off, X.HG2.1.32: in; piece, segment, Epicur.Ep.2.p.37 U.; Ph.2.77, cf. ib.124 , Diog.Oen.24; Ocell.3.3; of the moon in eclipse, Arist.Cael.297b25, cf. 294n4, Plot.6.4.7; end cut off, Dsc.5.120

ἀποτομία.definition: severity, D.S.12.16, POxy.237 vii; cutting off, Dem.Ophth. ap. Aët.7.81

ἀπότομος.definition: metaph., severe, relentless, E.Alc.981 ; LXXWi.6.6. Adv. ib.5.22, Plb.18.11.2, Plu.Crass.3, etc.; brusquely, prob. l. in Cic.Att.10.11.5

ἀποτορεύω.definition: dub. l. for sq., Ph.1.505 , Jul.Or.3.112a

ἀποτορνεύω.definition: round off as by the lathe, Ph.1.505: metaph. of polished language, . . Pl.Phdr.234e ; Jul.Or.3.112a; ib.2.77a

ἀποτραχύνω.definition: pf. D.H.Comp.22:—make rough or hard: metaph., l.c.; but grate on the ear, Id.Dem.43:—Pass., to be or become rough or hard, Thphr.HP6.4.2

ἀποτρέφω.definition: feed, support, Str.16.2.10; Lyd.Mag.1.34,al.; Just.Nov.43.1.2:—Pass., live off a thing, Poll.6.32, Just.Nov.80.5Intr.; Eust.1.14

ἀποτριάζω.definition: to be victorious in wrestling , Sch.A.Ch.339 ; to be victorious in the Poll.3.151: = AB438, Hsch

ἀποτριτόω.definition: boil down to a third part, v.l. in Ps.-Dsc.4.137 , cf. Gp.7.13.5, Alex.Trall.1.15

ἀποτρόπαιος.definition: averting evil, freq. of Apollo; of sacrifices, D.H.5.54, Plu.2.290d,292a

ἀποτροπάομαι.definition: poet. for Ps.-Phoc.133 codd., Numen. ap. Ath.7.304f

ἀποτροπιάζω.definition: utter a deprecatory prayer for, Aristaenet.1.1:—Med., avert evil by sacrifice, LXXEz.16.21; POxy.885.53, cf. Phleg.Mir.1, Sch.A.Pers.203

ἀποτροπιασμός.definition: averting by expiatory sacrifice, PTeb.140: in pl., Beros. ap. J.AJ1.3.6, Aesop.112b, D.L.8.32

ἀπότροπος.definition: turned away, far from men; from which one turns away, horrible, A.Ch.155 ; S.Aj.608 ; Id.OT1314; Ar.Ec.792; a stern, hostile decree, Pi.P.8.94; . . Ps.-Phoc.182

ἀποτροφή.definition: nourishment, support, PSI 1.76.6 ; f.l. for in D.H.7.28, dub. in Ph.1.617

ἀποτρόφιμος.definition: furnishing sustenance, means of subsistence, PFlor.295.2

ἀποτρύχω.definition: = sq., Ph.2.231:—Pass., ib.288, Plu.Ant.24; of land, Ph.2.371

ἀποτρύω.definition: rub away, wear out, S.Tr.125 ; Ph.2.341; Plu.Aem.13:—Med., S.Ant.339 :—Pass., harassed, Hierocl.p.53 A., cf. Plu.CG6

ἀποτρώγω.definition: aor. 2 Ph.1.224, Gal.6.864; c. gen., nibble at, Babr.46.6: metaph., i.e. you don't gobble your swathe, Theoc.10

ἀποτυγχάνω.definition: Pass., a failure ensues, Arist.Ph.199b3; of things, to be missed, D.H.Pomp.2.14; prophesied and not come to pass, Luc.Alex.28; rejected, not finding a purchaser, Dsc.5.79

ἀπότυπος.definition: moulded, J.AJ20.9.4; Subst. image, IG11.223B17 ; also as neut., ib.203 B 83

ἀποτύπωσις.definition: impression, Longin.13.4, cf. Thphr.Sens.51; v.l. for J.AJ12.2.8

ἀποτύφλωσις.definition: making blind, LXXZa.12.4: metaph. of the veins, blocking, Herod.Med. in Rh.Mus.49.555

ἀποτύφω.definition: burn, in pf. part. Pass. Hsch

ἀποτυχία.definition: Ion. failure, Democr.243, Din.1.29 , Plb.5.98.5, Phld.Rh.1.73 S., J.AJ16.9.1, etc.: c. gen., failure to obtain, Artem.5.78

ἀπουλόω.definition: cicatrize, Dsc.5.79: metaph., Plu.2.46f:—Pass., of sores, Arr.Epict.2.21.22, cf. Alex. Aphr.Pr.1.114; Gal.13.719

ἀπούλωσις.definition: cicatrization, v.l. in Dsc.2.4, cf. Crito ap.Gal.12.448, Aret.CD2.3, Alex.Aphr.Pr.1.111

ἀπούρησις.definition: making water, ib.30.6, Sor.1.66, Ruf. ap. Aët.11.29, Aret.SD2.3

ἀπουσιάζω.definition: waste one's goods, Suid.; Artem.1.78: c.gen., lose substance, Zos.Alch.p.235 B.:—Pass., to be expended, Sor.1.87

ἀποφαίνω.definition: show forth, display, Sol.15.33, etc; make known, declare, Batr.144; Hdt.1.40; give evidence of a legitimate mode of living, Id.2.177; cf.B.II

ἀποφάσκω.definition: = only in pres. inf. and part., and impf.:— deny, Plu.2.393c; Simp.in Ph.218.11:—Pass., Dam.Pr.445; in S.OT485 is interpreted by Sch. 'neither commanding assent nor suffering denial) name of a sophism, Arr.Epict.3.9.2…

ἀποφέρβομαι.definition: feed on, dub. l. in E.Med.826

ἀποφεύγω.definition: as law-term, Hdt.6.82; And.1.123; Ar.Nu.167, cf. 1151; Antipho2.1.16; Pl.Lg.946d: c. dupl. acc. pers. et rei, D.40.19

ἀποφθαλμόομαι.definition: look askance at: hence, covet, envy, PLond.1674.17

ἀποφθέγγομαι.definition: speak one's opinion plainly, Luc.Zeux.1; chant hymns, LXX1 Chr.25.1

ἀποφθεγματίας.definition: dealer in saws and proverbs, Metrod.45

ἀποφλαυρίζω.definition: treat slightingly, make no account of, disparage, Pi.P.3.12, Hdt.1.86

ἀποφλεγμαίνω.definition: cease to burn, of inflammation, Hp.Aph.6.49: metaph. of anger, Plu.2.13d

ἀποφλεγματίζω.definition: purge away phlegm or cleanse from it, Dsc.2.159, Antyll. ap. Orib.8.10.2; promote the discharge of phlegm or mucus, Gal.11.769, etc

ἀποφλεγματισμός.definition: purging of phlegm, Dsc.5.3, Antyll. ap. Orib.8.10 tit., Archig. ap. Gal.12.582

ἀποφλύζω.definition: give vent to, sputter out, A.R.3.583: aor. Archil.35 :— Hsch. has

ἀποφοιβάζω.definition: utter by inspiration, Str.14.5.15; foretell, D.S.34.2; Id.31.10; Plb.29.21.7

ἀποφοιτάω.definition: fut. Thom.Mag.p.7 R.:—cease to; desert, abscond, Plu.Lys.4, cf. Aristid.Or.21.15; of ships in battle, Procop.Goth.4.23; simply, depart, Dionys.Av.1.11

ἀποφορά.definition: payment of what is due, tax; effluvia, D.H.10.53, D.S.24.12, Plu.2.647f, Aret.SA1.10; Sch.Il.Oxy.221 xvii8

ἀποφόρητος.definition: carried away; presents which guests received at table to take home, Ath.6.229c, cf. Petron.56, Suet.Cal.55, Vesp.19

ἀπόφορος.definition: not to be borne or suffered; past bearing, Hsch.; cf. Id

ἀποφορτίζομαι.definition: Med., discharge one's cargo, Act.Ap.21.3; jettison, abs., Ph.2.413; Timae.61; unload one's stomach, Artem.2.26:—Pass., of Sor.1.40: generally, jettison, get rid of, Ph.2.434, etc

ἀποφορτισμός.definition: unloading: hence of vomiting, Archig. ap. Orib.8.23.1

ἀποφράγνυμι.definition: fence off, block, Th.7.74: metaph., S.Ant.241

ἀποφράσσω.definition: Att. fut. = block up, stop up, Hp.Carn.18, Mul.1.1; Pl.Ti.91c; D.55.17; Onos.32:—Med., bar their passage, Th.8.104

ἀποφυλάττω.definition: store up, Hsch. s.v. ward off, Id. s.v

ἀποφυλλίζω.definition: strip a plant of its leaves, Thphr.HP7.12.2, Dsc.1.49, Sch.Ar.Pax1147

ἀποφυτεία.definition: propagation by slips, Arist.Long.467a28, Juv.468b18, Thphr.CP1.4.3

ἀποφύω.definition: produce, Thphr.HP1.6.4; of veins, send; part asunder, separate, Hsch

ἀποχαρίζομαι.definition: confer upon, present, IGRom.4.182 , Alex.Aphr.in Metaph.483.25:—Pass., POxy.1208.16

ἀποχειρίζω.definition: cut off the hand, only in Pass., Anon. ap. Suid., cf. Eust.1960.10

ἀποχειροβίοτος.definition: or living by the work of one's hands, Hdt.3.42,X.Cyr.8.3.37

ἀποχειροτονέω.definition: vote by show of hands away from; and; vote a charge away from one, acquit him, D.21.214

ἀποχηρόομαι.definition: Pass., to be bereft of, Ar.Pax1013

ἀποχράω.definition: Dor. Archim.Aren.3.3, [Epich.]253; abs., in persons other than 3sg., 1sg. only in [Epich.] l.c.; Ar.Pl.484; Pl.Plt.279b; D.4.22; Pherecr.145.6; Ar.Fr.489; Pl.Alc.2.145c; of Stoic.3.50: c. inf., . . Hdt.5.31; Id.3.138,…

ἀποχρηματίζω.definition: carry to an end, close a discussion; Pass., to be deposited, registered, of an official copy, Inscr.Magn.293.5

ἀποχρυσόω.definition: turn into gold or money, Pass., Artem.1.50, cf. Poll.7.102

ἀποχυλίζω.definition: extract the juice, prob. in Arist.Pr.873b4, cf. Dsc.1.86: —Pass., Antyll. ap. Orib.4.11.3

ἀποχωλόομαι.definition: Pass., to be made quite lame, Hp.Aër.22, Th.7.27, Paus.10.1.3

ἀποχώννυμι.definition: bank up a river, etc., X.HG2.2.4,5.2.4; Plu.Phoc.11

ἀποχωρέω.definition: abs., depart, E.IT265; withdraw, v.l. in X.Cyr.1.6.36; esp. after a defeat, retire, retreat, Th.2.89, etc.; X.HG4.4.11; Th.2.94

ἀποχώρησις.definition: death, Eun.VSp.469B; voidance, opp. Pl.Ti.65a, 81a; esp. of excretions, Arist.GA726a21, al.; = 2, Plu.Lyc.20

ἀποψάλλω.definition: pluck off, Hsch.; spring a trap that is set, Lyc.407; twang a string, Id.915; rings out the purest Attic, metaph. from the lyre, Philostr.VS2.1.7

ἀποψεύδομαι.definition: cheat grossly: c. acc., forge, J.BJ4.3.5:— Pass., to be quite cheated of, Plu.Marc.29

ἀπόψηκτρον.definition: cleanser, name of a remedy for Gal.12.818

ἀποψηφίζομαι.definition: Att. fut. D.22.45: Dep., c. pf; refuse to elect, Plu.Cor.15

ἀποψήφισις.definition: acquittal, Antipho5.9; disfranchisement, D.57.2 and 4 , cf. IG2.841b102

ἀπραγμάτευτος.definition: impracticable, i.e; deprived of commerce, Anon. ap. Suid.s.v

ἀπραγμοσύνη.definition: freedom from politics, love of a quiet; = SIG876.8 , Poll.8.156

ἀπράγμων.definition: gen. free from business; of things, not troublesome or painful, . . X.Ap.7. Adv. without trouble, Th.4.61, X.HG6.4.27; Th.6.87; carelessly, Arist.Mete.369b27: Comp. X.Ages.4.1

ἀπρακτέω.definition: do nothing, to be idle, Arist.EN1095b33; opp; gain nothing, X.Cyr.1.6.6

ἀπρέπεια.definition: impropriety in writing, Id.Phdr.274b; ugliness, APl.4.319, cf. Dsc.Alex.27

ἀπροαιρεσία.definition: inconsistency, Hp.Ep.17; prob. in Sammelb. 4317.5 , for

ἀπροαίρετος.definition: without set purpose, not deliberate; of things, incapable of choice or purpose, Hermog.Id.2.4; not under the control of will, Phld.D.3 Fr.75, M.Ant.6.41,al

ἀπροβούλευτος.definition: unpremeditated, Arist.EN1135b11; not submitted to the D.22.5, Hyp.Fr.231, Plu.Sol.19; of the Roman Senate, App.BC1.59

ἀπρόθυμος.definition: unready, backward, Hdt.7.220, Th.4.86, X.An.6.2.7, etc. Adv. Pl.Lg.665e

ἀπρόϊτος.definition: not proceeding or emanating , Dam.Pr.34; Gal.14.729. Adv. Hsch

ἀπρόληπτος.definition: unanticipated, Stoic. 3.149, Onos.8.1; not prejudged, Hierocl.in CA24p.459M

ἀπρομήθεια.definition: or want of forethought, Pl.La.197b, J.BJ3.5.6

ἀπρομήθευτος.definition: later form for Adv. Suid. s.v

ἀπρονόητος.definition: Act., not considering beforehand, X.HG5.3.7; Plb.5.7.2, cf. Orph.Fr.233; J.Vit.13; Luc.Bis Acc.2, etc.; of the gods, not exercising providence, Epicur.Fr.368. Adv. X.Cyr.1.4.21, etc.; Str.2.5.1; opp. S.E.P.1.151; with…

ἀπροοιμίαστος.definition: without preface, Luc.Hist.Conscr.23, Corn. Rh.p.358 H. Adv. D.H.Lys.17

ἀπρόοπτος.definition: Act., not foreseeing, unwary, Poll.1.179; Id.3.117. Adv. Sor.1.71, Ael.NA1.8

ἀπροόρατος.definition: = foreg. I, D.S.20.96, Corn.ND10; not previously seen, Gal.14.279

ἀπροπτωσία.definition: freedom from precipitancy, deliberateness, Stoic. 2.39, Chrysipp.ib.40, M.Ant.3.9

ἀπρόπτωτος.definition: not precipitate, Chrysipp.Stoic.2.40; Arr.Epict.2.8.29, cf. M.Ant.4.49. Adv. Chrysipp.Stoic.3.50

ἀπροσαύδητος.definition: not accosted, Plu.2.29b,921f; unapproachable, Aristocl. ap. Eus.PE11.3

ἀπρόσβατος.definition: Dor. inaccessible, Arist.HA563a5, cf. Plu.Alex.58, Luc.Prom.1; unapproachable, S.Tr.1030 , cf. Max.Tyr.18.1

ἀπρόσβλεπτος.definition: not to be looked at, EM433.49

ἀπροσδεής.definition: without want of anything, LXX1 Ma.12.9, al., Phld.D.3.13; Plu.2.122f, cf. 381b, Luc.Hist.Conscr.36: abs., self-sufficient, Plu.Comp.Arist.Cat.4, Plot.5.9.4

ἀπρόσδεκτος.definition: inadmissible, BGU 1113.21; Act., not giving heed to, Phld.Vit.p.34J., dub. in Id.D.3.Fr.42; unacceptable, Plb.36.12.4; IG3.73.14, 74.8; Porph.Marc.24

ἀπροσδιόνυσος.definition: unconnected with the worship of; not to the point, mal à propos, proverbial like Cic.Att. 16.13a.1, Plu.2.612e, Luc.Bacch.6

ἀπροσδιόριστος.definition: undefined, Ulp. ad D.24.68; unqualified, Heliod.in EN109.19; of propositions, indefinite in quantification, Ammon.in APr.14.37. Adv. without distinction, Gal.16.558; par excellence, Olymp.in Mete.123.3

ἀπροσδόκητος.definition: unexpected, unlooked for, A.Pr.680; Act., not expecting, unaware, Th.2.33, cf. 7.39; Id.6.69; Id.7.29

ἀπροσεκτέω.definition: to be heedless, inattentive, Eustr.in APo.258.6

ἀπρόσεκτος.definition: heedless, careless, Tz.ad Lyc.314. Adv. unconcernedly, Porph.Sent.32

ἀπροσέλευστος.definition: not taken up, of an inheritance, Just.Nov.1.1.3, cf. Suid

ἀπροσηγορία.definition: want of intercourse, Poet. ap. Arist.EN1157b13

ἀπροσήγορος.definition: not to be accosted, unapproachable, of a man, S.OC1277; of a lion, Id.Tr.1093; without intercourse or conversation, Plu.2.679a

ἀπρόσθικτος.definition: untouched, not to be touched, Hsch. s.v

ἀπρόσιτος.definition: unapproachable, inaccessible, Plb.3.49.7, cf. Str.1.3.18; 1 Ep.Ti.6.16; of persons, Cic.Att.5.20.6, cf. Plu.2.68e; D.S.19.96: metaph., Plu.Alc.4; Luc.Dem.Enc.32. Adv. Plu.2.45f

ἀπρόσκεπτος.definition: unforeseen, not thought of; Act., improvident, D.51.15. Adv. Antiph.195

ἀπρόσκλητος.definition: without summons to attend a trial, IG1.27a10, Hyp.Fr.2; a prosecution in support of which no has been issued, D.53.15; ib.14; Id.21.92; without notice, Hld.6.8; unsummoned, Id.8.1

ἀπρόσκοπος.definition: not stumbling, void of offence; free from harm, IG5.20.19 ; PGiss.17.7 , cf. PBaden 39 iii 14 . Adv. ib.79iv8

ἀπρόσκοπτος.definition: without offence, IG14.404. Adv. without stumbling, Eust.925.28

ἀπρόσκρουστος.definition: free from blows; not taking offence, Plu.in Hes.65

ἀπρόσληπτος.definition: not taking or admitting a construction, A.D.Pron.14.15, Synt.63.21

ἀπρόσλογος.definition: not to the point, Sch.Ar.V.1311, al. Adv. Plb.9.36.6

ἀπροσμηχάνητος.definition: against whom no device avails, Sch.Il.16.29

ἀπροσμιγής.definition: = sq., Steph.Byz. s.v. Eust. ad D.P.752

ἀπρόσμικτος.definition: holding no communion with, Hdt.1.65: abs., solitary, isolated, Poll.3.64. Adv. Id.5.139

ἀπρόσοιστος.definition: hard to associate with or deal with, A.Pers.91 . Adv. unsociably, Isoc.9.49

ἀπρόσοπτος.definition: not to be looked at, faced, Poll.1.117

ἀπροσόρατος.definition: not to be looked on, frightful, Pi.O.2.67; epith. of Orph.H.39.2

ἀπροσόρμιστος.definition: where one cannot land, D.S.20.74, Sch.S.Ph.214

ἀπροστασίαστος.definition: without or guardian, Ph.1.170; of the universe, ib.696

ἀπροστάτευτος.definition: without a leader or guide, J.AJ20.8.8, Ael.NA15.8, f.l.for sq. in Hierocl.p.54A

ἀπρόσφορος.definition: dangerous, E.IA287 ; unsuitable, Herod.Med. ap. Orib.10.18.6; incongruous, Tz.ad Hes.Op.735. Adv. Steph.in Hp.1.223D

ἀπροσφυής.definition: incongruous, Eust.178.37; unrelated, Tz.H.8.158. Adv. Eust.529.31

ἀπρόσφυλος.definition: not belonging to the tribe, Hld.4.8

ἀπροσφώνητος.definition: not accosted, Cic.Att. 8.8.1; unnoticed, unremarked, Plu.2.575b, Sch.A.R.1.645

ἀπροτίοπτος.definition: = invisible, obscure, Man.2.19, Opp.H.3.159, Q.S.7.73, Ath.Mitt.27.339

ἀπροφάσιστος.definition: offering no excuse; admitting no excuse, implacable, E.Ba.1002

ἀπρόφατος.definition: unforetold, unexpected, Arat.424,768; unutterable, terrific, A.R.1.645

ἀπώθητος.definition: thrust or driven away, rejected, Suid

ἀπωμοσία.definition: denial upon oath, as law-term, opp. Poll.8.54, cf. Hsch

Ἀραβία.definition: Arabia, Hdt.2.8, etc. : poet. Theoc.17.86:—Adj. Arabian, Hdt.1.198, al.:—also PGen.29.8 , Plu.Ant.69, Hsch.:—later :—pecul. fem. Them.Or.34.56: St.Byz

Ἀραβίζω.definition: take part with the Arabs, Suid

ἀραγμός.definition: clashing, clattering, rattling, A.Th.249; crashing shower of stones, E.Ph.1143; beating of the breast in grief, S.OC1609; Lyc.940.—Rare in Prose, Hellanic.167 J

ἀράζω.definition: or snarl, growl, of dogs, Ael.NA5.51, Poll.5.86, Ph.1.694 codd

ἀραιόθριξ.definition: with thin hair, Hsch. s.v. cf. Moer.421

ἀραιόσαρκος.definition: with porous, spongy flesh, Hp.Nat.Puer.21, Mul.1.1, Hices. ap. Ath.7.288c

ἀραιόστημος.definition: of thin warp, fine, Hsch. s.v

ἀραιότης.definition: looseness of substance, porousness, rarity, opp. Hp.Aph.5.63, al., Arist.Pr.869b30: pl., Id.Ph.260b10, Epicur.Ep.2p.49U., Placit.3.12.1; Arist.Aud.802a24; opp. Plu.Fr.inc.149

ἀραιόφθαλμος.definition: with few eyes or buds, Gp.5.8.2

ἀραίωμα.definition: interstice, crevice, chink, Str.4.4.1, D.S.1.39, Luc.VH1.30, Placit.3.3.11, Plu.2.980c, etc.; of the body, Hp.Morb.4.45; pore, HeroSpir.1Praef., al., cf. Sor.1.115; a little bit, Longin.10.17

ἀργαίνω.definition: to be white, E.Fr.73, Philod.Scarph.126 , Opp.C.3.299:—in Pass., Nonn.D.34.145

Ἀργειφόντης.definition: voc. h.Hom.29.7; acc. to Paus.Gr.Fr.65, from serpent-slayer, i.e. Apollo, S.Fr.1024, cf. Sch.A.Pr.569; of Telephus, Parth.Fr.33

ἀργέω.definition: fut. aor. BGU698.4 : pf; Pass., to be left undone, X.Cyr.2.3.3; to be fruitless, Id.Hier.9.9

ἀργικέραυνος.definition: with bright, vivid lightning, epith. of Zeus, Il.19.121, al., Orph.Fr.21a, 168, Pi.O.8.3, Cleanth. Stoic1.122

ἀργιμήτας.definition: epith. of bull which carried Europa, Phryn.Trag.16

ἀργιόδους.definition: white-toothed, white- tusked, Il.10.264, cf. Od.8.60, etc.; Il.11.292:—also A.R.2.820

ἀργίπους.definition: gen. swift-footed, Il.24.211; of rams, S.Aj.237 ; = , Hsch

Ἀργολίζω.definition: take the part of the Argives, X.HG4.8.34, Ephor.137

Ἀργολίς.definition: Argolis, Hdt., etc; as Adj., of Argolis, Argolic, A.Supp.236:—later Plu.Rom.21. Adv. Eust.722.63

ἀργυραμοιβός.definition: money-changer, banker, Pl.Plt.289e, Theoc.12.37, etc.: as Adj., Maiist.32

ἀργύρειος.definition: = silver- mines, Th.2.55,6.91; X.Vect.4.5; D.21.167; alone, X.Mem.2.5.2, Aeschin.1.101, Pl.Lg.742d

ἀργυρήλατος.definition: of wrought silver, A.Fr.185; E.Ion1181; bearing silver, A.Fr.25A

ἀργυρίδιον.definition: = generally in a contemptuous sense, Ar.Pl.147,Fr.547, Eup.113; Isoc.13.4, cf. Socr.Ep.36, Olymp.in Grg.p.275J

ἀργυρίζομαι.definition: Med., get or extort money, Din.1.40,cf. OGI669.52 ; for a bribe, Sammelb.4416.19 ; from one, J.AJ14.14.6

ἀργυρισμός.definition: getting money, Str.7.3.7, Ph.1.145, al., D.C.59.15; OGI669.37 ; Sammelb.4416.11

ἀργυρογνώμων.definition: assayer of silver, Pl.Virt.378e, Arist.Rh.1375b5, Plu.Crass.2, Max.Tyr.2.2, etc

ἀργυροδάμας.definition: name of a precious stone, Plin.37.144

ἀργυροδίνης.definition: Dor. silver-eddying, epith. of rivers, Il.2.753, 21.8,130, Hes.Th.340, B.7.48, Call.Cer.13, Epic.Alex. Adesp.5, Nonn.D.19.304; late Prose, Philostr.VS2.1.14

ἀργυροειδής.definition: like silver, silvery, E.IA752 , Ion95 ; Orph.A.599; Tryph.98; of the pupils in disease, Hp.Prorrh.2.20

ἀργυροθήκη.definition: money-chest, Diocl.Com.1 D., Antiph.157, Thphr.Char.10.14, Poll.4.19

ἀργυροκοπεῖον.definition: silversmith's shop, mint, AntiphoFr.36, And.Fr.5, Aeschin.Socr.39, Arist.Pr.936b26, Plb.26.1.2:—also IG22.1013.30, 12.480

ἀργυροκόπος.definition: coiner, Phryn.Com.5; silversmith, Plu.2.830e, SIG 1263 , Poll.7.102,103, LXXJd.17.4, Act.Ap.19.24, PHaw. 68.3

ἀργυρολογέω.definition: levy money, X.HG1.1.12: c. acc., levy money upon, lay under contribution, Th.8.3, cf. 2.69; Aeschin.3.159, etc.; X.HG4.8.30; Them.Or.23.289d

ἀργυρολόγητος.definition: subject to a levy in money, LXX2; levying of money, X.HG1.1.8, etc

ἀργυρόπεζα.definition: silver-footed , epith. of Thetis, Il.1.538, al.; of Aphrodite, Pi.P.9.9, cf. Orph.Fr.275; of Artemis, Nonn.D.34.47:—hence Adj. AP5.59

ἀργυρόπους.definition: gen. with silver feet or legs, X.An.4.4.21; IG2.646, D.24.129; Plb.30.25.18

ἀργυρόπρυμνον.definition: vessel with silver- plated stern-post, PSI6.551.1

ἀργυροστερής.definition: robbing of silver, a robber's life, A.Ch.1002

ἀργυροταμίας.definition: treasurer of a city, IG22.1100,IGRom.4.774,775 , etc.; of a club, PLond. 3.1178.74

ἀργυρότοξος.definition: with silver bow, Homeric epith. of Apollo, Il.2.766, al.; also simply bearer of the silver bow, ib.1.37

ἀργυροτρύφημα.definition: a sort of blanc-mange, Chrysipp. Tyan. ap. Ath.14.647d, prob. in Gal.6.811

ἀργυροφεγγής.definition: silver-shining, Nonn.D.4.24; of a poor dinner served on silver plate, AP11.313

ἀργυρόφλεψ.definition: with veins of silver ore, Sch.Pl.Ti.25b

ἀργυροχόος.definition: melter of, worker in, silver, LXXWi.15.9

ἀργυρώνητος.definition: bought with silver, Hdt.4.72; A.Ag.949; i. e. slave, Isoc.14.18; E.Alc.676; PAvrom.1A 16 , cf. PLond.2.198

ἀργύφεος.definition: Ep. Adj. silver-shining, silver- white, Il.18.50; Od.5.230; Hes.Th.574; AP9.633 ; Orph.Fr.70, cf.Mus.Belg.16.71 , Epic. in POxy. 421.6

ἄργυφος.definition: = foreg., epith. of sheep, Il.24.621, Od.10.85

ἀρδαλόω.definition: smear, Hp.Nat.Mul.67, Philem.59; spread a plaster, Hp.Mul.1.20:—Pass., filthy, LXXSi.22.1; also Hsch

ἀρδεία.definition: irrigation, Str.4.6.7, Plu.2.688a , BGU283.6 ; Wilcken Chr.461.24 ; of a horse, Ael.NA7.12

ἄρδευσις.definition: = foreg., Hp.Hebd.1.87, Plb.9 43.5 , Moschio ap.Ath.5.207d, J.AJ3.1.3

ἀρδεύω.definition: = water, irrigate, A.Pr.852, Arist.HA601b13, Pr.924b15, Thphr.HP7.5.2, etc.:—Pass., Com.Adesp.29 D., Plb.10.28.3, PThead.16.10 ; M.Ant.5.4: metaph., Chor. in Philol.54.120:—Pass., Plot.2.9.3

ἄρδω.definition: impf. Pl.Ti.76a, Ion. 3sg; give drink to cattle, from or at the Meles, h.Hom.9.3; Euph.66; Hdt. l.c.; of rivers, furnish drink for men, Pi.O.5.12:—Pass., drink, h.Ap.263: metaph., to be drunk with light, Plot.2.9.3

ἀρειμάνιος.definition: = foreg., Ph.1.375; as pr. n., = Avest. angrō mainyuš, a name given by the Magi to the Spirit of Evil, opp. Oromasdes , Arist.Fr.6, Plu.2.369e, Dam.Pr.125 bis

ἀρεσκεύομαι.definition: to be complaisant to, Clearch.25, Hsch.: abs., to be obsequious, Plu.2.4d, M.Ant.5.5

ἀρεστήρ.definition: a cake, as a propitiatory offering, IG2.1651B6, cf. 1662, Ael.Dion.Fr.68, Poll.6.76

ἀρεταλογία.definition: celebration of divine LXXSi.36.19, cf. Sm.Ps.29.6; as a profession, recitation of Str.17.1.17 , Man.4.447

ἀρεταλόγος.definition: professional expounder of , writer of prob. in Phld.Po.5.1425.9; SIG1133, cf. Suet.Aug.74, Juv.15.16, Aus.Ep.13

Ἀρηΐθοος.definition: swift in war, Il.8.298, 15.315, A.R.1.1042; Simon.104

ἀρηΐφιλος.definition: dear to Ares, epith. of warriors in Hom., Il.2.778, al., cf. Hes.Th.317, Pi.I.8.25, etc.; of the river Thermodon, Tryph.33

ἀρήτειρα.definition: fem of Call.Cer.43, Musae.68, A.R.1.312, etc

ἀρητεύω.definition: to be president, IG12.1259 ; Dor. ib.4.497.4 , SIG56.43

ἀρθρεμβολέω.definition: insert part of a machine, in Pass., Ath.Mech.34.6

ἀρθρεμβόλησις.definition: setting of a limb, Apollon.Cit.1.1:—also Orib.49.9.5

ἀρθρέμβολον.definition: instrument for setting limbs, Gal.14.781: in pl., instruments of torture, LXX4 Ma.8.13

ἀριζήλωτος.definition: much to be envied, Ar.Eq.1329 : in Orac. ap. Eus.PE9.10

ἀρίθμησις.definition: counting, reckoning up, Hdt.2.143; account, BGU328i24 , etc

ἀριπρεπής.definition: very distinguished; of things, very bright, . . Il.15.309; . . 8.556; Lyr.Alex.Adesp.9.3; of a mountain, conspicuous, Od.9.22; Orph.Fr.114: Comp., Them.Or.18.223b

ἀρίσταρχος.definition: best-ruling, epith. of Zeus, Simon.231, B.12.58

ἀριστερόπηρος.definition: paralysed on the left side, BGU367.8

ἀριστεύς.definition: dual S.Aj.1304: :—used by Hom. mostly in pl. those who excel in valour, chiefs, Il.2.404, al.; Od.14.218, cf. Hdt.6.81, Alc. Supp.1a.8, Pi.P.9.107, Ant.Lib.2.2, etc.: sg., A.Pers.306; E.IA28 ; as an honorary title, CI…

ἀριστίζω.definition: give one breakfast, Ar.Eq.538; Id.Av.659; IG7.2712.62 :—Med., breakfast, Hp.VM10

ἀριστόβουλος.definition: best in counsel, epith. of Artemis at Melite, Plu.Them.22, cf. Artem.2.37; at Rhodes, Porph.Abst.2.54:—hence a confraternity of her worshippers, IG12.163

ἀριστογαλατίας.definition: title of chief citizen of the province of Galatia, Class.Rev.22.214

ἀριστοκρατέομαι.definition: Pass., to be governed by the best- born, live under an aristocracy, Ar.Av.125, Pl.R.338d, Arist.Pol.1288a41, etc

ἀριστοκρατία.definition: rule of the best-born, aristocracy; ideal constitution, rule of the best, Arist.Pol.1293b1 sqq., EN1160a33, Pl.Mx.238c, 238d, Plb.6.4.3

ἀριστολόχεια.definition: herb promoting child-birth, birthwort, Aristolochia, Nic.Th.509,937; = A. rotunda, = A. longa, = A. Clematitis, Dsc.3.4; = A. cretica, Plin.HN25.95:—also Hp.Nat.Mul.32

ἀριστόμαχος.definition: as pr.n., Hdt., etc.:—hence Adj. AP13.8

ἀριστοπάλας.definition: best of wrestlers, Epigr. in BKT5.77

ἀριστοπάτρα.definition: daughter of a peerless line, of Artemis, B.10.106

ἀριστοποιέω.definition: prepare breakfast, things prepared for breakfast, X.HG4.5.1:—mostly in Med., get one's breakfast, Th.4.30, 8.95, X.An.3.3.1, 4.3.9, Onos.42.10, etc.; X.HG4.5.8

ἀριστοπολιτευτής.definition: best of citizens, honorary title, esp. at Sparta, IG5.335, al.:—also best citizen, ib.468, IPE2.29 :— hence privileges of an IG5.65 , SIG893A 9

ἀριστοπόσεια.definition: wife of a noble husband, Opp.C.1.6

Ἀριστοτελίζω.definition: follow or imitate Aristotle, Str.13.1.54:—Adj. Aristotelian, Cic.Att.13.19.4:—also Luc.Demon.56. Adv. Iamb.Comm.Math.27

ἀριστοτέχνης.definition: Dor. best of artificers, of Zeus, Pi.Fr.57, cf. Hsch

ἀριστοτόκος.definition: bearing the best children; Pass., born of the best parents, E.Rh.909, cf. Epigr.Gr.896

ἀριστοφυής.definition: of best nature, Ecphant. ap. Stob.4.7.64

ἀρίφρων.definition: gen. very wise or prudent, Suid

Ἀρκαδίζω.definition: take the side of the Arcadians, Polyaen.6.36

ἀρκτεύω.definition: serve as an II, Lys.Fr.82:—in Med., Sch.Ar.Lys.645

Ἀρκτοφύλαξ.definition: the constellation Eudox. ap. Hipparch.1.2.5, Arat.92

ἀρκυστασία.definition: line of nets, in pl., X.Cyn.6.6

ἀρκύστατος.definition: surrounding toils, a place beset with nets, A.Eu.112, S.El.1476, cf. A.Ag.1375 Elmsl

ἀρκυωρός.definition: watcher of nets, Cratin.79, X.Cyn.6.5, Lycurg.Fr.79, Poll.5.17, etc

ἁρματαρχία.definition: squadron of sixteen war-chariots, Ascl.Tact.8, Ael.Tact.22.2

ἁρμάτειος.definition: of or belonging to a chariot, E.IA230; X.Cyr.6.4.9, Ant.Lib.11.3 ; Apoll.Lex. s.v. is prob. corrupt; Placit.2.20.1; name of a melody for the flute, Plu.2.335a, 1133e; stage-direction in E.Or.[1384]

ἁρματηλατέω.definition: go in a chariot, drive it, Hdt.5.9, X.Smp.4.6

ἁρματηλάτης.definition: Dor. charioteer, Pi.P.5.115, S.El.700, X.Smp.2.27, etc

ἁρματίζομαι.definition: place in a chariot: metaph., i.e. the Argo, Lyc.1319

ἁρμάτιον.definition: name of an eyesalve, Gal.12.779, Aët.7.41

ἁρματομαχέω.definition: fight in or from a chariot, Eust.1088.27

ἁρματοτροφέω.definition: keep chariot-horses, esp. for racing, X.Ages.9.6, D.L.4.17, Phld.Acad.Ind.p.47 M

ἁρματοτροχιά.definition: Ep. wheel-track of a chariot, Il.23.505, Ph.1.312, Luc.Dem.Enc.23, Ael.VH2.27, Q.S.4.516

ἁρμελάτης.definition: = foreg., Orac. ap; name of a bandage, Gal.12.497 Chart

Ἀρμενία.definition: Armenia, and Str.11.12.3 and 4 sq., cf. App.Mith.105:—Adj. Armenian: also Str.11.14.12: apricot, Prunus Armeniaca, Dsc.1.115, Gal.6.593 Id.12.76): limestone coloured blue by copper carbonate, Id.5.105; Dsc.5.89

Ἀρμενιάρχης.definition: president of the Anatolian Studies p.116

ἁρμολογέω.definition: join, pile together, AP7.554 :—Pass., PRyl.233.6 : metaph., closely connected with . . , S.E.M.5.78

Ἁρμονίδης.definition: Patron., son of a carpenter, Il.5.60

ἁρμόνιος.definition: fitting, harmonious, LXXWi.16.20, dub.l. in D.H.Dem.22. Adv. J.AJ8.3.2, Ph.1.179, Iamb.VP5.20

ἅρμοσις.definition: tuning, Phryn.PSp.24B. : metaph. of numbers, Theol.Ar.54

ἁρμοστήρ.definition: = sq., X.HG4.8.39, IG5.937.2; of stones, laid with the grain, Hsch

ἀρνευτήρ.definition: tumbler, acrobat, Herod.8.42; diver, Arat.656, Hsch

ἀρνευτής.definition: = epith. of the fish Numen. ap. Ath.7.322f, Eust.1083.59

ἄρνησις.definition: Gramm., negation, D.T.642.3, Lesb.Gramm.26; two negatives make an affirmative, Sch.S.OT1053

ἀρνοκόμης.definition: with lamb's hair, i.e. curly hair, epith. of Apollo, Macr.Sat.1.17.45

ἀροτήρ.definition: plougher, husbandman, Il.18.542; as Adj., steer for ploughing, Hes.Op.405, Arat.132, Plu.Pyrrh.5, OGI519.21 , etc.; Nonn.D.3.192; Orph.H.40.8

ἀρότης.definition: = foreg., Pi.I.1.48, Hdt.4.2, Pherecr.130; Hp.Art.8, cf.Ael.VH5.14; workmen of the Muses, i.e. poets, Pi.N.6.32; seaman, Call.Fr.436

ἄροτος.definition: crop, S.OT270: metaph., seed, E.Med.1281 ; Id.Ion1095; tillage, ploughing, Hes.Op.384,458; live by husbandry, Hdt.4.46; ritual ploughing, ceremonial at Athens, Plu.2.144a: pl., Ar.Ra.1034

ἀρότριος.definition: of husbandry, epith. of Apollo, Orph.H.34.3

ἀροτριόω.definition: = in Pass., v.l. in LXXIs.7.25, cf. Ps.-Plu.Fluv.21.2
