ἀροτροδίαυλος.definition: plougher, who goes backwards and forwards as in the AP10.101

ἀρουραῖος.definition: of or from the country, rural, rustic, field-vole, Hdt.2.141; A.Fr.227; of Euripides as the reputed son of a herb-seller, Ar.Ra.840; of Aeschines, who played the part of Oenomaüs 'in the provinces', D.18.242, cf. AB21…

ἀρουρηδόν.definition: surface measured in PRyl. 157.5 , PStrassb.112.10 , etc

ἁρπαγιμαῖος.definition: = sq., Orph.H.29.14, Phryn.PSp.6B.; scarcely visible, at close of month, Sch.Arat.735

ἁρπάγιμος.definition: ravished, stolen, Call.Cer.9, Fr.1.46P., AP11.290 , Doroth.20

ἅρπαγμα.definition: booty, prey, Lyc.87, LXXJb.29.17; windfall, Plu.2.330d; Hld.7.20

ἁρπαλέος.definition: Ep. Adj., : devouring; attractive, alluring, charming, Od.8.164; opp. Thgn.1353; Mimn.1.4; gift to be eagerly seized, Pi.P.8.65, cf. 10.62

ἅρπασμα.definition: Att. form of Pl.Lg.906d, Men.Epit.542; prob. in Aeschin.3.222, cf. Plu.Cat.Ma.13, IG12.123

ἁρπεδόνη.definition: cord, for binding or snaring game; yarn of which cloth is made, Hdt.3.47, Aristias2 , AP6.160 ; silk-worm's thread, Paus.6.26.8; bow-string, AP5.193

ἁρπεδονίζω.definition: snare with a Hsch.: also, = Id

ἀρρενογονέω.definition: beget or bear male children, Thphr.HP9.18.5, Ph.1.262

ἀρρενογόνος.definition: begetting or bearing male children, ib.573b32, 585b13; Hp.Steril.230; of drugs, promoting the conception of males, Dsc.3.140. 2. = III, dog’s mercury, Mercurialis perennis, Thphr.HP9.18.5, Dsc.3.125, Plin.HN26.162

ἀρρενόομαι.definition: become a man, do the duties of one, Luc.Am.19; of a woman, Ph.2.328; ib.53; Astrol., of stars , become masculine, Heph.Astr.1.2, Ptol.Tetr.20

ἀρρενοτοκέω.definition: bear male children, Arist.HA574a1, GA765a24, Dsc.Eup.2.96

ἀρρενοτόκιον.definition: drug promoting conception of males, Dsc.Eup.2.96

ἀρρενόφρων.definition: gen. of manly mind, Suid. s.v

ἀρρενωπία.definition: manly look, manliness, Pl.Smp.192a, Zeno Stoic.1.58

ἀρρωστέω.definition: to be unwell, Heraclit.58, X.Mem.3.11.10, D.19.124: c.acc. cogn., Hp.Coac.579, Arist.Rh.1372a28

ἀρρωστία.definition: weakness, sickness, Hp.VM6, etc.: pl; moral weakness, D.Prooem.53; loss of morale, Th.7.47; Arist.Ph.253a33: c. gen., lack of eagerness to serve, Th.3.15, cf. Phryn.PSp.10 B

ἀρσενόμορφος.definition: of masculine form or look, Orph.H.36.7

ἀρταβίειος.definition: of an PFlor.369.14; ), tax of one artaba per PTeb.119.11 , PLond.3.1171vii 15 , PFay.99: —also neut. pl. PTeb.5.59

ἀρτεμής.definition: safe and sound, Il.5.515; Od.13.43, cf.A.R.1.415, Call.Iamb.1.227.—Ep. word; etym. of Pl.Cra.406b

ἀρτεμώνιον.definition: Dim. of foreg. I, Tz.ad Lyc.359; name of an eye-salve, Gal.12.780

ἀρτηριοτομέω.definition: cut an artery, in Pass., have it cut, Antyll. ap. Orib.7.14.2, Gal.8.202

ἀρτηριοτομία.definition: severing of an artery, Antyll. ap. Orib.7.14 tit., Gal.11.312

ἀρτίγαμος.definition: just married, IG14.1835, cf. Opp.H.4.179, Nonn.D.48.298, al

ἀρτιγένειος.definition: with the beard just sprouting, AP9.219 , Nonn.D.18.135; as Subst., App.Pun.8; incorrectly used, = Luc.Sol.2

ἀρτιγενής.definition: just born or made, Nic.Al.357, Ael.NA4.34, Sor.1.87

ἀρτίδιον.definition: Dim. of small loaf, D.L.7.13; piece of bread, Sor.1.115; food, POxy.738.8

ἀρτίζω.definition: pf. PMag.Leid.W.10.42:—get ready, prepare, AP10.25 , PMag.l.c.:—Med., Theoc.13.43; D.S.14.20:—Pass., CIG3601.9 , S.E.M.11.208

ἀρτικροτέω.definition: = equip, Str.15.1.32; keep time, of rowers, Hsch

ἀρτιμαθής.definition: having just learnt, E.Hec.687; Gal.11.466: abs., beginner, Sor.1.4, cf. Longus3.20

ἀρτιμελής.definition: sound of limb, Pl.R.536b, Sor.1.3, D.C.69.20; perfect in all members, Them.Or.26.316c

ἀρτιοπέρισσος.definition: Att. even-odd, of even numbers, the halves of which are odd, as 6, 10, etc., Philol.5, Ph.1.3, Plu.2.1139f; of unity, Arist.Fr.199

ἀρτίπους.definition: sound of foot, opp. Od.8.31c, cf. Hdt.3.130, Them.Or.21.255c

ἀρτιστομία.definition: distinctness or precision in speech, Poll.6.150

ἀρτισύλληπτος.definition: newly conceived in the womb, Dsc.Eup.2.81

ἀρτίτομος.definition: just cut or severed, A.R.4.1515; parox. having just cut or hewn, Suid

ἀρτίτροπος.definition: of modest manners , A.Th.333 cod. Med

ἀρτίφρων.definition: gen. sound of mind, sensible, Od.24.261, cf. E.Med.294; Pl.R.536b; . . . . quite in one's senses except . . , E.IA877: c. gen., . . when he came to full consciousness of . . , A.Th.778

ἀρτιχόρευτος.definition: recently celebrated in the dance, Nonn.D.7.46, al

ἀρτιώνυμος.definition: of even denomination, epith. of all even numbers, Nicom.Ar.1.8:—hence to be even, Iamb.in Nic.p.22 P

ἀρτοζήτης.definition: one who begs for bread, Sch.Lyc.775

ἀρτοκοπεῖον.definition: bake-house, Dsc.2.36, BGU1202.5 , Gp.1.6.2; Charis.p.553 K.; OGI177.19

ἀρτοκόπος.definition: baker, whether fem., Hdt.1.51; or masc., Id.9.82, Pl.Grg.518b , X.An.4.4.21 , HG7.1.38, IG3.1452, IGRom.4.1244

ἀρτολάγανον.definition: savoury cake made with spices, wine, oil, and milk, Cic.Fam.9.20.2, Ath.5.113d

ἀρτοποιέω.definition: make into bread, bake, c. acc., App.BC2.61, cf. POxy.1459.9 : abs., bake bread, Longus3.10:—Med., Str.3.3.7; J.AJ4.4.4:—Pass., Dsc.2.189

ἀρτοπτεῖον.definition: place or vessel for baking, Poll.10.112

ἀρτόπτης.definition: baker, Hsch. s.v; pan for baking bread, Plin.HN18.107

ἀρτοπωλία.definition: dealing in bread, ib.24, Phryn.PSp.33 B

ἀρτοστροφέω.definition: turn bread, as in baking, Ar.Fr.748

ἀρτοφάγος.definition: bread-eater, Hecat.Fr.323 J.: name of a mouse in Batr.210

ἀρτοφοῖνιξ.definition: cake of bread and dates, PLond.2.90.37

ἀρτοφόριον.definition: bread-basket, S.E.M.1.234: the form; a festival, An.Ox.3.277

ἀρτοφόρος.definition: holding bread, Poll.6.32; = foreg. I, Ath.4.129e

ἄρτυσις.definition: dressing, seasoning, Ph.Bel.86.32, D.S.2.59, Plu.2.99c, Gal.6.478; mixing of metals in smelting, Plu.2.395c

ἀρύω.definition: Simon.45, Att. Pl.Phdr.253a; Med., draw water for oneself, having drawn water from . . , Hes.Op.550; Pherecr.130.5; X.Cyr.1.2.8; Pl.Criti.120a: c. acc., E.Hipp.209; Pl.Ion534a: c. gen. partit., Ar.Nu.272; having drawn…

ἀρχαιογονία.definition: origin of a race, Eust.1156.54, etc

ἀρχαιολογία.definition: antiquarian lore, ancient legends or history, Pl.Hp.Ma.285d, D.S.2.46, D.H.1.4, Str.11.14.12; title of works by Cleanthes, Josephus, and Hieronymus Aegyptius, cf. J.AJ1.3.6

ἀρχαιομελισιδωνοφρυνιχήρατος.definition: prob. in Ar.V.220 dear honey-sweet old songs from Phrynichus' Phoenissae

ἀρχαιοπινής.definition: with the patina of antiquity, D.H.Dem.38

ἀρχαιόπλουτος.definition: rich from olden time, of hereditary wealth, A.Ag.1043, S.El.1393 , Lys.19.49, Arist.Rh.1387a24

ἀρχαιοπρεπής.definition: time-honoured, venerable, A.Pr.409; of literary style, old-fashioned, D.H.Comp.23; Id.Pomp.2; Simp.in Ph.233.10 . Adv. ib.111.15

ἀρχαιότροπος.definition: old-fashioned, Th.1.71, cf. Ph.2.458, Iamb.Protr.21; of a person, D.C.59.29. Adv. Dam.Pr.5

ἀρχαιρεσιάρχης.definition: leader of a political party, Hdn.Epim.167

ἀρχέκακος.definition: beginning mischief, Il.5.63, Plu.2.861a, Hld.1.9, Ph.1.359, al., Porph.Chr.49.22

ἀρχερανίζω.definition: to be president of an , IG12.672.3

ἀρχεφηβεύω.definition: to be head of the IG4.589

ἀρχέφοδος.definition: chief of police, PTeb.90Intr. , PRyl.127.20 , PTeb. 331.15

ἀρχηγέτης.definition: generally, leader, chief, A.Supp.184,251, S.OT751, etc.; later, governor, Chor. in Rev.Phil.1.67: metaph., Jul.Or.6.188b; of a philosophical school, Phld.Sto.Herc.339.12

ἀρχίβακχος.definition: chief of college of IG22.1368.12, al

ἀρχιβδέλλιον.definition: = Ps.-Dsc.4.23 Wellm.; spelt archebion in Plin.HN22.51

ἀρχιβούκολος.definition: chief herdsman, Sch.Il.1.39; president of college of SIG1115.3 : hence Inscr.Perg.487.5

ἀρχίγαλλος.definition: head of college of in mystery- cult, Jahresh.14 Beibl.136 , JHS19.280 , etc

ἀρχιγραμματεύς.definition: chief clerk or secretary, Plb.5.54.12, Plu.Eum.1, etc

ἀρχιδικαστής.definition: chief judge, D.S.1.48, Plu.2.355a; at Alexandria, BGU1155.6 , OGI136,682, etc

ἀρχιεράομαι.definition: Med., to be high-priest or priestess, LXX4 Ma.4.18, J.AJ17.19.1, OGI544.14 , IG14.1878, BSA16.120 , etc.: pf. part. IGRom.3.1475

ἀρχιερατεύω.definition: ), to be high-priest, LXX1 Ma.14.47, PTeb.407 , OGI485.4 , IG14.1045, etc

ἀρχιεροθυτέω.definition: to be president of , IG12.836 :—Subst. president of ib.788, al

ἀρχιεταῖρος.definition: chief friend or companion, LXX2 Ki.16.16

ἀρχιευνοῦχος.definition: chief of the eunuchs, ib.Da.1.3, Hld.8.3

ἀρχιζάκορος.definition: chief keeper of a temple, CIG 4470

ἀρχιθέωρος.definition: chief of a or sacred embassy, And.1.132, Arist.EN1122a25, SIG2588.15, al. :—also ; Dor. SIG 558.24

ἀρχιθιασίτης.definition: leader of a IG11.1228.4 :—hence OGI591.5 , etc.; and BCH31.446

ἀρχικέραυνος.definition: ruling the thunder, Cleanth.1.31, v.l. for in Orph.Fr.21a

ἀρχικερδέμπορος.definition: president of guild of merchants, IG12.581

ἀρχικυνηγός.definition: chief-huntsman, a Ptolemaic court official, OGI99.2 , 143.3 , Ostr.1530, J.AJ16.10.3

ἀρχιμάγειρος.definition: chief cook, LXXGe.39.1, al., cf. Ph.2.63; title of a great officer in Oriental courts, LXXDa.2.14, cf. J.AJ10.10.3, Plu.2.11b:—also dignitary in Mithraic cult, BCH 37.97

ἀρχιμάχιμος.definition: officer of native Egyptian troops, PTeb.112.86 , 121.128

ἀρχιμύστης.definition: chief of the mystae, CIG 2052 , Arch.Anz.30.175 , BCH 11.483 , Jul.Laod.inCat.Cod.Astr.4.105.33:—hence Eph.Epigr.3.236

ἀρχιονηλάτης.definition: chief donkey-driver, CPHerm.127r Fr.2 vii 19:—also PLond.1.131r321

ἀρχιπαστοφόρος.definition: head of college of , Ostr.1174, POxy.241.10

ἀρχιπειράτης.definition: Lat. archipirata Cic.Off.2.11.40, al.:—pirate-chief, D.S.20.97, Plu.Pomp.45, Petron.101

ἀρχιποίμην.definition: chief shepherd, 1 Ep.Pet.5.4, Sm.4 Ki.3.4, PLips.97 xi 4

ἀρχιπολιαρχέω.definition: Thess. to be president of board of magistrates, IG9.1233

ἀρχιπροστάτης.definition: chief official of a synagogue, Arch.Pap.2.430

ἀρχιπροφήτης.definition: chief prophet, Ph.1.594; chief of , PGen.7.5 , Ps.-Callisth.3.34:—hence PGen.36.5

ἀρχιπρύτανις.definition: chief president, OGI494.3 , PTeb.397.8 , Inscr.Prien.246.20, etc.:—hence BCH11.70

ἀρχιραβδοῦχος.definition: chief lictor, Gloss.:— fem. leader of wand-bearers, in cult of Cybele, IGRom.1.614

ἀρχιστολιστής.definition: keeper of the sacred vestments, OGI111.18 , Sammelb. 4011

ἀρχισυνάγωγος.definition: ruler of a synagogue; master of a guild or company, IGRom.1.782 , etc

ἀρχισωματοφύλαξ.definition: chief of the body- guard, LXXEs.2.21, OGI99.1 , PTeb.79.52 , J.AJ12.2.5

ἀρχιτεκτονέω.definition: to be architecl, chief constructor, or; generally, contrive, Ar.Pax305, Fr.195; supervise, direct, Phld.Acad.Ind.p.15M

ἀρχιτέκτων.definition: chief-artificer, master-builder; generally, author, contriver, E.Cyc.477; Alex.149.2; D.56.11; Arist.EN1152b2; those that direct activities by thought, Id.Pol.1325b23

ἀρχιτρίκλινος.definition: president of a banquet; head-waiter, Hld.7.27

ἀρχιυπηρέτης.definition: chief minister, IG 14.914 , BGU21 iii 9 :—also Sammelb.599.61, Ostr.1538

ἀρχιφρουρέω.definition: command a IG9.1059 : also in form ib.1058

ἀρχιφυλακίτης.definition: commandant of , PRev.Laws37.5 , PHib.1.73, PTeb.5.142 :—hence office of ib.27.22 , and hold such office, PAlex.9.4 )

ἀρχοειδής.definition: of the nature of a principle, Arist.Metaph.999a2, APo.86b38, Plu.2.1085c, Theol.Ar.8, al.: Comp., Alex.Aphr.Febr.21, Simp.in Ph.7.21: Sup., Alex.Aphr.Febr.7, Dam.Pr.52ter. Adv. Procl.Inst.65, Syrian.in Metaph.3.23

ἀρχοντιάω.definition: wish to be ruler, Sch.Ar.V.342, Lyd.Mag.1.28

ἀρχωνέω.definition: to be an PRev.Laws 14.3, al., BCH1.410

ἀρχώνης.definition: chief contractor or farmer of revenue, And.1.133 , PRev.Laws 10.10, al., CIG 3912; = promagister portorii, Ephes.2 No.29; promagister quadragesimae . . , OGI525.5

ἀρωματίζω.definition: spice, Dsc.1.66:—Pass; intr., have a spicy flavour or scent, D.S.2.49, Str.16.2.41, Plu.2.623e

ἀρωματοφόρος.definition: spice-bearing, Str.1.2.32; Subst. servant in charge of spices, J.AJ17.8.3

ἀσάφεια.definition: want of clearness, uncertainty, obscurity, opp. Pl.R.478c, cf. Plu.Sol.19, Arr.Tact.1.3; personified, Emp.122.4:—later Plb.1.67.11; Ion. Hp.Praec.14

ἀσέβεια.definition: ungodliness, impiety, opp. X.Cyr.8.8.7; Antipho5.88, cf. Pl.R.615c, etc.; also LXX2 Ki.22.22; E.Ba.476; Lys.6.11; Pl.Euthphr.5c: at Rome, disloyalty to the Emperor , D.C.57.9; of Christianity, Id.68.1: in pl., Pl.Lg.890a

ἀσεβέω.definition: to be impious, act profanely, commit; c. acc. pers., sin against, A.Eu.271 ; D.S.1.77, Plu.2.291c; IG7.2418 ; POxy.1612.23 :—Pass., Lys.2.7; D.C.57.9; of households, to be affected with the consequences of sin, Pl.Lg.…

ἀσέβημα.definition: impious or profane act, sacrilege, opp. Antipho2.1.3, Th.6.27, D.21.104; Id.16.130

ἀσεβής.definition: ungodly, unholy, profane, sacrilegious, opp. Pi.Fr.132.1, A.Supp.9 ; of Oedipus, S.OT1382,1441; X.Mem.1.1.16: c. gen., against them, Paus.4.8.1; X.Cyr.8.8.27; J.BJ5.10.5. Adv. Sup. D.C.79.9

ἀσελγαίνω.definition: impf. D.21.31: fut. Id.24.143: aor. inf. D.C.52.31:—Pass., pf. : plpf. J.AJ17.5.6:—to be behave licentiously, And.4.7, Pl.Smp.190c; D.54.5:—Pass., of acts, outrageous acts, Id.21.19

ἀσέλγημα.definition: licentious act, prob. in Plb.38.2.2, cf. Plu.in Hes.64, Suid. s.v. vulgar abuse, in pl., POxy.903.21

ἀσήμαντος.definition: without leader or shepherd; unsealed, unmarked, Hdt.2.38, Pl.Lg.954a, Hyp.Fr.4; = Hsch

ἀσθένεια.definition: want of strength, weakness, Th.1.3, etc; disease, sickness, Id.2.49 , OGI244.11 , etc.; Ep.Gal.4.13

ἀσθενέω.definition: to be weak, feeble, sickly, to be; to be needy, Ar.Pax636; of those unable to pay taxes, PTeb.188

Ἀσιαγενής.definition: of Asiatic descent, D.S.17.77; = Asiaticus, cognomen of Scipio, Id.35.33: Ion. Opp.C.1.235

Ἀσιάρχης.definition: an Asiarch, priest of the Imperial cult in the province of Asia, Str.14.1.42, Act.Ap.19.31, IG12.531, 14.2405, etc.; OGI525.8 :—hence BMus.Inscr.481*.240 , etc

ἀσιλλοφορέω.definition: carry a yoke, Democr.132, prob. in EM160.34

ἀσκαρδαμύκτης.definition: one who does not blink, Hp.Epid.2.6.1

ἀσκαρδάμυκτος.definition: not blinking or winking, Ar.Eq.292, Adam.1.21. Adv. Eust.756.59, v.l. in Ar.l.c

ἀσκαρίζω.definition: fut. Att. form of , Hp.Nat. Puer.30, Cratin.26

ἀσκητέος.definition: to be practised, X.Cyr.5.3.43; one must practise, Pl.Grg.487c, 507d; Arist.Pol.1325a13

ἀσκωλιάζω.definition: hop on greased wineskins at the; hop on one leg, Arist.IA705b33, cf. Ael.NA3.13, Plu.2.621f, Gal.11.106; also, jump up and down with legs held together, Sch.Orib.3p.689D

ᾀσματοκάμπτης.definition: twister of song, of Trag. and Dithyrambic poets, Ar.Nu.333:—hence Tz. in An.Ox.3.339

ἀσμενίζω.definition: take or receive gladly, Plb.6.8.3; Plot.5.8.12; Them.Or.33.364d, 8.107b; Porph.Chr.27: intr., to be satisfied with a thing, Plb.3.97.5; Muson.Fr.6p.27H., cf. Agathin. ap. Orib.10.7.10, Ph.2.37, etc.; . . Plb.4.11.5: c…

ἀσμενισμός.definition: gratification, Ph.1.450; a form of Stoic.3.97

ἀσπαλιεύομαι.definition: angle, Suid.:—Act., fut. metaph. of a lover, Aristaen.1.17; AB183, may be f.l. for

ἀσπερμί.definition: or without the right to a loan of seed, PTeb.61.307, 67.97, PAmh.2.90.6, etc

ἀσπιδηφόρος.definition: shield-bearing, of warriors, Id.Th.19; E.Supp.390: Subst., Id.Ba.781

ἀσπιδίσκος.definition: Dim. of boss, Sch.Il.5.743; wide end of a clyster-pipe, Cael.Aur.TP4.3:—also boss, disk, Jahresh. 16 Beibl.51 , SIG2588.31 , Ausonia 10.171 , LXXEx.36.26 ; small shield, Ascl.Tact.1.2, HeroDioptr.5, etc.; name of a co…

ἀσπιδίσκιον.definition: IG2.733 Aii 7, Dsc.3.91, Gal.14.724; and Lyd.Mag.1.11

ἀσπιδόδηκτος.definition: bitten by an adder or asp, Dsc.2.34, Vett.Val.127.20, Gal.14.300

ἀσπιδοειδής.definition: shaped like a shield, Agatharch.105; adorned with serpents, OGI90.44

ἀσπιδοποιΐα.definition: the making of the shield, Gramm. name for Il.18, Hermog.Prog.2, Eust.1154.41

ἀσπιδότροφος.definition: feeding on adders or asps, Gal.11.143

ἀσπιδοφέρμων.definition: gen. living by the shield, i.e. by war, E.Ph.796

ἀσπίζω.definition: shield, protect, IGRom.4.1349 : pf. part. Hsch., Suid

ἀσπίλωτος.definition: = foreg. I, Sext.Sent.449, Suid.; without spots, Dsc.2.167

ἀσπορέω.definition: to be unsown, of land, PTeb.61b34 , etc.; written for Wilcken Chr.11A8

ἀσπούδαστος.definition: not zealously pursued or courted; not to be sought for, mischievous, E.Ba.913, IT202

ἀστάθμητος.definition: unsteady, unstable, = X.Mem.4.7.5; of persons, D.19.136, cf. Ar.Av.169, Pl.Ly.214d; of life, E.Or.981 ; the uncertainty of . . , Th.4.62; Id.3.59; Ph.2.85. Adv. D.Chr.4.122

ἀστεΐζομαι.definition: write or talk wittily or eloquently, Str.13.4.11, J.Ap.2.9, Demetr.Eloc.149, Plu.Marc.21; talk speciously, Ph.2.123:—Act. in St.Byz. s.v

ἀστεϊσμός.definition: wit, D.H.Dem.54, Demetr.Eloc.128 , 130, Phld.Rh.1.181 S.: pl., forms of wit, Longin.34.2, Philostr.VS1.25.9; esp. of ironical self-depreciation, mock-modesty, Phld.Acad.Ind.p.52M., Alex.Fig.1.18, TryphoTrop.24; = Hdn.…

ἀστεργής.definition: without love, implacable, S.Aj.776; repellent, Hp.Gland.16; unyielding, Id.Fract.16 , cf. Ruf. ap. Orib.49.28.3

ἀστεριαῖος.definition: like a star, Cleom.1.11; decorated with stars, prob.in PHamb.10.44

ἀστερισμός.definition: marking with stars, Ptol.Geog.1.22.4; = Herm. ap. Stob.1.49.44

ἀστερίτης.definition: name of a mythical precious stone, Ptol.Heph. ap. Phot.p.153B., Ps.-Democr.Alch.p.50B

ἀστεροδίνητος.definition: brought by the revolution of the stars, Procl.H.1.49

ἀστερομαρμαρυγή.definition: the brightness of the stars, v.l. in Sch.Arat.328

ἀστεροπητής.definition: lightener, of Zeus, Il.1.580, Hes.Th.390, S.Ph.1198

ἀστεροπληθής.definition: full of stars, Orac. ap. Eus.PE5.8

ἀστεροσκοπέω.definition: watch the stars, S.E.M.5.68:—hence Subst. ib.80

ἀστερόω.definition: turn into stars, Placit.2.13.3:—Pass., to be marked by stars, opp. Sch.Arat.273

ἄστομος.definition: speechless, S.Fr.76, Arr.Epict.2.24.26; with no mouth, Str.2.1.9, cf. Plu.2.938c, 940b

ἀστόμωτος.definition: with no orifice, Sor.1.57, Orib.45.3.8; unsharpened, untempered, of metal, Hsch. s.v

ἀστοργία.definition: want of natural affection, AntiphoFr.73, Men.522, D.H.3.18

ἀστοχέω.definition: miss the mark, miss, IG 9.517.28 ; Plb.5.107.2, al., Phld.Rh.1.219S.; Plu.2.414f; Luc.Am.22; fail, Plb.3.21.10; 1 Ep.Ti.6.21, 2.2.18; J.BJ2.8.12: abs.,Alciphr.3.53.—Rare in poetry, Lyr.Alex.Adesp.4.21

ἄστοχος.definition: missing the mark, aiming badly at; abs., aiming amiss, random, Arist.HA587a9; aimless, absurd, Plb.5.49.4; of a person, Phld.Ind.Sto.32. Adv. amiss, Alex.116.14, Plb.1.74.2, Phld.Mort.33

ἀστράβηλος.definition: = , a kind of shell, Agias I, Dercyl.1

ἀστραβής.definition: = not twisted, straight, steadfast, Pi.O.2.90; Hp.Art.31; Pl.Ti.73b; Arist.Pol.1336a12; IG7.3073.104 ; of timber, Thphr.HP3.9.2: Comp., ib.5.1.11: Sup., ib.5.3.5; rigid, stiff, Aret.SA1.6. Adv. Ael.NA2.11

ἀστραγάλειος.definition: covering the ankles, = Lat. talaris, Aq.Ge.37.3

ἀστραγαλίζω.definition: play with Pl.Ly.206e, Alc.1.110b; Cratin.165, cf. Telecl.1.14

ἀστραγαλίσκος.definition: Dim. of Roussel Cultes Égyptiens 218 , Poll.6.99; name of a surgical appliance, PMed.Lond.2.14

ἀστραγαλιστής.definition: dice-player; in pl., name of a comedy by Alex.Aet., Sch.Il.23.86

ἀστραπαῖος.definition: of lightning, a wind with thunderstorms, Arist.Mete.364b30, cf. Thphr.Sign.37; thunder-showers, Plu.2.664c; Arist.Mu.401a16, Corn.ND9, IGRom.3.17

ἀστραπή.definition: light of a lamp, A.Fr.386, Ev.Luc.11.36; metaph., flashing of the eyes, S.Fr.474; Ar.Ach.566; Antiph.195.4, cf. Ach.Tat.6.6

ἀστραπόπληκτος.definition: lightning-stricken, v.l. for in Seneca QN1.15

ἀστρατήγητος.definition: never having been general; incapable of command, no general, Cic.Att.7.13.1, cf. 8.16.1 , Onas.33.5. Adv. App.BC1.47, cf. Hierocl.p.17A

ἀστρατηγία.definition: lack of a general, Phryn.PSp.42 B

ἀστροβολέομαι.definition: Pass., to be sun-scorched, Thphr.HP4.14.2, etc.:—Act. in Porph.Plot.10

ἀστροβρόντης.definition: thundering from the stars, epith. of Mithras, IG14.998

ἀστροειδής.definition: starlike, starry, Ph.1.485 , Hierocl.in CA27p.483M.; like that of the stars, Str.3.5.8

ἀστροθέτημα.definition: a group of stars, constellation, Suid. s.v

ἀστρολάβος.definition: armillary sphere, Ptol.Alm.9.2, al; planisphere, Phlp.in Rh.Mus.6.127

ἀστρολογέω.definition: study or practise astronomy, Thphr.Sign.4, Sosip.1.15, Plb.9.20.5; Cleom.2.1

ἀστρολόγος.definition: astronomer, X.Mem.4.2.10, Epigr. ap; later, astrologer, Epicur.Ep.2p.40U., LXXIs.47.13, SIG771.2 , S.E.M.5.2, etc

ἀστρονομέω.definition: study astronomy, Ar.Nu.194, Pl.Tht.174a:—Med., D.L.1.34, Iamb.VP25.112:—Pass., as astronomy is now practised, Pl.R.530c

ἀστρονομία.definition: astronomy, Hp.Aër.2, Ar.Nu.201, Pl.Smp.188b, etc.; title of a work ascribed to Hesiod, and Ptolemy's Olymp.in Mete.68.20, al

ἀστυάναξ.definition: lord of the city, epith. of; by an obscene pun, = Eust.849.54

ἀστυβοώτης.definition: crying or calling through the city, epith. of a herald, Il.24.701

ἀστυγείτων.definition: gen. near or bordering on a; as Subst., neighbour to the city, borderer, Hdt.2.104, 5.66, Th.1.15, X.HG1.3.2, SIG633.10 , etc

ἀστυδρομέομαι.definition: Pass., filled with the turmoil of pursuers and pursued, A.Th.221

ἀστυνομέω.definition: to be an D.Prooem.55, OGI483.1; at Rome, to be praetor urbanus, D.C.42.22

ἀστυνόμος.definition: protecting the city; as Subst., a magistrate who had the care of the police, streets, and public buildings at Athens, Is.1.15, D.24.112, Arist.Ath.50.1, SIG313.17, Com.Adesp.25a D.: in other cities, as Tenos, IG 12.88…

ἀσυγγνώμων.definition: gen. not pardoning, merciless, D.21.100, Plu.2.59e: irreg. Sup. Phint. ap. Stob.4.23.61

ἀσύγγνωστος.definition: = foreg., Jul.Ep.184; unpardonable, Gal.1.13, Phalar.Ep.6, Him.Ecl.5.10, Lib.Or.59.144. Adv. Phld.Mort.20

ἀσυγκατάθετος.definition: withholding assent, Chrysipp.Stoic.2.40; Ph.1.287, cf. Aristocl. ap. Eus.PE14.18. Adv. Chrysipp.Stoic.3.42, Ph.1.78

ἀσυλλογιστία.definition: inconclusiveness, faultiness of logic, Ps.-Alex.Aphr.in SE135.31

ἀσυλλόγιστος.definition: non-syllogistic, formally or; unattainable by reasoning, incalculable, Men.355.1, J.AJ4.7.1, al., Plu.2.24b,580d

ἀσύμβολος.definition: without contribution; of the dinner, to which no one brings anything, Alex.257.2, Amphis39; Timocl.8.10: metaph., unsocial, solitary, Plu.2.957a

ἀσύμμετρος.definition: Att. incommensurable; disproportionate, X.Cyn.2.7; disproportionate to it, Arist.IA708a15; ill- proportioned, Id.Po.1461a13; of excessive length, Demetr.Lac.Herc. 1014.67F.; Phld.Mort.9. Adv. ib.8, Attic. ap. Eus.PE15.7

ἀσυμμνημόνευτος.definition: not remembered in connexion, Dsc.1 Praef.3

ἀσυμφανής.definition: dark, Arist.Mir.836b19; obscure, Porph.in Ptol.181: Sup., Dam.Pr.38. Adv. obscurely, Arg.4Ar.Ra., Suid

ἀσύμφορος.definition: Att. inconvenient, prejudicial, Hes.Op.782, cf. Hp.Acut.56, Antipho2.1.10, Th.3.40; Id.1.32; Id.2.91: Sup., E.Tr.491; D.19.2. Adv. X.HG6.3.1; Arist.Pol.1308b21

ἀσύμφυλος.definition: not akin, unlike, Dsc.1 Praef.3, J.AJ11.6.5, Luc.Hist.Conscr.11; incompatible, unsuitable, Plu.2.709b, etc. Adv. Sch.Il.9.643

ἀσύμφυτος.definition: not growing together or uniting, Hp.de Arte10; not able to unite, Aret.CA1.7, Gal.10.336: generally, detached, PLond.1207.6

ἀσυμφωνία.definition: want of harmony, discord, Pl.Lg.861a, Ph.1.5; incoherence, Carneisc.Herc.1027.10

ἀσύμφωνος.definition: Att. not harmonious; metaph., discordant, at variance, Pl.Grg.482c; Ocell.4.13; Act.Ap.28.25, Arr.An.Prooem. . Adv. Pl.Lg.860c; Arg.Str.I

ἀσυναίρετος.definition: Medic., not contracted or shortened; Gramm., uncontracted, Eust.50.36. Adv. Id.16.32

ἀσύνακτος.definition: incompatible, incoherent, illogical, Phld.Sign.14, Epict.Ench.44, S.E.P.2.137

ἀσυνάλειπτος.definition: without synaloephe, Hdn.Gr.2.912. Adv. Eust.19.39, Sch.Ven.Il.3.150

ἀσυναλλαξία.definition: lack of intercourse, SIG 684.14 , cf. Stob.2.7.25

ἀσυνάντητος.definition: not to be met, unsocial, Hsch. s.v

ἀσυνάρτητος.definition: disconnected, incoherent, D.H.Th.6; in Metric, verses compounded of independent Heph.15, Sch.Ar.Ra.1316, etc

ἀσύνδετος.definition: unconnected, loose, X.Cyn.5.30; of language, without conjunctions, Arist.Int.17a17; of style, Id.Rh.1413b29 ; in Rhet., style without conjunctions, Demetr.Eloc.268, cf. 192; Hermog.Id.2.1, al. Adv. Philostr.VS1.16.4, …

ἀσυνείδητος.definition: not privy to a thing, Onos.4.2. Adv. Plu.2.214e, cf. POxy.123.16

ἀσυνείκαστος.definition: not to be guessed, unintelligible, Sch.S.Tr.694

ἀσυνέλευστος.definition: non-coagulating, Diog.Oen.20: Gramm., not forming a compound, A.D.Pron.45.24; not entering into composition, Id.Synt.304.9

ἀσυνέμπτωτος.definition: not coinciding in form, Eust.879.30; not denoting coincidence in time, A.D.Synt.210.14

ἀσυνέξωστος.definition: not to be dislodged, of an athlete, IG14.1102, CPHerm.7 ii 3

ἀσυνετέω.definition: to be without understanding, Hp.Fract.25, cf. LXXPs.118.158, Hsch. s.v. fail to understand, Alc.18

ἀσυνήθεια.definition: unfamiliarity, Arist.Metaph.995a2, Thphr.HP9.17.2; inexperience in . . , Arist.Rh.1368a21, cf. Plb.15.32.7

ἀσύνθετος.definition: uncompounded, Pl.Phd.78c; bound by no covenant, faithless, D.19.136 , cf. Ep.Rom.1.31; making no covenants, Phld.Herc.1251.19

ἀσύνθηκος.definition: = II, Onos.37.2. Adv. through breach of contract, POxy.904.2

ἀσυννεφής.definition: unclouded, Sch.Pi.O.1.16; not bringing clouds, Thphr.Vent.11

ἀσύνοπτος.definition: not easily perceived, opp. Aeschin.2.146, J.BJ7.6.1, Secund.Sent.1,15

ἀσύντακτος.definition: Att. disorganized; undisciplined, disorderly, X.Cyr.7.5.21, D.13.15; Ph.2.120; Aen.Tact.3.1; Th.6.72; Nicostr.Com.19.5. Adv. Plu.Nic.3

ἀσύντατος.definition: v.l. for in Xenarch.1; without exertion, Antyll. ap. Orib.6.21.8

ἀσυντέλεστος.definition: incomplete, IPE12.32B57 , D.S.4.12, Plu.2.1056d, POxy.707.30 ; not executed, Annuario 4/5.225

ἀσύντριπτος.definition: not easily rubbed or crushed, Ph.Bel.60.47

ἀσυνύπαρκτος.definition: incapable of coexisting, A.D.Conj.221.8, Alex.Aphr.Quaest.97.28, S.E.P.2.202, Simp.in Cat.381.13

ἀσυστατέω.definition: to be incapable of, c. gen., A.D.Conj.228.14

ἀσφάλεια.definition: assurance from danger, personal safety, A.Supp.495, etc.; Antipho2.2.8; precaution regarding it, And.3.33, cf. Th.4.68, 8.4; opp. Lys.31.7; safe-conduct, Hdt.3.7; X.HG2.2.2, Cyr.4.5.28: freq. with Preps., Hdt.4.33; Ar…

Ἀσφάλειος.definition: epith. of Poseidon, the Securer, Ar.Ach.682, Paus.3.11.9, 7.21.7, Plu.Thes.36

ἀσφαλής.definition: not liable to fall; of friends and the like , unfailing, trusty, . . Id.Aj.1251; E.Ph.599, cf. Th.1.69: c. inf., the hasty in counsel are not safe, S.OT617, cf. Pl.Sph.231a; E.IT1062; of things, sure, certain, Th.4.10…

ἀσφαλίζω.definition: Plb.18.30.3:—mostly in Med., fut; secure, BGU829.9

ἀσφαλτωδεύομαι.definition: to be soaked in pitch, Aët.2.73

ἀσχημονέω.definition: behave unseemly, disgrace oneself, E.Hec.407, Cratin.151, Pl.R.506d, etc.: c. acc. cogn., . . D.22.53; Id.60.25; Arist.Pol.1273a34, cf. EN1119a30: c. part., Plu.2.178d:—Pass., many unseemly things are done, D.H.2.26

ἄσχημος.definition: late form for Phld.Herc.1457.9 , PRyl.144.18 , Polem.Phgn.13, Hippiatr.55: Sup. D.L.2.88. Adv. Sch.S.Aj.916

ἀσχημοσύνη.definition: ungracefulness, Pl.Smp.196a, R.401a; awkwardness, Id.Tht.174c; disfigurement, in playing on the flute, Arist.Pol.1341b5

ἀσχολία.definition: occupation, business, engagement; want of time or leisure, to have no leisure, for pursuing it, Pl.Phd.66d; to be engaged or occupied, Id.Ap.39e; Plu.Comp. Sol.Publ.2; opp. Arist.Pol.1333a35; Pl.Tht.172d; cause one tr…

ἀσωτεῖον.definition: abode of a prodigal, Stratt.51, Longus4.17

ἀτάκτημα.definition: disorderly or contumacious act, irregularity, Stoic.3.136, OGI 483.58 , Vett.Val.116.13

ἀτάομαι.definition: Pass., suffer, be in distress, in; as law-term, the injured party, Leg.Gort.4.29; but the loser in a suit, ib.10.21; suffers a penalty, IG 5.1155 :—Act., aor. subj. 3 sg. dub. in Leg.Gort.6.23,43

ἀταρακτοποιησία.definition: Ion. acting with perfect composure, dub. in Hp.Decent.12

ἀτάρακτος.definition: not disturbed, uniform; not disturbed, without confusion, steady, of soldiers, X.Cyr.2.1.31: generally, quiet, Id.Eq.7.10 . Adv. Sup. Id.Eq.Mag.2.1

ἀταραξία.definition: Ion. impassiveness, calmness, Democr. ap. Stob.2.7.3i, Hp.Ep.12, Epicur.Ep.1p.30U., Phld.Oec.p.63 J., Cic.Fam.15.19.2, HeroBel.71.2, Plu.2.101b, Plot.1.4.1, etc.; prob. f.l. for in Hp.Praec.14

ἀτάραχος.definition: = Arist.EN1117a31, cf. 1125b34, Epicur.Sent.Vat.79, Str.1.3.21, Onos.2.2, etc.; an eyesalve, Gal.12.786; of a will, unchallengeable PMasp.151.142 . Adv. unconfusedly, Epicur.Ep.1p.14U.; calmly, HeroBel.72.4, Phld.Herc…

ἀτεκνέω.definition: have no children, v.l. in Hp.Steril.217, cf. LXXCa.4.2, Ho.9.12

ἀτελείωτος.definition: unfinished, incomplete, Arist.Fr.70, Sor.1.33: neut. pl. as Adv., Sch.Nic.Th.456

ἀτελεσιούργητος.definition: not brought to an issue, Theol.Ar.55

ἀτέλεστος.definition: without end, issue, or effect; uninitiated in. . , c. gen., E.Ba.40: metaph., Plu.Flam.2: abs., Pl.Phd.69c, cf. Arist.Rh.1419a4, Phld.Acad.Ind.p.4 M.; Ael.VH3.9; prob. unmarried, Tab. Defix.Aud.68a

ἀτελεύτητος.definition: not brought to an end or issue; without an end, interminable, Parm.8.32, Arist.Ph.204a5, Cael.273a5; everlasting, Ocell.1.2, cf. Plu.2.114f, etc

ἀτερπής.definition: unpleasing, joyless, Il.19.354; of the nether world, Od.11.94, etc.; . . of a rocky shore, 7.279; A.Supp.685 , cf.Pr.31, Simon.37.6; E.El.293; Mosch.4.114; less attractive to the ear, Th.1.22; opp. Phld.Po.994.23, cf.…

ἄτευκτος.definition: not gaining or obtaining, Max.Tyr.11.8, Hsch

ἀτεχνέω.definition: to be to be unskilful, Sch.Ar.Nu.296

ἀτεχνής.definition: = S.E.M.7.395, interpol. in Babr.75.4: Comp. v.l. in Hp.Fract.16

ἀτεχνία.definition: want of art or skill, Hp.Lex4, Pl.Phd.90d, al., Arist.EN1140a21, Chrysipp.Stoic.2.269: pl., Simp. in Stoic.3.49

ἀτεχνίτευτος.definition: artless, simple, D.H.Lys.8:—hence Verb Hsch. s.v

ἄτεχνος.definition: without art, unskilful, Pl.Plt.274c; esp. ignorant of the rules or principles of art, opp. or unskilled, unprofessional, of persons, Id.Sph.219a, Gal.6.134, S.E.P.3.262; having no trade or profession, PFlor.4.14 ; uns…

ἀτημελέω.definition: take no heed of, neglect, pf. part. Pass. f.l. in Procop.Vand.1.21 , cf. Sch.A.R.1.609

ἀτημελής.definition: neglected, Plu.Ant.18; of persons, careless, neglectful, E.Fr.184. Adv. Plu.Agis17; A.R.1.812

ἀτημέλητος.definition: unheeded, unnoticed, X.Cyr.5.4.18; slovenly, Alciphr.3.55; Jul.Mis.365d

ἀτιθάσευτος.definition: untamable, wild, Agatharch.74, Aesop.342, Plu.Art.25, 2.728a; App.BC4.8; Agath.4.21

ἀτίθασος.definition: = foreg., dub. in Hdn.5.6.9; Ph.1.20, al

ἀτιμαγελέω.definition: forsake the herd, stray, Arist.HA572b19, 611a2, Theoc.9.5: metaph., try to escape, Luc.Lex.10

ἀτιμαγέλης.definition: Dor. despising the herd, i. e. straying, feeding alone, S.Fr.1026, Theoc.25.132, AP6.255

ἀτιμαλφέω.definition: fail to fetch a price, Hsch

ἀτίμητος.definition: unhonoured, despised; not valued or estimated, Is.3.35: esp. a cause in which the penalty is not assessed in court, but fixed by law beforehand, D.21.90, Aeschin.3.210; opp. , D.27.67, cf. Poll.8.54,63, Harp. s.v.; Su…

ἀτιμώρητος.definition: unpunished, to escape punishment, Hdt.2.100, Th.6.6, etc.; unpunished for . . , Pl.Lg.959c. Adv. with impunity, ib.762d

ἄτοκος.definition: having never yet brought forth, Hdt.5.41; not bearing interest, Pl.Lg.921c, cf.D.53.12, SIG330.7 , etc.: neut. pl.as Adv., PAmh. 2.50.10 ,al

ἀτολμέω.definition: to be be disheartened, Hp.Epid.6.7.3: c.inf., lack courage to . . , D.C.78.34:—also AB 407

ἀτόλμητος.definition: Dor. = not to be; not to be dared, Aristid.Or.45.2, cf. Gal.8.260; Him.Ecl.4.24

ἄτολμος.definition: daring nothing, cowardly, Pi.N.11.32, Th.2.39 , etc.; . . Ar.Nu.458; D.8.68, etc.; of women, A.Ch.630 ; of things, Jul.Or.2.75d: c. inf., . . I have not the heart to bind, A.Pr.14. Adv. Plb.3.103.3, Plu.2.47c: Comp. l…

ἀτόπημα.definition: strange sight or occurrence, POxy.1557.6 , al; offence, PTeb.303.11 , Procop.Pers.1.24

ἀτοπηματοποιός.definition: one who commits absurdities or offences, Gloss

ἀτραγῴδητος.definition: not treated tragically, Luc.Merc.Cond.19; absence of display or pomp, Ph.2.76

ἀτραπιτός.definition: = sq., Od.13.195, A.R.4.123, etc.: metaph. of studies, BCH36.230 , cf. AP9.540:—also Od.17.234: AB460

ἀτρεμέω.definition: Plu.Pomp.58, App.Syr.2, etc.: aor. v.l. in Hdt. , Hp.Morb.Sacr.14:—not to tremble, to keep still or quiet, Hes.Op.539; of a restless people, , etc.; of a state of health, remain stationary, Hp.Aph.1.3; Aret.SD1.15; of…

ἀτρεμίζω.definition: fut. aor. Hp.Morb.Sacr.7:—keep quiet, Thgn.303: in Ion. Prose, mostly with neg., . . never being kept still, Hdt.9.74; of restless, aggressive kings or nations, Id.1.185, 190; of people attacked, . . without a neg., I…

ἀτριβής.definition: not rubbed: hence; of places, not traversed, pathless, Th.4.8,29, Ph.2.257, al.; of roads, not worn or used, X.An.4.2.8, App.Hisp.62: generally, fresh, new, X.Mem.4.3.13, cf. Cyr.8.7.22

ἄτρομος.definition: fearless, Il.16.163; . . 5.126, 17.157; Orph.Fr.168.23; Aret.CA1.2; calm, undisturbed, AP6.69 . Adv. Plu.2.474d, 475f

ἄτροπος.definition: not to be turned, unchangeable, eternal; inflexible, rigid, AP7.483; ib.10.74 : pr. n., name of one of the Hes.Th.905, al., Pl.Lg.960c, Chrysipp.Stoic.2.264; IG3.1337: hence of the decrees of fate, Epigr.Gr.153.4; ib.288

ἀτροφέω.definition: have or get no food, Ael.NA10.21, etc.; waste away, Arist.Mu.395b28, Plu.Arat.24; of trees, Thphr.CP5.9.9, cf. Plu.Rom.20; of fire, have no fuel, Ph.2.620

ἀτταγᾶς.definition: francolin, Tetrao orientalis, Alex.Mynd. ap. Ath.9.387f; Ar.Av.247, 761; a delicacy, Hippon.36.1, Ar.Ach.875, Fr.433: prov., Id.V.257

ἀτταγηνάριον.definition: Dim. of foreg., Gramm. in GaisfordChoeroboscus1 p.43

Ἀττικίζω.definition: side with the Athenians, Th.3.62; speak Attic, Eup.8.3 D., Pl.Com.168.1; opp. Posidipp.28

Ἀττικισμός.definition: siding with Athens, loyalty to her; = foreg., Alciphr.2.4: pl., ibid., cf. Cic.Att.4.19.1

Ἀττικιστής.definition: one who affects or collects Attic expressions, Iamb.VP18.80, EM527.54, etc.; title of work by Moeris

ἀτύμβευτος.definition: without tomb, AP9.439 ; contemptuous neglect of burial, Onos.36.2; burial but not in a tomb, Opp.H.5.346

ἄτυφος.definition: not puffed up, Pl.Phdr.230a, Timo9.1; esp. of the Stoic sage, Cleanth.Stoic.1.127: Comp., Plu.Alex.45: Sup., D.L.4.37. Adv. Plu.2.32d, M.Ant.1.16.4: Comp. Hierocl.in CA19p.461M.: Sup. Ael.Fr.137:—also dub. in IG14.2094

ἀτυχέω.definition: fut. Ar.Nu.427, Eup.114: aor; c. gen.,fail of a thing, fail in getting it, Pl.Tht.186c; X.HG3.1.22: c. part., Th.2.62, cf. Men.Epit.470: c. inf., Vett. Val.358.30: c. acc., Eun.VSp.469B

ἀτύχημα.definition: misfortune, miscarriage; fault of ignorance, mistake, D.23.70; opp. Gorg.11, Arist.Rh.1374b6, EN1135b12: euphem., crime, Is.10.20, cf.Plb.12.14.2

ἀτυχία.definition: ill-luck, Amphis3; = miscarriage, mishap, Hp.Fract.25, Antipho2.2.13, X.Mem.3.9.8 , Men.674; defeat in war, Aeschin.3.55

Αὐγώ.definition: Daybeam, name of a dog, X.Cyn.7.3

αὐδάζομαι.definition: Dep., cry out, speak; name, Opp.H.1.127:—Act., fut. Lyc.892: aor. Id.360, dub. l. in AP6.218 :—Pass., aor. Orph.H.27.9

αὐθαδιάζομαι.definition: or late form for sq., J.BJ5.3.4, Polem.Call.24, S.E.P.1.237, Procop.Arc.14,15, Lib.Decl.15.47

αὐθαδίζομαι.definition: aor. Them.Or.34 p.467 D.:—to be self-willed, Pl.Ap.34d; to be puffed up, arrogant, Them.Or.29.346b

αὐθαίρετος.definition: self-chosen, self-elected; by free choice, of one-self, E.Supp.931; 2 Ep.Cor.8.17; independent, free, Th.1.78; Arist.EN1114b6

αὐθεντέω.definition: to have full power or authority over; commit a murder, Sch.A.Eu.42

αὐθέντης.definition: murderer, Hdt.1.117; perpetrator, author, Plb.22.14.2; D.S.16.61: generally, doer, Alex.Rh.p.2S.; master, E.Supp.442; voc. PMag.Leid.W.6.46; condemned by Phryn.96

αὐθεντία.definition: absolute sway, authority, CIG2701.9; restriction, LXX3 Ma.2.29

αὐθημερίζω.definition: return on the same day, Poll.1.64

αὐθομολογέομαι.definition: confess of oneself, a thing that speaks for itself, Luc.Herm.59

αὐθόρμητος.definition: self-impelled, Eustr.in EN33.29, Eust.1148.13. Adv. Id.1370.23:—also Sch.E.Hec.1227

αὐθυπόστατος.definition: self-substantial, Jul.Or.4.139d, Iamb. ap. Stob.2.8.45, Procl.in Prm.p.610S. Phlp.in de An.52.19

αὐθυπότακτος.definition: the subjunctive aor.2, sts. also, aor.I, Hdn.Epim.278,AB1086. Adv. in the subjunctive of this tense, ibid

αὐθωρός.definition: in that very hour, of a spell, taking immediate effect, PMag.Lond.121.300. Adv. immediately, Hp.Mochl.2, Str.3.5.7, PFlor.186.10 , Eun.VSp.471 B., Agath.3.9:—also or LXXDa.3.15, 3 Ma.3.25, Cic.Att.2.13.1, Plu.2.512e

αὐλακίζω.definition: —Med., fut. PFlor.326.10 (ii A; Dim. of Sch.D.T.p.196H

αὐλέω.definition: Boeot. part. IG7.3211,3212 (Orchom; of persons, play to, Philostr.VA2.34, cf. A.D.Synt.302.1:—mostly in Pass., to be played to, hear music, X.An.6.1.11, Cyr.4.5.7, Arist.Pr.917b19 , Thphr.Char.19.10, 20.10

αὐλητής.definition: flute-player, Thgn.941, Hdt.1.141; kind of wasp, Hsch

αὐλητρίδιον.definition: Dim. of sq., Theopomp.Hist.205, Com.Adesp.25.34D., D.L.7.13

αὐλητρίς.definition: flute-girl, Simon.178, Ar.Ach.551, X.HG2.2.23, Pl.Prt.347d, BCH6.24 , etc

αὐλιστήριον.definition: stall, steading, Herm. ap. Stob.1.49.68, Aq.Is.10.29, Hsch. s.v

αὐλοποιϊκή.definition: = foreg., Pl.Euthd.289c:—also Asp.in EN15.24: hence Adv. Poll.7.153

αὐξάνω.definition: increase in power, strengthen, increase their power, Hdt.8.30; S.Ant.191, cf. X.Mem.3.7.2; exalt by one's deeds, glorify, Pi.O.5.4, P.8.38, cf. IG22.834, etc.; exalt by praise, extol, Pl.Ly.206a; . . honour thee as . …

Αὐξησία.definition: Ion. the goddess of growth, Hdt.5.82, IG5.363

αὔξησις.definition: growth, increase, Hp.VM6; amplification, in Rhet., Arist.Rh.1368a27, 1413b34; Plb.10.27.8, cf. D.H.Th.19

αὐξομείωσις.definition: rise and fall of the tide; waxing and waning of the moon, Ant. Diog.4 , Ptol.Alm.2.1 ; variation in period, Cat.Cod.Astr.1.163.13

ἀϋπνέω.definition: to be sleepless, Philostr.Gym.53:—Med., Phryn.PSp.9 B

αὐτάγγελος.definition: carrying one's own message, S.Ph.568; bringing news of what oneself has seen, Th.3.33: c.gen. rei, S.OC333; Plu.2.489e, cf. Arr.An.4.2.6, Max.Tyr.14.2, Nonn.D.8.222

αὔτανδρος.definition: together with the men, men and all, Plb.1.23.7, cf. Sosyl.p.31 B., A.R.3.582, Luc.Bacch.3, etc.; D.H.7.60: hence the people, every man of them, J.BJ3.7.31

αὐτανέψιος.definition: own cousin, A.Supp.984, E.Heracl.987, Pl.Euthd.275b: Adj. A.Supp.933:—fem. Lyc.811

αὐτάρκεια.definition: self-sufficiency, independence; concrete, a sufficiency, PFlor.242.8 ; a competence, Vett.Val.289.32

αὐταρχέω.definition: to be an absolute ruler, Pi.Pae.4.37, D.C.44.2

αὐτενέργεια.definition: self-moving energy, Eustr.in EN330.27: Phlp.in de An.35.1

αὐτενέργητος.definition: or spontaneous, Procl.in Prm.p.611S. , in Alc.p.18C. , Theol.Plat.6.22, Iamb.Myst.4.3

αὐτεξούσιος.definition: in one's own power, free, Chrysipp.Stoic.2.284, cf. Diogenian.Epicur.3.61, Plot.1.4.8, Iamb.Myst.3.14; of persons, Muson.Fr.12p.66H., Arr.Epict.4.1.62, PLips.29.6 ; of captives, freed unconditionally, D.S.14.105; abso…

αὐτεξουσιότης.definition: free will, v.l. in LXX4 Ma.2.21: Eustr.in EN390.11

αὐτεπάγγελτος.definition: offering of oneself, of one's free; self invited, dub. in Luc.JTr.37

αὐτεπίβουλος.definition: plotting against oneself, interpol. in Aesop.18; = Hsch

αὐτεπίσπαστος.definition: drawn on oneself, self-incurred, Hsch. s.v

αὐτεπιστατέω.definition: to be present oneself, and Subst. Sch.Theoc.7.6

αὐτεπώνυμος.definition: of the same surname with, E.Ph.769

αὐτήκοος.definition: one who has himself heard, ear-; hearing oneself, i.e. a law unto oneself, Ph.2.2, al., Suid.; so, self-acquired, Ph.1.371,354

αὐτοαπλότης.definition: simplicity itself, of a person, Anon. ap. Suid. s.v

αὐτοβοάω.definition: bear testimony of oneself, AB465, Suid

αὐτοβοήθητος.definition: self-supporting, of an argument, Simp.in Ph.354.29

αὐτοβούλησις.definition: the abstract will, v.l. in Arist.Top.147a8

αὐτογενής.definition: self-produced, v.l. in Herm. ap; = Ps.-Dsc.4.158; = ib.176

αὐτογνωμονέω.definition: act of one's own judgement, X.HG7.3.6

αὐτογνώμων.definition: gen. on one's own judgement, at one's own discretion, opp. Arist.Pol.1270b29, cf. 1272a39. Plu.Demetr.6: —hence Subst. Zonar

αὐτόγνωτος.definition: self-determined, self-willed, S.Ant.875:—also knowable in itself, Simp.in Ph.1250.14, Dam.Pr.80

αὐτόγραφος.definition: written with one's own hand, D.H.5.7, Plu.Sert.27; one's own writing, Id.2.1115c

αὐτοδάϊκτος.definition: self-slain, AP9.293 , Opp.H.2.349; mutually slain, A.Th.735

αὐτόδερμος.definition: skin, bark and all, Hsch. s.v

αὐτοδέσποτος.definition: at one's own will, free, Hierocl.Prov.ap. Phot.Bibl.p.172 B.; absolute master, LXX4 Ma.1.1

αὐτοδημιούργητος.definition: self-made, i.e. in the natural state, Hsch. s.v

αὐτοδίδακτος.definition: self-taught, Od.22.347; A.Ag.991 ; D.H.5.12; of instinct, Gal.8.445. Adv. instinctively, Id.19.175, cf. Alex.Aphr.Pr.1.14; without instruction, Phld. Rh.1.129S

αὐτοδιηγούμενος.definition: narrating in the first person, ibid

αὐτοδίκαιον.definition: abstract right, Aristid.2.182 J., Procl.in Prm.p.773 S., Dam.Pr.60

αὐτοδιπλάσιον.definition: the ideal double, its Form, Arist.Metaph.990b32

αὐτοδόξαστον.definition: the object of opinion in the abstract, Suid. s.v

αὐτόδρομος.definition: running or moving of itself, Hp.Hebd.2

αὐτοέκαστος.definition: = Arist.Top.162a27; the idea of each object, Id.EN1096a35, cf. Dam.Pr.427

αὐτοέκτατος.definition: long by nature, of syllables, Eust.943.59

αὐτοέντης.definition: in S., = a murderer, OT107, El.272: also in late Prose, D.C.58.15

αὐτοεπιθυμία.definition: the Form of desire, v.l. in Arist.Top.147a8

αὐτοετής.definition: in or of the same year, of trees, Thphr.HP3.7.1; J.AJ3.9.3. Adv. within the year, Od.3.322, D.C.36.37; Arist.HA562b12; at one year old, ib.545a24

αὐτοθάνατος.definition: dying by one's own hand, Plu.2.293e

αὐτόθηκτος.definition: self-sharpened, epith. of cold-forged iron, A.Fr.356

αὐτοκάβδαλος.definition: done carelessly, slovenly; buffoons, improvisers, Eup.2co, Semus20, Luc.Lex.10

αὐτοκέλευθος.definition: going one's own road, Tryph.314, AP9.362.5, Nonn.D.6.369: neut. pl. as Adv., ib.21.167

αὐτοκέλευστος.definition: self-bidden, i. e. unbidden, X.An.3.4.5, D.H.8.66, AP5.21 ; Ph.2.90, al. Adv. Aristeas92

αὐτοκίνησις.definition: self-motion, Syrian.in Metaph.45.26, etc.; Plot.6.2.18, cf. 6.6.6

αὐτοκίνητος.definition: self-moved, Arist.Ph.258a2, Plu.2.952e, etc.; Ph.1.36, cf. Procl.Inst.14, Dam.Pr.78; of live-stock, PMasp.122.3 , etc. Adv. Procl.Inst.195, Olymp.in Alc.p.61 C

αὐτόκλητος.definition: self-called, i.e. uncalled, unbidden, A.Eu.170 , S.Tr.392, Pl.Ep.331b; Phld.Ir.p.46 W.; natural allies , Hierocl.p.57 A.; Him.Ecl.5.14; personally invited, Plu.2.707f

αὐτόκρανος.definition: self-accomplishing, prob. in; Pass., self-accomplished, self-evident, Hsch.,EM173.34

αὐτοκρατής.definition: ruling by oneself, absolute, independent, Anaxag.12; Hp.Loc.Hom.46; E.Andr.482 ; Pl.Ti.91b; Dam.Pr.394; Plu.2.1026d. Adv. Lyd.Mag.1.33

αὐτοκρατορεύω.definition: to be or become Emperor, D.C.69.4, POxy.33 ii 9

αὐτοκρατορία.definition: sovereignty, of the Emperors, D.C.67.12; also reign of an Emperor, PFlor.56.13 , etc

αὐτοκρατορίς.definition: the residence of a sovereign, J.AJ18.2.1

αὐτοκράτωρ.definition: of persons or states, free, independent, Th.4.63, IG12 .189.44, etc.: of a youth that has come of age, X.Mem.2.1.21

αὐτόκτιτος.definition: self-produced, i.e. made by nature, natural, A.Pr.303; S.Fr.332

αὐτοκτόνος.definition: self-slaying, of Medea, who; slaying one another, Id.Th.810; mutual death by each other's hand, ib.681; AP7.152 . Adv. A.Th.734

αὐτολαλητής.definition: one who talks to himself, Timo50

αὐτολήκυθος.definition: one who carries his own oil-flask; flatterer, parasite, Luc.Lex.10, Plu.2.50c

αὐτόλυσις.definition: couple or leash for hounds, Hsch

αὐτομάθεια.definition: self-teaching or learning, Plu.2.973e:—also Aristid. Quint.2.9

αὐτομαθής.definition: having learnt of oneself, Ph.1.35, al., Plu.2.992a; self-taught, of persons, in a thing, AP6.218 ; of that which is learnt, Ph.1.164; spontaneous, Phld.Po.2.47. Adv. Philostr.VS1.15.2, Ph.1.62

αὐτοματισμός.definition: that which happens of itself, chance, Hp.Acut. 57, Alcid.Soph.25 , D.H.1.4, J.AJ10.11.7; Phleg.Mir.1

αὐτόματος.definition: Hom. and Att.; Hes.Op.103; of inanimate things, self-acting, spontaneous, of the gates of Olympus, Il.5.749; of the tripods of Hephaistos, which ran of themselves, . . 18.376, cf. Pl.Com.188; . . Hdt.8.37; marionettes…

αὐτομαχέω.definition: fight for oneself, plead one's own cause, in a law-court, Lys.Fr.102S., Hsch., Suid

αὐτονομέομαι.definition: Dep. c. aor. Pass. Str.12.3.11:—to be independent, Th.1.144, D.4.4, etc

αὐτόνοος.definition: contr. of the Phaeacian ships, instinct with sense, Eust.1153.32, with allusion to the nymph Autonoe

αὐτόξυλος.definition: of one piece of wood, S.Ph.35, cf. APl.4.235 , Str.11.4.3

αὐτόπαις.definition: the own child, S.Tr.826 ; prob. a mere child, Id.Fr.1029; dub. l. in PPetr. 3p.110

αὐτοπάτωρ.definition: self-engendered, Orph.H.10.10, Iamb.Myst.8.2; of Zeus, Aristid.Or.43.9

αὐτόπιστος.definition: credible in itself, HeroDef.136.6, cf. Olymp.in Phd.p.225N., Heliod.in EN117.36, Simp.in Ph.649.12; f.l. in Oenom. ap. Eus.PE5.33

αὐτοπολίτης.definition: citizen of a free state, prob. in X.HG5.2.14

αὐτοπραγέω.definition: act independently, Str.8.3.30; do one's own work, Procl.in R.1.23K

αὐτοπραγία.definition: free, independent action, Pl.Def.411e, Chrysipp.Stoic.3.176, Ph.2.51, Procl.in Prm.p.664S.; Stoic.3.86

αὐτόπρακτος.definition: enjoying the privilege of collecting one's own taxes, PMasp.19.3 ; ib.2 iii 8, cf. Cod.Theod.11.22.4

αὐτόπρεμνος.definition: together with the root, root and branch, S.Ant.714, cf. Antiph.231.7; Ar.Ra.903 ; give in absolute possession, A.Eu.401

αὐτοπροαίρετος.definition: self-chosen, Hierocl.in; Act., self-acting, acting of free will, Proll.Hermog.in Rh.4.27W.; free will, Olymp.in Grg.p.264J

αὐτοπρόσωπος.definition: in one's own person, without a mask, of an actor, Ath.10.452f, cf. Jul.Mis.367b; Luc.Pr.Im.3; Id.Tim.27; Id.JTr.29; speaking in one's own person, Sch.Il.Oxy.1086.64, al.; in which the author speaks in his own person, …

αὐτοπτέω.definition: see with one’s own eyes, Paus.4.31.5, Hld.3.1; esp. witness a divine manifestation, Porph. ap. Eus.PE4.20:-Pass., Marin.Procl.28

αὐτόπτης.definition: seeing oneself, eyewitness, Hdt.2.29, 3.115, al., Pl.Lg.900a, Euang.1.4, Din.3.15, D.22.22, etc.:— fem. Sch.Il.Oxy.1086.96

αὔτοπτος.definition: self-revealed, Jul.Or.7.221b, Suid; = II, PMag.Lond.121.319,727, PMag.Par.1.162

αὐτόπυρος.definition: of whole wheaten meal, Alex.121, Gal.15.577, PPetr.3p.179; opp. Plu.2.466d:—also Phryn.Com.38, Hp.Int.20,22, Luc.Pisc.44

αὐτοπώλης.definition: selling one's own products, Pl.Plt.260c; Id.Sph.231d, cf. Sch.Ar.Pl.1155

αὐτόρρυτος.definition: self-flowing, flowing unbidden, AP9.669 ; of resin, Gal.13.626: poet. Pi.P.12.17

αὐτοσκεύαστος.definition: self-made, i. e. natural, Sch.Opp.H.1.22, Hsch. s.v

αὐτόσκωμμα.definition: essence of wit, in pl., Alciphr.3.43

αὐτοστατέω.definition: to be independent, self- sufficient, Ph.1.688

αὐτόστοιχος.definition: going by oneself, independent, Anon. ap.Suid. s.v

αὐτόστολος.definition: self-sent, going or acting of oneself, S.Ph.496, cf. AP7.585 : metaph. of Leander swimming, Musae.255; to let a ship by private contract, OGI572.41

αὐτοσφαγής.definition: slain by oneself or by kinsmen, both in S.Aj.841 , cf. E.Ph.1316

αὐτοσχεδές.definition: a kind of woman's shoe, Hsch.; cf

αὐτοσχεδιάζω.definition: aor. part. Pass. Stratt.4 D.: :-act or speak offhand, extemporize, Pl.Cra.413d, Mx.235c, X.Mem.3.5.21. 2. c. acc., extemporize, Th.1.138, cf. X.HG5.2.32. II. mostly in bad sense, act, speak, or think unadvisedly, v.l.…

αὐτοσχεδίασμα.definition: work done offhand, impromptu, improvisation, Arist.Po.1448b23, Pl.Com.87

αὐτοσχεδιαστής.definition: one who acts or speaks offhand: and so, raw hand, bungler, opp. X.Lac.13.5

αὐτοσχέδιος.definition: also Plu.Sull.7:—hand to; offhand, improvised, rough and ready, h.Merc.55; D.H.2.34; Plu.Sull.7; Arist.Fr.600; D.H.1.40, 3.67; Hld.2.4; Max.Tyr.12.2; of persons, Plu.2.642a; Ach.Tat.5.27; D.C.73.1; opp. in Empiric med…

αὐτόταγος.definition: without a master, independent, dub. in Hsch., cf. EM173.47

αὐτοτέλεια.definition: perfection, completeness, Ocell.1.9; complete sentence, proposition, A.D.Synt.12.4, al.; ib.5.20

αὐτοτέλεστος.definition: self-accomplished, spontaneous, Opp.H.1.763, AP1.19.6 , Nonn.D.43.233, al

αὐτοτράπεζος.definition: eating at the same table with, Emp.147.1

αὐτοτρίγωνον.definition: the ideal triangle, the Form of triangle, Arist.GC316a12, Them.Or.13.165a

αὐτούργημα.definition: a piece of one's own work, D.Chr.12.57: pl., PMasp.244

αὐτόφλοιος.definition: with the bark on, Theoc.25.208, cf. Ep.4.3, AP6.99

αὐτοφόντης.definition: murderer of kin, E.Med.1269; prob. corrupt in S.El.272; Lyc.438

αὐτοφυής.definition: self-grown, of home production, X.Vect.2.1; Ar.Fr.110; natural, opp. artificial, Hes.Th.813; Th.1.93; native gold, D.S.3.45; Thphr.Lap.39; hills in their natural state, not quarried or mined, X.Vect.4.2; a natural gro…

αὐτόφωρος.definition: mostly in the phrase to catch in the act, Lys.13.85, D.19.132; E.Ion1214; Lys.7.42: with pass. Verbs, Hdt.6.72; Ar.Pl.455, Eup.181: hence

αὐτοχάρακτος.definition: self-engraven or impressed, of an image in a mirror, Nonn.D.5.599

αὐτόχειρ.definition: with one's own hand, creative; abs., one who kills himself, suicide, S.Ant.1175; Arist.Fr.502; simply, murderer, S.OT231, D.21.116; . . ib.106: c. gen., Isoc.4.111, cf. Men.Sam.216; in full, S.OT266, cf. El.955, D.18.287

αὐτοχειρία.definition: murder perpetrated by one's own hand; mostly in dat. Ion. used adverbially, = mostly of slaughter, Hdt.1.140; Id.3.74, cf. 66: generally, Id.1.123; Id.3.13, cf. Ar.Fr.33 D.; D.25.57; Democr.260

αὐτοχειρίζω.definition: do a thing or commit a murder with one's own hand, Philist.60 ap.Poll.2.154, where the word is called

αὐτόχειρος.definition: = foreg., Hsch. Adv. = Sch.E.Or.1040, v.l. in Hierocl.Facet.152

αὐτόχθων.definition: gen. sprung from the land itself; Adj., indigenous, native, Hdt.4.197; PGiss.99.5 ; Lys.2.43; Polioch.2.6; Philod.Scarph.127; urbanitas, racy of the soil, Cic.Att.7.2.3

αὐτόχυτος.definition: poured out of itself, self-flowing, Hes.Fr.96.102; Aristid.Or.39.7,16, cf. Sch.Pi.O.7.12; Nonn.D.24.131

αὐτοψία.definition: seeing with one's own eyes, Dsc.Praef.5; supernatural manifestation, vision, Procl.in Alc.p.92 C. , Iamb.Myst.2.4 , 7.3 ; Porph.Plot.10, cf. Dam.Isid.13 ; opp. Ps.-Callisth.1.6; magical operation for the production of…

αὐχένιον.definition: Dim. of An. Ox.2.356; = II.5, Eust.1533.46

αὐχενιστήρ.definition: halter, Lyc.1100; ligature for neck, Hippiatr.10

ἀφαιμάσσω.definition: Att. draw blood, of leeches, Sor.2.11; bleed, Hippiatr.69

ἀφαιρέτης.definition: one who deprives, Vett.Val.55.18, cf. Ptol.Tetr.189, Sch.Od.13.224, Suid. s.v

ἀφαμματίζω.definition: fasten off, Antyll. ap. Orib.45.24.4:—hence Sor.1.56

ἀφανέω.definition: fail to put in an appearance, dub. in PTeb.43.22 :— but thrash, beat, Ar.Eq.394; cf. and Hsch.; v

ἀφανισμός.definition: extermination, destruction, Plb.5.11.5; = foreg.II, Arist.HA580b21, Luc.Alex.19; Thphr.Sign.2 , cf. Cleom.2.5; occultation, Theo Sm.p.137 H.; title of work by Eudoxus, on occultations of stars by the sun, Phld.D.1.21;…

ἀφανιστής.definition: destroyer, dub. l. in Plu.2.828f, cf. Sch.A.Th.175, etc.; scavenger, PLond.2.387.9 :—fem. Sch.Opp.H.2.487:—hence causing to disappear, A.D.Pron.33.15; Archig. ap. Aët.6.63, cf. Crito ap.Gal.12.447; destroying, Sch.A.T…

ἀφαντασίαστος.definition: not manifested, Corp.Herm.5.1, Olymp.in Phd.p.35N. Adv. Ascl.in Metaph.151.6, Olymp.in Phd.p.38 N

ἀφαντασίωτος.definition: unable to imagine a thing, Plu.2.960d, Cat.Cod. Astr.7.215.7

ἄφαντος.definition: made invisible, blotted out; obscure, Id.N.8.34; Epimenid.II.—Poet. and late Prose, D.S.3.60, 4.65, Ev.Luc.24.31; Aristid.1.260 J., cf. Sch.Arat.899

ἀφαντόω.definition: make hide, Eust.882.45:—Pass., disappear, Sch.Arat.899; evaporate, Syn.Alch.p.67 B.; to be sublimated, Zos.Alch.p.163 B

ἀφαρμάκευτος.definition: without medicine, not physicked, Hp.Acut.27; without cosmetics, Alciphr.Fr.5.4

ἀφάρμακος.definition: without medicinal properties; without bloom, Eust.1416.2, Hsch

ἀφάσσω.definition: Ion., Ep., and late Prose, = feel, Hp.Nat.Mul.11, etc.; Hdt.3.69, cf. A.R.2.710, 4.428, v.l. in Call.Fr.317, cf. Musae.82, etc.; groping, Dam.Pr.42, cf. Iamb.Myst.3.6, etc.:—Med., A.R.4.181:—Pass., Hp.Morb.2.30 and 41

ἀφειδέω.definition: to be unsparing, lavish of, S.El.980; take no care for, neglect, S.Ant.414 ; reck not of, Musae.303; A.R.2.98 , 869, 3.630; Nonn.D.8.217: also in Prose, Str.1.2.6

ἀφέλεια.definition: Ion. simplicity, Hp.Decent.3, Antiph.163.8; Plb.6.48.3; of style, Ath.15.693f, Hermog.Id.1.1, al.; opp. ib.11; of terminology, Gal.10.269

ἀφελής.definition: without a stone, even, smooth; artless, simple, of persons, S.Fr.723, D.Ep.4.11, Luc.DDeor.4.3; Plu.Cat. Ma.6; Phylarch.43; frater Cic.Att.1.18.1; Plb.11.10.3; also Id.18.49.4; simple, in good sense, IG14.1839. Adv. P…

ἀφελληνίζω.definition: hellenize, i. e. civilize thoroughly, Ph.2.567:—Pass., aor. D.Chr.37.26

ἀφερέπονος.definition: incapable of labour, Vett.Val.77.1, 150.27, Ptol.Tetr.156, Sch.A.R.1.269. Adv. carelessly, Simp.in Ph.43.4

ἀφερμηνεύω.definition: interpret, expound, Pl.Sph.246e: abs., Id.Lg.660c; translate, Plu.Rom.21

ἀφερπετόομαι.definition: Pass., become a reptile, prob. in Herm. ap. Stob.1.49.69

ἀφέρπω.definition: to creep off, steal away, S.Tr.813, OC490: generally, go away, retire, Id.Aj.1161, Theoc.4.29, Herod.6.98; die, Pempel. ap. Stob.4.25.52

ἀφετήριος.definition: starting-point of a race, CIG2758iiiD7 , Sch.Ar.Eq.1156: hence whose statues adorned the race- course, Paus.3.14.7; AP9.319 : metaph., S.E.M.1.41; Phld.Rh.1.223S

ἀφέψημα.definition: decoction, Dsc.2.107, Lyc. ap. Orib.8.25.2, Ruf.ib.7.26.67, Gal.13.9

ἀφηβάω.definition: to be past the prime of life, Lib.Decl.23.59; Ph.1.516; Poll.1.236: pf. part. Pass., Id.2.10,18

ἀφηγέομαι.definition: Ion. lead the way from a point; tell, relate, Hdt.1.24, al., E.Supp.186; assert, Aret.CA2.7:—pf. in pass. sense, Hdt.5.62; what has been told, Id.1.207, cf. 9.26

ἀφήγησις.definition: Ion. narration, worth telling, Hdt.2.70; in a way not fit to be told, Id.3.125; D.H.2.7; J.BJ1.11.4, cf. Arr.An.Prooem.2, Luc.Hist.Conscr.30, Aristid.1.154J., Hermog.Id.1.1, al.; report, SIG578.54

ἀφημερεύω.definition: to be absent for a day, Decr. ap. D.18.37, cf. PHib.148 , etc

ἀφηνιάζω.definition: refuse to obey the reins, Ph.1.85; Med. or Pass., Hsch

ἄφθαρτος.definition: uncorrupted, undecaying, Ph.Bel.67.37; incorruptible, Epicur.Ep.1p.29U., al., Phld.D.3 Fr.88b, al., Diog.Oen.63, al

ἄφθεγκτος.definition: of places, etc., where none may speak, S.OC156; Pass., unspeakable, unutterable, B.Fr.2.2, Pl.Sph.238c. Adv. Iamb.Myst.7.4

ἀφθονία.definition: freedom from envy or grudging, liberality; of things, plenty, abundance, Pi.N.3.9; Pl.Ap.24e, cf. 23c; Men.589; abundance of matter for . . , Lys.12.2; Telecl.1.10; D.21.102; in abundance, X.An.7.1.33; opp. Id.Smp.4.5…

ἀφίδρυσις.definition: Setting up a statue, Id.8.7.2, Plu.2.1136a

ἀφιζάνω.definition: rise from one's seat, Suid.:—also Hsch

ἀφιλαργυρία.definition: freedom from avarice, Hp.Decent.5, Onos.1.8, D.S.9.12

ἀφιλάργυρος.definition: not loving money, Inscr.Prien.137.5 , D.S.9.11, 1 Ep.Ti.3.3, Ep.Hebr.13.5, Sor.1.4, POxy.33 ii 11 . Adv. IG22.1343.25 , SIG708.17

ἀφιλίωτος.definition: not to be made a friend of or reconciled, Hsch. s.v

ἀφιλόδοξος.definition: free from conceit or ambition, Id.Rh.2.273S., Lib.p.42 O.; Cic.Att.2.17.2, Ph.2.458

ἀφιλοκάλητος.definition: without adornment, Procl.ad Hes.Op.746, cf. Eust.669.41

ἀφιλόκαλος.definition: without love for beauty or honour, Plu.2.672e, Gal.5.39

ἀφιλόνεικος.definition: not fond of strife, Arist.VV1250a43, 1251a15, Andronic.Rhod.p.575 M., Ph.2.5; ib.555. Adv. Plb.21.20.1, cf.Ph.1.324, al., Luc.Symp.37

ἀφιλοσόφητος.definition: not versed in philosophy; without philosophical significance, Arg. Sch.Od.1

ἀφιλοστάχυος.definition: without ears of corn, starving, AP6.40.8

ἀφιλότιμος.definition: lacking in ambition, Is.7.35; simply, indifferent, J.AJ2.9.6. Adv. lukewarmly, PPetr.2p.5

ἀφιλοχρηματία.definition: contempt for riches, Plu.Comp.Ag.Gracch.1, Socr.Ep.5.2:— hence Adj. Ph.2.458, Eun.Hist.p.243 D

ἀφιππάζομαι.definition: Hld.7.29, etc.:—ride off or away, Plb.29.6.18, Str.7.2.1, J.AJ14.13.5, Plu.Aem.19, Luc.Tox.50

ἀφιππεύω.definition: ride off, away, or back, X.An.1.5.12, D.S.2.19, Plu.Arat.40:—also Med., Hld.4.18

ἀφιπποδρομά.definition: contest of riders who dismounted while racing, IG 9.527

ἀφίπταμαι.definition: = fly away, E.IA1608, Luc.Somn.16, Lib.Decl.51.15, Aët.7.103

ἀφιστάνω.definition: later form of CPR5.14 , Dsc.3.87, Luc.Sol.7:—Pass., renounce, PRyl.117.22 :—also Ath.1.9b, Lib.Decl.51.14; opt. dub. in X.Smp.2.20 , cf. Luc.Sol.7

ἀφλέγμαντος.definition: free from inflammation, Hp.Acut.46; relieving or checking inflammation, Thphr.Od.35, cf. Heliod. ap. Orib.46.8.1, Dsc.1.73

ἄφνω.definition: Adv. unawares, of a sudden, A.Fr.195, E.Med.1205, Alc.420, Eup.268, etc.: in Prose, Th.4.104, 7.37, D.21.41, Act.Ap.2.2, etc.:—also Epigr.Gr.468

ἀφοβία.definition: fearlessness, Pl.Lg.649a sq., Arist.EN1107b1, Plu.Cleom.9, Onos.13.3

ἀφόδευμα.definition: excrement, Dsc.Eup.1.89, Gp.12.11; = ajowan, PMag.Leid.V.12.30, W.6.27

ἀφομιλέω.definition: avoid, escape, a comitatu Cic.Fam.16.17.2; cf. Hsch. s.v

ἀφομοίωσις.definition: making like, comparison, Plu.2.988d, Iamb.Myst.1.11; representation of . . , Phld.Po.2.24

ἀφορισμός.definition: delimitation, assignment of boundaries; separation, distinction, Thphr.CP3.14.2; Thd.Is.56.3: hence, banishment, = Lat.relegatio, Lyd.Mag.3.17 , Ost.9c

ἀφορμή.definition: starting-point, esp. in war, base of; generally, starting-point, origin, occasion or pretext, Id.Hec.1239, Ph.199; D.18.156; Id.21.98, cf. 2 Ep.Cor.5.12; Isoc.4.61, Ep.Rom.7.8; BGU615.6 , 923.22 ; Inscr.Prien.105.16 ;…

ἀφορολόγητος.definition: not subjected to tribute, IG22.1009.41, GDI5160.10 , OGI223 , Plb.4.25.7, LXX1 Es.4.50, Plu.Flam.10

ἀφοσίωσις.definition: purification, expiation, D.H.2.52; doing as matter of form, for form's sake, Plu.Eum.12; outward, formal respect, Id.Tim.39; Dam.Pr.171

ἀφράδμων.definition: in Trag. gen. = c. inf., without sense to foresee, h.Cer.256; A.Ag.1401, cf. S.Fr.613. Adv. A.Pers.417.—Only poet

ἀφράζω.definition: = sq., cited from Hp. by Gal.19.87; cf. Hsch

ἄφραστος.definition: unutterable, marvellous; not perceived, unseen, h.Merc.353; not to be observed, known, or guessed, A.Supp.95 ; incomprehensible, Orph.L.46; the place least likely to be thought of, unforeseen, A.R.2.824. Adv. beyond t…

ἀφρίζω.definition: = foam, S.El.719, Hp.Mul.2.123, Thphr.CP6.1.5; of a wine-cup, Antiph.174.6, Alex.119.3

ἀφρογένεια.definition: foam-born, Aphrodite, Mosch.2.71, Coluth.167; the planet Venus, Max.402, Doroth.ap.Cat.Cod.Astr.2.82.2

Ἀφροδισιάζω.definition: have sexual intercourse: —Act., of the man, Hp.Vict.3.73, al., Pl.R.426a, X.Mem.1.3.14, etc.:—Pass., of the woman, Id.Hier.3.4, Arist.HA581b17, etc

Ἀφροδισιάς.definition: sacred to Aphrodite, name of an island, Hdt.4.169. II. = Apul.Herb.6

ἀφροδισιαστής.definition: voluptuary, Polem.Phgn.14; lessee of public brothel, POxy.511.3

Ἀφροδίσιος.definition: also D.H.2.24, Luc.Am.12; sexual pleasures, Hp.Mochl.36, freq. in Pl., as Phd.81b, al.; Pi.N.7.53; X.Mem.2.6.22; Hp.Jusj.:—also as concrete, = amasius, X.Mem.1.3.8

Ἀφροδιτάριον.definition: name of an eyesalve, Gal.12.752; name of a horse-medicine, Hippiatr.129

ἀφρονίζω.definition: make foolish, prob. in Aq.2 Ki.15.31

ἄφροντις.definition: free from care, careless, c. gen., E.Fr.958; Plu.2.45d; Luc.Dem.Enc.25: abs., Plu.2.792b , cf. Max.Tyr.3.9: Comp. Steph.in Hp.1.263 D

ἀφροντιστέω.definition: have no care of, pay no heed to, ib.885a, v.l. in X.An.5.4.20, cf. Plb.9.13.1; Hp.Praec.7 ; Philostr.VA1.38

ἀφροντιστία.definition: in pass. sense, being unheeded, Phld.Mort.36

ἀφρόντιστος.definition: thoughtless, heedless, X.Smp.6.6; without causing anxiety, Ruf. ap. Orib.45.30.20

ἀφρούρητος.definition: unguarded, Pl.Lg.760a, Plu.2.34of; ungarrisoned, Plb.4.25.7, al., Plu.Flam.10: metaph., Gal.18.321

ἀφυγιάζω.definition: cure, heal, Archig. ap. Gal.12.821, Philum.Ven.5.3, 17.5 , Iamb.VP25.114, Paul.Aeg.5.4

ἀφυλακτέω.definition: bark out, Luc.Am.17; to be off one's guard, X.An.7.8.20, Eq.Mag.5.15: c. gen., to be careless about, Id.Cyr.1.6.5:—Pass., to be ill-guarded, Plb.5.73.10, cf. Onos.42.15

ἀφύλακτος.definition: unguarded, unwatched; unguarded, off one's guard, Hdt.9.116, Th.7.32; Arist.Rh.1372a19; sleep securely through the night, A.Ag.337; catch one off his guard, X.Cyr.1.6.37; . . D.4.18; want of precaution, Th.3.30: Comp.…

ἀφυλακτηρίαστος.definition: not protected by a phylactery, PMag.Par.1.2507

ἀφυλαξία.definition: carelessness in watching, X.Oec.4.10; negligence, Antipho3.4.7; absence of guards, X.Hier.6.4, D.C.55.15

ἀφυλίζω.definition: strain off, AP6.191.5 , f.l. in Dsc.2.76.8

ἀφυπνίζω.definition: awaken from sleep, E.Rh.25, Plu.Nic.9, Longus1.25, etc.:—Pass., wake up, keep awake, Cratin.306 , Pherecr.191 : intr. in Act., Philostr.VA2.36

ἀφυσιολόγητος.definition: not to be explained by science; without knowledge of natural laws, in Adv. prob. in M.Ant.10.9

ἀφυσιόλογος.definition: not versed in natural philosophy, prob. l. in Id.9.41

ἀχάλινος.definition: unbridled, E.Ba.386 , cf. HF382 , Ar.Ra.838, Pl.Lg.701c; APl.4.223; i.e. uncorrupted by bribes, IG9.270 : neut. pl. as Adv., E.HF l.c

ἀχάλκευτος.definition: not forged of metal, A.Ch.493, Critias20 D.; S.Fr.708

ἀχαριστέω.definition: show ingratitude, Antipho Soph.54; disoblige, Pl.Smp.186c, cf. SIG495.159 , Luc.DMar.9.2, Nic.Dam.p.5 D

ἀχείμαντος.definition: not stormy, Alc.16; not vexed by storms, B.Fr.22:—also J.AJ3.5.3

ἀχειροποίητος.definition: not made by hands, of buildings and statues, Ev.Marc.14.58, 2 Ep.Cor.5.1; i.e. spiritual, Ep.Col.2.11

ἀχειροτόνητος.definition: not elected, D.19 Arg.ii 13; not granted by vote, Max.Tyr.12.5

ἀχθηδών.definition: weight, burden, A.Pr.26; metaph., vexation, annoyance, Th.2.37, Pl.Lg.734a; for the sake of teasing, Th.4.40; Luc.Tox.9

ἀχθοφορέω.definition: bear burdens, Plb.4.32.7, Plu.Mar.13; to be; bear as a burden, AP7.468 ; IG14.1301; APl.4.333

ἀχθοφορία.definition: bearing of burdens, Plu.2.1130d , cf. Luc.Asin.19; M.Ant.7.3; any heavy pressure, Hp.Art.63

ἀχθοφόρος.definition: bearing burdens, Hdt.7.187; as Subst., porter, Gell.5.3.2, Luc.Herod.5

ἄχλαινος.definition: without cloak or mantle, Simon.167.3, Call.Dian.115, Lyc.763; ib.635

ἀχόρταστος.definition: unfed, starving, Men.690, Sm.Ps.58.16; = Hsch.:—hence Subst. ravenous hunger, Sm.De.28.20

ἀχρειόω.definition: or , pf. useless, disable, damage, Dicaearch.2.3, Plb.3.64.8, LXXDa.4.11, OGI l.c.:—Pass., SIG569.31 , cf. Plb.1.14.6, BCH35.286 ; to be corrupted, LXXPs.13.3; Apollon.Cit.1.1

ἀχρηματέω.definition: to be without money, Hsch. s.v

ἀχρηματία.definition: want of money, Th.1.11, D.H.7.24, Eus.Mynd.7

ἀχρημάτιστος.definition: a day on which no; disused, PMag.Lond.46.345

ἀχρήματος.definition: without money or means, Hdt.1.89, Timocl.9.7; Arist.Pol.1271b16; on the poor, A.Pers.167

ἀχρημονέω.definition: to be in want of money, Poll.6.196

ἀχρήσιμος.definition: useless, CPHerm.119riv9 , cf. Sopat. in Rh.8.10 W., Hippiatr.14

ἀχρηστεύω.definition: Gramm., not to be in use, Sch.D.T.p.195H

ἀχρηστολογέω.definition: to speak unprofitably or amiss, EM463.25

ἄχρηστος.definition: useless, unprofitable, Batr.70; = , useless, do-nothing, D.19.135 , etc.; Is.7.37; prob. l. in Lys.33.3; non-effective, unwarlike, Eun.Hist.p.239D.; so Ath.3.98c. Adv. D.61.43

ἀχρώματος.definition: colourless, Pl.Phdr.247c, Plu.2.97b; unblushing, shameless, Suid. s.v

ἀχυρόω.definition: mix chaff or straw with mud, Thphr.HP4.8.8:— Pass., mixed with chaff, Polioch.2; IG 22.463.18; Ph.Bel.86.44; to be strewn with straw, of the orchestra, Arist.Pr.901b30

ἄψαυστος.definition: untouched, Hdt.8.41, Thphr.HP5.5.6; Act., not touching, c. gen., S.OT969; of persons dying young, Epigr.Gr.241.2

ἀψεύδεια.definition: truthfulness, Corinn.Supp.2.70, Pl.R.485c, Iamb.Protr.20; reliability, of times and seasons, Arist.Mu.397a11: Ph.Fr.110H., Them.Or.21.257c

ἄψευστος.definition: later form of Ph.Fr.51 H.; Plu.Art.28; unfeigned, AP7.638.6 . Adv. PMag.Lond.121.248

ἁψιδοειδής.definition: arched, vaulted, D.C.68.25; wheel- shaped, Eudox.Ars19.13

ἁψικορία.definition: rapid satiety, Plb.14.1.4, Plu.2.504d, Andronic.Rhod.p.572M.; fickleness, PLond.5.1711

ἁψιμαχέω.definition: skirmish with an enemy, Hyp.Fr.131, Plb.18.8.4, D.S.11.52; entice or lead on to fight, Plu.Crass.10, Dio39

ἁψιμαχία.definition: skirmishing, D.S.20.29, Plu.Brut.39, al.: metaph., altercation, Aeschin.2.176, cf. Hyp.Oxy.1607.1i26, Plb.5.49.5, Plu.Lyc.2, PPetr.3p.104: pl., personal encounters, D.H.6.22; ib.34

ἁψιμισία.definition: trivial and transient enmity, Hsch., Suid

ἀψινθᾶτον.definition: draught of wormwood, Aët.3.69, Alex.Trall.1.15: —also PLond.3.1259.32

ἄψοφος.definition: = S.Tr.967 , E.Tr.887, Com.Adesp.1310, Arist.de An.420a7. Adv. and EM183.22

ἀψυχαγώγητος.definition: not rejoicing the heart, Plb.9.1.5. Adv. without being comforted, Jul.Or.8.252a

ἀωρέω.definition: to be careless , Hsch., Suid.:—also, = , Hsch

ἀωροθανής.definition: = foreg., CIG3846 q , Calder Philadelphia and Montanism 35

ἄας.definition: to-morrow or the day after to-morrow, gen. of = read by Zenod. for in Il.8.470 ; as Adv. in Boeot., Hsch.; cf

ἄγαν.definition: Adv. very much, chiefly Aeol. Dor. and Trag., not in Hom., rare in Ion., as Hdt.2.173, Hp.Art.4, al., Democr.222; freq. in bad sense, too much:—prov., Pi.Fr.216 ; Thgn.335:—with Verbs, Hp.Fract.8; A.Pr.182; Pl.R.563e:…

ἀγελαστί.definition: Adv. without laughter, Pl.Euthd.278e, Thphr.Fr.124, Plu.2.727a

ἀγεληδόν.definition: Adv. in herds or companies, Il.16.160, Hdt.2.93, AP9.24 , etc.:—also Arat.965,1079

ἄγκαθεν.definition: Adv. in the arms, A.Eu.80; resting on the elbows, A.Ag.3; also expl. as contr. for = on the top, cf. Sch.ad l. c., Hsch., AB337

ἀγλαφύρως.definition: Adv. without polish, inelegantly, Hegesand.22, cf. Eust.1295.15

ἀγρόθεν.definition: Adv. from the country, Od.13.268, 15.428, Epich.161, E.Or.866, Luc.Macr.22: also AP7.398

ἀγρόθι.definition: Adv. in the country, Call.Cer.136, Poll.9.12

ἀγχιστίνδην.definition: Adv. within the near kin, Poll.6.175, Lex ap.Hsch

ἀγχόθι.definition: Poet. Adv.near, Il.14.412, cf. Od.13.103, A.R.1.37, etc.: abs., Theoc.22.40, IG9.645

ἀδελφοπρεπῶς.definition: Adv. as befits a brother, LXX4 Ma.10.12

ἀδιακωλύτως.definition: Adv. without hindrance, Herm. ap. Stob.1.49.68, BGU1048.19

Αἰγυπτιστί.definition: Adv. in the Egyptian tongue, Hdt.2.46; in Egyptian fashion, i.e. craftily, Theoc.15.48

αἰετηδόν.definition: Adv. like an eagle, Apollon.Lex.68, Sch.Il.18.410

αἶψα.definition: 36), Adv. quick, forthwith, on a sudden, freq. in Hom. , cf. Sapph.1.13, Thgn.663, Sol.2, Pi.P.4.133, Emp.35.14, A.Supp.481.—Poet., exc. in Mon.Ant.18.322

ἀκινδυνί.definition: Adv. of sq., without danger, Suid

ἀκινητίνδα.definition: Adv., play the game 'who stirs first', Poll.9.110

ἀκλαυστεί.definition: or or Adv. of sq., without weeping, Call.Dian.267, A.D.Adv.133.19, Sor.1.79, Longus1.5

ἀκληρωτεί.definition: or Adv.without casting lots, Lys.16.16, Arist.Ath.30.5, CIG2880

ἀκοιλάντως.definition: Adv. without deficiency, in full, PLond.3.954.18 , al

ἀκουόντως.definition: Adv. as one that listens, i.e. with deference, Sch.Il.Oxy.1085.72

ἀκροποδητί.definition: or Adv., on tiptoe, Luc.Prom.1, DMar.14.3,al

ἅλαδε.definition: Adv., to or into the sea, Il.1.308; name of the second day of the Eleusinian mysteries, 16th Boedromion, Polyaen.3.11.2, cf. IG1.53a35, 2.385d20

ἀλανές.definition: · Hsch. Adv. , Id.; dub. sens., GDI 1156.4

ἀλλαχόθεν.definition: Adv. from another place, LXX4 Ma1.7, Ev.Jo.10.1, Plu.2.1129e; from another source, Antipho3.4.3

ἀλλαχόθι.definition: Adv. elsewhere, A.D.Synt.333.26, Plu.2.20d, AP9.378 , Jul.Or.1.5c

ἀλλαχόσε.definition: Adv. elsewhither, v.l. in X.Cyr.7.4.7, Simp.in Ph.1164.38

ἀλλαχοῦ.definition: Adv. elsewhere, S.OC43, X.HG2.3.20; Ev.Marc.1.38, cf. Arr.Epict.3.26.4.—These forms are censured by Moer.11 as less Att. than

ἄλλην.definition: acc. fem. of used as Adv., elsewhither, X.Cyr.4.1.15, cf. Aen.Tact.26.3 : also of Time, again and again, Pl.Euthd.273b

ἄλλοθεν.definition: Adv. from another place, one from one place, another from another, Il.2.75, etc., cf. Alc.86, Emp.23, Thgn.518, A.Ag.92,595, etc. ; he came from abroad, Od.3.318 ; 7.52 ; in Att., or from what other place soever, Pl.L…

ἄλλοσε.definition: Adv. elsewhither, Od.23.184; A.Pers.359; . . . S.Tr.272; to foreign lands, to export, X.HG6.1.11; to no other place, Pl.Cri.52b; to many other places, Id.Mx.241e; to what other place? Id.Phd.82a; to some other place, …

ἄλλυδις.definition: Adv., Ep. for elsewhither, in Hom. only with one hither, another thither, Il.11.486, Od.5.71, cf.A.R.2.980, etc.; his colour changes now one way, now another, Il.13.279; imitated from Hom. by Eup.159.11; later by itse…

ἁμαλῶς.definition: Adv. = , v.l. in Hp.Morb.1.8, 2.8, Int.30, cf. Gal.19.76

ἀμαχεί.definition: Adv. of without stroke of sword, without resistance, Th.1.143, X.An.1.7.9, etc.: without question, undoubtedly, prob. f.l. for Plu.2.433c:—written Phot.p.88R

ἀμέλει.definition: properly imper. of (cf; as Adv., doubtless, by all means, of course, Ar.Ach.368, Nu.488, al., Pl.Phd.82a, al., X.Mem.1.4.7, Men.Sam.8; freq. ironically, as Ar.Ra.532; freq. in Thphr.Char. to introduce a subject, 13.1,…

ἀμισθί.definition: Adv. of without reward or hire, Archil.41. E.Tr.409, D.24.99; rent-free, SIG344 ; without reward of money or honour, Plu.Arist.3; only paid with praise, Brut.Ep.38; without paying, Plu.CG12. Archil. l.c.]

ἀμογητί.definition: Adv. of sq., without toil or effort, Il.11.637, Call.Dian.25, D.H.Dem.8, Luc.Nav.21, Plot.6.2.21, etc

ἀμοιβήδην.definition: A.R.2.1071, Orph.L.691. Adv., alternately, in succession, Il.18.506, Od.18.310, h.Cer326. Hp.Ep.17; read by Aristarch. in Il.18.506

ἀμφαδόν.definition: Adv., poet. for = , publicly, openly, without disguise, opp. Il.7.243; opp. Od.14.330; opp. 1.296; Il.9.370; Ion Trag. ap. Phot.p.9 R.—Prop. neut. of Adj. which occurs in Od.19.391 discovered, known, cf. A.R.3.615

ἀμφιετεί.definition: Adv., year by year, prob. in SIG963.7 , cf. Suid., Eust.1385.1

ἀμφιπεριπλέγδην.definition: Adv. twined round, AP5.275 , prob. in Jo.Gaz.1.6; Nonn.D.36.360

ἀμφοτεράκις.definition: Adv. in both ways, Arist.Mech.855b32, Pr.902b31

ἀμφοτέρωθεν.definition: Orph.Fr.168.14, Androm; from both ends, Od.10.167

ἀμφοτέρως.definition: Adv. in both ways, Pl.Prm.159a, Grg.469a, etc

ἀναβάδην.definition: Adv., lit.going up, but usu. with one's feet up, lying down, Ar.Pl.1123, D.Chr.62.6, Plu.2.336c, cf. Ath.12.528f, Poll.3.90; so prob. in Ar.Ach.399,410, but expl. by a Sch. as upstairs

ἀναιμακτί.definition: Adv. of sq., without bloodshed, Them.Or.7.90a, Hsch

ἀναιμωτί.definition: Adv. without shedding blood, Il.17.363, cf. Od.18.149, Ph.1.323, al., Gal.2.604, Them.Or.16.213a

ἀναλογούντως.definition: Adv. pres. part., = c. dat., CIG2766 ; fittingly, BGU248.21

ἀναμετρικῶς.definition: Adv. by measurement, f.l. in Gem.17.5

ἀνάμιγα.definition: poet. Adv. = promiscuously, confusedly, A.Th.239, S.Tr.839 , IG5.726; with . . , A.R.1.573, AP7.12; also ib.22

ἀναμίξ.definition: Adv. promiscuously, pell-mell, Hdt.1.103, Hellanic.71J., Th.3.107: c. dat., Str.3.3.7, cf. 4.6.3, Jul.Gal.100c

ἀνανευστικῶς.definition: Adv. showing a disposition to refuse, Arr.Epict.1.14.7

ἀναπεπτωκότως.definition: Adv. pf. part. of despondingly, Poll.3.123

ἀναπεφλασμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass. of q.v

ἀναστρόφως.definition: Adv. conversely, vice versa, Stoic.2.71, Iamb.VP26.118

ἀνατεταμένως.definition: Adv. pf.part. Pass. of stretched or strained to the utmost Sch.Ar.Ra.1282

ἀνατί.definition: Adv. of without harm, with impunity, A.Eu.59, S.Ant.485, E.Med.1357, Pl.Lg.871e, prob. in Th.8.67, cf. Is.Fr.2, D.S.20.58, etc

ἀναφανδόν.definition: Adv. = foreg., Il.16.178, Hdt.2.35,46, Pl.Prt.348e, etc.: poet. Pi.P.9.41

ἀνδριστί.definition: Adv. like a man, like men, Ar.Ec.149, cf. Crates Com.3D., Theoc.18.23; with a male voice, D.Chr.33.38

ἀνειλιγμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass. of explicitly, opp. Herm.in Phdr.p.137A., cf. Phlp.in Ph.20.5; Anon.Incred.21

ἀνεκάς.definition: Adv. upwards, . . Pi.O.2.22; . . Ar.V.18, cf. Fr.188; Crates Com.10; Eup.50, cf. Pherecr.169 ; Hp.Mul.1.1. cf. Num.13: but perh. as in , : does not contain Phot.p.129.13 R., i.e. not

ἀνεπιρρήτως.definition: Adv. without demur or subterfuge, PAmh.2.147.11

ἀνεσταλμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass. of tucked up, gloss on Sch.Hes.Sc.287

ἀνεστραμμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass. of inversely, EM584.20; perversely, PTeb.25.16

ἀνιδρωτί.definition: Adv. without sweat, Id.Prorrh.1.61, X.Cyr.2.1.29: metaph., without toil or trouble, Il.15.228; lazily, slowly, X.Cyr.2.2.30, Oec.21.3

ἀνόπιν.definition: Adv. backwards, Hsch.; farther back, in a book. etc., Eust.1031.46

ἀνορμητικῶς.definition: Adv. with an upward rush, Sch.Opp.H.5.210

ἀντιδιεσταλμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass. of as distinguished from, opposed to, Iamb.in Nic.p.12 P

ἀντικρύ.definition: Adv. = over against, right opposite; = straight on, right on, Od.10.162; Il.13.137: mostly followed by a Prep., 5.74; 4.481, cf. Od.22.16; right in the middle, Il.16.285; once in X., Cyr.7.1.30; cf

ἀντιπέρα.definition: Adv. for Plb.1.17.4 : c. gen., Ev.Luc.8.26: proparox. in Hsch

ἀντιπέρηθεν.definition: Adv. from the opposite side, A.R.1.613, AP9.551 : c. gen., A.R.2.1030

ἀντίπροικα.definition: Adv. for next to nothing, cheaply, X.Ages.1.18, Poll.7.10

ἀντιτεταγμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass. of in the opposite sense, Plot.5.3.15

ἄνωθεν.definition: like above, on high, opp. or A.Ag.871 : of the gods, Id.Supp.597 , Pl.Lg.717b; of men on earth, the living, A.Ch.834 , E.Hel.1014; those on deck , Th.7.63; of birds of the air, S.El.1058 ; upper Phrygia, D.23.155

ἀνωνυμεί.definition: and Adv. without name, v.l. in Sch.D.T.p.18 H., EM764.22

ἀπαντικρύ.definition: Adv. (in Att. Inscr. IG2.834bi25; in the first instance, opp. Hp.Art.41

ἀπάριστα.definition: neut. as Adv., after luncheon, Tab.Defix.Aud. 187.63

ἀπαρτί.definition: Adv. completely, and, of numbers, exactly, just, Hdt.5.53, cf. 2.158; Telecl.37; Hp.Art.73: of Time, . . Id.Acut.41. II. just the contrary, . . on the contrary, I expect to receive . ., Pherecr.93, cf.71, Ar.Pl.388. I…

ἀπαρτιζόντως.definition: Adv. adequately, precisely, Antip.Stoic.3.247, cf. Apollod.ib.3.260; Alex.Aphr.in Top.42.27; of division, without remainder, Theo Sm.p.76 H

ἀπεγνωσμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass. of desperately, Plu.Nic.21

ἀπειράκις.definition: Adv., times without number, Arist.Ph.193a28, Xen.975a26, Plu.2.426e; Arist.Pol.1329b27; Id.Cael.270b19, cf. Phld.D.3 Fr.35; Ph.1.499, Dam.Pr.21

ἀπέναντι.definition: Adv., opposite, c. gen., Plb.1.86.3; abs., Inscr.Prien.37.168

ἀπεντεῦθεν.definition: Adv. at this point, Plb.39.1.1; henceforth, POxy.93.16 , Eustr.in EN339.16

ἀπερριμμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass. of negligently, Aristeas28

ἀπηλεγέως.definition: Adv. without caring for anything, outright, bluntly, Hom. only in phrase Il.9.309, Od.1.373; A.R.4.1469; straightforwards, without looking about, Id.1.785; sternly, 4.687; prob.f.l. for Q.S.1.226:—also Nic.Th.495, Opp…

ἀπηλλαγμένως.definition: Adv., c. gen., apart from, dub.l. in J.AJ17.5.6

ἀπηρτημένως.definition: Adv., consistently with; to be discontinuous, M.Ant.4.45

ἀπηρτισμένως.definition: Adv., adequately, completely, D.H.1.90; precisely, Procl.Hyp.4.80

ἀπνευστί.definition: Adv. of without breathing, Arist.Pr.898b24, Resp.475a23; hold one's breath, Pl.Smp.185d; without drawing breath, Hp.Int.12; D.18.308 , cf. Thphr.Char.2.9; Antiph.74.14, Alex.244.3; without breathing, i.e. lifeless, Pl…

ἀποδεδειλιακότως.definition: Adv., in a cowardly way, censured by Poll.5.123

ἀποδιδρασκίνδα.definition: Adv. a game in which all but one ran away, described by Poll.9.117

ἀποκεκαλυμμένως.definition: Adv. openly, Isoc.8.62, D.H.Rh.8.3, Lib.Or.1.37, al

ἀποκριδόν.definition: Adv., apart from, c. gen., A.R.2.15: abs., Opp.H.1.548, cf. IG3.1416a:—also Hdn.Gr.1.496

ἀπολελυμένως.definition: Adv. absolutely, opp; Gramm., in the positive degree, opp. , Phryn.PSp.1 B

ἀπονενοημένως.definition: Adv., desperately, X.HG7.2.8, Luc.DMort.19.2, etc.; to be obstinately averse to food, to be recklessly indifferent to life, Isoc.6.75

ἀπόπαλαι.definition: Adv. from of old; condemned by Phryn.32

ἀπόπροθι.definition: Adv. far away, Od.4.811, al., cf.Theoc.13.61, etc.; fields extending far and wide, Il.23.832, cf. Od.4.757

ἀποσκωπτικῶς.definition: Adv. in a jeering way, Sch.Luc.Lex.15

ἀποτάδην.definition: Adv., stretched at length; diffusely, prolixly, Philostr.VS1 Praef., cf. 1.15.4; Id.VA6.11; Poll.4.94; also with Herm.in Phdr.p.184A

ἀποχρώντως.definition: Dor. Archim.Aren.3.2, Adv. pres. part. of sufficiently, Th.1.21,7.77, Pl.R.429a; Antiph.191.16; J.AJ15.2.7; Phld.Piet.22

ἀπριάτην.definition: Adv. of without purchase-money, . . Od.14.317; so in late Prose Agath.4.22:—also as fem. of Adj. h.Cer.132; . . Il.1.99: acc. pl., Pi.Fr.169.7

ἀπροσφωνητί.definition: Adv. of sq., without accosting, Aesop.35

ἀπτερέως.definition: Adv., quickly, swiftly, Hes.Fr.96.46, Parm.1.17, A.R.4.1765

ἄπωθεν.definition: (in late Poets also Q.S.6.647, AP7.172; c. gen., far from, E.IT108, cf. Ar.Pl.674, Th.3.111, Babr.1.12; cf

Ἀργόθεν.definition: Adv. from Argos, S.Ant.106 , E.IT70, Heracl.775

ἀριστίνδην.definition: Adv., according to birth or merit, IG1.61, cf.9.333.12 , Lex ap.D.43.57, Theopomp. Hist.217a; And.3.30, cf. Isoc.4.146, Pl.Lg.855c; Plb.6.10.9; opp. Arist.Pol.1273a23, cf. Ath.3.1, Plu.Lys.13

ἄρτι.definition: Adv. just, exactly, of coincidence of Time, just now : 1. mostly of the present, with pres. tense, Thgn.998, Pi.P.4.158, A.Th.534; opp. with pf., S.Ant.1283; Id.El.1386; Pl.Cri.43a; more fully Ar.Lys.1008; . . or . . …

ἀρτιάκις.definition: Adv. an even number of times, opp. Pl.Prm.144a, Plu.2.429d; even times even, of powers of two, Pl.Prm.143e, cf. Ascl.Tact.2.7

ἀσκαρδαμυκτί.definition: Adv. of sq., without winking, with unchanged look, X.Cyr.1.4.28, Luc.Tim.14, Gal.7.91, Poll.2.67, v.l. in Ar.Eq.292

ἀσυλεί.definition: or Adv. of inviolably, IG1.41, Supp.Epigr.1.362.23 , SIG110.10 , Theognost.Can.165.10

ἀτέχνως.definition: Adv. of without art, without rules of; Adv. of simply, i.e. really, absolutely, freq. in Com., Pl., etc.; Ar.Ach.37, cf. Nu.408,1174, al.; simply beautiful, Id.Av.820; Id.Ra.106; simply a swine's snout, Pherecr.102; E…

ἀτρέμας.definition: Adv. without trembling, without motion, Il.13.438; Od.19.212; Il.14.352, Od.13.92; sit still! Il.2.200; to keep quiet, Hdt.5.19, 8.16; Id.9.53; ib.54; E.Or.149 ; Ar.Av.1200, Luc.Herm.41; gently, softly, E.Hipp.1358; D…

ἀτρεμεί.definition: Adv. of Ar.Nu.261; dub. in Alex.124.12

Ἀττικιστί.definition: Adv. in the Attic. dialect, D.Prooem.8 ; Antiph.97; Alex.195

αὐθημερεί.definition: or Adv. = Inscr.Prien.28.17 , IG 2.471.71, 3.73, v.l. in Sch.Aeschin.1.128

αὐτεῖ.definition: Adv., Dor. for Isyll.73, IG12.248.19 , A.D.Synt.238.9; Boeot. Schwyzer 462 A 5

αὐτοβοεί.definition: Adv. by a mere shout, at the first shout, take without a blow, Th.2.81, 3.113, 8.62, etc.; = AB 465

αὐτόθεν.definition: before a conson. sts. Theoc.5.60; of Place, = from the very spot: freq. with a Prep., straight from his seat, without rising, Il.19.77; Od.13.56, cf. 21.420; Th.5.83; Theoc.25.171: rare in Trag., from where you stand,…

αὐτοῦ.definition: Dor. and Adv., prop. gen. of there or just here, Hom., etc.; stop there! Cratin.66:—freq. with the place added, here in Troy, etc., Il.2.237, Od.10.271; Il.8.207; somewhere there on the farm, Od.4.639; 8.68; A.Ag.452 …

αὐτοχειρί.definition: Adv. of foreg., with one's own hand, Lycurg.122, Paus.7.16.6, Onos.33 tit.; dub. l. in E.Or.1040

αὔτως.definition: in this very manner, even so, unarmed just as I am like a woman, Il.22.125; in the self-same way, likewise, S.Ant.85, cf. Numen. ap. Ath.7.328d; . . S.Aj.1179; Id.Tr.1040 ; . . Hes.Th.702, A.R.1.90: c. dat., Anacr.21.…

ἀφιλέχθρως.definition: Adv. with no disposition towards enmity, Sch.Od.8.77

ἀψοφητί.definition: or Adv. of sq., Pl.Tht.144b, D.25.90, Arist.HA533b32, Men.298, Ph.1.643; D.H.Dem.20

ἀωρί.definition: ), Adv. of at an untimely hour, too early, Heraclid.Com.1.2, Luc.Bis Acc.1, AP12.116; Ar.Fr.663 cod.; at dead of night, Theoc.11.40, 24.38; Antipho2.1.4, 2.4.5; Ar.Ec.741, Phalar.Ep.141.2
